title: Goldman Backs Fintech Startup Payhawk at $2 Billion Value
title_en: Goldman Backs Fintech Startup Payhawk at $2 Billion Value
author: Bloomberg
content_snippet: Payhawk, a fintech startup that helps businesses manage expenses, has raised fresh financing led by the growth equity arm …
summary_en: London-based fintech startup Payhawk raised $280 million in a Series C funding round led by Goldman Sachs, reaching a post-money valuation of $2 billion. The company provides enterprise-grade expense, invoice, and procurement management software, aiming to digitize traditional corporate finance workflows.
title_zh: Payhawk获高盛领投2.8亿美元融资，估值达20亿美元
summary_zh:
孙亚洲/彭博社：
总部位于伦敦的 Payhawk 提供企业费用和采购管理工具，以 20 亿美元的估值筹集了由高盛领投的 2.8 亿美元 C 轮融资 - Payhawk 是一家帮助企业管理费用的金融科技初创公司，已筹集了新的资金
article_content_zh:
Payhawk提供的一站式支出管理解决方案，主要面向中大型企业，通过整合企业信用卡、在线发票系统与财务报表生成，显著降低了企业的合规成本与财务流转周期。在全球化运营日益复杂的背景下，该工具的自动化处理能力成为其进入高估值梯队的竞争核心。

本轮由高盛领投的资金，预计将主要用于加速产品研发迭代，并进一步渗透欧洲与北美的中型企业市场。随着财务数字化转型的深入，Payhawk在整合银行API与自动化合规审计方面的技术领先地位，已成为其抵御传统银行卡发卡机构竞争的重要护城河。

title: Anthropic IPO set to deliver windfall to handful of smaller VC firms
title_en: Anthropic IPO set to deliver windfall to handful of smaller VC firms

inline_images.caption: Manager of pop superstar Madonna, Guy Oseary, stands to net more than $7bn from an early investment of just over $400mn © Jordan Vonderhaar/Bloomberg
inline_images.alt: Manager of pop superstar Madonna, Guy Oseary, stands to net more than $7bn from an early investment of just over $400mn © Jordan Vonderhaar/Bloomberg

author: George Hammond
article_content:
Anthropic’s initial public offering on Thursday will reorder Silicon Valley’s power rankings, with a small group of venture capitalists who bet early and aggressively on the AI lab set for a combined windfall of well over $100bn.

Anthropic is expected to be valued at $1.4tn or more when it lists. That would be about 2,300 times its value when Anjney Midha — an angel investor and founder of AMP PBC — first backed the company in 2021.

His firm is among a handful of lesser-known groups primed for massive returns at multiples that would surpass those of larger, blue-chip rivals. Others include Spark Capital, which would own about $11bn of stock at a $1.4tn valuation, and Factorial Funds, which would own just over $10bn, according to FT calculations.

Spark’s Yasmin Razavi and Factorial’s Sol Bier invested in Anthropic’s series C funding round, which closed in 2023, when the company was valued at about $4bn. Razavi sits on Anthropic’s board.

Meanwhile, the manager of pop superstar Madonna, Guy Oseary, stands to net more than $7bn from an early investment of just over $400mn.

“The deck chairs are shifting around in the VC landscape,” said a partner at one midsized VC firm which stands to make billions of dollars. “The leaders in the AI wave are not the same as they were in the previous waves. Different firms are moving up the leaderboard, and we’re glad to be among them.”

Amazon and Google, which have provided investment and computing resources to Anthropic, will collectively own close to 30 per cent of the company after the IPO.

The largest financial investor in the company, Iconiq Capital, holds a fraction of that. Nevertheless, its stake would be worth about $28bn at a $1.4tn valuation. It is followed by Lightspeed Ventures — which has invested roughly $3.2bn for a stake worth just over $25bn at the same valuation — and Menlo Ventures, which stands to return $21bn from an initial $1bn investment.

Coatue and Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund GIC invested later but went big. The pair led a funding round earlier this year which valued Anthropic at $380bn, and have each put close to $5bn into the company. Those stakes would be worth more than $10bn at an IPO price of $1.4tn.

Sound Ventures, which was founded by Oseary and actor Ashton Kutcher, and Bessemer Venture Partners are each poised for returns of about $7bn. For Bessemer, that would mark an eightfold increase on its initial investment, while Sound stands to make roughly 17 times its outlay.

Even those massive multiples are dwarfed, though, by the roughly 70-times return jailed crypto exchange founder Sam Bankman-Fried would have made if his company had not been forced to sell its $500mn stake in bankruptcy proceedings in 2024. That stake would be worth about $35bn at an IPO price of $1.4tn.

The clamour to own a stake in the AI company has increased in the past year, as the group’s revenues have leapfrogged rival OpenAI. A partner at one of Anthropic’s large investors said they “wrote [chief financial officer Krishna Rao] a love letter” as they jostled for access to a funding round earlier this year.

The take-off prompted OpenAI’s investors, including Brad Gerstner’s Altimeter, Sequoia Capital and Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund, to pour money into Anthropic, an unusual move in Silicon Valley, where VCs tend to back a single company in each field and founders prize fealty.

Other big-name venture firms, including Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, skipped Anthropic entirely.

“Call us old school . . . but we are serial monogamists,” said Josh Kushner, founder of Thrive, which is one of OpenAI’s largest and most vocal backers, in a since-deleted post on X.

Andreessen’s partners and Anthropic’s executives, meanwhile, have clashed over how best to regulate AI.

A successful IPO would also make thousands of Anthropic employees multimillionaires.

However, the company’s executives have framed fundraising as a necessary evil in the pursuit of their mission to responsibly “develop advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity”.

While its investors celebrate once-in-a-lifetime returns, Anthropic’s leadership is plotting a low-key IPO. The company has no plans for a party to celebrate the listing and intends to keep fanfare around what is set to be the biggest listing fundraise of all time to a minimum, said people with knowledge of the matter.

title_zh: Anthropic启动IPO，VC市场权力格局重塑
summary_zh: Anthropic计划上市，预估市值达1.4万亿美元，将导致早期风投机构获得千亿美元级回报，并改变硅谷创投权力排行榜
article_content_zh:
Anthropic 周四的首次公开募股将重新调整硅谷的实力排名，一小群早期积极押注人工智能实验室的风险投资家预计将获得远远超过 1000 亿美元的意外之财。

Anthropic 上市时预计估值为 1.4 兆美元或更高。这将是天使投资人兼 AMP PBC 创始人 Anjney Midha 于 2021 年首次支持该公司时市值的 2,300 倍。

他的公司是少数几家鲜为人知的集团之一，它们的回报倍数将超过规模更大的蓝筹竞争对手。根据英国《金融时报》的计算，其他公司包括 Spark Capital 和 Factorial Funds，前者将以 1.4 万亿美元的估值持有约 110 亿美元的股票，后者将持有略高于 100 亿美元的股票。

Spark 的 Yasmin Razavi 和 Factorial 的 Sol Bier 投资了 Anthropic 的 C 轮融资，该轮融资于 2023 年结束，当时该公司估值约为 40 亿美元。 Razavi 是 Anthropic 的董事会成员。

与此同时，流行巨星麦当娜的经纪人 Guy Oseary 有望从刚刚超过 4 亿美元的早期投资中净赚超过 70 亿美元。

“风投领域的躺椅正在发生变化，”一家中型风投公司的合伙人表示，该公司有望赚取数十亿美元。 “人工智能浪潮中的领导者与之前浪潮中的领导者不同。不同的公司正在排行榜上攀升，我们很高兴成为其中之一。”

为 Anthropic 提供投资和计算资源的亚马逊和谷歌在 IPO 后将共同持有该公司近 30% 的股份。

该公司最大的金融投资者 Iconiq Capital 持有其中的一小部分。尽管如此，按 1.4 万亿美元的估值计算，其股份价值约为 280 亿美元。紧随其后的是 Lightspeed Ventures（该公司已投资约 32 亿美元，以相同估值购买了价值略高于 250 亿美元的股份）和 Menlo Ventures（该公司将从最初 10 亿美元的投资中获得 210 亿美元的回报）。

Coatue 和新加坡主权财富基金 GIC 后来投资，但规模很大。今年早些时候，两人领投了一轮融资，对 Anthropic 的估值为 3800 亿美元，并各自向该公司投资了近 50 亿美元。按 1.4 万亿美元的 IPO 价格计算，这些股份的价值将超过 100 亿美元。

由 Oseary 和演员阿什顿·库彻 (Ashton Kutcher) 创立的 Sound Ventures 和 Bessemer Venture Partners 预计将获得约 70 亿美元的回报。对于 Bessemer 来说，这意味着其初始投资增加了 8 倍，而 Sound 的支出将增加约 17 倍。

不过，如果他的公司没有在 2024 年破产程序中被迫出售其 5 亿美元的股份，那么与被监禁的加密货币交易所创始人 Sam Bankman-Fried 获得的大约 70 倍的回报相比，即使是这些巨大的倍数也显得相形见绌。按 1.4 万亿美元的 IPO 价格计算，这些股份的价值约为 350 亿美元。

去年，随着该集团的收入超越了竞争对手 OpenAI，入股这家人工智能公司股份的呼声越来越高。 Anthropic 的一位大型投资者的合伙人表示，他们在今年早些时候争夺一轮融资时“写了一封情书”。

这一腾飞促使 OpenAI 的投资者，包括布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 的 Altimeter、红杉资本 (Sequoia Capital) 和彼得·泰尔 (Peter Thiel) 的创始人基金 (Peter Thiel) 等创始人基金，向 Anthropic 注入资金，这在硅谷是一个不寻常的举动，在硅谷，风投倾向于支持每个领域的一家公司，并且创始人会高度忠诚。

其他知名风险投资公司，包括 Thrive Capital 和 Andreessen Horowitz，完全跳过了 Anthropic。

article_content_en:
The Solana Foundation has taken a majority interest in CoinGecko, one of the crypto ecosystem’s most popular price-tracking platforms.

The deal could bring Solana-based trading to CoinGecko's 18 million registered users, according to a Solana Foundation announcement. The platform also supplies market data to 180,000 crypto apps and businesses through its data interfaces, the foundation said.

Solana Foundation’s chief product officer, Vibhu Norby, revealed the majority stake on social media, though neither side disclosed the purchase price or the foundation’s exact stake.

CoinDesk has reached out for comments but hasn’t heard back at the time of writing.

The deal, announced at the Breakpoint conference in London, will focus on expanding CoinGecko's market data, research tools and exploring trading.

The foundation said it plans to bring Solana-powered trading to CoinGecko's website, GeckoTerminal platform and mobile app. Norby also outlined plans for decentralized finance tools and broader coverage of stocks and tokenized real-world assets.

CoinGecko's own announcement described trading as an area under exploration. The move could let users research tokens, track prices and place trades without leaving CoinGecko, giving Solana a new way to reach crypto investors.

CoinGecko also plans to expand coverage of blockchain-based assets, derivatives and tokenized real-world assets while improving its data services for businesses and financial firms.

The deal comes years after leading cryptocurrency exchange Binance acquired rival crypto market data provider CoinMarketCap in 2020

CoinGecko said it would maintain coverage of the wider crypto market using its own technology and public data methods.

article_content_zh:
Solana 基金会持有 CoinGecko 的多数股权，CoinGecko 是加密生态系统中最受欢迎的价格跟踪平台之一。

根据 Solana 基金会的公告，这笔交易可以为 CoinGecko 的 1800 万注册用户带来基于 Solana 的交易。该基金会表示，该平台还通过其数据接口向 180,000 个加密应用程序和企业提供市场数据。

Solana 基金会首席产品官 Vibhu Norby 在社交媒体上透露了多数股权，但双方均未透露购买价格或基金会的确切股权。

CoinDesk 已联系征求意见，但截至撰写本文时尚未收到回复。

该交易于伦敦 Breakpoint 会议上宣布，将专注于扩展 CoinGecko 的市场数据、研究工具和探索交易。

该基金会表示，计划将 Solana 支持的交易引入 CoinGecko 的网站、GeckoTerminal 平台和移动应用程序。诺比还概述了去中心化金融工具以及更广泛的股票和代币化现实世界资产覆盖范围的计划。

CoinGecko 自己的公告将交易描述为一个正在探索的领域。此举可以让用户在不离开 CoinGecko 的情况下研究代币、跟踪价格和进行交易，从而为 Solana 提供了接触加密货币投资者的新方式。

CoinGecko 还计划扩大基于区块链的资产、衍生品和代币化现实世界资产的覆盖范围，同时改善其为企业和金融公司提供的数据服务。

这笔交易是在领先的加密货币交易所 Binance 于 2020 年收购竞争对手加密市场数据提供商 CoinMarketCap 数年后达成的

CoinGecko 表示，它将利用自己的技术和公共数据方法来维持对更广泛的加密货币市场的覆盖。

author: Nick Indge
article_content:
Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”

The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.

### All about agents

Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability.

Also announced as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a company’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

Copilot Workspaces is a collaborative environment currently available through Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program, but coming soon will be the ability to bring personal Autopilot agents into Workspaces. Early in the keynote address, Nadella said that “Until now, AI interactions have mostly been single-player. Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience, where people and agents drive towards a common goal, with shared context.”

### Governance over trust

Trust, the third pillar of Microsoft’s new frontier ecosystem, was something that Nadella continued returning to during his presentation, and not in a way that some might expect. “We find ourselves in a place where alignment is elusive. Mechanistic understanding of these models is elusive. The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,” he said.

In a departure from the norms of “AI is magic” corporate hype sentiment, Nadella conceded that the internal workings of AI thought processes remain difficult to understand, and models cannot be trusted to govern themselves, regardless of whether their answers are accurate. Nadella described the solution as “an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence” from the authority granted to it. Microsoft says each Autopilot agent will have a unique ID, and administrators can restrict permissions or block it entirely. All agent activities are logged for human review, and Autopilot can ask for human approval before engaging in certain actions.

The promised agent controls and admission that AI systems can’t always be trusted are meaningful, but Microsoft is asking businesses and users to place their trust in the company’s own safeguards instead, though the effectiveness of those safeguards against mistakes, rogue actions, or data exposure will still have to be demonstrated. In Microsoft’s view, the solution to untrustworthy intelligence is not to make AI agents trustworthy, but to control what they’re permitted to do. Businesses will have to decide how much autonomy they delegate to agents.

Along with the guardrails, Microsoft announced what it calls the “AI Transparency Initiative.” The effort has partnered with 40-plus major companies, including Adobe and Mastercard, to develop open, industrywide standards for AI governance and security. Nadella described the initiative as a way for industry to “help establish an open standard that makes AI safer, more transparent, and more accessible.”

### Minding and measuring token-spend

Along with the other announced additions, Microsoft also announced expanding capabilities for Agent 365, its existing control plane for managing AI agents across enterprise environments. The new agent sheriff extends existing identity, security, and management systems to AI agents. Microsoft describes the objective as providing “observability at every layer of the stack.” Agent 365 offers governance controls over agent behavior in what Microsoft says is “autonomous in execution, but bounded and supervised.”

Along with Agent 365 comes Agent 365 Business Analytics: “You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage. You can see exactly what’s driving the spend and connect the spend to the outcomes that drive business value,” said Nadella. Customers will be able to see real-world costs associated with AI token-spend, and compare those metrics to the value of work performed. Microsoft acknowledged that the estimations of assisted work hours are determined by a model, and not a direct measurement of time that may have been saved. This is a telling concession for Microsoft to make as businesses evaluate whether there will be an ROI on AI implementations, but according to Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, “anything you can do with Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, for less.”

### The outage in the room

Nadella offered only a brief acknowledgment of last week’s outage that disrupted access to services like Exchange Online and Teams for users across the globe. “Last week was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world,” he said. “We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously, and in that context I know we have work to do.”

That statement was all the time the elephant in the room was given, but Microsoft did seem to acknowledge the public’s growing concern over data center projects by highlighting the previously discussed “community-first AI infrastructure plan.” Not a surprise in a presentation that asks organizations to extend more autonomy to software agents, at a time when Microsoft’s existing infrastructure is under increased scrutiny.

title_zh: Copilot 是“新的工作操作系统”，现在 Office 在其中运行
summary_zh: 微软在Ignite大会宣布Office三件套深度集成至Copilot，并推出具备自主代理能力的Copilot Autopilot及组织智能平台Work IQ
article_content_zh:
微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉在Ignite大会的主旨演讲开场时，阐述了公司对其全新“前沿生态系统”的愿景，并于周二宣布Word、Excel和PowerPoint在Copilot中的正式上线，他将Copilot描述为“全新的工作操作系统”。

这一公告与我们传统上使用软件的方式截然相反。微软设想的新版Copilot集成不再是像Word这样的应用程序成为亮点，而Clippy则作为助手帮助您使用它，而是……

### 关于代理商的一切

根据微软的说法，Copilot Autopilot（不要与 Windows Autopilot 混淆）是“持久、主动的个人生产力代理”。简而言之，Autopilot 是一个基于云的自主人工智能代理，用户可以将职责委派给它，而不仅仅是单个任务。 Autopilot 可以被授权跨电子邮件和日历等服务工作，并完成分配给它的任务，作为其角色的一部分。 Autopilot 将通过 Copilot Credits 使用基于使用情况的计费，但最终定价尚未在全面上市之前公布。

主题演讲中还宣布全面推出 Microsoft IQ，这是一个包含 Work IQ 的智能平台，Work IQ 是一个上下文层，可帮助代理了解公司的通信、关系和正在进行的工作。纳德拉将工作智商描述为也许是公司最有价值的数据库：“它对人、他们与其他人的关系、你的电子邮件、你的会议、聊天、构成工作所有结构的项目有深入的了解。”公司是否希望自主代理能够访问内部文档和消息传递数据必须由他们自己的内部 IT 审查决定。

Copilot Workspaces 是一种协作环境，目前可通过 Microsoft Frontier 早期访问计划获得，但很快就能将个人 Autopilot 代理引入 Workspaces。在主题演讲的早期，纳德拉表示，“到目前为止，人工智能交互大多是单人游戏。工作空间使其成为真正的多人游戏体验，人们和代理在共享背景下朝着共同的目标前进。”

### 信任治理

信任是微软新前沿生态系统的第三个支柱，纳德拉在演讲中继续提到这一点，但方式却出乎一些人的预料。 “我们发现自己处于一个难以捉摸的境地。对这些模型的机械理解也难以捉摸。问题是：你怎么能相信所有这些强大的技术？现实是，根据定义，你不能，”他说。

纳德拉与“人工智能是魔法”的企业炒作情绪的规范背道而驰，他承认人工智能思维过程的内部运作仍然难以理解，而且无论模型的答案是否准确，都不能相信模型能够自我管理。纳德拉将该解决方案描述为“将情报供应与授予的权限分开的架构上的必要条件”。微软表示，每个 Autopilot 代理都会有一个唯一的 ID，管理员可以限制权限或完全阻止它。所有代理活动都会被记录下来以供人工审核，并且 Autopilot 可以在执行某些操作之前请求人工批准。

承诺的代理控制和承认人工智能系统并不总是值得信任是有意义的，但微软要求企业和用户转而信任公司自己的防护措施，尽管这些防护措施针对错误、流氓行为或数据泄露的有效性仍需证明。在微软看来，解决不可信情报问题的方法不是让人工智能代理变得值得信赖，而是控制他们被允许做的事情。企业必须决定将多少自主权委托给代理商。

除了护栏之外，微软还宣布了所谓的“人工智能透明度倡议”。该项目已与 Adob​​e 和 Mastercard 等 40 多家大公司合作，为人工智能治理和安全制定开放的全行业标准。纳德拉将该倡议描述为行业“帮助建立开放标准，使人工智能更安全、更透明、更容易获得”的一种方式。

### 关注和衡量代币支出

除了宣布的其他功能外，微软还宣布扩展 Agent 365 的功能，Agent 365 是其现有的控制平面，用于跨企业环境管理 AI 代理。新的特工警长将现有的身份、安全和管理系统扩展到人工智能 智能体。微软将目标描述为“在堆栈的每一层提供可观察性”。 Agent 365 提供对代理行为的治理控制，微软称其“执行自主，但有界和监督”。

与 Agent 365 一起推出的还有 Agent 365 业务分析：“您可以简单地将其视为人工智能使用的 ERP 系统。您可以准确地看到推动支出的因素，并将支出与推动业务价值的结果联系起来。”纳德拉说道。客户将能够看到与人工智能代币支出相关的实际成本，并将这些指标与所执行工作的价值进行比较。微软承认，辅助工作时间的估计是由模型确定的，而不是对可能节省的时间的直接测量。当企业评估人工智能实施是否会带来投资回报时，这是微软做出的一个有说服力的让步，但根据微软商业业务首席执行官 Judson Althoff 的说法，“任何你能用 Claude 或 ChatGPT 做的事情，你都可以用 Copilot 做得更好，而且成本更低。”

### 房间停电了

纳德拉仅简要承认上周的服务中断，导致全球用户对 Exchange Online 和 Teams 等服务的访问中断。 “上周提醒人们，数字基础设施作为世界的拨号音是多么重要，”他说。 “我们知道您对我们服务的信任，并非常认真地对待这一责任，在这种情况下，我知道我们还有很多工作要做。”

这种说法一直是房间里的大象，但微软确实通过强调之前讨论的“社区优先的人工智能基础设施计划”，似乎承认了公众对数据中心项目日益增长的担忧。在微软现有基础设施受到更严格审查的情况下，要求组织向软件代理提供更多自主权的演讲并不令人意外。

article_content_en:
Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company’s vision for its new “frontier ecosystem,” announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as “the new OS for work.”

The announcement is a striking inversion of how we’ve traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent’s work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications.

The rollout marks a major step toward the Copilot redesign the company first announced in September. Parts of that vision are now becoming “generally available,” as Nadella puts it, with autonomous agents and new governance tools arriving alongside them.

### All about agents

Copilot Autopilot (not to be confused with Windows Autopilot) is a “persistent, proactive agent for personal productivity” according to Microsoft. In a nutshell, Autopilot is a cloud-based autonomous AI agent that users can delegate responsibilities to, not just single tasks. Autopilot can be authorized to work across services like email and calendars and complete tasks assigned to it as part of its role. Autopilot will use usage-based billing via Copilot Credits, but final pricing has not been announced ahead of general availability.

Also announced as generally available at the keynote speech was Microsoft IQ, an intelligence platform that houses Work IQ, a context layer that helps agents understand a company’s communications, relationships, and ongoing work. Nadella described Work IQ as perhaps a company’s most valuable database: “It has a deep understanding of the people, their relationships to other people, your emails, your meetings, chats, projects that make up all the fabric of work.” Whether companies want autonomous agents to have access to internal documents and messaging data will have to be determined by their own internal IT review.

Copilot Workspaces is a collaborative environment currently available through Microsoft’s Frontier early-access program, but coming soon will be the ability to bring personal Autopilot agents into Workspaces. Early in the keynote address, Nadella said that “Until now, AI interactions have mostly been single-player. Workspaces makes it a truly multiplayer experience, where people and agents drive towards a common goal, with shared context.”

### Governance over trust

Trust, the third pillar of Microsoft’s new frontier ecosystem, was something that Nadella continued returning to during his presentation, and not in a way that some might expect. “We find ourselves in a place where alignment is elusive. Mechanistic understanding of these models is elusive. The question is: How can you even trust all this powerful technology? The reality is, by definition, you can’t,” he said.

In a departure from the norms of “AI is magic” corporate hype sentiment, Nadella conceded that the internal workings of AI thought processes remain difficult to understand, and models cannot be trusted to govern themselves, regardless of whether their answers are accurate. Nadella described the solution as “an architectural imperative to separate the supply of intelligence” from the authority granted to it. Microsoft says each Autopilot agent will have a unique ID, and administrators can restrict permissions or block it entirely. All agent activities are logged for human review, and Autopilot can ask for human approval before engaging in certain actions.

The promised agent controls and admission that AI systems can’t always be trusted are meaningful, but Microsoft is asking businesses and users to place their trust in the company’s own safeguards instead, though the effectiveness of those safeguards against mistakes, rogue actions, or data exposure will still have to be demonstrated. In Microsoft’s view, the solution to untrustworthy intelligence is not to make AI agents trustworthy, but to control what they’re permitted to do. Businesses will have to decide how much autonomy they delegate to agents.

Along with the guardrails, Microsoft announced what it calls the “AI Transparency Initiative.” The effort has partnered with 40-plus major companies, including Adobe and Mastercard, to develop open, industrywide standards for AI governance and security. Nadella described the initiative as a way for industry to “help establish an open standard that makes AI safer, more transparent, and more accessible.”

### Minding and measuring token-spend

Along with the other announced additions, Microsoft also announced expanding capabilities for Agent 365, its existing control plane for managing AI agents across enterprise environments. The new agent sheriff extends existing identity, security, and management systems to AI agents. Microsoft describes the objective as providing “observability at every layer of the stack.” Agent 365 offers governance controls over agent behavior in what Microsoft says is “autonomous in execution, but bounded and supervised.”

Along with Agent 365 comes Agent 365 Business Analytics: “You can simply think of this as an ERP system of AI usage. You can see exactly what’s driving the spend and connect the spend to the outcomes that drive business value,” said Nadella. Customers will be able to see real-world costs associated with AI token-spend, and compare those metrics to the value of work performed. Microsoft acknowledged that the estimations of assisted work hours are determined by a model, and not a direct measurement of time that may have been saved. This is a telling concession for Microsoft to make as businesses evaluate whether there will be an ROI on AI implementations, but according to Judson Althoff, CEO of Microsoft Commercial Business, “anything you can do with Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, for less.”

### The outage in the room

Nadella offered only a brief acknowledgment of last week’s outage that disrupted access to services like Exchange Online and Teams for users across the globe. “Last week was a reminder of how critical digital infrastructure is as the dial tone for the world,” he said. “We know the trust you place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously, and in that context I know we have work to do.”

That statement was all the time the elephant in the room was given, but Microsoft did seem to acknowledge the public’s growing concern over data center projects by highlighting the previously discussed “community-first AI infrastructure plan.” Not a surprise in a presentation that asks organizations to extend more autonomy to software agents, at a time when Microsoft’s existing infrastructure is under increased scrutiny.

title: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship
title_en: Over a Third of Gen Z-ers Rely on AI for Friendship

inline_images.caption: Person sitting looking out of a window while in a silhouette of two people taking a selfie.
inline_images.alt: Person sitting looking out of a window while in a silhouette of two people taking a selfie.

author: Jason Parham
article_content:
As generational cohorts go, Gen Z has been saddled with its share of labels. They scarcely have sex, are “quiet quitters” when it comes to office jobs, and, as they avoid traditional partnership, have learned to solomaxx.

Whether these labels are deserved or completely off the mark, what continually connects this unique class of young people is a desire to reconstruct how they think about connection.

In “Friendship in an Online-Offline World: Digital Life, Connection and Wellbeing” researchers from public polling firm Gallup and the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children’s Hospital found that more than one-third of Gen Z (33 percent) rely on AI for companionship. The percentage was higher among daily AI users, spiking to 50 percent, and 42 percent among those with online-only friends.

Rather than measure the consequences of screen time alone, the report examines who Gen Z connects with and how those relationships not only account for their social lives but also how they impact their mental health. While in-person friendships were rated the highest for “strength and support” and were “associated with the most positive emotional experiences,” young people who rely on online-only friends or AI as a social companion may have higher odds of loneliness than those who do not.

Researchers examined three modes of what they consider close connection: in-person friendships, friendships that started IRL but are sustained online, and online-only friendships where a young person has never met their friend in real life. The survey, conducted between May and August, sampled 15,925 people aged 15 to 22 across 16 countries, and suggests that Gen Z benefits more from IRL relationships compared to digital ones, despite nearly half of young people in the US having at least one close online-only friend.

“Adolescence is a time when you thrive when you socialize, and so they’re looking for all of these contexts to socialize in,” says David Bickham, research director of the Digital Wellness Lab. “I don’t necessarily see it as, oh, these kids have some sort of major deficit and are looking to AI. I see it as these are young people who are growing up in a time of AI, the most powerful way to find information online, and the more they use it, they see and are more engaged with the social side of it.”

While AI may help fill a genuine social gap, it hasn’t yet taken the place of their IRL bonds. “In-person and digitally mediated friendships coexist within the same social life,” write the authors of the report.

When it comes to maintaining those affiliations, Instagram and Discord—surprisingly, not TikTok—were the top platforms in the US for staying in touch with online-only friends. Bickham also noted that “loneliness specifically may be something that these online relationships can’t quite compensate for.”

“Kids who are reporting loneliness really do things online that are consistent with trying to make friends. They talk to people they don't know, which is always a risk, but it’s also how you make friends,” Bickham says. The report found that Gen Z men, who were more likely to have digital friendships than women, often encountered new acquaintances through gaming, while young women mentioned social media as their most common category to cultivate connection. “What’s intriguing is that boys who are higher in social anxiety are less likely to make connections. They tend to do things by themselves, but when it comes to AI, what we found is that kids who are still lonely are going to seek out connections” with chatbots, Bickham says.

Recent debates over teen screen time have centered on whether digital devices are driving a youth mental health crisis or if the concerns are overstated. Some critics believe that by only measuring screen time it overlooks the type of content young people watch. This year, social media bans and age-restriction policies for minors took effect in Australia and the UK. In the US, where state legislators have introduced bills to curb addictive design features, a majority of Americans support banning kids under 16 from using social media, according to a recent Pew Research survey.

Jon-Patrick Allem, an associate professor at the Rutgers School of Public Health, wrote last year in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine that research on the topic has primarily focused on “blunt measures of screen time” and that doing so would “treat all content consumed online as uniform.” Allem concluded that this approach is “deficient” and called on researchers to set a new agenda that instead investigates the actual content kids were consuming, not just time spent.

It was also important to Bickham and his team to look beyond a surface-level analysis of screen time and consider the nature of the relationships being formed while young people were online, zeroing in on how that time is spent and who it’s spent with.

“It’s very difficult to measure screen time accurately in a survey. Mainly because half the kids told us this was something they’re doing all the time. article_content_zh:
随着一代人的发展，Z 世代已经背负着自己的标签。他们几乎没有性生活，在办公室工作中是“安静的放弃者”，并且由于他们避免传统的伙伴关系，所以学会了独奏。

无论这些标签是实至名归还是完全不合时宜，将这一独特的年轻人阶层不断联系在一起的是重建他们对联系的看法的愿望。

公共民意调查公司盖洛普和波士顿儿童医院数字健康实验室的研究人员在《线上线下世界中的友谊：数字生活、联系和幸福》中发现，超过三分之一的 Z 世代 (33%) 依靠人工智能来陪伴。日常 AI 用户中这一比例更高，飙升至 50%，而那些只在网上交朋友的用户中这一比例为 42%。

该报告并没有单独衡量屏幕时间的影响，而是研究了 Z 世代与谁有联系，以及这些关系如何影响他们的社交生活，以及如何影响他们的心理健康。虽然面对面的友谊在“力量和支持”方面被评为最高，并且“与最积极的情感体验相关”，但依赖网上朋友或人工智能作为社交伴侣的年轻人可能比那些不依赖网络朋友或人工智能的年轻人更容易感到孤独。

研究人员研究了他们认为的密切联系的三种模式：面对面的友谊、在现实生活中开始但在网上维持的友谊，以及年轻人在现实生活中从未见过朋友的纯网络友谊。这项调查于 5 月至 8 月期间进行，对 16 个国家 15,925 名 15 至 22 岁的人进行了抽样调查，结果表明，尽管近一半的美国年轻人至少拥有一位只在网上的亲密朋友，但与数字关系相比，Z 世代从现实关系中受益更多。

数字健康实验室研究主任戴维·比克汉姆 (David Bickham) 表示：“青春期是一个社交能力强的时期，因此他们会寻找所有这些社交环境。” “我不一定认为，哦，这些孩子有某种重大缺陷，正在寻求人工智能。我认为这些年轻人是在人工智能时代长大的，人工智能是在线查找信息的最强大方式，他们使用它的次数越多，他们就会看到并更多地参与其中的社交方面。”

虽然人工智能可能有助于填补真正的社会差距，但它尚未取代他们的现实生活纽带。该报告的作者写道：“面对面的友谊和数字化的友谊在同一个社交生活中共存。”

在维持这些联系方面，Instagram 和 Discord（令人惊讶的是，而不是 TikTok）是美国与只在网上的朋友保持联系的顶级平台。比克汉姆还指出，“特别是孤独感可能是这些在线关系无法完全弥补的。”

“那些表示孤独的孩子确实会在网上做一些与试图交朋友相一致的事情。他们与不认识的人交谈，这总是存在风险，但这也是交朋友的方式，”比克汉姆说。报告发现，Z 世代男性比女性更有可能拥有数字友谊，他们经常通过游戏结识新朋友，而年轻女性则将社交媒体视为最常见的培养联系的类别。 “有趣的是，社交焦虑程度较高的男孩不太可能建立联系。他们倾向于自己做事，但当谈到人工智能时，我们发现仍然孤独的孩子会寻求与聊天机器人的联系”，比克汉姆说。

最近关于青少年屏幕时间的争论集中在数字设备是否正在引发青少年心理健康危机，或者这种担忧是否被夸大了。一些批评者认为，仅衡量屏幕时间会忽略年轻人观看的内容类型。今年，针对未成年人的社交媒体禁令和年龄限制政策在澳大利亚和英国生效。在美国，各州立法者提出了遏制令人上瘾的设计功能的法案，根据皮尤研究中心 (Pew Research) 最近的一项调查，大多数美国人支持禁止 16 岁以下的儿童使用社交媒体。

罗格斯大学公共卫生学院副教授乔恩·帕特里克·阿勒姆（Jon-Patrick Allem）去年在《美国预防医学杂志》上撰文称，该主题的研究主要集中在“对屏幕时间的直接测量”，这样做将“将所有在线消费的内容视为统一的”。阿勒姆得出的结论是，这种方法是“有缺陷的”，并呼吁研究人员制定一个新的议程，调查孩子们实际消费的内容，而不仅仅是花费的时间。

对于比克汉姆和他的团队来说，同样重要的是要超越对屏幕时间的表面分析，并考虑年轻人上网时形成的关系的性质，重点关注如何度过这些时间以及与谁一起度过。

“在调查中准确测量屏幕时间非常困难。主要是因为一半的孩子告诉我们这是他们一直在做的事情。更重要的发现是关系的质量。决定你结果的是你使用这些平台的方式，而不仅仅是你使用它们的时间。”

数字健康实验室之前的一份报告绘制了美国、巴西和法国青少年对人工智能的使用情况，发现 13 至 17 岁的青少年除了寻求陪伴之外，还向人工智能寻求个人建议和创造性工作。

article_content_en:
As generational cohorts go, Gen Z has been saddled with its share of labels. They scarcely have sex, are “quiet quitters” when it comes to office jobs, and, as they avoid traditional partnership, have learned to solomaxx.

Whether these labels are deserved or completely off the mark, what continually connects this unique class of young people is a desire to reconstruct how they think about connection.

In “Friendship in an Online-Offline World: Digital Life, Connection and Wellbeing” researchers from public polling firm Gallup and the Digital Wellness Lab at Boston Children’s Hospital found that more than one-third of Gen Z (33 percent) rely on AI for companionship. The percentage was higher among daily AI users, spiking to 50 percent, and 42 percent among those with online-only friends.

Rather than measure the consequences of screen time alone, the report examines who Gen Z connects with and how those relationships not only account for their social lives but also how they impact their mental health. While in-person friendships were rated the highest for “strength and support” and were “associated with the most positive emotional experiences,” young people who rely on online-only friends or AI as a social companion may have higher odds of loneliness than those who do not.

Researchers examined three modes of what they consider close connection: in-person friendships, friendships that started IRL but are sustained online, and online-only friendships where a young person has never met their friend in real life. The survey, conducted between May and August, sampled 15,925 people aged 15 to 22 across 16 countries, and suggests that Gen Z benefits more from IRL relationships compared to digital ones, despite nearly half of young people in the US having at least one close online-only friend.

“Adolescence is a time when you thrive when you socialize, and so they’re looking for all of these contexts to socialize in,” says David Bickham, research director of the Digital Wellness Lab. “I don’t necessarily see it as, oh, these kids have some sort of major deficit and are looking to AI. I see it as these are young people who are growing up in a time of AI, the most powerful way to find information online, and the more they use it, they see and are more engaged with the social side of it.”

While AI may help fill a genuine social gap, it hasn’t yet taken the place of their IRL bonds. “In-person and digitally mediated friendships coexist within the same social life,” write the authors of the report.

When it comes to maintaining those affiliations, Instagram and Discord—surprisingly, not TikTok—were the top platforms in the US for staying in touch with online-only friends. Bickham also noted that “loneliness specifically may be something that these online relationships can’t quite compensate for.”

“Kids who are reporting loneliness really do things online that are consistent with trying to make friends. They talk to people they don't know, which is always a risk, but it’s also how you make friends,” Bickham says. The report found that Gen Z men, who were more likely to have digital friendships than women, often encountered new acquaintances through gaming, while young women mentioned social media as their most common category to cultivate connection. “What’s intriguing is that boys who are higher in social anxiety are less likely to make connections. They tend to do things by themselves, but when it comes to AI, what we found is that kids who are still lonely are going to seek out connections” with chatbots, Bickham says.

Recent debates over teen screen time have centered on whether digital devices are driving a youth mental health crisis or if the concerns are overstated. Some critics believe that by only measuring screen time it overlooks the type of content young people watch. This year, social media bans and age-restriction policies for minors took effect in Australia and the UK. In the US, where state legislators have introduced bills to curb addictive design features, a majority of Americans support banning kids under 16 from using social media, according to a recent Pew Research survey.

Jon-Patrick Allem, an associate professor at the Rutgers School of Public Health, wrote last year in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine that research on the topic has primarily focused on “blunt measures of screen time” and that doing so would “treat all content consumed online as uniform.” Allem concluded that this approach is “deficient” and called on researchers to set a new agenda that instead investigates the actual content kids were consuming, not just time spent.

It was also important to Bickham and his team to look beyond a surface-level analysis of screen time and consider the nature of the relationships being formed while young people were online, zeroing in on how that time is spent and who it’s spent with.

“It’s very difficult to measure screen time accurately in a survey. Mainly because half the kids told us this was something they’re doing all the time. A more important finding is the quality of relationship. It’s how you use these platforms that’s going to dictate your outcome, not just how long you use them for.”

A previous report from the Digital Wellness Lab mapped the use of AI among teenagers in the US, Brazil, and France and found that teens aged 13 to 17 were turning to AI for personal advice and creative work, in addition to companionship.

While researchers are wary of classifying the report as a permanent shift in how young people form relationships, they say it does signal a growing reliance on AI companionship as part of a pattern of digital social engagement unfolding among Gen Z.

“It wouldn’t be surprising if AI companionship becomes more common over the next five years as AI becomes integrated into young people’s everyday lives,” says Andrew Dugan, a principal researcher at Gallup. “But whether young people are turning to AI because they feel lonely, or whether AI companionship might reinforce those feelings, remains an important question for future research.”

title: YouTube found a new way to inflate view counts
title_en: YouTube found a new way to inflate view counts
author: Emma Roth
article_content:
YouTube’s view counts will now include the number of people that it estimates are watching a video together on TV. In an update on Monday, the platform says it’s bringing “co-views” to public view counts across long-form videos, Shorts, and live content to provide a more “complete picture” of how people are using its platform.

YouTube, which has become even more popular on TVs than phones, also says the change will help it align with “TV industry standards,” which similarly record views by estimating the number of people watching shows. The company says it doesn’t use devices, like cameras or microphones, to estimate how many people are watching a video on TV. Instead, it estimates co-views using a “privacy safe statistical model” that takes into account “demographic patterns and viewing times.”

This marks yet another update to YouTube’s view count system. In August, the platform began counting a view as soon as a video starts playing. The company said at the time that creators will notice their view counts increasing faster as a result of this change, and it seems like adding co-views could boost these numbers as well.

YouTube notes that it will only apply co-views to new views on TV going forward, and that they won’t appear retroactively. Co-views also won’t affect a creator’s ad revenue, YouTube Partner Program eligibility, or revenue.

YouTube notes that it will only apply co-views to new views on TV going forward, and that they won’t appear retroactively. Co-views also won’t affect a creator’s ad revenue, YouTube Partner Program eligibility, or revenue.
paragraphs: YouTube’s view counts will now include the number of people that it estimates are watching a video together on TV. In an update on Monday, the platform says it’s bringing “co-views” to public view counts across long-form videos, Shorts, and live content to provide a more “complete picture” of how people are using its platform.

YouTube, which has become even more popular on TVs than phones, also says the change will help it align with “TV industry standards,” which similarly record views by estimating the number of people watching shows. The company says it doesn’t use devices, like cameras or microphones, to estimate how many people are watching a video on TV. Instead, it estimates co-views using a “privacy safe statistical model” that takes into account “demographic patterns and viewing times.”

YouTube 的观看次数现在将包括估计在电视上一起观看视频的人数。该平台在周一的更新中表示，它将在长视频、短视频和直播内容的公众观看次数中引入“共同观看次数”，以提供人们如何使用其平台的更“完整的画面”。

YouTube 在电视上比手机上更受欢迎，该公司还表示，这一变化将有助于其与“电视行业标准”保持一致，该标准同样通过估计观看节目的人数来记录观看次数。该公司表示，它不使用摄像头或麦克风等设备来估计有多少人正在观看电视上的视频。相反，它使用“隐私安全统计模型”来估计共同观看次数，该模型考虑了“人口统计模式和观看时间”。

这标志着 YouTube 观看次数系统的又一次更新。八月份，该平台开始在视频开始播放后计算观看次数。该公司当时表示，创作者会注意到，由于这一变化，他们的观看次数增加得更快，而且增加共同观看次数似乎也可以提高这些数字。

YouTube 指出，它只会将共同观看次数应用于未来电视上的新观看次数，并且不会追溯显示。共同观看也不会影响创作者的广告收入、YouTube 合作伙伴计划资格或收入。

title: LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform
title_en: LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform
author: Kyt Dotson
article_content:
LanceDB Inc., the developer of database technology designed to speed up artificial intelligence models, today announced it has raised $57.5 million in early-stage funding to bring a multimodal lakehouse to researchers, model builders and platform teams.

Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led the Series B round. Other investors in the round included Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV and Y Combinator, bringing the company’s total funding to $98.5 million.

AI is making it easier to create and interpret increasingly complex forms of data, but creating it also brings an infrastructure problem. LanceDB is tackling this problem by providing a unified multimodal data lakehouse, giving researchers, enterprise outfits and AI agents a unified way to access, find, prepare and train on that data without spending weeks managing the underlying infrastructure.

“Typically, research teams have to put different parts of their dataset in different places, and they lose weeks or months getting a whole training dataset ready for that single training run at the end of the day,” co-founder and Chief Executive Chang She told SiliconANGLE in an interview. “There’s a missing data layer for AI today, and that’s what we’re trying to build.”

LanceDB’s technology is built on Lance, an open-source data format designed for AI workloads that combines structured information with images, video and other large files. Unlike traditional analytics formats optimized for processing entire tables, Lance supports the rapid retrieval and modification of individual records, making it particularly useful for searching and preparing massive training datasets.

The company built this format into a large-scale data lakehouse for retrieval, which is needed for the sheer scale of information needed to train modern AI models. A lakehouse combines the flexibility of a data lake, which can store enormous amounts of raw information, with database-style capabilities for organizing, querying and managing that data.

“Part of what makes multimodal data different and more difficult is the size of the data,” She explained.

By bringing multimodality to the lakehouse format, LanceDB brings different forms of AI training data into a single platform, allowing developers to search, organize and prepare their datasets without maintaining separate systems for each data type. It can connect directly to customers’ existing cloud storage, where the data remains, while distributing computational workloads across the infrastructure required to process it.

### The challenge of multimodal data for AI

Multimodal AI involves more than combining text, audio, images and video. Autonomous vehicles, robotics and world models also involve three-dimensional sensor information, geospatial coordinates, time-series data and annotations that explain what the sensors are detecting.

For example, a self-driving car doesn’t merely capture an image. Its sensors might produce a three-dimensional representation of the surrounding environment, which then needs to be associated with information that identifies roads, pedestrians, vegetation and other objects.

The sheer amount of data included in lidar 3D clouds, images, video, audio and more can take up, on average, 10 to 20 petabytes of data in a single table for many large training workflows, with some becoming even larger – potentially approaching 80 to 100 petabytes. Researchers and model builders may maintain huge pools of data across different systems because conventional platforms weren’t designed around the requirements of multimodal AI.

Researchers must then assemble, reconcile and store different components of a training dataset to enrich it for training. The curation itself can take weeks or months just to move, prepare and process. LanceDB’s answer is to manage the infrastructure itself without ever copying or moving data from enterprise or research storage, giving it a single unified access point.

“The data stays in place,” She explained. “It remains yours. We don’t need to copy it.”

In short, LanceDB isn’t simply introducing a new way to store data; the objective is to provide a way to access the data less often, without needing to copy, convert or move it through network infrastructure. This greatly speeds up what She refers to as the “AI flywheel,” which is currently driven by feeding AI models good data as quickly as possible to mint and roll them out.

“The faster we can make that spin, the faster research teams can get to higher quality models and allow us to make even more interesting AI applications,” She said.

Notable customers include Runway AI Inc., which adopted LanceDB’s enterprise platform as its AI training needs expanded. Netflix Inc. built a media data lake on the technology for content creation. And Microsoft Corp. uses the platform as a data layer for training models on tens of billions of rows of image and code data. The platform lets these organizations consolidate data management, search, curation and feature engineering into a unified workflow, helping researchers prepare training datasets at petabyte scale without juggling separate infrastructure systems.

“A training example at Runway doesn’t stay still,” said Runway Chief Technology Officer Kamil Sindi. “It starts as a video and a prompt, then we add embeddings, resolution and duration metadata, whatever the next experiment needs. We first started using the Lance format in 2024 because it was the only option that handled unstructured data, column appends, distributed reads and ad-hoc SQL all at once. We’ve since become a LanceDB Enterprise customer.”

She said LanceDB intends to use the new funding to expand its multimodal data platform and accelerate the AI model development cycle, particularly by improving large-scale data curation, feature engineering and data loading to keep thousands of graphics processing units supplied efficiently during training. The company will also deepen its support for emerging AI workloads, including video generation, world models and robotics, where researchers must manage growing volumes of first-person sensor data, synthetic data and other multimodal information.

article_content_zh:
LanceDB Inc. 是一家旨在加速人工智能模型速度的数据库技术开发商，今天宣布已筹集 5750 万美元的早期资金，为研究人员、模型构建者和平台团队提供多模式湖屋。

Bessemer Venture Partners 和 Innovation Endeavors 领投了 B 轮融资。此轮融资的其他投资者包括 Theory Ventures、Dimension、Swift Ventures、CRV 和 Y Combinator，使该公司的融资总额达到 9850 万美元。

人工智能使创建和解释日益复杂的数据变得更加容易，但创建它也带来了基础设施问题。 LanceDB 正在通过提供统一的多模式数据湖库来解决这个问题，为研究人员、企业机构和人工智能代理提供一种统一的方式来访问、查找、准备和训练这些数据，而无需花费数周时间来管理底层基础设施。

联合创始人兼首席执行官张佘在接受 SiliconANGLE 采访时表示：“通常情况下，研究团队必须将数据集的不同部分放在不同的地方，他们需要花费数周或数月的时间才能为一天结束时的单次训练准备好整个训练数据集。” “当今的人工智能缺少一个数据层，而这正是我们正在努力构建的。”

LanceDB 的技术建立在 Lance 的基础上，Lance 是一种专为人工智能工作负载而设计的开源数据格式，它将结构化信息与图像、视频和其他大型文件相结合。与针对处理整个表而优化的传统分析格式不同，Lance 支持快速检索和修改单个记录，这使其对于搜索和准备大量训练数据集特别有用。

该公司将这种格式构建到一个用于检索的大型数据湖库中，这是训练现代人工智能模型所需的庞大信息所必需的。 Lakehouse 结合了数据湖的灵活性（可以存储大量原始信息）和用于组织、查询和管理数据的数据库式功能。

“多模式数据之所以不同且更加困难的部分原因在于数据的大小，”她解释道。

通过将多模态引入 Lakehouse 格式，LanceDB 将不同形式的 AI 训练数据引入单一平台，使开发人员能够搜索、组织和准备其数据集，而无需为每种数据类型维护单独的系统。它可以直接连接到客户现有的云存储（数据保留在其中），同时在处理数据所需的基础设施之间分配计算工作负载。

### 多模态数据对人工智能的挑战

多模态人工智能不仅仅涉及文本、音频、图像和视频的结合。自动驾驶车辆、机器人和世界模型还涉及三维传感器信息、地理空间坐标、时间序列数据和解释传感器检测内容的注释。

例如，自动驾驶汽车不仅仅是捕捉图像。它的传感器可能会产生周围环境的三维表示，然后需要将其与识别道路、行人、植被和其他物体的信息相关联。

对于许多大型训练工作流程，激光雷达 3D 云、图像、视频、音频等中包含的数据量平均会在单个表中占用 10 到 20 PB 的数据，有些数据甚至更大，可能接近 80 到 100 PB。研究人员和模型构建者可能会在不同系统中维护大量数据，因为传统平台并不是围绕多模式人工智能的要求而设计的。

然后，研究人员必须组装、协调和存储训练数据集的不同组成部分，以丰富训练数据集。策划本身可能需要数周或数月的时间来移动、准备和处理。 LanceDB 的答案是管理基础设施本身，无需从企业或研究存储中复制或移动数据，从而为其提供单一的统一访问点。

“数据保持不变，”她解释道。 “它仍然是你的。我们不需要复制它。”

简而言之，LanceDB 不仅仅是引入一种新的数据存储方式；目标是提供一种减少访问数据的方法，无需通过网络基础设施复制、转换或移动数据。这大大加快了她所说的“人工智能飞轮”的速度，目前该飞轮是通过尽快向人工智能模型提供良好的数据来铸造和推出它们来驱动的。

她说：“我们的旋转速度越快，研究团队就能越快地获得更高质量的模型，并让我们能够开发出更有趣的人工智能应用程序。”

著名客户包括 Runway AI Inc.，该公司随着人工智能培训需求的扩大而采用了 LanceDB 的企业平台。 Netflix Inc. 基于内容创建技术构建了媒体数据湖。微软公司使用该平台作为数据层，在数百亿行图像和代码数据上训练模型。该平台使这些组织能够将数据管理、搜索、管理和特征工程整合到一个统一的工作流程中，帮助研究人员准备 PB 级的训练数据集，而无需处理单独的基础设施系统。

“Runway 的训练示例不会保持静止，”Runway 首席技术官卡米尔·辛迪 (Kamil Sindi) 说道。 “它从视频和提示开始，然后我们添加嵌入、分辨率和持续时间元数据，无论下一个实验需要什么。我们于 2024 年首次开始使用 Lance 格式，因为它是同时处理非结构化数据、列追加、分布式读取和即席 SQL 的唯一选项。从那时起，我们就成为了 LanceDB Enterprise 客户。”

她表示，LanceDB 打算利用新资金扩展其多模式数据平台并加快人工智能模型开发周期，特别是通过改进大规模数据管理、特征工程和数据加载，以保持数千个图形处理单元在训练期间高效运行。该公司还将加深对新兴人工智能工作负载的支持，包括视频生成、世界模型和机器人技术，研究人员必须管理不断增长的第一人称传感器数据、合成数据和其他多模式信息。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To address infrastructure inefficiencies in managing and preparing large-scale AI training datasets
[Key Metrics] Financing: $57.5M Series B, $98.5M total.
[Key Position & Outlook] Market Pain Point: Eliminating fragmentation in AI training data preprocessing.
article_content_en:
LanceDB Inc., the developer of database technology designed to speed up artificial intelligence models, today announced it has raised $57.5 million in early-stage funding to bring a multimodal lakehouse to researchers, model builders and platform teams.

Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led the Series B round. Other investors in the round included Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV and Y Combinator, bringing the company’s total funding to $98.5 million.

AI is making it easier to create and interpret increasingly complex forms of data, but creating it also brings an infrastructure problem. LanceDB is tackling this problem by providing a unified multimodal data lakehouse, giving researchers, enterprise outfits and AI agents a unified way to access, find, prepare and train on that data without spending weeks managing the underlying infrastructure.

“Typically, research teams have to put different parts of their dataset in different places, and they lose weeks or months getting a whole training dataset ready for that single training run at the end of the day,” co-founder and Chief Executive Chang She told SiliconANGLE in an interview. “There’s a missing data layer for AI today, and that’s what we’re trying to build.”

LanceDB’s technology is built on Lance, an open-source data format designed for AI workloads that combines structured information with images, video and other large files. Unlike traditional analytics formats optimized for processing entire tables, Lance supports the rapid retrieval and modification of individual records, making it particularly useful for searching and preparing massive training datasets.

The company built this format into a large-scale data lakehouse for retrieval, which is needed for the sheer scale of information needed to train modern AI models. A lakehouse combines the flexibility of a data lake, which can store enormous amounts of raw information, with database-style capabilities for organizing, querying and managing that data.

“Part of what makes multimodal data different and more difficult is the size of the data,” She explained.

By bringing multimodality to the lakehouse format, LanceDB brings different forms of AI training data into a single platform, allowing developers to search, organize and prepare their datasets without maintaining separate systems for each data type. It can connect directly to customers’ existing cloud storage, where the data remains, while distributing computational workloads across the infrastructure required to process it.

### The challenge of multimodal data for AI

Multimodal AI involves more than combining text, audio, images and video. Autonomous vehicles, robotics and world models also involve three-dimensional sensor information, geospatial coordinates, time-series data and annotations that explain what the sensors are detecting.

For example, a self-driving car doesn’t merely capture an image. Its sensors might produce a three-dimensional representation of the surrounding environment, which then needs to be associated with information that identifies roads, pedestrians, vegetation and other objects.

The sheer amount of data included in lidar 3D clouds, images, video, audio and more can take up, on average, 10 to 20 petabytes of data in a single table for many large training workflows, with some becoming even larger – potentially approaching 80 to 100 petabytes. Researchers and model builders may maintain huge pools of data across different systems because conventional platforms weren’t designed around the requirements of multimodal AI.

Researchers must then assemble, reconcile and store different components of a training dataset to enrich it for training. The curation itself can take weeks or months just to move, prepare and process. LanceDB’s answer is to manage the infrastructure itself without ever copying or moving data from enterprise or research storage, giving it a single unified access point.

“The data stays in place,” She explained. “It remains yours. We don’t need to copy it.”

In short, LanceDB isn’t simply introducing a new way to store data; the objective is to provide a way to access the data less often, without needing to copy, convert or move it through network infrastructure. This greatly speeds up what She refers to as the “AI flywheel,” which is currently driven by feeding AI models good data as quickly as possible to mint and roll them out.

“The faster we can make that spin, the faster research teams can get to higher quality models and allow us to make even more interesting AI applications,” She said.

Notable customers include Runway AI Inc., which adopted LanceDB’s enterprise platform as its AI training needs expanded. Netflix Inc. built a media data lake on the technology for content creation. And Microsoft Corp. uses the platform as a data layer for training models on tens of billions of rows of image and code data. The platform lets these organizations consolidate data management, search, curation and feature engineering into a unified workflow, helping researchers prepare training datasets at petabyte scale without juggling separate infrastructure systems.

“A training example at Runway doesn’t stay still,” said Runway Chief Technology Officer Kamil Sindi. “It starts as a video and a prompt, then we add embeddings, resolution and duration metadata, whatever the next experiment needs. We first started using the Lance format in 2024 because it was the only option that handled unstructured data, column appends, distributed reads and ad-hoc SQL all at once. We’ve since become a LanceDB Enterprise customer.”

She said LanceDB intends to use the new funding to expand its multimodal data platform and accelerate the AI model development cycle, particularly by improving large-scale data curation, feature engineering and data loading to keep thousands of graphics processing units supplied efficiently during training. The company will also deepen its support for emerging AI workloads, including video generation, world models and robotics, where researchers must manage growing volumes of first-person sensor data, synthetic data and other multimodal information.

Investing.com -- Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is facing another layer of scrutiny as short seller Muddy Waters disclosed a short position in the chipmaker, raising questions about a possible connection between former Nvidia executive Ajay K. Puri and former Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen.

Our AI stock portfolio is beating the S&P 500 by 118%. Discover the stocks we're buying and the opportunities we're watching next. Exclusive for Yahoo! Finance readers: 55% off for Black Friday, plus an extra 15% at checkout. Subscribe today! »

The disclosure comes amid a turbulent period for Nvidia, following Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as CEO on November 12 and growing congressional scrutiny of the company's exposure to alleged Chinese chip-diversion schemes. Huang has agreed to answer questions from three House committees on December 1, with Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter scheduled to appear the following day.

In a post on X, Muddy Waters questioned whether a woman identified as Cenly Chen, and in some photograph tags as Cenly Puri, who has reportedly been photographed publicly with Puri between 2024 and 2026, is the same Cenly Chen formerly employed by Super Micro.

Puri was previously Nvidia's EVP of Worldwide Field Operations and was among the company's most senior executives before leaving the position in June 2026. He continues to serve in a senior advisory role to Nvidia, according to Muddy Waters.

Stop chasing stocks after they've already rallied. Find your next investment opportunity with AI stock picks, earnings insights, and market-moving news. Yahoo! Finance readers get an extra 15% off on top of the 55% off Black Friday price. Join today! »

The short seller draws attention to an October 2026 consolidated class action complaint against Super Micro, which alleges that its former Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen managed the company's acquisition of Nvidia GPUs and determined how they were distributed among customers. The complaint further alleges that Chen could not have been unaware of Super Micro's alleged illicit sales.

The allegations relate to a separate U.S. criminal case announced in March, involving three individuals associated with Super Micro who were indicted over an alleged scheme to sell approximately $2.5 billion of Nvidia-powered servers to end customers in China through a Southeast Asian front company.

Muddy Waters acknowledges that neither Cenly Chen nor Puri has been accused of criminal conduct by the government and that the allegations in the shareholder lawsuit remain unproven.

The short seller's central question is whether the woman photographed with Puri is the same individual named in the Super Micro litigation. That identification, as well as any potential implications for Nvidia, has not been independently established.

title: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
title_en: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
author: Kiki Intarasuwan
article_content:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there's "zero evidence" that recent tech outages in U.S. air travel, banking and other systems are connected.

"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said Wednesday morning local time during a news conference in the Philippines.

Rubio acknowledged that people are fearful and uncertain, saying he wanted to be clear that the United States is not under systemic attack.

"We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind," Rubio said.

Rubio, who is traveling with President Trump ahead of a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, added that the administration is "always on the lookout" for any potential attacks and reiterated multiple times that reports of technical issues are not interconnected.

"Each of them are distinct, and they're different in their causation," he said.

On Thursday, Microsoft said it experienced a worldwide outage affecting services like Outlook and Teams, impacting users, companies and government operations worldwide. The company said the outage was linked to a technical issue, not malicious or cyber activity.

The following day, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on all departing U.S. flights for several hours, throwing the aviation industry into turmoil. Federal officials identified a contractor performing maintenance updates as the cause of Friday's disruption, but key questions remain about the underlying cause of the systemwide failure.

Other recent outages that have since been resolved include disruptions to major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and U.S. Bank, and issues with Apple's services. On Tuesday, the National Security Agency's internal network used to store and share classified information went offline, multiple U.S. officials familiar told CBS News.

Democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also said on Tuesday that there's no indication these incidents are the result of an attack, but noted that artificial intelligence is creating pressure for companies to deal with vulnerabilities.

"AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren't built to handle that pace of change," Warner said in a post on X. "It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences. This is exactly why I've been pushing for commonsense guardrails on AI and stronger cybersecurity protections."

When asked Wednesday about the role of AI in recent incidents, Rubio said he didn't want to speculate because every incident is unique and referred to individual companies.

title_zh: 卢比奥否认近期美技术宕机系系统性攻击
summary_zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥明确指出，近期民航、银行及微软等领域的技术中断事件互无关联，非网络攻击所致
article_content_zh:
美国国务卿卢比奥表示，“没有证据”表明美国航空旅行、银行和其他系统最近发生的技术中断之间存在关联。

卢比奥当地时间周三上午在菲律宾举行的新闻发布会上表示：“微软事件与我们在美国联邦航空局看到的情况无关。美国联邦航空局与我们几天前在银行看到的情况无关。我们从技术角度看到的这些问题完全无关。”

卢比奥承认人们感到恐惧和不确定，并表示他想明确美国并未受到系统性攻击。

卢比奥说：“我们没有任何证据或任何理由相信这些孤立或个别的事件与邪恶行为者、网络黑客、犯罪分子、另一个民族国家、任何类型的恶意行为者有任何关系。”

卢比奥在本周与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和中国国家主席习近平举行三边会议之前与特朗普总统一起旅行，他补充说，政府“始终在警惕”任何潜在的攻击，并多次重申，技术问题的报告并不相互关联。

“它们每个都是独特的，而且它们的因果关系也不同，”他说。

周四，微软表示，它经历了全球范围内的中断，影响了 Outlook 和 Teams 等服务，影响了全球用户、公司和政府运营。该公司表示，此次中断与技术问题有关，而不是恶意或网络活动。

次日，美国联邦航空管理局下令在全国范围内对所有出发的美国航班进行数小时的地面停飞，令航空业陷入混乱。联邦官员确定，周五中断的原因是一名执行维护更新的承包商，但关于整个系统故障的根本原因仍然存在关键问题。

最近已解决的其他中断包括摩根大通、美国银行和合众银行等主要银行的中断，以及苹果服务的问题。多位熟悉情况的美国官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，周二，国家安全局用于存储和共享机密信息的内部网络离线。

参议院情报委员会副主席、民主党参议员马克·沃纳 (Mark Warner) 周二也表示，没有迹象表明这些事件是攻击造成的，但他指出，人工智能正在给公司带来处理漏洞的压力。

华纳在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“人工智能使得以前所未有的速度识别大量系统中的漏洞成为可能，这给公司和政府机构带来了巨大的压力，要求他们立即修补这些漏洞，通常是一次性修补这些漏洞，这给那些无法应对这种变化速度的系统带来了巨大的压力。”“感觉每一天都在提醒我们，人工智能的发展速度超过了我们管理其后果的能力。这正是我一直在推动人工智能常识护栏和更强大的网络安全保护的原因。”

当周三被问及人工智能在最近发生的事件中所扮演的角色时，卢比奥表示，他不想猜测，因为每起事件都是独一无二的，并且都涉及个别公司。

title: Exclusive: Some Nvidia directors continue push to bring Huang back
title_en: Exclusive: Some Nvidia directors continue push to bring Huang back
author: Reed Albergotti and Rohan Goswami
article_content:
Despite Nvidia’s proclamation Tuesday that it didn’t plan to bring ousted CEO Jensen Huang back to the chipmaker, a faction of board members is pushing for his return, according to people familiar with the matter.

Huang has met with a number of tech executives and spoken with at least one board member about the possibility of his return, the people said.

The conversation with the director took place before the company’s earnings report and before Huang issued a public statement Tuesday that he’d be willing to return to the company if the board decides it is in the “best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.”

Hours later, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that the chipmaker wasn’t considering bringing Huang back and that the board had voted unanimously to accept his resignation.

Spokespeople for Huang and Nvidia declined to comment.

Despite the pushback from three directors, other board members are starting to narrow the search for Huang’s replacement, some of the people familiar with the deliberations said.

ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have both been considered, the people said. Haas has spoken to at least some Nvidia directors about taking the job, one of the people said, but he’s said he’s concerned about the optics of taking it over calls to bring Huang back to the helm.

Spokespeople for ARM and Marvell didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s also unclear whether Marvell’s Murphy would be able to take over as Nvidia’s CEO given the company is navigating a mega-merger with rival Lumentum.

title_zh: 英伟达董事会内部分化：部分成员推动黄仁勋回归
summary_zh: 英伟达董事会成员正就黄仁勋去留问题产生分歧，部分董事私下接触黄仁勋商讨回归可能性，而主席哈维·琼斯则重申目前无此计划
article_content_zh:
据知情人士透露，尽管英伟达周二宣布不打算将被罢免的首席执行官黄仁勋带回该芯片制造商，但董事会的一部分成员正在推动他的回归。

知情人士称，黄仁勋会见了多位科技高管，并与至少一名董事会成员讨论了他回归的可能性。

与董事的谈话是在公司财报发布之前进行的，黄仁勋周二发表公开声明称，如果董事会认为这符合“我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益”，他愿​​意重返公司。

几个小时后，英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯在公司财报电话会议上表示，该芯片制造商并未考虑让黄仁勋回归，董事会已一致投票接受他的辞职。

黄仁勋和英伟达的发言人拒绝置评。

一些知情人士表示，尽管遭到三名董事的反对，其他董事会成员仍开始缩小黄继任人选的范围。

知情人士称，ARM 首席执行官雷内·哈斯 (Rene Haas) 和 Marvell 首席执行官马特·墨菲 (Matt Murphy) 都曾被考虑过。一位知情人士称，哈斯已经与至少一些英伟达董事就接任这一职务进行了交谈，但他表示，他担心接任该职务而不是让黄重新掌舵的呼声。

ARM 和 Marvell 的发言人没有立即回应置评请求。鉴于英伟达正在与竞争对手 Lumentum 进行大规模合并，目前还不清楚 Marvell 的墨菲是否能够接任 Nvidia 首席执行官。

article_content_en:
Despite Nvidia’s proclamation Tuesday that it didn’t plan to bring ousted CEO Jensen Huang back to the chipmaker, a faction of board members is pushing for his return, according to people familiar with the matter.

Huang has met with a number of tech executives and spoken with at least one board member about the possibility of his return, the people said.

The conversation with the director took place before the company’s earnings report and before Huang issued a public statement Tuesday that he’d be willing to return to the company if the board decides it is in the “best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.”

Hours later, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that the chipmaker wasn’t considering bringing Huang back and that the board had voted unanimously to accept his resignation.

Spokespeople for Huang and Nvidia declined to comment.

Despite the pushback from three directors, other board members are starting to narrow the search for Huang’s replacement, some of the people familiar with the deliberations said.

ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have both been considered, the people said. Haas has spoken to at least some Nvidia directors about taking the job, one of the people said, but he’s said he’s concerned about the optics of taking it over calls to bring Huang back to the helm.

Spokespeople for ARM and Marvell didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s also unclear whether Marvell’s Murphy would be able to take over as Nvidia’s CEO given the company is navigating a mega-merger with rival Lumentum.

title: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial
title_en: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial

inline_images.caption: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial

author: Reuters
article_content:
Prosecutors accuse Huawei of scheming to defraud HSBC and other banks about its business in Iran and conspiring to steal trade secrets from five US tech companies. It was also indicted as a criminal enterprise.

“They began with guilt and worked backwards,” defense lawyer Brian Heberlig told jurors in Brooklyn federal court in his closing argument. “When the evidence didn’t fit its theory, it moved the goal posts,” he said.

The government offered jurors a very different picture of the company on Monday, and said prosecutors proved beyond a reasonable doubt that Huawei operated as a criminal enterprise.

“For 20 years, Huawei committed a pattern of crimes targeted at American companies, the American financial system and the American government,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa said in her closing statement. “It is time to finally hold Huawei accountable,” Arfa said.

However, Heberlig argued the banks all knew Huawei operated in Iran, which is under US sanctions. He said the banks accepted the risk and competed for Huawei’s business.

In relation to the alleged theft of trade secrets, “the government cherry-picked a handful of incidents … and tried to convert them into a 20-year conspiracy,” Heberlig said.

“Huawei didn’t steal its way to success,” he said. “It earned it, plain and simple,” he added.

The Huawei case burst into the headlines in 2018 when Meng Wanzhou, its CFO and daughter of the founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant for her role in the alleged bank fraud.

She entered into an agreement with prosecutors in 2021 and the charges against her were dismissed, but the case dragged on.

The jury is likely to begin deliberations on Wednesday. The case went to trial in September. The prosecution put on over 60 witnesses, and the defence about 15.

The jury will deliver its verdict as US-China tensions heat up in the battle over artificial intelligence and amid a fragile trade truce between the two countries.

title_zh: 华为应对美国刑事指控案件进入陪审团裁决阶段
summary_zh: 美国布鲁克林联邦法院就华为被控银行欺诈及窃取商业机密一案进入结案陈词阶段，陪审团即将开始审议
article_content_zh:
检察官指控华为密谋就其在伊朗的业务欺骗汇丰银行和其他银行，并合谋窃取五家美国科技公司的商业机密。它还被指控为犯罪企业。

“他们从愧疚开始，然后倒退，”辩护律师布莱恩·赫伯利格在布鲁克林联邦法院的结案陈词中告诉陪审员。 “当证据不符合其理论时，它就会改变目标，”他说。

周一，政府向陪审员提供了该公司截然不同的形象，并表示检察官毫无疑问地证明华为是一家犯罪企业。

“20年来，华为针对美国公司、美国金融体系和美国政府犯下了一系列犯罪行为，”检察官梅雷迪思·阿尔法(Meredith Arfa)在结案陈词中表示。 “现在是最终让华为承担责任的时候了，”阿尔法说。

然而，赫伯利格辩称，这些银行都知道华为在伊朗运营，而伊朗正受到美国的制裁。他表示，银行接受了风险并争夺华为的业务。

赫伯利格表示，就涉嫌窃取商业机密的事件而言，“政府挑选了几起事件……并试图将它们转化为一场长达 20 年的阴谋”。

“华为的成功之路并不是靠偷来的，”他说。 “它赢得了它，简单明了，”他补充道。

华为案于 2018 年成为头条新闻，当时华为首席财务官、创始人的女儿孟晚舟因涉嫌银行欺诈而因美国逮捕令而在加拿大被拘留。

她于 2021 年与检察官达成协议，对她的指控被驳回，但案件一拖再拖。

陪审团可能会在周三开始审议。该案于九月开庭审理。控方提供了 60 多名证人，辩方则提供了大约 15 名证人。

陪审团将在人工智能之争中美中紧张局势升温以及两国之间脆弱的贸易休战之际做出裁决。

title: Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco
title_en: Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco

inline_images.caption: Bloomberg/Getty Images Michael Burry, the investor of "The Big Short" fame.
inline_images.alt: Bloomberg/Getty Images Michael Burry, the investor of "The Big Short" fame.

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Michael Burry says Anthropic's IPO filing this week has reinforced his concerns that the entire AI ecosystem is at risk of disaster. The investor of "The Big Short" fame wrote in a Substack post on Tuesday that the first in-depth look at Claude's parent company, ahead of what could be the biggest IPO in history, threw up a bunch of red flags.

Burry pointed to Anthropic's huge spending commitments, slowing revenue, and tangled ties. He said that Anthropic has struck deals to buy about $537 billion of compute from the likes of Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft, and reached preliminary agreements worth hundreds of billions more with others such as SpaceXAI, putting its total commitments at about 12 times its current annual run-rate revenue.

"This is not stated clearly in the S-1, and in my view it is the most deserved headline from it," Burry wrote in a Tuesday Substack post. He underscored how hyperscalers like Amazon and Alphabet act as Anthropic's "lenders, vendors, channel providers, and shareholders." He also outlined its deal with Broadcom, which involves Apollo and Blackstone and includes convertible notes and structured credit tranches.

"Just remember, the reason this is so complex is because too much debt is needed, and it must be unloaded from the balance sheets of those involved," Burry wrote. "While some may see all the circularity and connectedness as security on the way up, and that is not wrong, it does leave the entire organism catastrophically vulnerable either on a pause or on the way down," he added.

He also described financing arrangements in the AI space as "garish and audacious," and said hyperscalers aren't generating enough cash to fund the AI buildout so they're resorting to "Byzantine" deals. Burry said it was a "very similar" situation with vendor financing during the dot-com bubble, saying "people keep making the same mistakes with every new thing." In its filing, Anthropic said its revenue surpassed $16 billion for the first six months of this year, a 14-fold increase from the first half of 2025.

Its operating loss narrowed by about two-thirds to below $700 million, and it generated nearly $4 billion in operating cash flow. Burry initially commented on Anthropic's filing in a Substack chat thread on Monday. He said that revenue was "slowing," citing Anthropic's claim that third-quarter revenue was 86 times the $197 million it generated in the fourth quarter of 2024, or about $16.9 billion.

That would mean Anthropic's revenue grew by about 46% between the second and third quarters of this year, after soaring 144% between the first and second quarters. "Overall slowing of growth is not attributed to a decline in tokenmaxxing, but I did not expect that to be mentioned," Burry wrote.

Burry was referring to the trend of maximizing AI token consumption, which has fallen out of favor in recent months given its costs. In another comment, Burry wrote that large language models (LLMs) like Claude are "improving" and "already being used more efficiently and that trend will continue, to the detriment of their growth rate." Burry said he's focused on the complexity and fragility of the debt financing many AI deals, hurdles to installing new graphics chips shoring up demand for older chips, a potential crash in memory chip prices once the shortage eases, compression and small language models (SLMs) reducing the need for computing power, and the "fundamentals behind not just companies but the deals they are doing." Responding to a subscriber who said that Big Tech companies are shifting from Anthropic's AI models to their own, and that tokens are rapidly being commoditized, Burry wrote: "Yes, that is what I hear." Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Burry's posts.

The contrarian investor shot to fame after his massive wager against the mid-2000s housing bubble was chronicled in the book and movie "The Big Short." He pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing about his personal investments on Substack last winter. A recurring theme of his work since then has been deep skepticism of the AI boom.
