article_content_en:
OpenAI releases two new language models. GPT-6.2 Astra is aimed at demanding professional work, while GPT-6.2 Sol is built for everyday use. OpenAI says both outperform their predecessors on benchmarks and cost less to run.

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available now for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Pro-500 subscribers can use Ultrafast mode with both models. For the first time, Pro-200 subscribers also get Ultrafast access, starting with GPT-6.2 Sol.

Developers can access both models through the OpenAI API. OpenAI says API pricing for GPT-6.2 Astra is 20 percent cheaper than its predecessor's, at $8 per million input tokens, $0.40 for cached inputs, and $40 per million output tokens. GPT-6.2 Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's pricing at $2 for input, $0.10 for cached inputs, and $10 for output per million tokens.

### OpenAI calls Astra "the world's best model for scientists"and touts polished slides

OpenAI trained GPT-6.2 Astra to handle professional conventions in fields like law, finance, and accounting more reliably. The company says presentations pull layouts, colors, and typography from templates, matching exact font sizes. Slide titles are meant to capture a slide's main point, while body text stays focused on key details.

OpenAI's announcement leans hard on the price-to-performance ratio of its models. On Agents' Last Exam, a benchmark that tests multi-step professional workflows, GPT-6.2 Astra scores 5.2 points above its predecessor GPT-6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, according to OpenAI. It leads Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 by 5.5 points at just 5 percent of the cost. Only Google's Gemini 4 Carbon keeps up with Astra on this benchmark.

On the legal benchmark Harvey LAB-AA, which covers tasks like contract clause analysis, GPT-6.2 Astra more than doubles Claude Fable 5.2's pass rate at about one-sixth of the cost, according to OpenAI. On the internal GDPval-v2 benchmark, which includes consulting, finance, and design tasks, OpenAI says Astra gains 6.2 percentage points over its predecessor while using 22 percent fewer output tokens.

OpenAI says computer use, already a strong suit of the predecessor, got better again. In testing, the model reportedly built a 3D car model, wrote a physics solver in Python, and animated the results in Blender. In another demo, it modeled a remote-controlled car part by part and produced an animated assembly guide.

OpenAI also claims progress in web design. On the 3D benchmark AA-3D, human judges compare two blinded interactive experiences. GPT-6.2 Astra takes first with 1,318 Elo points, ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at 1,271 and GPT-6.2 Sol at 1,259.

On Terminal-Bench-Science, a benchmark that tests scientific workflows in a terminal, the model scores 9 percentage points above GPT-6 Astra, again at less than a third of the cost, according to OpenAI. Astra also sets a new high on the Vals Science Index, which measures how well models interpret biological data and run experiments, OpenAI says.

### Sol nearly matches the original Astra at a fraction of the cost

GPT-6.2 Sol is for users who want a fast, versatile model for everyday tasks, OpenAI says. On the coding benchmark FrontierCode 2.0, which checks whether code changes meet the quality bar of real projects, Sol trails Astra by just 0.5 points at one-fifth the cost. OpenAI says the model also handles non-work tasks well.

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol have also gotten better at cybersecurity, according to OpenAI. They find and exploit vulnerabilities more effectively, write more secure code, and deliver better bug fixes, with notably higher token efficiency in several tests. Both models hit the "Critical"threshold for cybersecurity in OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, just as GPT-6 Astra did before them.

OpenAI is adding stricter safeguards for potentially risky cybersecurity requests in response. These safeguards should make abuse harder but will also limit legitimate vulnerability research and security testing, OpenAI says.

OpenAI plans to offer the new models through OpenAI Daybreak, which already gives vetted security researchers access to other models with fewer guardrails. The published cybersecurity benchmark numbers come from internal tests with safeguards and classifiers turned off. OpenAI lays out its methodology in the accompanying safety report.

### Astra takes second in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index

In the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, which rolls up nine evaluations across knowledge work, coding, science, and general knowledge, GPT-6.2 Astra finishes second, just behind Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2. Astra jumps five points over GPT-6 Astra, according to Artificial Analysis, passing Google's Gemini 4 Carbon (60 points) and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 (59 points). GPT-6.2 Sol picks up two points to reach 57, matching GPT-6 Astra's level at only about 15 percent of the cost per task.

OpenAI owns the Pareto frontier on cost versus performance, the line where no other model is both cheaper and better, according to Artificial Analysis. Only Anthropic and Meta models also land on that frontier. OpenAI holds most of the top spots on efficiency too, measured by output tokens per task. Claude Fable 5.2 is the only outside model that shows up there.

Artificial Analysis backs up OpenAI's claims in science and factual knowledge. GPT-6.2 Astra leads on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 and places second behind Claude Fable 5.2 on the physics reasoning test CritPt v2, the factual knowledge benchmark AA-Omniscience, and the knowledge benchmark HLE-Diamond. Astra also leads in 3D design (AA-3D) and robotics (AA-Robotics v0.1), scoring 79 on robotics against Sol's 78 and Claude Fable 5.2's 75.

Coding is a different story, though. According to Artificial Analysis, both models have flatlined there. In the Coding Agent Index, measured with the Codex harness at max compute, GPT-6.2 Astra stays right where GPT-6 Astra was. GPT-6.2 Sol actually drops three points from GPT-6.1 Sol. That decline comes from a 14-point slide on SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA, where the model omits key facts from its answers more often than its predecessor did.

Artificial Analysis also flags a high hallucination rate. At maximum effort, GPT-6.2 Astra hallucinates 59 percent of the time, Sol 55 percent. The metric is AA-Omniscience Hallucination Rate, which measures how frequently a model guesses on factual questions instead of saying it doesn't know. These are unusually hard questions, so the numbers don't reflect everyday hallucination rates.

### Epoch AI finds Astra on par with Fable 5.2 but weaker on real-world tasks

Research organization Epoch AI tested GPT-6.2 Astra on its own benchmarks before launch. The model scores 174 points in the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), tying Anthropic's Fable 5.2. Both models beat what the previous trend for reasoning models would have predicted before Astra, according to Epoch AI.

On real-world tasks pulled from Epoch AI's own research, Astra fell behind Fable 5.2 and barely improved over GPT-6 Astra. According to Epoch AI, the model missed the central question on simpler research projects and spun its wheels trying to fix things. On a task about researching AI data centers, Astra played it too safe and skipped key estimates, something Epoch AI says no contractor could get away with. Epoch AI rated Astra's writing as relatively strong compared to other tested models but still below its own bar.

One thing that stands out is Astra's ability to run complex reasoning within a single output token, with no visible chain of thought. Epoch AI clocks 12.3 serial steps for Astra, up from 10.5 for GPT-6 Astra and 4.2 for Claude Fable 5.1, the strongest non-OpenAI model at the time. Models that can reason this way without showing their work are harder to monitor, a safety concern that already came up with the first Astra model.

On FrontierMath Erdős, a benchmark of unsolved math problems, GPT-6.2 Astra cracked 7 of 68 tasks, each formally verified in the proof assistant Lean. The old record was 3 of 68, set by GPT-6.1 Sol. One of the seven had no known solution before.

### Vals AI puts Astra and Sol in the top 10 but finds legal weak spots

GPT-6.2 Astra ranks 7th and GPT-6.2 Sol 9th in the Vals Index, separated by just 1.6 points. The price gap is wide, though. Sol runs $3.18 per task, less than a third of Astra's $10.68, making it the cheapest model in the top 10, according to Vals AI. Astra also got cheaper than its predecessor, scoring 2.6 points above GPT-6 Astra at roughly half of its $21.28 per-task cost. Vals AI says Astra uses the fewest output tokens in the top 10, averaging 91,000 per task.

Vals AI backs OpenAI's claim to the top spot on the Vals Science Index. Astra leads that ranking and takes first on Terminal-Bench Science and VCB 1–100 at about half the cost and half the runtime of GPT-6 Astra. Sol comes in third on Terminal-Bench Science at roughly a quarter of Astra's cost. On the broader Terminal-Bench 4 for agentic coding, Astra places 5th and Sol 7th.

Legal tests are where the models fall short, according to Vals AI. On the HLAB benchmark, Astra and Sol double their predecessors' scores but rank only 11th and 21st. On the Legal Research benchmark, the drop is even steeper, with Astra at 30th and Sol at 52nd. Vals AI says the models make nearly twice as many tool calls as their predecessors but write shorter answers.

In September, OpenAI announced a specialized product called "Astra for Law."It does significantly better than the base model on the Legal Research Bench, reaching 6th place. Vals AI tested both models with a one-million-token context window and 128,000 max output tokens at full reasoning effort.

### GPT-6.2 Astra is the first released model to hit OpenAI's "High"threshold for AI self-improvement

According to OpenAI, GPT-6.2 Astra is the first externally released model to reach the "High"threshold for AI self-improvement. OpenAI says the model can meaningfully speed up AI research, on par with giving every OpenAI researcher an extra, highly skilled research engineer.

OpenAI calls this out explicitly as a risk. Models that can help build future AI systems could push the field forward faster than safety measures and human oversight can keep up. The industry is currently wrestling with this under the label "RSI".

As countermeasures, OpenAI points to tighter controls in research environments and its monitoring system Control Room, which can track research tasks and shut them down if needed. The company also says it has expanded monitoring that examines how models reason and act and automatically flags unauthorized behavior.

On alignment, meaning how well the model follows user instructions and communicates openly, the new models match their predecessors, according to OpenAI. In two tests, however, they more often failed to flag obstacles blocking their work, like a missing file or an unavailable search tool.

title: Apple services, including iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, and more, hit by outage
title_en: Apple services, including iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, and more, hit by outage
author: Sarah Perez
article_content:
After a recent slew of tech outages, service disruptions, and flight chaos this week, it’s now Apple customers who are facing technical issues.

The iPhone maker’s System Status page indicates that there are issues with iCloud’s Account & Sign In services affecting “all users,” which could make the service slow or unavailable. The App Store, AppleCare on Device, and Apple Music are also experiencing issues, the page indicates.

Like all major tech companies, Apple faces outages and other technical issues affecting its cloud services at times. However, today’s issues are likely more noticeable to end users because problems with iCloud can lead to account sign-in problems. This could cause your iPhone to ask for your Apple ID and password, and you could see other attempts to sign in to services with your Apple account information fail.

On Reddit, some folks also noted that they were unable to activate a new iPhone, which is likely related to these ongoing issues.

Given the recent increase in AI-driven cyberattacks, users across social media have already begun to speculate about the cause. In particular, users are expressing concerns about the Apple outage, as it arrives only days after technical failures at Microsoft led to its cloud systems that power flagship services like Outlook and Teams failing due to cascading software issues.

Similarly, a brief outage of Chase’s banking app this week garnered attention, as did an ongoing partial outage (at the time of publication) of the National Security Agency’s internal classified network, both of which were blamed on software glitches.

So far, none of the outages in the past week have been attributed to cyberattacks, but rather to technical problems.

Apple responded to TechCrunch’s request for comment (which it initially gave to Bloomberg), noting that the outages were caused by an internal update and not a cyberattack. “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible,” the statement read.

After the initial outages were reported, Apple’s status page was updated to include other outages impacting Apple School Manager, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com), Schoolwork, and the Volume Purchase Program.

By 6 PM ET on Tuesday, the status page showed all the outages were resolved.

This article was updated after publication with the status of the outages.

article_content_zh:
本周发生了一系列技术中断、服务中断和航班混乱之后，现在面临技术问题的是苹果客户。

iPhone 制造商的系统状态页面显示，iCloud 的帐户和登录服务存在影响“所有用户”的问题，这可能导致该服务变慢或不可用。该页面显示，App Store、设备上的 AppleCare 和 Apple Music 也遇到了问题。

与所有主要科技公司一样，苹果有时会面临影响其云服务的中断和其他技术问题。然而，今天的问题对于最终用户来说可能更引人注目，因为 iCloud 问题可能会导致帐户登录问题。这可能会导致您的 iPhone 要求您提供 Apple ID 和密码，并且您可能会看到使用您的 Apple 帐户信息登录服务的其他尝试失败。

在 Reddit 上，一些人还指出他们无法激活新 iPhone，这可能与这些持续存在的问题有关。

鉴于最近人工智能驱动的网络攻击有所增加，社交媒体上的用户已经开始猜测其原因。特别是，用户对苹果的服务中断表示担忧，因为就在几天前，微软的技术故障导致其为 Outlook 和 Teams 等旗舰服务提供支持的云系统因级联软件问题而出现故障。

同样，本周大通银行应用程序的短暂中断引起了人们的关注，国家安全局内部机密网络的持续部分中断（截至本文发布时）也引起了人们的关注，这两起事件都被归咎于软件故障。

到目前为止，过去一周的中断都不是由网络攻击造成的，而是由技术问题造成的。

苹果公司回应了 TechCrunch 的置评请求（最初是向彭博社提交的），指出中断是由内部更新引起的，而不是网络攻击。声明中写道：“今天早上内部更新导致一些中断后，我们的许多系统都已恢复并运行。我们正在努力让其余系统尽快上线。”

在报告最初的中断后，Apple 的状态页面已更新，包括影响 Apple School Manager、iCloud Mail、iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com)、Schoolwork 和批量购买计划的其他中断。

到美国东部时间周二下午 6 点，状态页面显示所有中断均已解决。

本文在发布后更新了中断状态。

title: Google to keep Gemini chats for 2 months, up from 72 hours, even with history off
title_en: Google to keep Gemini chats for 2 months, up from 72 hours, even with history off
author: Jagmeet Singh
article_content:
Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.

The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.

OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations.

Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models.

The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models.

Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. They can, though, decide separately whether Google can use their conversations to train AI models.

article_content_zh:
谷歌将临时 Gemini 聊天和关闭聊天记录的对话的保留时间延长至两个月左右，并表示这一变化旨在随着人工智能系统变得更加强大，提高安全性。

根据 11 月 12 日的存档版本，这一变化将在未来几周内在 Gemini 应用程序中在全球范围内推出，这标志着 Google Gemini 应用程序隐私中心提到的之前 72 小时保留期的显着增加。

相比之下，OpenAI 表示，它可能会在 ChatGPT 中保留临时聊天最多 30 天，而 Anthropic 默认情况下会在 Claude 中保留隐身聊天 30 天。然而，出于法律或安全原因，或者为了调查政策违规行为，公司可能会将某些数据保留更长时间。

谷歌没有回答有关促成这一变化的原因以及它是否会影响对话的访问或审查方式的问题，而是指出一篇博客文章称，聊天会保留更长时间，以响应用户、处理反馈并保护其服务和用户。其更新的 Gemini Apps Privacy Hub 也将潜在的系统故障作为保留聊天的原因，并表示临时对话不用于训练人工智能模型。

随着谷歌为Gemini的聊天记录和人工智能训练引入了单独的设置，保留时间更长了。到目前为止，两者都绑定到一个单一的“保持活动”设置。用户现在可以将他们的对话保存在聊天记录中，而无需使用它们来训练b谷歌的生成式人工智能模型。

谷歌表示，对于之前禁用“保持活动”的用户，这两项新设置将默认关闭。对于那些打开了“保持活动”的人，他们的聊天记录将保持启用状态。不过，他们可以单独决定谷歌是否可以利用他们的对话来训练人工智能模型。

article_content_en:
Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable.

The change, which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12.

OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations.

Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models.

The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models.

Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. They can, though, decide separately whether Google can use their conversations to train AI models.

title: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free
title_en: Google’s Spark AI agent becomes ‘Tasks’ — and now it’s free

inline_images.caption: Tasks in Gemini
inline_images.alt: Tasks in Gemini

author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Google is rebranding its Spark AI agent as “Tasks” and making it free to use. The feature, which is powered by Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen AI model, can do things like create meal plans, manage your calendar, and dig through your emails to find recurring expenses you might not need.

Users in the US will get access to a few other features, including the ability for the AI agent to call businesses to compare product pricing and check inventory, purchase items with Google Pay, and sign into accounts that support Google Password Manager. US users can also assign Gemini tasks by emailing gemini@google.com or texting it.

Google first introduced its Spark AI agent in May, but it was only available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. The launch of tasks in Gemini brings Spark’s capabilities to all users in the US, Canada, Japan, Korea, Australia, and India. You can find tasks by opening Gemini and changing the toggle on the homepage from “Chat” to “Tasks.”

Tasks in Gemini is just one of the many agentic AI features that have emerged over the past year, including Claude Duet, OpenAI’s Dots, and Meta’s Muse. Google says Gemini will perform tasks in a “hardware-isolated virtual machine that’s dedicated to your account and never shared with other users.” You can also provide instructions for Gemini while it completes tasks. When performing more sensitive tasks, like purchasing an item, it will stop working and ask for your permission before following through.

title: Roundtables: Inside the Quest for Cognitive Immortality

author: MIT Technology Review
article_content:
In an effort to reach an elusive continuity of the self, some far-thinking technologists are working on ways to keep your brain going—even beyond death. Science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado explore possible paths to keep your mind going, including gradual brain replacement and uploading our memories to the cloud.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 该议题已从伦理科幻转向神经科学与计算架构的交叉工程领域，核心卡点在于高保真神经网络映射与长时记忆的数据一致性读取。长期来看，一旦神经生物学数据接口标准化，将彻底重塑医疗与数字存储产业的价值边界，引发关于人类本质定义的数据主权博弈。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This discourse has transitioned from ethical speculation to the intersection of neuroscience and computational architecture, where the core bottleneck lies in high-fidelity neural mapping and data consistency of long-term memory. Once standardized biological-to-digital interfaces emerge, they will redefine the value boundaries of healthcare and data storage, triggering profound geopolitical and regulatory conflicts regarding human consciousness sovereignty.

In an effort to reach an elusive continuity of the self, some far-thinking technologists are working on ways to keep your brain going—even beyond death. Science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado explore possible paths to keep your mind going, including gradual brain replacement and uploading our memories to the cloud.

Six wild ideas for perpetuating your mind

Inside the stealthy startup that pitched brainless human clones

Technology that lets us “speak” to our dead relatives has arrived. Are we ready?

This researcher wants to replace your brain, little by little

title: Xreal Aura review: portable, crisp display, and runs multiple Android apps on a virtual display, but Android XR lacks unique apps and VR controller support (Scott Stein/CNET)

author: CNET
article_content:
The most fascinating and frustrating device I've used in a long time pushes at the edges of where headsets are heading, and glasses are evolving.

Let me tell you about a strange, fascinating and rough tweener product called Xreal Aura.

There are VR headsets, and there are smart glasses. And there’s a new class of devices that’s falling right in between. What do we call these things? I have no idea. The category includes the Meta VR Glasses coming next year and now the Aura, a collaboration by Google and Xreal.

The Xreal Aura shoots for the moon, aiming to bridge glasses and VR, and to shrink everything down on the go. It’s often fascinating, and more often frustrating. At times, it almost feels like a VR headset. At other times it feels like a superpowered version of the tethered display glasses that Xreal and several others already make, that act like wearable monitors for your phone or laptop or almost anything else.

I think it’s actually an experimental bridge to a future where phones will play nicer with advanced smart glasses. Those future glasses could create floating displays and workspaces all around you, if you wish. Consider the Aura, in a way, Google’s early attempt to get there.

Emphasis on early. Right now, the Xreal Aura’s features, OS and especially inputs feel rough to use at times and sometimes hard to get into a natural flow with. But it shows what something of this size could be capable of with more software and input-flow tweaks. And when it does work, it feels wildly like a portable VR/AR headset in a way I’ve never really seen before.

The Aura aspires to be a shrunk-down version of last year’s Samsung Galaxy XR, an expensive mixed-reality headset similar to Apple’s Vision Pro. Like the Galaxy XR, the Aura runs Android XR, a variant of Android that floats apps all around. It even runs VR apps. At times it gets close. Other times, it’s not nearly close enough.

What’s wild about the Aura is that it folds down into a case that’s truly small enough to slide into my bag. But setting up and using the Aura often involves patience and experimentation. When it works, it’s a heck of a peek at a future that’s likely around the corner. But the hoops you have to jump through to make it happen sometimes make me want to hop out.

Android XR is Google’s OS for AR/VR/AI devices and wearables, and aims to connect glasses and headsets of all shapes and sizes to Google and Gemini services and apps. The Samsung Galaxy XR, released last year, was the first. Coming up next, in just a few weeks, are Google and Samsung’s Warby Parker- and Gentle Monster-designed AI smart glasses.

The Xreal Aura is more Galaxy XR than smart glasses, in concept: It’s an AR/VR headset that you can take on the go. The glasses connect with a USB-C cable to an included processor puck that runs Android XR. It can display Android apps in both 2D and immersive 3D.

The Aura supports hand tracking and can allow full spatial movement to place floating 3D objects or play immersive games. It can float apps all around you, and you can navigate apps at the same time. You can use hand tracking to open or tap those apps, or a trackpad that’s built into the top of the processor puck. You can also pair a Bluetooth keyboard, or game controller, or a mouse, like I’m doing.

The kit tucks into an included carry case that’s smaller than the one I carry my Nintendo Switch 2 in. It’s easy to pack away for travel. I love this part of the Aura so, so much.

It’s $1,279 for the version with 256GB of storage and 12GB RAM or $1,499 for 512GB/16GB, but it’s on sale until the end of the year for $1,099/$1,299. That onboard storage is all you get, though. There’s no expandable microSD card slot. I reviewed the 256GB version.

The display tech in the Aura is an enhanced version of what’s already on Xreal’s other tethered display glasses, and similar to what Viture and TCL RayNeo use. The twin micro OLED displays are impressively bright and crisp, projected via prisms to look like they’re floating in the room with you. The “birdbath” display tech means the lenses are chunky and odd-looking, but they’re also a lot bigger and better-looking than what’s possible on display-enabled wireless glasses like Meta’s Ray-Ban Displays.

They have a 70-degree field of view, something that beats out previous generations of AR glasses like Magic Leap or the upcoming Snap Specs. The fidelity, although capping at 1,920×1,200 pixels per eye, is also really crisp and great for movie watching or games (up to 120Hz refresh). It’s enough to feel like a big movie screen is projected across the room or to lay out a virtual computer monitor, but there are clear edges where the image is still cut off compared to VR headsets (which tend to have 90 degree or better fields of view).

When running VR apps, which this can shockingly do, the graphics look sharp but narrowly framed. It’s good enough to use VR in a pinch, though: I floated through 3D Immersive Google Maps, dragging and scrolling with my fingers in the air, or played the VR role-playing game Demeo, exploring a tabletop board game dungeon, or played back 360-degree videos on YouTube. But the limits of the viewing field become a lot more stark in these modes, making me wish I had a VR headset instead. Then again, I never travel with VR headsets, and I’d travel with this.

The display’s visuals seemed to tear a few times while playing YouTube videos. Tracking, using the built-in cameras, also sometimes drifted. Mostly, the displays stayed where I put them, but sometimes they’d shift slightly out of alignment.

The processor puck means the Xreal Aura can open up most Android and Chrome-based apps I can think of, but not all of them. The Qualcommm Snapdragon Reality Elite chip on the puck seems more than zippy enough to handle whatever multiple games and apps (even VR ones) I throw at it, but not all Android apps are available: Developers can choose not to opt in, as with Netflix and Disney Plus, but they can be loaded up in-browser.

Other apps aren’t necessarily optimized for the fluid way the Aura can open an app in any size. I watched a Jets game on Paramount Plus on the Aura, and it stayed in a fixed window size. I could move closer or further away, but it wouldn’t enlarge.

The whole Aura interface feels new-ish, even if you’ve used VR. The glasses enable hand tracking that’s surprisingly OK: Tapping and pinching works, and an extended pointer can reach at a distance and click and drag or adjust windows. When my hand passes in front of the Aura’s display, it even gets overlaid with a virtual hand mapped onto mine, like VR.

There’s no eye tracking, though, something Apple Vision Pro, Samsung Galaxy XR and Meta VR Glasses do. Eye tracking is helpful: It means you can lock into something and click it without lifting your hand. Here, I found I had to lift and aim my hand a lot, like an interactive remote. Hand tracking does work somewhat below the display’s field of view, but you often won’t know if you’re interacting until that hand’s lifted up higher. This is where the Aura’s smaller-than-VR viewing area becomes a problem.

It’s particularly an issue when playing some VR games. I tried Synth Riders, a popular fitness music movement game that’s also on Android XR. I could see what was further off in front of me, but the limited viewing area meant my hands were out of sight when in my peripheral vision, so I couldn’t reach for targets near me or off to the sides.

There’s a second way to control Aura: The processor puck itself has a touchpad across its whole top. Hold it and it’s a touch remote: I can drag my finger and touch-click. On a table next to a paired keyboard, it’s a trackpad.

That’s super clever, but the trackpad’s performance ranged from OK to poor depending on the apps I ran. There are some multitouch elements too, but it still felt less effective as a headset control than I wanted.

The puck has discrete volume controls and a power button with a fingerprint sensor for secure logins. But the side button wasn’t always in an easy place to press, depending on how I held the puck.

You could also just use voice to control things: Saying “Hey Google” or launching live Gemini can open apps, handle dictation and feel like a control system of sorts. But Gemini can’t always do things in apps. It’s more of a launcher.

There aren’t a ton of unique immersive Android XR experiences, unfortunately, even a year after the Samsung Galaxy XR debuted. The Aura can technically run almost all of those same apps, including many 2D ones that show up on the Google Play store in-headset. On the plus side, VR apps working at all on glasses this small feels like magic, despite some limits.

Demeo, one of several VR games I found that run on these glasses, looks great and is surprisingly playable. I can cast up a virtual tabletop RPG game in front of me, and my hands bring up cards that I can pick and play on the field. An included Galapagos immersive 3D documentary app looks lovely.

YouTube and Google Maps are once again stars of Android XR, just like they were on Galaxy XR when I reviewed it last year. YouTube has plenty of 3D and 360-degree videos you can view, and Google Maps’ immersive 3D earth modes and, occasionally, 3D scanned interior locations are still great to browse on the Aura’s smaller screens.

I fell in love with a demo of Sock Puppet Superstar, too. It’s a hand-puppet-singing VR game that works well on the Aura.

Mixed reality VR experiences that try to project a few simple things into a room work best, effectively turning the glasses into augmented reality. Cubism, a hand-tracking enabled puzzle game I’ve played on other VR headsets, works well here too. The accuracy of the hand tracking isn’t always great for precision gripping the corners of the virtual floating blocks, though.

The refresh rate on these VR apps isn’t as ultrasmooth as on Quest 3 or Steam Frame, but they do look sharp. Except, as I said before, the viewing area ends up clipped more narrowly, so immersion feels blindered.

Some VR apps didn’t run at all, though. A VR air hockey game on Android XR wouldn’t let me use my hands to control the pucks, for some reason. I know this is a prelaunch review of the Aura, but expect some apps to act oddly. You can sideload APKs of other VR apps, which is great. Google’s AI Studio tools also work in spatial 3D in these glasses, which means you could vibecode experiences on them.

Think of the Aura as a pair of super-powered Xreal glasses with a better viewing area and an included processor puck. Xreal’s existing line of other display glasses float microOLED displays via a USB-C tether in a similar way. The Aura glasses have similar Xreal controls on the arm, but they’re modified to Android XR interface controls that are a little different. There are volume buttons, a button that changes the dimming level of the electrochromic lenses from clear to nearly full black, and a top button that brings up the home app grid when clicked once, or launches live Gemini when held.

There’s also an array of three built-in cameras that handle room tracking, visual awareness for Gemini and hand tracking. Two are in the corners of the frame, one’s above the nose. Xreal’s other glasses, for the most part, are camera-free unless you buy a snap-in module.

The prism-like lenses that reflect the microOLED displays from the top of the frame are flatter like the Xreal One Pro line, and prescription lens inserts snap in the same way – I used the ones from the Pro and they work fine.

Speakers are embedded in the arms, pumping out audio that sounds as good as Xreal’s other glasses. Fine for games and movies, but you might prefer earbuds for isolation and privacy.

The display’s field of view, at 70 degrees, is bigger than Xreal’s largest size on the One Pro (57 degrees), and it feels like a larger projected display in front of me. The resolution is still just the same as Xreal’s other recent glasses, but things still look crisp, even for reading.

Sizewise, they’re like many other tethered glasses: bulkier and weirder than normal glasses, but a lot lighter than any VR headset. Three sets of nosepads are included for fit adjustment, and the arms bend at several angles, too.

I’m writing this review now in the Aura, at my dining room table, with a separately sold folding wireless keyboard made by Xreal. The keyboard performance in Chrome and Docs is fantastic. The trackpad, not quite as much. But I really feel like I can write on this.

Navigating Chrome and work apps also is possible: Logged into my office’s Google-based system, I’ve been handling emails and chats and little needs fine.

Getting files on and off the Aura is the trick. I’m Mac- and iPhone-based, so I’d need to put things in Drive and Google apps to triangulate more easily.

But what’s also impressive is that I can plug in other devices, including my MacBook, and use the Aura as a virtual screen. I can float my MacBook and the Aura apps side by side.

Here’s the catch: My MacBook keyboard only controls my Mac, and the Aura’s keyboard and hand tracking only work for the Aura apps. So I need two keyboards side by side to multitask.

To be clear, no one’s handled handing off of peripherals between connected devices well, not even Apple. But it points to the biggest thorn in Aura’s device-bridging dreams.

Connecting to lots of other devices via the Xreal Aura is a wild experience. You just need to cable in with a DisplayPort-ready USB-C cable to do it. The second cable included in the Aura box won’t do it; oddly, that’s just a charging cable.

Right now, I’m connecting the new iPad Mini and casting a second display up in the air. I’m typing on a Logitech keyboard and mouse paired to the iPad, because the Xreal inputs won’t control it. But the point, mainly, is that it connects. And Gemini can still give me feedback on what it sees on my iPad’s virtual screen.

Whatever you plug in can cast a virtual monitor in-glasses: MacBook, iPhone, Steam Deck. Shockingly, even a Nintendo Switch 2 works, something Xreal’s team has been excited about. There are caveats: The Switch 2 goes into docked mode and needs the Joy-Cons detached, and only certain higher-fidelity DisplayPort USB-C cables work. I played Ocarina of Time on the Aura’s screen and it looked great, but the framerate was a bit lower than what I get on the Switch 2 normally. But again, I can ask Gemini questions about the game as I’m playing, and it sees and gives me answers, provided I’ve clicked a little on-screen toggle to share my screen with Gemini’s visual mode.

Bridging between devices is exciting to me, but it’s really just limited to treating the input like a video-in that pops on a second screen in-glasses. Meta’s VR Glasses will do this too. It’s a great bonus addition, but having to cable both my glasses and my other device to the Aura puck means too many cables for my comfort.

The glasses also work on their own without the puck, defaulting to standard Xreal glasses firmware and controls. That’s great if I want to use them with my laptop/phone/etc on the fly without needing the Aura puck, at least.

Turning on Gemini Live with a press of the top button on Aura’s glasses means you can have Gemini in your life constantly, if you wish. Toggle a little upward-arrow icon to share your camera feed and on-screen apps, and suddenly Gemini can also describe YouTube videos for you, or read what you’re writing, or tell you what’s in your hand.

It’s an all-seeing assistant that can even work with Google’s circle-to-search, although that feature’s hard to trigger (press and hold my fingers and click to bring it up, it seems). But I can then circle something in front of me, capture it, and Google AI search brings up results instantly (a book I’m holding, a freezeframe on TV or something on one of my virtual screens).

This is a step beyond the type of live, camera-enabled AI modes in smart glasses. It can see the world via its cameras and all the virtual apps that get conjured.

That being said, it’s hit or miss. The video feed quality isn’t great, so the AI can’t always read things at a distance. But I wore the Xreal Aura across my kitchen, making coffee while floating a YouTube window in front of me and talking to Gemini, and it felt like some sort of cyberpunk future I’d only experienced in bits and pieces before. It’s something you could walk around with, technically, but not a device I’d wear all day (nor is it designed to be).

Xreal promises four hours of battery life on the Aura, which is more than most VR headset claims of 2 to 3 hours. In practice, it feels good. I can use it for several hours and still have a fair amount of battery left, which seems promising. I’ve only been testing for a week, though.

But the processor puck can overheat. The puck has venting fans that can pump very warm air, and it’s not meant to be put in a pocket, even though that’s exactly what I want to do with it when I’m wearing Aura on my face. Instead, there’s an included belt clip. I tried putting it in my pocket, and pretty soon I got an overheating warning pop-up message. Don’t put it in your pocket.

I don’t think I’ve ever been as fascinated and borderline overwhelmed as I have with the Xreal Aura. It points in all sorts of directions for where phones, AI assistants and glasses can be heading. Could this little tweener device be my portable workstation eventually?

Right now it’s more of an experiment with fascinating side benefits. It can’t replace a standard VR headset, though parts come close.

The Xreal Aura tested even my new-device tolerance, although I see amazing glimmers. It’s coming with me on my next trips for sure, and I’ll let you know what happens when I do. But it’s not yet the true fusion solution I’m waiting for. And yet, I’m still convinced that the concept, remixed and refined, will be.

article_content_zh:
我长期以来使用过的最令人着迷和令人沮丧的设备推动了耳机发展的边缘，眼镜也在不断发展。

让我告诉你一个奇怪的、迷人的、粗糙的中间产品，叫做 Xreal Aura。

有VR耳机，也有智能眼镜。还有一类新的设备正好介于两者之间。我们怎么称呼这些东西呢？我不知道。该类别包括明年推出的 Meta VR 眼镜，以及现在由 Google 和 Xreal 合作推出的 Aura。

Xreal Aura 瞄准月球，旨在架起眼镜和 VR 的桥梁，并在旅途中缩小一切。它常常令人着迷，但更多时候却令人沮丧。有时，它感觉就像是一个 VR 耳机。有时，它感觉就像是 Xreal 和其他几家公司已经制造的系留显示眼镜的超级版本，就像手机、笔记本电脑或几乎任何其他设备的可穿戴显示器。

我认为这实际上是通向未来的实验桥梁，未来手机将与先进的智能眼镜一起更好地发挥作用。如果您愿意，这些未来的眼镜可以在您周围创建浮动显示器和工作空间。从某种程度上来说，Aura 是谷歌实现这一目标的早期尝试。

强调早。目前，Xreal Aura 的功能、操作系统，尤其是输入有时感觉很难使用，有时很难进入自然流程。但它展示了这种规模的东西可以通过更多软件和输入流调整来实现。当它真正发挥作用时，它给人的感觉就像是一款我从未真正见过的便携式 VR/AR 耳机。

Aura 渴望成为去年三星 Galaxy XR 的缩小版，这是一款类似于苹果 Vision Pro 的昂贵混合现实耳机。与 Galaxy XR 一样，Aura 运行 Android XR，这是 Android 的一个变体，可以在各处浮动应用程序。它甚至可以运行 VR 应用程序。有时它会接近。其他时候，它还不够接近。

Aura 的神奇之处在于，它可以折叠成一个真正小到足以滑入我的包里的盒子。但设置和使用 Aura 通常需要耐心和实验。当它发挥作用时，我们就能看到可能即将到来的未来。但为了实现这一目标，你必须跨越重重障碍，有时让我想跳出去。

Android XR 是谷歌针对 AR/VR/AI 设备和可穿戴设备的操作系统，旨在将各种形状和尺寸的眼镜和耳机连接到谷歌和 Gemini 服务和应用程序。去年发布的三星 Galaxy XR 是第一款。接下来，几周后，谷歌和三星将推出由 Warby Parker 和 Gentle Monster 设计的人工智能智能眼镜。

从概念上讲，Xreal Aura 更像 Galaxy XR，而不是智能眼镜：它是一款可以随身携带的 AR/VR 耳机。该眼镜通过 USB-C 电缆连接到运行 Android XR 的随附处理器盘。它可以以 2D 和沉浸式 3D 方式显示 Android 应用程序。

Aura 支持手部追踪，可以允许完整的空间移动来放置浮动 3D 物体或玩沉浸式游戏。它可以让应用程序漂浮在您周围，并且您可以同时导航应用程序。您可以使用手部跟踪来打开或点击这些应用程序，或者使用处理器圆盘顶部内置的触控板。您还可以像我一样配对蓝牙键盘、游戏控制器或鼠标。

该套件可放入附带的手提箱中，该手提箱比我携带 Nintendo Switch 2 的手提箱还要小。旅行时很容易打包。我非常非常喜欢光环的这一部分。

256GB 存储和 12GB RAM 版本的售价为 1,279 美元，512GB/16GB 版本的售价为 1,499 美元，但它的售价为 1,099 美元/1,299 美元，直到今年年底。不过，板载存储空间就是您所拥有的一切。没有可扩展的 microSD 卡插槽。我评测的是256GB版本。

Aura 中的显示技术是 Xreal 其他系留显示眼镜上现有技术的增强版本，与 Viture 和 TCL RayNeo 使用的技术类似。双微型 OLED 显示屏非常明亮、清晰，通过棱镜投射，看起来就像漂浮在您的房间里一样。 “鸟浴”显示技术意味着镜片厚实且看起来很奇怪，但它们也比 Meta 的 Ray-Ban Displays 等支持显示的无线眼镜更大、更好看。

title: Microsoft unveils six AI models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, and voice, saying MAI Code 2 has 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price (Ina Fried/Axios)
title_en: Microsoft unveils six AI models spanning coding, cybersecurity, images, and voice, saying MAI Code 2 has 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol's performance at 40% of the price (Ina Fried/Axios)

author: Axios
article_content:
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman tells Axios the software giant is making significant progress toward building its own frontier general-purpose AI model, even as it introduces six specialized models that it claims rival leading offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic at a fraction of the cost.

Why it matters: Microsoft has long relied on OpenAI and other AI companies for its most advanced models. Now it's demonstrating that it can develop competitive technology of its own, and the new offerings show how aggressively the tech giant plans to compete on price.

Driving the news: Microsoft is announcing six new AI models Tuesday at its Ignite conference in San Francisco. The models span coding, cybersecurity, image generation and voice.

OpenAI is releasing new models, including Astra and Sol 6.2, which

Between the lines: Microsoft's strategy is to build models specialized for particular tasks, allowing them to achieve comparable performance at significantly lower costs.

"It basically means that you cram more tokens and knowledge and expertise into the same amount of parameters," Suleyman told Axios.

The big picture: Even as Microsoft targets the industry's leaders, frontier AI keeps moving forward as well. OpenAI on Tuesday announced GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol, with the new Astra priced 20 percent less than the prior version.

The intrigue: The new models could reshape Microsoft's relationship with OpenAI and other outside AI providers.

Zoom in: Microsoft is also offering enterprise customers access to licensed model weights, allowing them to customize its models with proprietary data while requiring deployment within Azure.

What to watch: How quickly Microsoft can translate its progress in specialized AI into a competitive general-purpose model — and whether its cost advantages are enough to persuade customers to switch from established rivals.

为什么重要：微软长期以来一直依赖 OpenAI 和其他人工智能公司提供最先进的模型。现在，它正在证明它可以开发自己的有竞争力的技术，而新产品也表明这家科技巨头计划如何积极地进行价格竞争。

重磅消息：微软周二在旧金山举行的 Ignite 会议上宣布了六种新的人工智能模型。这些模型涵盖编码、网络安全、图像生成和语音。

OpenAI 正在发布新模型，包括 Astra 和 Sol 6.2，其中

言外之意是：微软的战略是构建专门用于特定任务的模型，使它们能够以显着降低的成本实现可比的性能。

“这基本上意味着你将更多的代币、知识和专业知识塞进相同数量的参数中，”Suleyman 告诉 Axios。

总体情况：尽管微软瞄准了行业领导者，但前沿人工智能也在不断向前发展。 OpenAI 周二发布了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol，新 Astra 的价格比之前的版本低 20%。

看点：微软能够以多快的速度将其在专业人工智能领域的进展转化为有竞争力的通用模型，以及其成本优势是否足以说服客户放弃老牌竞争对手。

title: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT and Codex with new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models
title_en: OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT and Codex with new GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models
author: Zac Hall
article_content:
OpenAI kicked off the GPT-6 generation with Astra in September, then upgraded Sol to GPT-6.1 a few weeks later at DevDay.

Today, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are coming to ChatGPT Work and Codex together. OpenAI says both can finish demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done before hitting your usage limit.

### What’s new in GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol?

Astra is still the model OpenAI recommends for your hardest projects.

Say you have a screenshot of a slide and want the rest of your presentation to look like it. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra can use that screenshot as a template and match the layout, colors, and even the font size.

On the Codex side, OpenAI says Astra is better at making and testing changes in an existing project.

“Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision,” OpenAI says.

Sol is the more affordable model for everyday coding and writing, and it gets surprisingly close to Astra on one coding test.

Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 measures whether changes to real codebases are good enough for maintainers to merge.

With both models at maximum reasoning effort, OpenAI says Sol came within half a point of Astra at about one-fifth the cost.

“Some of you have been asking very politely. Some of you have just been asking. GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available. Super efficient and built to perform where it counts—the real world.” — OpenAI (@OpenAI)

### Who gets GPT-6.2?

Both models are available starting today in ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu.

The $200/month Pro plan also gets Ultrafast mode for the first time with Sol. The $500/month Pro plan gets Ultrafast on both models, as do eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces once an admin enables it.

How fast is Ultrafast? OpenAI says it can generate tokens at up to 4.5 times the standard rate on either model, although it uses more of your allowance. You can switch speeds from the model picker.

Developers can use both models through the API today as well. Astra’s standard input and output prices are 20% lower than with GPT-6 Astra, while Sol keeps its GPT-6.1 pricing.

You can read more in OpenAI’s full announcement.

OpenAI 在 9 月份与 Astra 一起启动了 GPT-6 一代，然后在几周后的 DevDay 上将 Sol 升级到了 GPT-6.1。

今天，GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 将一起来到 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex。 OpenAI 表示，两者都可以用更少的输出令牌完成要求较高的任务，因此您可以在达到使用限制之前完成更多工作。

### GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 有哪些新功能？

Astra 仍然是 OpenAI 为您最困难的项目推荐的模型。

假设您有一张幻灯片的屏幕截图，并希望演示文稿的其余部分看起来像它。 OpenAI 表示，GPT-6.2 Astra 可以使用该屏幕截图作为模板，并匹配布局、颜色甚至字体大小。

在 Codex 方面，OpenAI 表示 Astra 更擅长在现有项目中进行更改和测试。

“早期测试人员报告了更清晰的代码风格和更集中的测试，并且修改次数更少，”OpenAI 表示。

Sol 是日常编码和写作更实惠的模型，并且在一项编码测试中它与 Astra 惊人地接近。

Cognition 的 FrontierCode 2.0 衡量对实际代码库的更改是否足以让维护者进行合并。

OpenAI 表示，在两种模型都发挥最大推理能力的情况下，Sol 与 Astra 的差距只有半个百分点，而成本约为 Astra 的五分之一。

“你们中的一些人一直在非常礼貌地询问。你们中的一些人刚刚询问过。GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 现已推出。超级高效，专为在重要的地方（现实世界）执行而设计。” — OpenAI (@OpenAI)

### 谁获得 GPT-6.2？

从今天开始，这两种模型均可在 Plus、Pro、Enterprise 和 Edu 上的 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中使用。

每月 200 美元的 Pro 计划还首次通过 Sol 获得超快模式。每月 500 美元的 Pro 计划在两种型号上都可以实现超快，一旦管理员启用，符合资格的 Enterprise 和 Edu 工作区也是如此。

超快有多快？ OpenAI 表示，尽管它使用了更多的配额，但它可以在任一模型上以标准速率的 4.5 倍生成代币。您可以从模型选择器切换速度。

如今，开发人员也可以通过 API 使用这两种模型。 Astra 的标准输入和输出价格比 GPT-6 Astra 低 20%，而 Sol 保持其 GPT-6.1 定价。

您可以在 OpenAI 的完整公告中阅读更多内容。

article_content_en:
OpenAI kicked off the GPT-6 generation with Astra in September, then upgraded Sol to GPT-6.1 a few weeks later at DevDay.

Today, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are coming to ChatGPT Work and Codex together. OpenAI says both can finish demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done before hitting your usage limit.

### What’s new in GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol?

Astra is still the model OpenAI recommends for your hardest projects.

Say you have a screenshot of a slide and want the rest of your presentation to look like it. OpenAI says GPT-6.2 Astra can use that screenshot as a template and match the layout, colors, and even the font size.

On the Codex side, OpenAI says Astra is better at making and testing changes in an existing project.

“Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision,” OpenAI says.

Sol is the more affordable model for everyday coding and writing, and it gets surprisingly close to Astra on one coding test.

Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 measures whether changes to real codebases are good enough for maintainers to merge.

With both models at maximum reasoning effort, OpenAI says Sol came within half a point of Astra at about one-fifth the cost.

“Some of you have been asking very politely. Some of you have just been asking. GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are now available. Super efficient and built to perform where it counts—the real world.” — OpenAI (@OpenAI)

### Who gets GPT-6.2?

Both models are available starting today in ChatGPT Work and Codex on Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu.

The $200/month Pro plan also gets Ultrafast mode for the first time with Sol. The $500/month Pro plan gets Ultrafast on both models, as do eligible Enterprise and Edu workspaces once an admin enables it.

How fast is Ultrafast? OpenAI says it can generate tokens at up to 4.5 times the standard rate on either model, although it uses more of your allowance. You can switch speeds from the model picker.

Developers can use both models through the API today as well. Astra’s standard input and output prices are 20% lower than with GPT-6 Astra, while Sol keeps its GPT-6.1 pricing.

You can read more in OpenAI’s full announcement.

article_content:
### A new standard for professional work

We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. For businesses and developers, that means frontier performance at costs that make sense at scale.

GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new quality bar for AI in complex professional work. Its slides, spreadsheets, and documents read less like AI, and more closely follow the templates you provide and the conventions of your field. It writes cleaner code and builds frontends that look and work better, particularly for websites, gaming, and 3D design.

On Agents’ Last Exam, which tests multistep professional work, GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT‑6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, and 5.5 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost.

We believe GPT-6.2 Astra is the best model in the world for scientists. It sets a new high on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which tests how well models can carry out scientific work in a terminal. GPT-6.2 Astra scores 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than one-third the cost. It also sets a new high on the Vals Science Index, which asks models to interpret real biological data and run experiments to infer how a simulated system works.

In the API, GPT‑6.2 Astra’s input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT‑6 Astra’s, with a 60% discount on cached input ($8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output, all per million tokens). GPT‑6.2 Sol keeps GPT‑6.1 Sol’s API token prices. On several benchmarks, both models come close to or outperform other leading models at a small fraction of the cost per task.

### GPT-6.2 Sol: our go-to model for everyday work

Compared with GPT‑6.1 Sol, GPT‑6.2 Sol is smarter, more efficient, and lets you complete more tasks on the same paid plan. It powers through multistep agentic workflows, writes clearly and naturally, and is intuitive to collaborate with. Many employees at OpenAI use it as their default model for both technical and non-technical tasks.

In Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0, GPT‑6.2 Sol comes within 0.5 points of GPT‑6.2 Astra at about one-fifth the cost (both at max).

Its speed and intelligence also make it ideal for the important tasks people turn to AI for outside of work. On our recently released LifeVal evaluation, which measures performance on challenging everyday tasks, GPT‑6.2 Sol outscores GPT‑6 Astra at about one-seventh the cost.

### Professional outputs that match industry standards

We trained GPT‑6.2 Astra to create clearer, better-designed slides, spreadsheets, and documents that more closely follow the conventions professionals use in fields like law, sales, finance, and accounting. The writing is more direct and specific, with fewer generic takeaways and less filler.

Harvey LAB‑AA v1.1 uses legal assignments to test whether models can find the relevant facts across source documents, apply them to a detailed brief, and produce an accurate deliverable that meets every requirement. GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new state of the art, more than doubling Claude Fable 5.2’s pass rate at about one-sixth the cost. Astra for Law, our configuration of GPT-6.2 Astra for lawyers, scores even higher on this benchmark.

Our internal GDPval v2 benchmark is our next iteration of GDPval that measures complex, long-horizon workflows from real projects in sectors like consulting, finance, and design. GPT‑6.2 Astra leads the models we tested, up 6.2 percentage points from GPT‑6 Astra while using 22% fewer output tokens. GPT‑6.2 Sol improves 5.3 points from GPT‑6.1 Sol.

### Workbooks and memos

Building a valuation workbook or writing an investment memo starts with finding the relevant figures in source files and working out how they fit together. Artificial Analysis’s AA‑AnalystAgent tests that work on real spreadsheets and reports. In one task, models use California Medicaid’s expenditure reports to calculate how much the program spent on medical transport. GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, answering 62.5% of questions correctly on all five independent attempts.

### Slideshows

GPT‑6.2 Astra is our best model yet at designing slides and following slide templates, whether given an original file or even a screenshot. It can match the layout, colors, and typography down to the exact font size, and carry the template’s writing style into new slides. Early testers found the decks easier to use directly with fewer edits, thanks to titles that state the main takeaway and concise body copy that focuses on the details readers need.

### Computer use and interactive web design

GPT‑6.2 Astra’s more precise computer use lets it work down to individual parts and connections in CAD and simulation tools. Engineers can use that additional detail to check how components fit, see where loads shift as a design moves, and test revisions before building a prototype.

### Driving simulation

We asked GPT‑6.2 Astra to visualize chassis dynamics of a car on a mountain road. Astra created the 3D model and wrote a Python solver to simulate complex dynamics between the tires and suspension, then animated the results in Blender. This enables engineers to quickly test new designs and improve simulation accuracy over time.

### Mechanical design and assembly

GPT‑6.2 Astra can model a mechanical system part by part, giving engineers a way to show how it goes together and test how design changes affect its behavior.

### From CAD to a paper lamp

Our team used GPT‑6.2 Astra to turn the scalloped balconies of Chicago’s Marina City towers into a lamp. The video follows the design from reference photos through CAD revisions to a physical lamp assembled by hand. The site, generated by GPT-6.2 Astra, can be used to create your own paper lamp.

GPT‑6.2 Astra brings stronger visual reasoning to web design, choosing layouts and imagery that give each site a distinctive look and building elements around the actual goal of the site.

Those gains in visual reasoning and computer use carry over to 3D design. GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol can turn a written brief into an interactive browser experience, from a pinball table you can play to a recreation of the Colosseum you can explore from different angles. On Artificial Analysis’s AA‑3D, human judges try two blinded experiences built from the same prompt and vote for the one they prefer. GPT‑6.2 Astra ranks first with 1,318 Elo, followed by Claude Fable 5.2 at 1,271 and GPT‑6.2 Sol at 1,259.

### Efficient workflows with cleaner code style

GPT‑6.2 Astra has better judgment about how to execute a task, including matching its tools and effort to the workflow, and knowing when to use plugins versus computer use.

On coding, GPT-6.2 Astra is better at implementing and testing complex changes in existing codebases. Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision.

### Cybersecurity capabilities

GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol mark another significant jump in cyber capabilities. They find and exploit vulnerabilities more effectively, write more secure code, and produce better patches, with substantial token-efficiency gains on several evaluations. Like GPT‑6 Astra, 6.2 Astra and Sol meet the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework.

Due to their increased capabilities, we’re launching GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol with tighter safeguards for higher-risk cybersecurity assistance. These protections reduce misuse risk, but also restrict some legitimate vulnerability research and security testing workflows. Through OpenAI Daybreak, defenders can currently access GPT‑6 Sol with reduced cyber refusals on Daybreak Blue, in addition to our alpha for GPT-6 Astra, and GPT‑6 Cyber for advanced, authorized security testing on Daybreak Red. We will work to bring GPT‑6.2 models to Daybreak.

We highlight key benchmark results below, using internal testing configurations with cybersecurity safeguards and classifiers disabled. See the accompanying system card for full results and methodology.

### Giving cyber defenders an edge

Developers increasingly rely on coding agents to write production software, even as more capable agents lower the barrier to finding and exploiting vulnerabilities. PHP2Shell showed how AI can help researchers uncover critical flaws. With GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol, we made defensive capabilities a core focus, introducing new training signals to help developers prevent and repair those flaws—writing secure code from the start and producing patches that preserve intended behavior.

### Safety and alignment

We're deploying GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol with our strongest safeguards to date. We've tightened restrictions and strengthened the systems we use to monitor models and intervene when needed.

Like GPT-6 Astra, in addition to meeting the Critical threshold for cybersecurity, both GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meet the High threshold for biological and chemical capabilities under our Preparedness Framework. We’ve implemented protections to mitigate the associated risks, alongside increased restrictions across a set of potential dual-use biological and cybersecurity requests.

More details about our safeguards and testing are available in the GPT-6.2 system card.

### AI research capabilities and safeguards

GPT-6.2 Astra is our first externally released model to meet the High threshold for AI Self-improvement, which measures a model’s ability to accelerate AI research. A ‘High’ designation reflects our assessment that the model’s impact is equivalent to giving every OpenAI researcher an additional, highly capable research engineer as an assistant, relative to their 2024 baseline. We track this capability because models that can help develop future AI systems could also introduce new risks to safety, like accelerating progress faster than safeguards or human oversight can adapt.

To address these risks, we’ve built more oversight and controls into how we train and deploy our models. Before expanding internal access to GPT-6.2 Astra, we evaluated its alignment and verified that required safeguards were in place at each stage. We strengthened containment in our research environments, and tested those protections with our most capable models. We also built Control Room, a system that tracks research workloads and can halt further model output when intervention is needed. Our expanded monitoring examines models’ reasoning and actions across internal workloads and supported external deployments. It can automatically flag unauthorized behavior, and, where supported, pause workloads or conversations.

### Alignment

Both models performed similarly to GPT-6 Astra on most alignment evaluations, and took fewer improper actions in simulated workplace tasks. However, in two tests, they were more likely to omit mentioning obstacles that blocked their work, such as a missing file or unavailable search tool. We added instructions in Codex that substantially reduce these omissions, and we’re continuing to investigate the behavior.

### Pricing and availability

Starting today, GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. Pro 500 subscribers can use Ultrafast with either model. For the first time, we’re also bringing Ultrafast to Pro 200 subscribers, starting with GPT-6.2 Sol. Eligible Enterprise and Edu users get the same access once their workspace admin enables it. Developers can also access gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol through the OpenAI API, with Ultrafast available for both models at launch.

GPT‑6.2 Astra costs significantly less per task than GPT‑6 Astra, driven by better token efficiency, a 20% discount on input and output tokens, and a deeper 60% discount on cached input tokens. Standard API rates per million tokens are $8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output. GPT‑6.2 Sol carries forward GPT‑6.1 Sol’s rates of $2 for input, $0.10 for cached input, and $10 for output per million tokens.

For GPT-6.2 Astra & Sol, in order to improve cache reuse, help lower costs and latency, and preserve reasoning across turns, we recommend keeping prompt prefixes unchanged and appending new instructions to the conversation.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI发布了GPT-6.2 Astra与GPT-6.2 Sol两款模型，Astra专注于复杂多步骤专业工作与科学推理，在Agents’ Last Exam基准测试中表现显著优于前代；Sol则作为轻量化版本，在维持低成本前提下提升了日常工作效率。两款模型均通过优化输出Token效率，将API价格下调20%并提供60%的输入缓存折扣，以强化在B端与开发者市场的渗透率。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, with Astra targeting complex professional workflows and scientific reasoning, while Sol focuses on efficient everyday task execution. The company lowered API prices by 20% and introduced a 60% discount for cached inputs, aiming to consolidate its market share in enterprise and developer ecosystems.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: OpenAI此举标志着模型竞争逻辑从单一的参数规模竞赛转向“单位推理成本下的任务完成度”优化，意在通过极具侵略性的定价挤压竞争对手的生存空间。通过针对科学计算（Terminal-Bench-Science）的专项优化，其目标已明确指向高价值科研数据资产的处理权，这将迫使云服务厂商进一步压缩大模型托管的利润率。
ai_analysis.insight_en: OpenAI's strategy shifts from parameter scaling to optimizing task completion per unit of inference cost, aggressively compressing the market space for rivals. By specializing in scientific computing, OpenAI aims to capture high-value research data processing, forcing cloud providers to compress margins on LLM hosting services.

article_content_zh:
### 专业工作的新标准

我们推出了 GPT-6.2 Astra，这是我们为您最困难的项目设计的新前沿模型，以及 GPT-6.2 Sol，我们为日常工作设计的高效、多功能模型。两种模型都能以更少的输出令牌在要求较高的任务上提供更好的结果，因此您可以在使用限制内完成更多工作。对于企业和开发人员来说，这意味着以规模化的成本实现前沿性能。

GPT-6.2 Astra 为复杂专业工作中的人工智能设定了新的质量标准。它的幻灯片、电子表格和文档读起来不太像人工智能，而是更严格地遵循您提供的模板和您所在领域的惯例。它编写更清晰的代码并构建外观和工作效果更好的前端，特别是对于网站、游戏和 3D 设计。

在测试多步骤专业工作的 Agents’ Last Exam 中，GPT-6.2 Astra 创下了新高，比 GPT-6 Astra 高出 5.2 分，而成本却不到 GPT-6 Astra 的三分之一，比 Claude Fable 5.2 领先 5.5 分，而成本仅为 GPT-6 Astra 的 5%。

我们相信 GPT-6.2 Astra 对于科学家来说是世界上最好的模型。它为 Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 设定了新的高度，该版本测试模型在终端中执行科学工作的能力。 GPT-6.2 Astra 的得分比 GPT-6 Astra 高 9 个百分点，而成本却不到 GPT-6 Astra 的三分之一。它还创下了 Vals 科学指数的新高，该指数要求模型解释真实的生物数据并进行实验以推断模拟系统的工作原理。

在 API 中，GPT-6.2 Astra 的输入和输出代币价格比 GPT-6 Astra 低 20%，缓存输入有 60% 的折扣（输入 8 美元，缓存输入 0.40 美元，输出 40 美元，均为每百万代币）。 GPT-6.2 Sol 保留 GPT-6.1 Sol 的 API 代币价格。在多个基准测试中，这两种模型都接近或优于其他领先模型，而每项任务的成本仅为其一小部分。

### GPT-6.2 Sol：我们日常工作的首选模型

与 GPT-6.1 Sol 相比，GPT-6.2 Sol 更智能、更高效，让您在相同的付费套餐中完成更多任务。它通过多步骤代理工作流程提供支持，书写清晰自然，并且协作直观。 OpenAI 的许多员工都将其用作技术和非技术任务的默认模型。

在 Cognition 的 FrontierCode 2.0 中，GPT-6.2 Sol 与 GPT-6.2 Astra 相差不到 0.5 个点，成本约为 GPT-6.2 Astra 的五分之一（均为最大值）。

它的速度和智能也使其成为人们在工作之外求助于人工智能的重要任务的理想选择。在我们最近发布的 LifeVal 评估（衡量具有挑战性的日常任务的性能）中，GPT-6.2 Sol 的得分超过了 GPT-6 Astra，成本约为 GPT-6 Astra 的七分之一。

### 符合行业标准的专业输出

我们训练 GPT-6.2 Astra 创建更清晰、设计更好的幻灯片、电子表格和文档，更严格地遵循专业人士在法律、销售、财务和会计等领域使用的惯例。写作更加直接和具体，一般性要点和填充物更少。

Harvey LAB-AA v1.1 使用法律作业来测试模型是否可以在源文档中找到相关事实，将其应用到详细的摘要中，并生成满足每项要求的准确交付成果。 GPT-6.2 Astra 树立了新的技术水平，以大约六分之一的成本将 Claude Fable 5.2 的通过率提高了一倍以上。 Astra for Law（我们为律师配置的 GPT-6.2 Astra）在此基准测试中得分甚至更高。

我们的内部 GDPval v2 基准是 GDPval 的下一代迭代，用于衡量咨询、金融和设计等领域实际项目的复杂、长期工作流程。 GPT-6.2 Astra 在我们测试的模型中领先，比 GPT-6 Astra 提高了 6.2 个百分点，同时使用的输出代币减少了 22%。 GPT-6.2 Sol 比 GPT-6.1 Sol 提高了 5.3 点。

### 作业簿和备忘录

构建估值工作簿或撰写投资备忘录首先要在源文件中查找相关数据，并弄清楚它们如何组合在一起。 Artificial Analysis 的 AA-AnalystAgent 测试适用于真实的电子表格和报告。在一项任务中，模型使用加州医疗补助的支出报告来计算该计划在医疗运输上的支出。 GPT-6.2 Astra 创下新高，在所有五次独立尝试中正确回答了 62.5% 的问题。

### 幻灯片

GPT-6.2 Astra 是我们迄今为止设计幻灯片和遵循幻灯片模板的最佳模型，无论是给定原始文件还是屏幕截图。它可以将布局、颜色和版式匹配到精确的字体大小，并将模板的书写风格带入新幻灯片中。早期测试人员发现这些套牌更容易直接使用，编辑次数也更少，这要归功于陈述主要内容的标题和专注于读者需要的细节的简洁正文。

### 计算机使用和交互式网页设计

GPT-6.2 Astra 更精确的计算机使用使其能够在 CAD 和模拟工具中细化到各个零件和连接。工程师可以使用这些额外的细节来检查组件的配合情况，查看负载随着设计的变化而变化的位置，并在构建原型之前测试修订。

### 驾驶模拟

我们要求 GPT‑6.2 Astra 可视化山路上汽车的底盘动态。 Astra 创建了 3D 模型并编写了一个 Python 解算器来模拟轮胎和悬架之间的复杂动力学，然后在 Blender 中对结果进行动画处理。这使得工程师能够快速测试新设计并随着时间的推移提高仿真精度。

### 机械设计与装配

GPT-6.2 Astra 可以对机械系统的各个部分进行建模，为工程师提供了一种展示其如何组合并测试设计变更如何影响其行为的方法。

### 从 CAD 到纸灯

我们的团队使用 GPT-6.2 Astra 将芝加哥滨海城塔楼的扇形阳台变成了一盏灯。该视频讲述了从参考照片到 CAD 修订再到手工组装的实体灯的设计过程。该网站由 GPT-6.2 Astra 生成，可用于创建您自己的纸灯。

GPT-6.2 Astra 为网页设计带来了更强大的视觉推理，选择为每个网站提供独特外观的布局和图像，并围绕网站的实际目标构建元素。

这些视觉推理和计算机使用方面的进步也延续到了 3D 设计中。 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 可以将书面简报转变为交互式浏览器体验，从可以玩的弹球桌到可以从不同角度探索的罗马斗兽场的娱乐。在 Artificial Analysis 的 AA-3D 中，人类评委尝试根据同一提示构建的两种盲体验，并投票选出他们喜欢的一种。 GPT-6.2 Astra 以 1,318 Elo 排名第一，其次是 Claude Fable 5.2（1,271）和 GPT-6.2 Sol（1,259）。

### 高效的工作流程和简洁的代码风格

GPT-6.2 Astra 对如何执行任务有更好的判断，包括将其工具和工作与工作流程相匹配，以及知道何时使用插件而不是计算机。

在编码方面，GPT-6.2 Astra 更擅长在现有代码库中实现和测试复杂的更改。早期的测试人员报告了更清晰的代码风格和更集中的测试，并且修改次数更少。

### 网络安全能力

GPT-6.2 Astra 和 GPT-6.2 Sol 标志着网络能力的又一次重大飞跃。他们更有效地发现和利用漏洞，编写更安全的代码，并生成更好的补丁，并在多项评估中获得了显着的令牌效率提升。与 GPT-6 Astra 一样，6.2 Astra 和 Sol 也满足我们的准备框架下的网络安全关键阈值。

由于功能增强，我们推出了 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，为高风险网络安全援助提供更严格的保障措施。这些保护措施降低了误用风险，但也限制了一些合法的漏洞研究和安全测试工作流程。通过 OpenAI Daybreak，防御者目前可以在 Daybreak Blue 上访问 GPT-6 Sol，减少网络拒绝，此外还可以在 Daybreak Red 上访问 GPT-6 Astra 的 alpha 版，以及在 Daybreak Red 上进行高级授权安全测试的 GPT-6 Cyber​​。我们将努力将 GPT-6.2 模型引入 Daybreak。

我们在下面重点介绍关键基准测试结果，使用内部测试配置并禁用网络安全保障措施和分类器。有关完整结果和方法，请参阅随附的系统卡。

### 为网络防御者提供优势

开发人员越来越依赖编码代理来编写生产软件，尽管功能更强大的代理降低了发现和利用漏洞的障碍。 PHP2Shell 展示了人工智能如何帮助研究人员发现关键缺陷。借助 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，我们将防御能力作为核心焦点，引入新的训练信号来帮助开发人员预防和修复这些缺陷 - 从一开始就编写安全代码并生成保留预期行为的补丁。

### 安全和对准

我们正在部署 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，并提供迄今为止最强大的保障措施。我们加强了限制并加强了用于监控模型并在需要时进行干预的系统。

与 GPT-6 Astra 一样，除了满足网络安全的关键阈值之外，GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 还满足我们的准备框架下的生物和化学能力的高阈值。我们已经实施了保护措施来减轻相关风险，同时增加了对一系列潜在的双重用途生物和网络安全请求的限制。

有关我们的防护措施和测试的更多详细信息，请参阅 GPT-6.2 系统卡。

### 人工智能研究能力及保障

GPT-6.2 Astra是我们第一个对外发布的满足AI自我提升高门槛的模型，衡量模型加速AI研究的能力。 “高”称号反映了我们的评估，即相对于 2024 年的基准，该模型的影响相当于为每位 OpenAI 研究人员提供了一名额外的、能力很强的研究工程师作为助理。我们跟踪这种能力是因为有助于开发未来人工智能系统的模型也可能会给安全带来新的风险，比如加速进步的速度快于保障措施或人类监督所能适应的速度。

为了解决这些风险，我们对训练和部署模型的方式进行了更多的监督和控制。在扩大对 GPT-6.2 Astra 的内部访问之前，我们评估了其一致性并验证了每个阶段所需的保护措施是否到位。我们加强了研究环境的遏制，并用我们最有能力的模型测试了这些保护措施。我们还构建了控制室，这是一个跟踪研究工作量的系统，可以在需要干预时停止进一步的模型输出。我们的扩展监控检查模型在内部工作负载和支持的外部部署中的推理和操作。它可以自动标记未经授权的行为，并在支持的情况下暂停工作负载或对话。

### 结盟

在大多数对齐评估中，这两种模型的表现与GPT-6 Astra相似，并且在模拟工作场所任务中采取的不当行为较少。然而，在两个测试中，他们更有可能忽略那些阻碍他们工作的障碍，比如丢失的文件或不可用的搜索工具。我们在食品法典中增加了大量减少这些遗漏的说明，我们正在继续调查这种行为。

### 定价和供货情况

从今天开始，GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 可供 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中的所有 Plus、Pro、Enterprise 和 Edu 用户使用。 Pro 500 订阅者可以使用任一型号的 Ultrafast。从 GPT-6.2 Sol 开始，我们还首次为 Pro 200 订阅者带来 Ultrafast。一旦工作区管理员启用，符合条件的企业和教育用户将获得相同的访问权限。开发人员还可以通过 OpenAI API 访问 gpt-6.2-astra 和 gpt-6.2-sol，这两种模型在发布时都可以使用 Ultrafast。

GPT-6.2 Astra 每项任务的成本明显低于 GPT-6 Astra，这得益于更好的令牌效率、输入和输出令牌 20% 的折扣以及缓存输入令牌 60% 的更深折扣。每百万代币的标准 API 费率为输入 8 美元、缓存输入 0.40 美元、输出 40 美元。 GPT-6.2 Sol 继承了 GPT-6.1 Sol 的每百万代币 2 美元的输入费率、0.10 美元的缓存输入费率以及 10 美元的输出费率。

对于 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol，为了提高缓存重用、帮助降低成本和延迟并保留轮流推理，我们建议保持提示前缀不变并向对话附加新指令。
