article_content_en:
When Silicon Valley entrepreneur Chad Steelberg decided he wanted to get involved in the war in Ukraine, he had no idea where to start. So the then CEO of enterprise AI company Veritone did what he knew best: built an artificial intelligence model to help him figure it out. Today, he has proprietary munition and missile designs, several government partnerships, and a defense-as-a-service business valued at more than $1 billion.

Steelberg, alongside fellow Google alumnus and former Apple executive Andy Baynes, says they are trying to break the Russia-Ukraine war “stalemate,” Silicon Valley–style. They believe their experience building and iterating technology quickly can help bring Western weapon manufacturing in line with the rapid innovation cycles seen on the battlefield and beat the “attritional cat-and-mouse technology game” that the war, as Baynes describes it, has become.

Steelberg, originally from Newport Beach, California, started itching to “make a difference” on the battlefield after he took in a couple hundred Ukrainian refugees into his French chateau in early 2022. He says he was regularly “heartbroken” by the outpouring of grief whenever bad news arrived about a husband, father, or son back home. “I believe I could really change the outcome of this and every war,” Steelberg tells WIRED. "I'm not saying this is purely altruistic,” he adds. “Of course we're going to be making money doing it."

This week, their firm, Tiberius Aerospace, said it had secured $85 million in Series A financing, led by European technology investment firm Lakestar and Rochefort Asset Management, a national-security-focused investment firm licensed under the US Defense Department. Ukrainian venture capital firm UA1 is also an investor.

Tiberius began as Steelberg’s private research lab, incorporated in 2021, which employed people across France, the UK, and US to experiment on left-field ideas across a range of technologies, from drones and electric vertical takeoff aircraft to quantum computing. After the invasion, he pivoted the lab’s AI and aerospace engineers into writing code and building spreadsheets to objectively analyze the war’s many factors and calculate what could move the needle. The AI model they created quickly ruled out building better defensive technology because that would just harden the stalemate.

With his aim narrowed to building an offensive weapon, Steelberg developed several metrics to numerically analyze the lethality of different systems, including cost-effectiveness, and used the AI engine to simulate weapons under different conditions and identify what would disrupt the market. Don’t build another drone, it suggested, build longer-range artillery munitions. The resulting system, called Sceptre, can be fired from a 155-millimeter howitzer—the most common artillery weapon donated to Ukraine. As well as traveling farther than currently available rounds, they claim they can reach supersonic speeds and altitudes beyond jamming range.

Giving Ukraine’s guns extra range is important, Sam Cranny-Evans, an associate fellow at UK defense think tank the Royal United Services Institute, tells WIRED, because it would allow Ukrainian gunners to operate beyond the reach of Russian drone attacks. 155-mm shells “can cause massive damage to a group of vehicles or infantry,” he says. “Any technology that can help Ukraine extend the reach of its howitzers and return them to combat would be valuable.”

With a prototype he’d designed with the help of AI, Steelberg also started to expand the Tiberius team, including bringing on board Baynes as chief strategy officer in 2023. Baynes had first traveled to Ukraine around a decade ago to investigate how local startup Ring, now owned by Amazon, had outdone Nest, which he’d been working on and eventually sold to Google. He fell in love with Kyiv’s ambitious software engineers and booming tech scene–responsible for globally successful tech tools like Grammarly and Snapchat’s face filters. In 2016, he bought a local life-science tech company with the aim of accelerating next-generation medicines through automating clinical trials and improving protein modeling. “What drew me into Kyiv was the hunger and ambition in the engineering community,” he tells WIRED. “It was difficult to not be enormously attracted to that and to see if it's something that could be put into really critical-mission problem sets like cancer drugs or speeding up clinical trials for life-science companies.”

After the Russian invasion, Baynes set himself up in Budapest for around six months to help with the logistics of evacuating women and children and moving equipment into the country. He asked his global network for help finding medical equipment, vehicles, and accommodation for refugees—bringing him back in touch with Steelberg. Baynes believes the West’s response to the invasion has been “inadequate” and that Ukraine needs better offensive capabilities to push Russia’s army back.

In April, Tiberius announced it had successfully fired one of its Sceptre projectiles from a NATO-standard 155-mm howitzer for the first time. It is now working with the US Army to mature the system, and it has announced a $500 million technology collaboration contract with UK partners to manufacture, license, and distribute the munition. It is also developing a missile, which it expects to start generating revenue next year.

Tiberius has turned the AI system it initially built into a product called GRAIL (Generative Real-Time Artificial Intelligence for Lethality). Steelberg says he is “most excited about” this. He hopes the platform can enable continuous upgrades to the weapon designs Tiberius licenses by decentralizing manufacturing. Steelberg says that, as well as automating supply chain management and compliance, the software simulates weapons against different targets in a range of environments and weather conditions, such as an Arctic peninsula. In addition to open-sourced data, the team is trying to get hold of much sought-after active combat data from around the world, including Ukraine. The idea is that this all enables users to test, iterate, and design weapons for specific uses much quicker.

“In the world of AI and design and development getting faster and faster, what is it that the West or the group of allied nations have an undeniable advantage on?” Baynes asks. “If you can weaponize all of the spare capacity and precision manufacturing across the UK, France, Germany, the Nordic countries, the US,” he says, “that's something that our adversaries today can never ever match.” Tiberius aims to achieve this by copying “the Apple model,” continues Baynes, who reported to Steve Jobs for four years. He says outsourcing manufacturing to many third-party subcontractors can accelerate development and deployment and keeps expensive production costs off Tiberius’ balance sheet during peacetime.

“We're taking the approach of Silicon Valley,” says Steelberg. “When you run into a big, hard, hairy problem, you not only cross that, but you turn around, you build a bridge—it’s a toll bridge, obviously—so the entire industry can cross that hurdle faster, better, stronger. They might pay a small fee, but it's better than dying in the ditch and not making it across it.”

Steelberg says that, as well as automating supply chain management and compliance, the software simulates weapons against different targets in a range of environments and weather conditions, such as an Arctic peninsula. In addition to open-sourced data, the team is trying to get hold of much sought-after active combat data from around the world, including Ukraine. The idea is that this all enables users to test, iterate, and design weapons for specific uses much quicker.

“In the world of AI and design and development getting faster and faster, what is it that the West or the group of allied nations have an undeniable advantage on?” Baynes asks. “If you can weaponize all of the spare capacity and precision manufacturing across the UK, France, Germany, the Nordic countries, the US,” he says, “that's something that our adversaries today can never ever match.” Tiberius aims to achieve this by copying “the Apple model,” continues Baynes, who reported to Steve Jobs for four years. He says outsourcing manufacturing to many third-party subcontractors can accelerate development and deployment and keeps expensive production costs off Tiberius’ balance sheet during peacetime.

“We're taking the approach of Silicon Valley,” says Steelberg. “When you run into a big, hard, hairy problem, you not only cross that, but you turn around, you build a bridge—it’s a toll bridge, obviously—so the entire industry can cross that hurdle faster, better, stronger. They might pay a small fee, but it's better than dying in the ditch and not making it across it.”

author: Amrith Ramkumar and Robbie Whelan
content_snippet: The letter, also sent to Jensen Huang's roughly 60 direct reports, escalates an internal push to get him reinstated as CEO
summary_en: Nader Khalil, Nvidia's Director of Developer Technology, wrote to the board and roughly 60 of Jensen Huang's direct reports, expressing concerns regarding a potential leadership transition. The correspondence highlights Huang's critical role in maintaining company culture and attracting top-tier engineering talent, warning that failing to retain him could trigger a catastrophic loss of irreplaceable human capital.
article_content_en:
A senior Nvidia employee sent a letter to the company’s top executives and board of directors arguing that failure to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could lead to the loss of “irreplaceable talent,” according to people familiar with the matter.

The letter, written by director of developer technology Nader Khalil, escalates an internal push to bring Huang back following his resignation on Thursday. It argues that Huang is uniquely qualified to lead Nvidia and deserves the benefit of the doubt as the board investigates his relationship with a Singapore data-center executive suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset.

Nvidia is stuck between a rock and a hard place, as "irreplaceable talent" wants to leave if Jensen Huang isn't reinstated as CEO amidst the spy affair controversy.

Following the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang, there are warnings that important Nvidia employees are planning to leave if the company doesn’t reinstate him. According to the Wall Street Journal, an employee sent an internal letter to the top executives and board of directors stating that “failure to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could lead to the loss of ‘irreplaceable talent.’” Huang resigned last week amidst a firestorm of reports about an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, a further affair with VP of health care Kimberly Powell, and allegations the former relationship may have facilitated chip smuggling into China.

According to WSJ’s sources, director of developer technology Nader Khalil wrote the letter, urging that Huang be reinstated as CEO, lest the company lose loyal and important employees. The letter’s recipients, according to WSJ, comprised roughly 60 direct reports and the 10 members of the board, and Khalil warned that “Irreplaceable talent at Nvidia is now contemplating departing.”

The internal letter, along with the standwithjensen.com open letter to reinstate him, shows how important Huang is to the employees of Nvidia. Without the key long-term employees, which the company heavily depends on, progress could halt, or possibly regress, as Nvidia would lose the employees who have worked on and built the architectures and systems that make Nvidia what it is, along with their leader, Huang — who has recently stated that he would be honored to come back as CEO.

The open letter, signed by multiple Nvidia current and former employees, and tech CEOs and investors, states that employees are concerned that Huang was ousted unfairly and without due process, expressing that the employees do not have “access to the board’s private deliberations,” and that they have not been shown evidence that Alice Huang was indeed a spy, which even US intelligence doesn’t have solid evidence of. The open letter demands that Huang be reinstated as CEO while ensuring an independent investigation and a fair hearing, including providing a “specific, evidence-based explanation” of why Nvidia shouldn’t keep Huang as CEO — with Huang scheduled to appear before a House of Foreign Affairs panel concerning his affairs with the alleged spy.

Despite the letter, the support of other Silicon Valley CEOs, and even President Trump, Nvidia is still not considering bringing Huang back as CEO. Nvidia is the hottest AI hardware company at the moment, and its employees are highly desirable not only within the US, but possibly China as well. China surely wouldn’t mind getting its hands on a few key employees, who, if they choose to leave, are likely not going to have a hard time finding another job.

article_content_zh:
据知情人士透露，英伟达的一名高级员工致信该公司高管和董事会，称如果未能恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官，可能会导致“不可替代的人才”流失。

这封信由开发技术总监纳德·哈利勒 (Nader Khalil) 撰写，在黄周四辞职后，内部加大了要求其回归的力度。报告认为，黄仁勋具有领导英伟达的独特资格，在董事会调查黄仁勋与一名涉嫌中国情报资产的新加坡数据中心高管的关系时，他理应享有无罪推定。

英伟达陷入进退两难的境地，如果黄仁勋在间谍事件争议中不恢复首席执行官职务，“不可替代的人才”就会离开。

前首席执行官黄仁勋辞职后，有人警告称，如果公司不恢复他的职位，英伟达的重要员工将计划离职。据《华尔街日报》报道，一名员工向高管和董事会发送了一封内部信，表示“未能恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职务可能会导致‘不可替代的人才’流失。”黄仁勋上周辞职，原因是黄仁勋与 Megaspeed 高管爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)有染，与医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔(Kimberly Powell)有染，以及指控前关系可能促进芯片走私到中国。黄仁勋上周辞职。

据《华尔街日报》消息人士透露，开发者技术总监纳德·哈利勒(Nader Khalil)写了这封信，敦促黄仁勋恢复首席执行官职务，以免公司失去忠诚和重要的员工。据《华尔街日报》报道，这封信的收件人包括大约 60 名直接下属和 10 名董事会成员，哈利勒警告说，“英伟达不可替代的人才现在正在考虑离职。”

这封内部信件，以及standwithjensen.com上要求黄仁勋复职的公开信，显示出黄仁勋对英伟达员工的重要性。如果没有公司严重依赖的关键长期员工，进展可能会停滞不前，甚至可能倒退，因为英伟达将失去那些参与并构建了英伟达的架构和系统的员工，以及他们的领导者黄先生。黄先生最近表示，他很荣幸能回来担任首席执行官。

这封由多名英伟达现任和前任员工、科技公司首席执行官和投资者签署的公开信表示，员工们担心黄仁勋在没有正当程序的情况下被不公平地解雇，并表示员工无权“了解董事会的私人审议”，并且没有向他们提供证据证明爱丽丝黄确实是间谍，而即使美国情报部门也没有确凿的证据。这封公开信要求恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官职务，同时确保进行独立调查和公平听证会，包括提供“具体的、基于证据的解释”，说明为什么英伟达不应让黄仁勋继续担任首席执行官——黄仁勋计划就他与所谓间谍的关系出席众议院一个小组的听证会。

尽管有这封信，以及其他硅谷首席执行官甚至特朗普总统的支持，英伟达仍然没有考虑让黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官。英伟达是目前最热门的人工智能硬件公司，其员工不仅在美国非常受欢迎，在中国也可能如此。中国肯定不会介意得到一些关键员工，如果他们选择离开，找到另一份工作可能不会很难。

title: Introducing ChatGPT for Sales
title_en: Introducing ChatGPT for Sales

inline_images.caption: Sales tools grouped by workflow: content and enablement, accounts and deals, prospecting, customer conversations, performance and risk, and quotes and agreements.
inline_images.caption_en: Sales tools grouped by workflow: content and enablement, accounts and deals, prospecting, customer conversations, performance and risk, and quotes and agreements.

author: OpenAI
article_content:
Help every seller shorten the sales cycle, from finding the right accounts to following through on customer commitments, with a new Sales experience and over 30 new and expanded partner plugins.

We’re introducing ChatGPT for Sales to help every sales team understand customers better, spend less time on busywork, and close more deals. It includes our new Sales plugin with dedicated skills for sellers, and more than 30 new and enhanced partner plugins in ChatGPT, so you can use information from the tools your team already relies on to prepare for calls, tailor proposals, and follow up faster.

### A starting point for every seller

The new Sales plugin from OpenAI gives you ready-to-use workflows for everyday sales work, from deciding which accounts to pursue to preparing for a call and drafting the follow-up. Sales teams work best when everyone has a shared understanding of the customer. Which accounts are worth pursuing? What does a buyer need to move forward? Which deals need attention, and why? The answers often sit across teammates, prospecting tools, customer calls, and the CRM. Bringing that information together gives teams more time to make informed decisions and follow through on customer commitments. That starts with the work you do every day.

### Connect your sales process to ChatGPT

ChatGPT for Sales brings your tools, customer context, and sales workflows into one place. It also gives your team access to partner plugins, so ChatGPT can use customer context from your existing tools to help move opportunities forward. Choose the partner plugins that fit your sales process.

Create content and equip sellers. Learn your sales process and the latest product updates with Confluence, Guru, and Seismic. Rehearse pitches and practice handling objections with ChatGPT Voice. Build tailored presentations with ChatGPT Slides, Gamma, Figma, or Canva, or create an interactive demo or ROI calculator with ChatGPT Sites.

Manage accounts and advance deals. Bring together account context from Salesforce, HubSpot, Close CRM, or monday CRM to prepare for calls, review customer commitments, and plan next steps.

Find and engage buyers. Combine account signals from Apollo, Clay, and Common Room with ChatGPT’s web research to understand what’s changing at an account and identify reasons to reach out. Use Outreach or Salesloft to plan your outreach.

Turn customer conversations into action. Use call notes from the Meetings plugin in ChatGPT, Gong, Otter.ai, or Granola to understand buyer priorities, capture agreed next steps, and draft follow-ups.

Track performance and spot deal risk. Use signals from Backstory to identify deals that need attention. Analyze connected sales data with the Data plugin in ChatGPT or Hex to explain what changed in the pipeline and where to focus next.

Prepare quotes and agreements. Bring in Docusign, Ironclad, PandaDoc, or ServiceNow CPQ to help prepare quotes and agreements when a buyer is ready to move forward.

You can also keep work moving between conversations by delegating to your dot —an always-on agent in ChatGPT. Your dot can use these same plugins and customer context to prepare meeting briefs, track deal updates, and proactively bring you relevant changes and proposed next steps for review.

### Use cases for every sales team

### Build pipeline in the right accounts

Use ChatGPT to build a prioritized account list from your CRM information and prospect research from tools like ZoomInfo and Clay. Ask why each account fits, identify missing information, and refine the list around your team’s priorities. Then turn that research into outreach with a specific reason to engage—all in the same conversation.

### Make a stronger case to each buyer

article_content_zh:
通过全新的销售体验和 30 多个新的和扩展的合作伙伴插件，帮助每个卖家缩短销售周期，从找到合适的帐户到履行客户承诺。

我们推出 ChatGPT for Sales 来帮助每个销售团队更好地了解客户、花更少的时间在繁忙的工作上并达成更多交易。它包括我们新的销售插件，为卖家提供专门的技能，以及 ChatGPT 中的 30 多个新的和增强的合作伙伴插件，因此您可以使用团队已经依赖的工具中的信息来准备通话、定制建议并更快地跟进。

### 每个卖家的起点

OpenAI 的新销售插件为您提供了日常销售工作的现成工作流程，从决定要寻求哪些客户到准备电话和起草后续工作。当每个人都对客户有共同的了解时，销售团队才能发挥最佳效果。哪些账户值得关注？买家需要什么才能继续前进？哪些交易需要关注，为什么？答案通常来自团队成员、勘探工具、客户电话和 CRM。将这些信息整合在一起可以让团队有更多时间做出明智的决策并履行客户承诺。这要从你每天所做的工作开始。

### 将您的销售流程连接到 ChatGPT

ChatGPT for Sales 将您的工具、客户背景和销售工作流程整合到一处。它还使您的团队可以访问合作伙伴插件，因此 ChatGPT 可以使用现有工具中的客户上​​下文来帮助推动机会。选择适合您的销售流程的合作伙伴插件。

创建内容并装备卖家。通过 Confluence、Guru 和 Seismic 了解您的销售流程和最新产品更新。使用 ChatGPT Voice 排练推介并练习处理异议。使用 ChatGPT Slides、Gamma、Figma 或 Canva 构建定制演示文稿，或使用 ChatGPT 站点创建交互式演示或 ROI 计算器。

管理账户并推进交易。汇集来自 Salesforce、HubSpot、Close CRM 或星期一 CRM 的客户上下文，以准备通话、审查客户承诺并计划后续步骤。

寻找并吸引买家。将来自 Apollo、Clay 和 Common Room 的帐户信号与 ChatGPT 的网络研究相结合，以了解帐户的变化并确定联系的原因。使用 Outreach 或 Salesloft 来规划您的外展活动。

将客户对话转化为行动。使用 ChatGPT、Gong、Otter.ai 或 Granola 中会议插件的通话记录来了解买家的优先事项、捕获商定的后续步骤并起草后续行动。

跟踪绩效和现货交易风险。使用 Backstory 中的信号来识别需要关注的交易。使用 ChatGPT 或 Hex 中的数据插件分析互联销售数据，以解释管道中发生的变化以及下一步关注的重点。

准备报价和协议。当买家准备好继续前进时，引入 Docusign、Ironclad、PandaDoc 或 ServiceNow CPQ 来帮助准备报价和协议。

您还可以通过委托给您的点（ChatGPT 中始终在线的代理）来保持对话之间的工作顺利进行。您的网点可以使用这些相同的插件和客户上下文来准备会议摘要、跟踪交易更新，并主动为您提供相关更改和建议的后续步骤以供审核。

### 每个销售团队的用例

### 在正确的账户中建立管道

使用 ChatGPT 根据您的 CRM 信息和 ZoomInfo 和 Clay 等工具的前景研究构建优先帐户列表。询问每个帐户为何适合，找出缺失的信息，并围绕团队的优先事项完善列表。然后将研究转化为具有特定参与原因的外展活动——所有这些都在同一次对话中进行。

### 向每个买家提出更有力的理由

在会议之前，要求获得一份简报，其中包含客户历史记录、之前的通话记录和买家的优先事项。探索仍需要答案的问题，然后将准备工作转化为针对 Gamma 或 Canva 的客户特定推介。在会议前的谈话中完善故事。

### 通过明确的后续步骤保持交易进展

通话后，让 ChatGPT 起草后续行动，捕获商定的后续步骤，并准备更新客户记录。完善对话中的消息并审查建议的更改。借助 Attio 等互联工具，您可以将下一步从 ChatGPT 保存到 CRM。

### 查看您的管道存在风险的地方

让 ChatGPT 使用 CRM 历史记录和客户对话来帮助您了解是什么阻碍了交易。通过 Rox，您还可以要求工作人员每天早上检查交易，标记需要注意的更改，并准备会议摘要或后续顺序供您审核。

查看整个销售生态系统中的一些示例，展示这些工具如何在 ChatGPT 中工作：

### 销售团队如何利用 ChatGPT 取胜

从客户研究到交易跟进，了解销售团队如何将 ChatGPT for Sales 投入使用。

### 开始使用

安装 Sales 插件以开始使用，并了解有关 ChatGPT for Sales 和合作伙伴插件的更多信息。合作伙伴插件和功能的可用性因计划、区域和工作区设置而异。

ChatGPT 商业和企业管理员可以通过打开管理控制台、选择您的工作区并选择插件来为您的团队启用 ChatGPT for Sales。使销售插件和相关合作伙伴插件可供成员安装，或者默认为您的团队安装它们。查看对所需应用程序的访问权限以及它们可以使用的操作。工作区成员可以在出现提示时完成任何所需的帐户连接。

我们将继续围绕销售团队每天所做的工作构建 ChatGPT for Sales 和合作伙伴插件生态系统。我们的目标是将更多此类工作引入 ChatGPT，通过互联工具和客户环境，从寻找机会到准备对话并进行后续操作。

The new Sales plugin from OpenAI gives you ready-to-use workflows for everyday sales work, from deciding which accounts to pursue to preparing for a call and drafting the follow-up. Sales teams work best when everyone has a shared understanding of the customer. Which accounts are worth pursuing? What does a buyer need to move forward? Which deals need attention, and why? Bringing that information together gives teams more time to make informed decisions and follow through on customer commitments. That starts with the work you do every day.

Prepare quotes and agreements. Bring in Docusign, Ironclad, PandaDoc, or ServiceNow CPQ to help prepare quotes and agreements when a buyer is ready to move forward.

You can also keep work moving between conversations by delegating to your dot —an always-on agent in ChatGPT. Your dot can use these same plugins and customer context to prepare meeting briefs, track deal updates, and proactively bring you relevant changes and proposed next steps for review.

title: China taps US AI models to train homegrown rivals as chip curbs bite

inline_images.caption_en: The words "AI Artificial Intelligence" and a keyboard in this illustration taken October 19, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Dado Ruvic)
inline_images.caption_zh: “AI 人工智能”键盘概念示意图。(摄影：路透社/Dado Ruvic)

author: Reuters
article_content:
Chinese entities are adopting increasingly sophisticated ways to use output from leading American AI models to train domestic competitors, as Beijing seeks workarounds to tightening US curbs on advanced chips.

A Reuters review of more than 300 Chinese academic papers, patents, corporate disclosures, recruitment notices and government documents from the past year revealed the scale of the practice, which has moved from the laboratory to mainstream industrial use.

The records describe Chinese researchers using US models to produce answers to questions, build computer code and find solutions to complex problems, and using that output to teach and train domestic rivals.

The documents also show that Beijing is encouraging distillation to make AI cheaper and easier to deploy across China's massive manufacturing sector.

Distillation is not illegal and is prevalent in other parts of the world. While the process cannot reproduce a leading model's full capabilities or entirely replace heavy computing power, it helps developers retain important skills in smaller, cheaper systems.

China's broadening use of distillation could undercut the effectiveness of US curbs on the sale of advanced semiconductors, especially graphics processing units (GPUs) made by US chip giant Nvidia.

Distillation is also a source of friction between the world's two biggest economies ahead of the November 19-20 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen.

US authorities publicly accused Chinese companies in September of aggressive, targeted distillation of US models to bridge Beijing's computing power gap.

And at meetings in Chengdu in July, US Commerce Department officials raised concerns with Chinese regulators and tech executives about companies in China distilling American models, two people familiar with the discussions said.

Chinese officials defended distillation as a standard AI-development technique and said they were open to discussing the issue, one person said.

The US Commerce Department and China's Cyberspace Administration did not respond to requests for comment.

Distillation involves a powerful 'teacher' model generating answers or demonstrating how to complete a task, while a smaller 'student' model learns to mimic the teacher's outputs and reasoning processes.

For Chinese developers facing constraints on computing power, the attraction is in making one expensive request to a foreign model to produce data that can then train domestic models multiple times at much lower cost.

In a November 2024 paper, Shanghai Jiao Tong University researchers described selecting about 5,000 questions answered by OpenAI's GPT-4o, converting the answers into data points, and using them to train a domestic model for complex reasoning.

The researchers also cautioned that excessive reliance on distillation could stifle original innovation, writing that it "might result in the model learning to mimic rather than truly understand".

The project illustrated how American model output can become reusable data, allowing developers to improve capabilities while spending far less on training.

Alibaba researchers described a more systematic approach in an April 2025 paper, using OpenAI's GPT-4o to generate answers for training data, and then deploying a verification system to check the quality of that data.

In a February 2026 paper, researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Chinese food-delivery giant Meituan wrote of using GPT-4o and Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet to train a multi-modal model to handle complex visual and textual information.

Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Alibaba and Meituan did not respond to requests for comment.

Among leading American AI companies, OpenAI's terms restrict using its output to develop competing models. Anthropic's terms say outputs cannot be used to create products that compete with its services.

A US official familiar with the July Chengdu regulatory discussions said Washington believes industrial distillation of American models on this scale goes beyond normal developer activity.

Two people familiar with Chinese developers' operations disputed that assessment, saying distillation is common practice across the global AI industry and that developers follow international standards.

Chinese government documents do not instruct companies to distil American models but encourage distillation to make AI technology affordable and scalable for manufacturing and services.

A national AI+Manufacturing policy package published by eight Chinese government agencies in January explicitly prioritised using distillation to develop lightweight, industry-specific AI models.

The policies reflect Beijing's ambition to deploy smaller, cheaper AI systems across industries.

Concerned by distillation's growing geopolitical sensitivities, Chinese AI developers have in recent months asked Beijing to provide clearer guidance on the practice.

China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to a request for comment.

article_content_zh:
随着中国积极寻求突破美国不断收紧的先进芯片限制措施，中国各机构与企业正在采用日益精细复杂的技术手段，借助顶尖美国人工智能大模型的输出数据来训练本土竞争模型。

路透社对过去一年中 300 多份中国学术论文、专利申请、企业披露、招聘启事及政府文件的系统审阅显示，该做法在全行业已具备相当规模，并已从早期学术实验室研究全面迈向主流工业化应用。

相关文献详细记录了中国科研人员如何利用美国先进模型生成问题答案、编写计算机代码并求解复杂任务，随后将这些高价值输出作为训练数据集，用来指导和训练本土对标模型。

审阅的文件还显示，中国政府正在积极鼓励推广模型蒸馏技术，以降低 AI 应用成本，并加速其在庞大制造业基础中的广泛铺开。

模型蒸馏本身并不属于违法行为，且在世界其他地区的 AI 研发中亦广泛存在。尽管这一过程无法完全复制顶尖大模型的全部综合能力，也不能彻底摆脱对高算力硬件的需求，但它能帮助开发者将关键智能技能浓缩并保留在体积更小、部署成本显著更低的轻量化系统中。

中国对模型蒸馏的日益普及，可能会在一定程度上削弱美国限制先进半导体出口措施的实际效果，尤其是对美国芯片巨头英伟达（Nvidia）制造的图形处理芯片（GPU）的限售令。

在 11 月 19 日至 20 日于深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会前夕，蒸馏技术的使用也已成为世界两大经济体之间新的地缘摩擦焦点。

美国有关部门在 9 月份曾公开指责中国企业对美国先进模型进行“激进且具有针对性”的蒸馏训练，以弥补其面临的算力供给缺口。

据两位知情人士透露，在今年 7 月于成都举行的闭门会议上，美国商务部官员曾就中国企业蒸馏美国模型的问题，直接向中国监管部门及科技界高管表达了严正关切。

一名知情人士表示，中方官员当时为蒸馏技术进行了辩护，指出这是国际通行的标准 AI 研发手段，并表示愿就相关议题保持开放沟通。

美国商务部和中国国家互联网信息办公室均未回应路透社的置评请求。

模型蒸馏的基本原理在于：由能力强大的“教师模型”（Teacher Model）生成答案或示范复杂任务的求解路径，而体积较小的“学生模型”（Student Model）则学习模仿教师模型的输出逻辑与推理链路。

对于面临严苛算力瓶颈的中国开发者而言，这种模式的核心吸引力在于：只需向境外先进模型发起一次成本高昂的高质量查询请求，生成的精准数据即可被反复用于低成本训练本土多套模型。

在 2024 年 11 月发表的一篇学术论文中，上海交通大学的研究人员描述了他们如何筛选出由 OpenAI 旗下 GPT-4o 回答的约 5,000 个复杂问题，将其转化为结构化数据，并用于训练专注于复杂推理的本土模型。

研究人员在论文中同时警示，过度依赖蒸馏技术可能会在一定程度上抑制自主原创性创新，并写道这种方式“可能导致模型仅学会机械模仿而非真正理解”。

该项目清晰展现了美国大模型的输出如何被转化为可反复重用的数据资产，从而帮助开发者在大幅缩减算力开销的同时快速提升模型性能。

阿里巴巴的研究人员在 2025 年 4 月的一篇论文中介绍了一种更为系统化的工程方案：使用 GPT-4o 生成大量候选训练数据，随后部署专用的自动化质检系统对数据质量进行多维度校验过滤。

在 2026 年 2 月的一篇研究论文中，来自上海交通大学与中国本地生活配送巨头美团的研究人员，记述了如何结合 GPT-4o 与 Anthropic 的 Claude 3.5 Sonnet，共同训练一个能够处理复杂图文多模态任务的小型垂直模型。

上海交通大学、阿里巴巴与美团均未回应置评请求。

在几家主要的美国顶尖 AI 公司中，OpenAI 的用户服务条款明确禁止将其输出数据用于开发与之竞争的模型；Anthropic 的服务条款亦规定，不得利用其输出创建与其现有产品相竞争的竞品服务。

一名熟悉 7 月成都监管讨论情况的美国官员表示，华盛顿方面认为，中方目前在此种规模上进行的工业化模型蒸馏，已经超出了常规开发者的技术探索范畴。

两位熟悉中国开发者实际运作的业内人士对美方评估提出异议，指出蒸馏在整个全球 AI 产业中属于普遍且成熟的技术手段，中国团队的研发实践完全符合国际通行技术标准。

官方指导文件并未直接指示企业蒸馏特定美国模型，但明确鼓励通过蒸馏等模型轻量化路径，使人工智能技术以更经济可行的成本广泛赋能制造业与现代服务业。

今年 1 月由八部门联合印发的“人工智能+制造”专项政策指南中，明确将基于蒸馏技术研发轻量化、垂直行业专属 AI 模型列为优先支持方向。

这些政策充分映射出北京推动轻量化、高性价比 AI 系统深入赋能实体产业各细分赛道的战略意图。

出于对蒸馏技术面临的地缘政治敏感性上升的担忧，部分中国 AI 开发机构近几个月来已主动向有关部门寻求关于该项研发实践更明确的合规指引。

中国工业和信息化部未回应置评请求。

上海交通大学、阿里巴巴与美团均未回应置评请求。
在几家主要的美国顶尖 AI 公司中，OpenAI 的用户服务条款明确禁止将其输出数据用于开发与之竞争的模型；Anthropic 的服务条款亦规定，不得利用其输出创建与其现有产品相竞争的竞品服务。
一名熟悉 7 月成都监管讨论情况的美国官员表示，华盛顿方面认为，中方目前在此种规模上进行的工业化模型蒸馏，已经超出了常规开发者的技术探索范畴。
两位熟悉中国开发者实际运作的业内人士对美方评估提出异议，指出蒸馏在整个全球 AI 产业中属于普遍且成熟的技术手段，中国团队的研发实践完全符合国际通行技术标准。
官方指导文件并未直接指示企业蒸馏特定美国模型，但明确鼓励通过蒸馏等模型轻量化路径，使人工智能技术以更经济可行的成本广泛赋能制造业与现代服务业。
今年 1 月由八部门联合印发的“人工智能+制造”专项政策指南中，明确将基于蒸馏技术研发轻量化、垂直行业专属 AI 模型列为优先支持方向。
这些政策充分映射出北京推动轻量化、高性价比 AI 系统深入赋能实体产业各细分赛道的战略意图。
出于对蒸馏技术面临的地缘政治敏感性上升的担忧，部分中国 AI 开发机构近几个月来已主动向有关部门寻求关于该项研发实践更明确的合规指引。
中国工业和信息化部未回应置评请求。
article_content_en:
Chinese entities are adopting increasingly sophisticated ways to use output from leading American AI models to train domestic competitors, as Beijing seeks workarounds to tightening US curbs on advanced chips.

A Reuters review of more than 300 Chinese academic papers, patents, corporate disclosures, recruitment notices and government documents from the past year revealed the scale of the practice, which has moved from the laboratory to mainstream industrial use.

The records describe Chinese researchers using US models to produce answers to questions, build computer code and find solutions to complex problems, and using that output to teach and train domestic rivals.

The documents also show that Beijing is encouraging distillation to make AI cheaper and easier to deploy across China's massive manufacturing sector.

Distillation is not illegal and is prevalent in other parts of the world. While the process cannot reproduce a leading model's full capabilities or entirely replace heavy computing power, it helps developers retain important skills in smaller, cheaper systems.

China's broadening use of distillation could undercut the effectiveness of US curbs on the sale of advanced semiconductors, especially graphics processing units (GPUs) made by US chip giant Nvidia.

Distillation is also a source of friction between the world's two biggest economies ahead of the November 19-20 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen.

US authorities publicly accused Chinese companies in September of aggressive, targeted distillation of US models to bridge Beijing's computing power gap.

And at meetings in Chengdu in July, US Commerce Department officials raised concerns with Chinese regulators and tech executives about companies in China distilling American models, two people familiar with the discussions said.

Chinese officials defended distillation as a standard AI-development technique and said they were open to discussing the issue, one person said.

The US Commerce Department and China's Cyberspace Administration did not respond to requests for comment.

Distillation involves a powerful 'teacher' model generating answers or demonstrating how to complete a task, while a smaller 'student' model learns to mimic the teacher's outputs and reasoning processes.

For Chinese developers facing constraints on computing power, the attraction is in making one expensive request to a foreign model to produce data that can then train domestic models multiple times at much lower cost.

In a November 2024 paper, Shanghai Jiao Tong University researchers described selecting about 5,000 questions answered by OpenAI's GPT-4o, converting the answers into data points, and using them to train a domestic model for complex reasoning.

The researchers also cautioned that excessive reliance on distillation could stifle original innovation, writing that it "might result in the model learning to mimic rather than truly understand".

The project illustrated how American model output can become reusable data, allowing developers to improve capabilities while spending far less on training.

Alibaba researchers described a more systematic approach in an April 2025 paper, using OpenAI's GPT-4o to generate answers for training data, and then deploying a verification system to check the quality of that data.

In a February 2026 paper, researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Chinese food-delivery giant Meituan wrote of using GPT-4o and Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet to train a multi-modal model to handle complex visual and textual information.

Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Alibaba and Meituan did not respond to requests for comment.

Among leading American AI companies, OpenAI's terms restrict using its output to develop competing models. Anthropic's terms say outputs cannot be used to create products that compete with its services.

A US official familiar with the July Chengdu regulatory discussions said Washington believes industrial distillation of American models on this scale goes beyond normal developer activity.

Two people familiar with Chinese developers' operations disputed that assessment, saying distillation is common practice across the global AI industry and that developers follow international standards.

Chinese government documents do not instruct companies to distil American models but encourage distillation to make AI technology affordable and scalable for manufacturing and services.

A national AI+Manufacturing policy package published by eight Chinese government agencies in January explicitly prioritised using distillation to develop lightweight, industry-specific AI models.

The policies reflect Beijing's ambition to deploy smaller, cheaper AI systems across industries.

Concerned by distillation's growing geopolitical sensitivities, Chinese AI developers have in recent months asked Beijing to provide clearer guidance on the practice.

China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to a request for comment.

title: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC GPU with 'record number of CUDA cores' at Supercomputing 2026 — new chip accelerates agentic HPC workloads, arrives in 2028
title_en: Nvidia announces Rubin HPC GPU with 'record number of CUDA cores' at Supercomputing 2026 — new chip accelerates agentic HPC workloads, arrives in 2028
author: Jeffrey Kampman
article_content:
The Supercomputing 2026 conference is under way, and despite continuing turmoil elsewhere in the company, Nvidia has lots to reveal at the show. Foremost among its announcements today, Nvidia took the wraps off a new member of the Rubin GPU family called Rubin HPC, a chip that the company says is meant to accelerate agentic workflows and simulation for scientists, engineers, and analysts working with large data sets.

To accelerate those most demanding workloads, Nvidia says Rubin HPC has the highest number of CUDA cores on any of its GPUs - "more than 50,000" - which might imply that this chip uses a configuration similar to the four-die Rubin Ultra GPU, which links those dies together using NVLink-C2C.

Today's Rubin GPU has 224 SMs and 28,672 CUDA cores, so scaling compute resources to the degree Rubin HPC does would necessarily require more dies on a package. Nvidia didn't reveal more details of the chip's physical layout alongside the announcement. (The representative image shared by the company wouldn't appear to take this into account.)

To keep data moving between Rubin HPC GPUs, Nvidia will use its NVLink 7 interconnect. The company didn't share any new details of the bandwidth or physical layer of this interconnect within the rack, but past disclosures about the tech have indicated that it retains the 3.6 TB/s of per-GPU bandwidth that NVLink 6 delivers while enlarging the size of its scale-up domain.

Nvidia didn't share any details of the Rubin HPC GPU's HBM capacity or bandwidth, and it also didn't share whether this part includes a rebalancing of compute resources towards native FP64, as AMD and Intel are touting at the conference with their own GPUs this week.

Nvidia instead touts the suitability of this chip for scientists and engineers using agentic workflows, for which the company expects faster simulation performance and therefore faster opportunities for discovery in those fields thanks to better agent performance in those domains.

In fields like climate research, genomic analysis, and financial simulation, Nvidia says the Rubin HPC GPU's "balanced design," with both higher compute resources and (presumably) faster data movement between nodes, will help feed the chip with the massive data sets typical of those workloads, minimizing idle compute resources and achieving better utilization.

Researchers, engineers, and analysts marshaling agent swarms to explore the problem spaces in their domains will also be able to take advantage of Nvidia's CUDA-X domain-specific libraries to boost performance on Rubin HPC, tightening the reasoning loop from hypothesis to simulation to refinement and hastening the pursuit of the most promising results.

Nvidia says Rubin HPC will arrive sometime in 2028.

article_content_zh:
超级计算 2026 大会正在进行中，尽管公司其他部门持续动荡，英伟达还是在展会上透露了很多内容。在今天发布的公告中，Nvidia 揭开了 Rubin GPU 系列的新成员 Rubin HPC 的面纱，该公司表示，该芯片旨在加速处理大型数据集的科学家、工程师和分析师的代理工作流程和模拟。

为了加速那些要求最苛刻的工作负载，Nvidia 表示 Rubin HPC 在其所有 GPU 上拥有最多的 CUDA 核心数量——“超过 50,000 个”——这可能意味着该芯片使用类似于四芯片 Rubin Ultra GPU 的配置，后者使用 NVLink-C2C 将这些芯片连接在一起。

如今的 Rubin GPU 拥有 224 个 SM 和 28,672 个 CUDA 核心，因此将计算资源扩展到 Rubin HPC 所需的程度必然需要在封装上使用更多芯片。英伟达在发布公告的同时并未透露该芯片物理布局的更多细节。 （该公司分享的代表性图片似乎没有考虑到这一点。）

为了保持数据在 Rubin HPC GPU 之间移动，Nvidia 将使用其 NVLink 7 互连。该公司没有透露机架内这种互连的带宽或物理层的任何新细节，但过去有关该技术的披露表明，它保留了 NVLink 6 提供的 3.6 TB/s 的每 GPU 带宽，同时扩大了其扩展域的大小。

Nvidia 没有透露 Rubin HPC GPU 的 HBM 容量或带宽的任何细节，也没有透露这部分是否包括针对本机 FP64 的计算资源重新平衡，正如 AMD 和英特尔在本周的会议上用自己的 GPU 宣传的那样。

相反，英伟达宣称该芯片非常适合使用代理工作流程的科学家和工程师，该公司期望更快的模拟性能，并且由于这些领域中更好的代理性能，因此在这些领域有更快的发现机会。

Nvidia 表示，在气候研究、基因组分析和金融模拟等领域，Rubin HPC GPU 的“平衡设计”具有更高的计算资源和（可能）节点之间更快的数据移动，将有助于为芯片提供这些工作负载中典型的海量数据集，从而最大限度地减少闲置计算资源并实现更好的利用率。

研究人员、工程师和分析师通过编组代理群来探索其领域中的问题空间，也将能够利用 Nvidia 的 CUDA-X 特定领域库来提高 Rubin HPC 的性能，收紧从假设到模拟到细化的推理循环，并加快对最有希望的结果的追求。

Nvidia 表示 Rubin HPC 将于 2028 年某个时候推出。

title: US releases details of Megaspeed probe, says investigation began in 2024
title_en: US releases details of Megaspeed probe, says investigation began in 2024

inline_images.caption_zh: 新加坡大型企业 Megaspeed 注册办公地址所在的新加坡海洋金融中心大厦。(摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: US releases details of Megaspeed probe, says investigation began in 2024

author: Reuters
article_content:
WASHINGTON, Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Commerce Department and Justice Department released information on Sunday about an investigation into Singapore-based company Megaspeed, saying the probe began in 2024.

Megaspeed has come under scrutiny after reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang stepped down following an investigation that found a Singaporean executive at the company, Alice Huang, had ties to Chinese intelligence.

Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia on November 12 and Reuters has not been able to reach him for comment. Alice Huang has denied the allegations.

"After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential export control violations, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024," the Commerce Department and Justice Department said in a joint statement.

In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia about its dealings with Megaspeed, according to the statement.

US agents, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted search operations at multiple locations associated with Megaspeed in Singapore, and at an affiliated data centre site in Newark, California, the statement said.

Following the enforcement action, the Justice Department took the lead role in a criminal investigation with support from the Department of Commerce, it said.

The statement said that while US agencies typically did not comment on ongoing investigations, they were doing so now to provide clarity and to prevent the spread of inaccurate information.

US AND SINGAPORE DISCUSSIONS ON MEGASPEED

Megaspeed said on Sunday that Alice Huang officially left the company on August 31, 2025, but was suspended as chief executive officer on July 10, 2025.

Singapore's government said on Monday it had agreed to continue discussions with the US after Washington released the details of its Megaspeed investigation.

It said last week that Alice Huang had previously worked as the company's chief marketing officer, and then as chief executive officer, before stepping down in August 2025.

Police found insufficient evidence that she had committed offenses relating to spying or the theft of trade secrets, it said.

The city-state has barred her from re-entering Singapore, while investigations into Megaspeed and its dealings continue, the Singapore government said.

Several news organizations, including the New York Times, have reported that US intelligence agencies concluded Alice Huang had links to the Chinese government.

Reuters has not been able to verify any of the allegations made in the New York Times or other reports.

US intelligence agencies are still trying to determine her relationship with Chinese intelligence, according to two people briefed on the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.

Evidence gathered so far indicated she was probably an intelligence asset, someone who provides information to an intelligence service, rather than a trained intelligence officer, they said.

Beijing has rejected allegations that Alice Huang is a spy.

article_content_zh:
华盛顿，11月16日（路透社）- 美国商务部与司法部周日联合公布了针对新加坡公司 Megaspeed 的调查细节，证实该项调查早在 2024 年就已启动。

在有报道披露英伟达（Nvidia）前首席执行官黄仁勋因一项调查而辞职后，Megaspeed 受到了严格审查。该调查发现该公司一名新加坡籍高管黄秀媛（Alice Huang）与中国情报机构存在关联。

黄仁勋已于 11 月 12 日从英伟达辞职，路透社未能联系到他置评。黄秀媛则对相关指控予以否认。

美商务部和司法部在联合声明中表示：“通过对潜在出口管制违规行为的主动监测发现可疑活动后，商务部于 2024 年正式对 Megaspeed 启动了调查。”

声明指出，2025 年 5 月，商务部调查人员向英伟达调取了其与 Megaspeed 往来业务的相关记录。

声明称，美国执法人员联合新加坡执法部门，对 Megaspeed 在新加坡的多处关联地点以及位于加利福尼亚州纽瓦克市的一处关联数据中心执行了联合搜查。

在采取执法行动之后，司法部在商务部的全力支持下主导展开了刑事调查。

联合声明还强调，尽管美国政府机构通常不对正在进行的调查发表评论，但此次通报旨在澄清事实，防止不准确信息的扩散。

美新两国就 MEGASPEED 展开高级别磋商

Megaspeed 周日表示，黄秀媛已于 2025 年 8 月 31 日正式离开公司，但早在 2025 年 7 月 10 日就已被暂停首席执行官职务。

在华盛顿公布调查细节后，新加坡政府周一表示，已同意与美方就此案继续进行双边磋商。

新方上周表示，黄秀媛此前曾担任该公司首席营销官，随后升任首席执行官，直至 2025 年 8 月正式离职。

新加坡警方此前调查认为，尚无充分证据表明她触犯了与间谍活动或窃取商业机密相关的罪行。

新加坡政府同时表示，已禁止黄秀媛再次入境新加坡，而对 Megaspeed 及其业务往来的调查仍在持续进行。

包括《纽约时报》在内的多家新闻媒体报道称，美国情报机构认定黄秀媛与中国政府部门存在联系。

路透社目前尚无法独立核实《纽约时报》或其他媒体报道中所提及的指控细节。

据两位听取了相关案情通报但不愿具名的知情人士透露，美国情报机构目前仍在评估她与中国情报部门的具体关系。

他们表示，迄今为止搜集到的证据表明，她更可能是一名向情报机构提供信息的“情报资产”，而非经过专业训练的情报官员。

北京方面坚决否认了有关黄秀媛从事间谍活动的指控。

title: Amazon’s $17bn Ohio AI data centre bet threatened by voter backlash
title_en: Amazon’s $17bn Ohio AI data centre bet threatened by voter backlash

inline_images.caption: Amazon has invested billions of dollars in Ohio and committed to making it one of several data centre hubs across the US in a bid to service huge AI demand © Doral Chenoweth/USA Today Network via Reuters
inline_images.alt: Amazon has invested billions of dollars in Ohio and committed to making it one of several data centre hubs across the US in a bid to service huge AI demand © Doral Chenoweth/USA Today Network via Reuters

inline_images.caption: Ohio voters backed 21 ballot measures aimed at slowing data centre development in the state © David Maxwell/AFP via Getty Images
inline_images.alt: Ohio voters backed 21 ballot measures aimed at slowing data centre development in the state © David Maxwell/AFP via Getty Images

author: Rafe Rosner-Uddin
article_content:
Amazon’s multibillion-dollar bet on turning Ohio into an AI data centre hub is at risk after the state’s voters backed measures to stall development, threatening to derail more than $17bn in planned investment.

The cloud giant has emerged as one of the largest corporate casualties of a backlash against the US data centre boom, with three of its proposed projects impacted by restrictions approved during November’s midterm elections, according to FT research and data from regulatory tracking platform Regbase.

Ohio was the centre of specific ballot measures against data centres, with voters backing 21 initiatives to slow down development in the state. Several proposals directly targeted Amazon developments. Across the country, a further 19 such measures went in the same direction last week.

The affected Amazon projects were expected to consume roughly 1.8 gigawatts of power and account for approximately $17bn in planned spending by the company in the region, according to filings. The spending figure excludes chips and other equipment to fill these data centres. While other so-called hyperscalers such as Meta and Microsoft were also impacted by this month’s ballot measures across the US, the moves in Ohio meant Amazon is the most visibly impacted cloud computing giant.

“Amazon is going to have an uphill battle if they want to get these sites developed,” said Natalie Aresta-Katz, founder of Regbase. “They will have to find ways to convince communities to let them in or find another place to build.”

Amazon is racing to bring computing capacity online, having committed to spend the bulk of its planned $220bn in capital expenditure on AI infrastructure. It has invested billions of dollars in Ohio and committed to making it one of several data centre hubs across the US in a bid to service huge AI demand, with plans to invest $23bn in the state by 2030.

But Nick Owens, a lifelong Republican and co-founder of Conserve Ohio, a grassroots movement behind several ballot measures, said that voters had been angered by opacity around data centre projects.

“I don’t know how you can say that this is going to be a community partnership if people are completely in the dark about what’s going on,” he said.

Local residents are continuing to oppose a $4bn Amazon development in Wilmington, Ohio, with the potential for further legal challenge, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Prologis, a real estate company developing a site for Amazon in Trenton, filed a suit last Thursday challenging recent ballot measures.

The FT and Regbase analysed local permit documents for developments in dozens of counties across the US to determine how many projects were now threatened with delays or cancellation. The bulk of measures passed impact sites not yet under construction, while some measures threaten to delay development.

Nearly a dozen sites impacted by ballot measures last week did not disclose the end tenant for the project. The measures across the US impacted at least 10 gigawatts of proposed data centre capacity, according to figures compiled from public statements, hearings and local planning documents.Campaigners have challenged vast AI developments on environmental and social grounds, raising concerns around rising air and noise pollution.

Three sites across Maine and Ohio had already seen developers abandon data centre projects earlier this year after ballot measures were approved for the November poll, according to Regbase data.

“Voters do not believe that they can trust these companies to regulate themselves . . .[Big tech’s] response thus far has been symbolic and performative,” said Alli Finn, an organiser at the AI Now Institute. Big Tech companies have tried to respond to the concerns around data centres. Microsoft in March said it would stop using non-disclosure agreements with local officials around data centre projects, in response to local concern about a lack of information around the sites. Amazon and Google followed suit in October, while OpenAI said it would do so in the wake of the midterm results.

The companies have also made commitments around energy and water consumption alongside setting out billions of dollars in community-oriented investments. Amazon said: “We remain committed to setting a high bar for responsible data centre development, continuing to engage communities early in our development process, and delivering capacity for our customers.” Microsoft declined to comment. Meta did not respond to a request for comment.

title_zh: 亚马逊（Amazon）在俄亥俄州投资170亿美元的人工智能数据中心项目受到选民反对的威胁
summary_zh: 亚马逊在俄亥俄州规划的170亿美元数据中心投资，因州内多项针对性基建限制提案通过而面临开发停滞风险
article_content_zh:
在俄亥俄州选民支持阻碍发展的措施后，亚马逊斥资数十亿美元将俄亥俄州打造成人工智能数据中心的赌注面临风险，这可能导致超过 170 亿美元的投资计划脱轨。

根据英国《金融时报》的研究和监管跟踪平台 Regbase 的数据，这家云巨头已成为美国数据中心繁荣的强烈抵制中最大的企业受害者之一，其拟议的三个项目受到 11 月中期选举期间批准的限制的影响。

俄亥俄州是反对数据中心的具体投票措施的中心，选民支持了 21 项减缓该州发展的举措。有几项提案直接针对亚马逊的发展。上周，全国范围内又采取了 19 项此类措施。

根据备案文件，受影响的亚马逊项目预计将消耗约1.8吉瓦的电力，并约占该公司在该地区的计划支出170亿美元。该支出额不包括用于填充这些数据中心的芯片和其他设备。虽然Meta和微软等其他所谓的超大规模企业也受到了本月美国各地公投措施的影响，但俄亥俄州的举措意味着亚马逊是受影响最明显的云计算巨头。

但终身共和党人、保护俄亥俄州联合创始人尼克·欧文斯表示，数据中心项目的不透明激怒了选民。该组织是多项投票措施背后的草根运动。

他说：“如果人们对正在发生的事情完全一无所知，我不知道你怎么能说这将是一种社区伙伴关系。”

据两位知情人士透露，当地居民继续反对亚马逊在俄亥俄州威尔明顿耗资 40 亿美元的开发项目，这可能会引发进一步的法律挑战。

Prologis 是一家在特伦顿为亚马逊开发网站的房地产公司，上周四提起诉讼，质疑最近的投票措施。

英国《金融时报》和 Regbase 分析了美国数十个县的当地开发许可文件，以确定目前有多少项目面临延误或取消的威胁。大部分措施都通过了尚未建设的影响场地，而一些措施则可能会推迟开发。

上周受投票措施影响的近十几个地点没有透露该项目的最终租户。根据公开声明、听证会和当地规划文件汇总的数据，美国各地的这些措施影响了至少 10 吉瓦的拟议数据中心容量。活动人士在环境和社会方面对人工智能的巨大发展提出了挑战，引发了人们对空气和噪音污染加剧的担忧。

根据 Regbase 的数据，今年早些时候，在 11 月份的投票措施获得批准后，缅因州和俄亥俄州的三个站点已经看到开发商放弃了数据中心项目。

AI Now Institute 的组织者艾莉·芬恩 (Alli Finn) 表示：“选民不相信他们可以信任这些公司能够自我监管……到目前为止，[大型科技公司]的反应只是象征性的和表演性的。”大型科技公司试图回应围绕数据中心的担忧。微软三月份表示，将停止与当地官员就数据中心项目签订保密协议，以回应当地对数据中心缺乏信息的担忧。亚马逊和谷歌在 10 月份也纷纷效仿，而 OpenAI 则表示将在中期业绩公布后这样做。

这些公司还就能源和水消耗做出了承诺，并提供了数十亿美元的面向社区的投资。亚马逊表示：“我们仍然致力于为负责任的数据中心开发设定高标准，在开发过程的早期继续让社区参与进来，并为我们的客户提供容量。”微软拒绝置评。 Meta 没有回应置评请求。

article_content_en:
Amazon’s multibillion-dollar bet on turning Ohio into an AI data centre hub is at risk after the state’s voters backed measures to stall development, threatening to derail more than $17bn in planned investment.

The cloud giant has emerged as one of the largest corporate casualties of a backlash against the US data centre boom, with three of its proposed projects impacted by restrictions approved during November’s midterm elections, according to FT research and data from regulatory tracking platform Regbase.

Ohio was the centre of specific ballot measures against data centres, with voters backing 21 initiatives to slow down development in the state. Several proposals directly targeted Amazon developments. Across the country, a further 19 such measures went in the same direction last week.

The affected Amazon projects were expected to consume roughly 1.8 gigawatts of power and account for approximately $17bn in planned spending by the company in the region, according to filings. The spending figure excludes chips and other equipment to fill these data centres. While other so-called hyperscalers such as Meta and Microsoft were also impacted by this month’s ballot measures across the US, the moves in Ohio meant Amazon is the most visibly impacted cloud computing giant.

“Amazon is going to have an uphill battle if they want to get these sites developed,” said Natalie Aresta-Katz, founder of Regbase. “They will have to find ways to convince communities to let them in or find another place to build.”

Amazon is racing to bring computing capacity online, having committed to spend the bulk of its planned $220bn in capital expenditure on AI infrastructure. It has invested billions of dollars in Ohio and committed to making it one of several data centre hubs across the US in a bid to service huge AI demand, with plans to invest $23bn in the state by 2030.

But Nick Owens, a lifelong Republican and co-founder of Conserve Ohio, a grassroots movement behind several ballot measures, said that voters had been angered by opacity around data centre projects.

“I don’t know how you can say that this is going to be a community partnership if people are completely in the dark about what’s going on,” he said.

Local residents are continuing to oppose a $4bn Amazon development in Wilmington, Ohio, with the potential for further legal challenge, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Prologis, a real estate company developing a site for Amazon in Trenton, filed a suit last Thursday challenging recent ballot measures.

The FT and Regbase analysed local permit documents for developments in dozens of counties across the US to determine how many projects were now threatened with delays or cancellation. The bulk of measures passed impact sites not yet under construction, while some measures threaten to delay development.

Nearly a dozen sites impacted by ballot measures last week did not disclose the end tenant for the project. The measures across the US impacted at least 10 gigawatts of proposed data centre capacity, according to figures compiled from public statements, hearings and local planning documents.Campaigners have challenged vast AI developments on environmental and social grounds, raising concerns around rising air and noise pollution.

Three sites across Maine and Ohio had already seen developers abandon data centre projects earlier this year after ballot measures were approved for the November poll, according to Regbase data.

“Voters do not believe that they can trust these companies to regulate themselves . . .[Big tech’s] response thus far has been symbolic and performative,” said Alli Finn, an organiser at the AI Now Institute. Big Tech companies have tried to respond to the concerns around data centres. Microsoft in March said it would stop using non-disclosure agreements with local officials around data centre projects, in response to local concern about a lack of information around the sites. Amazon and Google followed suit in October, while OpenAI said it would do so in the wake of the midterm results.

The companies have also made commitments around energy and water consumption alongside setting out billions of dollars in community-oriented investments. Amazon said: “We remain committed to setting a high bar for responsible data centre development, continuing to engage communities early in our development process, and delivering capacity for our customers.” Microsoft declined to comment. Meta did not respond to a request for comment.

title: Meta is testing Direct, a standalone messaging app for Instagram that doesn't require an existing Instagram account to use, in Thailand and Turkey (Karissa Bell/Engadget)
title_en: Meta is testing Direct, a standalone messaging app for Instagram that doesn't require an existing Instagram account to use, in Thailand and Turkey (Karissa Bell/Engadget)

inline_images.caption: Screenshots of a message thread in Direct.
inline_images.alt: Screenshots of a message thread in Direct.

author: Engadget
article_content:
It’s only available in Turkey and Thailand for now.

Meta Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Meta is working on a dedicated messaging app for Instagram that could also expand the reach of the app's DMs. The company is starting to test Direct, a new standalone app that brings Instagram's inbox to a separate app, but doesn't require an existing Instagram account to use. Direct will only be available in Thailand and Turkey for now, Meta said in an update.

Direct looks pretty similar to Instagram's inbox at first glance. It has an almost identical layout, with existing chats carrying over from the main app if you log in with your Instagram credentials. It even has some of the same personalization features, like the ability to set custom backgrounds for individual threads and Instagram's status update feature, Notes.

Meta says it's also bringing some of Instagram's safety features to Direct. The app won't allow people to start chats with accounts they aren't already connected with via their contacts. And parents will be able to monitor who their teen is chatting with and how much time they spend in the app if they use the company's parental control features. Additionally, Meta says it will "use technology to detect and act on potentially inappropriate interactions with young people," though it's vague about what exactly that will entail.

The test of Direct is an interesting move for Meta. Instagram head Adam Mosseri often notes that messaging is Instagram's most-used feature. But he was also reluctant to give Threads its own inbox because it seemed "redundant" to use multiple apps to reach the same people when Meta briefly considered bringing Instagram's inbox to Threads. He said at the time that mirroring the Instagram inbox could cause "notification routing weirdness" and generally seemed like a less than ideal experience for most people.

The app also raises questions about whether Direct would compete with WhatsApp in the countries where it's rolled out. It's unlikely an Instagram-centric app would replace WhatsApp for many people, but it could eat into that app's engagement if non-Instagram users can use Direct to message friends instead.

That may also be why Direct seems fairly limited for now. Meta describes it as a test that will only be available to people in Turkey and Thailand for the time being. But if the app is a success, it's likely the company will consider expanding it to more places.

title_zh: Meta在泰国与土耳其测试独立Instagram消息应用
summary_zh: Meta推出独立通讯应用Direct进行区域性测试，用户无需关联Instagram主账号即可实现社交连接
article_content_zh:
目前仅在土耳其和泰国提供。

Meta 在 Google 上添加 Engadget：首选来源 Google Discover Meta 正在开发一款专门用于 Instagram 的消息应用程序，该应用程序还可以扩大该应用程序 DM 的覆盖范围。该公司开始测试 Direct，这是一款新的独立应用程序，它将 Instagram 的收件箱带到一个单独的应用程序中，但不需要现有的 Instagram 帐户即可使用。 Meta 在更新中表示，Direct 目前仅在泰国和土耳其提供。

乍一看，Direct 与 Instagram 的收件箱非常相似。它具有几乎相同的布局，如果您使用 Instagram 凭据登录，现有的聊天记录将从主应用程序继承。它甚至还具有一些相同的个性化功能，例如为单个线程设置自定义背景的能力以及 Instagram 的状态更新功能“注释”。

Meta 表示，它还将 Instagram 的一些安全功能引入 Direct。该应用程序不允许人们与尚未通过联系人连接的帐户开始聊天。如果父母使用该公司的家长控制功能，他们将能够监控孩子正在与谁聊天以及他们在应用程序中花费了多少时间。此外，Meta 表示，它将“利用技术来检测与年轻人之间潜在的不当互动并采取行动”，尽管它并不清楚这到底意味着什么。

Direct的测试对Meta来说是一个有趣的举动。 Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 经常指出，消息传递是 Instagram 最常用的功能。但他也不愿意为 Threads 提供自己的收件箱，因为当 Meta 短暂考虑将 Instagram 的收件箱引入 Threads 时，使用多个应用程序来联系同一个人似乎“多余”。他当时表示，镜像 Instagram 收件箱可能会导致“通知路由怪异”，而且对于大多数人来说，这似乎并不是一种理想的体验。

该应用程序还引发了人们的疑问，即 Direct 是否会在其推出的国家与 WhatsApp 竞争。对于很多人来说，以 Instagram 为中心的应用程序不太可能取代 WhatsApp，但如果非 Instagram 用户可以使用 Direct 向朋友发送消息，那么它可能会削弱该应用程序的参与度。

这也可能是为什么 Direct 目前看起来相当有限的原因。 Meta将其描述为一项暂时仅适用于土耳其和泰国人的测试。但如果该应用程序取得成功，该公司可能会考虑将其扩展到更多地方。

title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos slashed software work to onboard AMD GPUs from up to 12 months to around three days —writing almost 100% of kernels autonomously chips away at Nvidia's CUDA moat
title_en: Anthropic says Claude Mythos slashed software work to onboard AMD GPUs from up to 12 months to around three days —writing almost 100% of kernels autonomously chips away at Nvidia's CUDA moat

inline_images.caption: (Image credit: Anthropic)
inline_images.caption_en: (Image credit: Anthropic)

author: Shane Downing
article_content:
Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to get its AI running on AMD’s GPUs in about three days, with “basically no human intervention,” a job it says used to take six to 12 months. The three days cover prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs “at a useful level of performance,” with Mythos porting or writing “almost 100% of the kernels.” That kind of low-level code, which ties an AI model to one company’s chips, has long been part of Nvidia’s CUDA moat, and an AI that can write it in days would suggest that moat is eroding.

Tom Brown, Anthropic’s co-founder and chief compute officer, made the time comparison, noting to investors that the original meant using a team of “dozens of engineers.” The company already runs its models on multiple kinds of chips — on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Google’s TPUs, and AWS Trainium — and its fleet is managed as “one fungible pool of compute.” Brown called the early multi-chip decision “an unconventional bet.” It may have been a wise one, given that Google’s TPUs can now natively run AI models built in PyTorch, and Meta uses them in production.

Anthropic's claim that the job used to take six to 12 months comes from past work, from its “historical experience bringing up new accelerators using traditional engineering approaches,” where tailoring the code to each hardware platform was a challenge. Removing that onboarding barrier could reduce things to a purchase decision, and Anthropic started working with AMD GPUs for the first time this year, with an agreement for up to 2 gigawatts now in place.

CUDA, Nvidia’s programming platform, is very mature at nearly two decades old. AMD has an equivalent, ROCm, with HIP as its programming layer. Code written for CUDA has to be transformed to work there, and AMD even built a tool called HIPify for the process. There is still a conversion cost to switching, and AMD’s vice president of AI software, Anush Elangovan, told EE Times in April that “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in.”

AMD has been making the argument that AI can write this type of code since August of last year, presenting a research agent that fell short of human experts at the time. In September of that year, AMD CEO Lisa Su said on the Possible podcast that much of AI software is written in CUDA, which needs to be “translated to AMD,” and “a ton of that can now be done in software.”

Moving forward to July earlier this year, AMD’s senior vice president of AI, Vamsi Boppana, said its engineers were using AI models to generate GPU kernels, and Su said that when she asked whether her team was helping the Anthropic engineer working on the MI355X, she was told they didn’t need any help. Boppana said that in some cases, the resulting kernels were even “better than the most manually tuned versions.” Under its July agreement with Anthropic, AMD is also using Claude to optimize workloads for its Instinct GPUs and to speed up ROCm development.

At AMD’s Advancing AI event in July, OpenAI’s Philippe Tillet said that once OpenAI got its Helios racks, a single engineer confirmed everything worked within a few days, and that “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers.” Before the event, AMD’s Andrew Dieckman, corporate vice president and general manager of the company’s data center GPU business, told reporters that he has had practically zero conversations with AMD’s customers about CUDA.

• Date: Aug. 1, 2025 | Who: AMD researchers | What they said or showed: Published GEAK, an AI agent that writes GPU kernels; against 30 expert-written kernels it got 19 right, at 0.92 times the experts’ speed on average | Where: AMD’s ROCm blog

• Date: Sept. 24, 2025 | Who: Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO | What they said or showed: Asked about AI coding tools, said much of the code written for CUDA can now be translated to AMD in software: “We’re using software to significantly optimize our customers’ code so that they can run on AMD” | Where: Possible podcast

• Date: April 1, 2026 | Who: Anush Elangovan, AMD vice president of AI software | What they said or showed: Compared Claude with HIPify, AMD’s tool for converting CUDA code: “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in” | Where: EE Times interview

• Date: April 15, 2026 | Who: Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO | What they said or showed: “We use a ton of AI to create the kernels that we have”; “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” | Where: Dwarkesh Patel interview

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Andrew Dieckman, AMD corporate vice president and general manager, data center GPU business | What they said or showed: “I have almost zero conversations with our customers about CUDA at this point in time” | Where: PC Gamer, from a pre-event AMD briefing

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Vamsi Boppana, AMD senior vice president of AI | What they said or showed: AI-assisted GPU programming will “remove any remaining barriers to broad adoption” | Where: AMD Advancing AI keynote

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Philippe Tillet, OpenAI | What they said or showed: “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers” | Where: AMD Advancing AI keynote

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | What they said or showed: One engineer asked Claude to bring up an MI355X rack and left it running “over the weekend” | Where: AMD Advancing AI keynote

• Date: Nov. 10, 2026 | Who: Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | What they said or showed: Mythos “got Claude running on AMD in just three days with basically no human intervention”; the slide footnote limits the three days to prompt processing for one model | Where: Anthropic’s IPO roadshow video

Until this week, though, all of this came from AMD or its stage, not from Anthropic to its own investors. Anthropic buys the chips rather than selling them, and it’s heading into its IPO next week, so its multi-chip approach — now with at least some numbers to back it up — carries more weight than a chipmaker’s claims. Its prospectus says it in writing, too, though without a number: “We can onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time it once took.”

• Where Anthropic said it: AMD’s Advancing AI keynote, July 23 | Who did the work: One engineer and Claude | How long: Not stated; left running “over the weekend” | What it covered: Its “leading model” on an MI355X rack, with performance climbing | What it replaced: What it called “a big effort”

• Where Anthropic said it: IPO roadshow video, narration, Nov. 10 | Who did the work: Mythos, with “basically no human intervention” | How long: Three days (“in just three days”) | What it covered: Getting “Claude running on AMD”; Claude “ported or wrote almost 100% of the kernels” | What it replaced: Work that “took dozens of engineers months”

• Where Anthropic said it: IPO roadshow video, slide footnote, Nov. 10 | Who did the work: Claude Mythos Preview | How long: About three days (“~3 day timeline”) | What it covered: Bringing up “prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs at a useful level of performance” | What it replaced: Six to 12 months (“~6-12-month estimate”), from “historical experience bringing up new accelerators”

• Where Anthropic said it: Prospectus (S-1/A No. 2), Nov. 10 | Who did the work: Its engineering teams, “leveraging Claude” | How long: No figure; “more quickly” | What it covered: Bringing “new chip platforms into production”; no chip named | What it replaced: What it calls “intense engineering effort over many months”

The prompt processing (prefill) part of the workload is the step where a model reads and processes what it’s been given before it starts replying, and Anthropic hasn’t said whether the replying step (decode) was included as well. Anthropic’s chart, with its axis labeled “Time to onboard new silicon,” shows both lines reaching the same “~100%” mark without saying 100% of what. The company also hasn’t said how fast the model ran on AMD’s GPUs versus Nvidia’s, and that’s the comparison we want to see to show whether AMD’s chips, running AI-written code, can match Nvidia silicon.

On the other hand, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in an April interview with Dwarkesh Patel that Nvidia already uses AI on its own kernels and knows its chips best — “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” — and can get the most out of them. Asked why labs like Anthropic use other accelerators, he called Anthropic “a unique instance, not a trend.” Nvidia and AMD, among seven companies, are buying $26.0 billion of Anthropic’s stock at the IPO price, so Nvidia is investing in the very company Huang called the exception.

In late July, SemiAnalysis published an article, “Can AMD break the CUDA Moat?,” which essentially said that software creation is not the same moat it was even a year ago. That said, the catch for AMD is that with agentic coding, “each agent requires GPUs to test their code against,” which means that the AI writing the code still needs the hardware. It has found a constant lack of GPUs inside AMD for this type of development, which has held AMD back and may be a new bottleneck.

That leaves CUDA’s moat somewhere in between. Getting a model running on a new chip, once the expensive part, appears to be getting cheaper, and better AI may wear down Nvidia’s claim that it knows its hardware best. As for Anthropic’s fungible pool, the chips in it aren’t fully interchangeable — Google’s TPUs are increasingly specialized, for example — and getting the most out of any of them still takes the hardware to test on. The moat is narrowing, but is not gone.

Anthropic’s first AMD MI450 chips, in Helios racks, are expected in the first half of 2027. That’s a new generation and an opportunity to see if the three-day bring-up can be repeated. Anthropic’s IPO comes sooner, after which it will report as a public company.

article_content_zh:
Anthropic 告诉 IPO 投资者，其 Claude Mythos Preview 模型在大约三天内完成了使其人工智能在 AMD GPU 上运行所需的软件工作，“基本上没有人工干预”，据称这项工作过去需要 6 到 12 个月的时间。这三天的内容是在 AMD MI355X GPU 上“以有用的性能水平”快速处理一个 Anthropic 模型，并通过 Mythos 移植或编写“几乎 100% 的内核”。这种将人工智能模型与一家公司的芯片联系起来的低级代码长期以来一直是 Nvidia CUDA 护城河的一部分，而能够在几天内编写出来的人工智能则表明护城河正在被侵蚀。

Anthropic 的联合创始人兼首席计算官汤姆·布朗 (Tom Brown) 进行了时间比较，他向投资者指出，最初意味着使用一个由“数十名工程师”组成的团队。该公司已经在多种芯片上运行其模型——Nvidia 和 AMD 的 GPU、谷歌的 TPU 和 AWS Trainium——并且其机群作为“一个可替代的计算池”进行管理。布朗称早期的多芯片决策是“一次非常规的赌注”。这可能是明智之举，因为谷歌的 TPU 现在可以本地运行 PyTorch 中构建的 AI 模型，并且 Meta 在生产中使用它们。

Anthropic 声称，这项工作过去需要 6 到 12 个月的时间，这来自过去的工作，来自其“使用传统工程方法开发新加速器的历史经验”，其中为每个硬件平台定制代码是一项挑战。消除这一入门障碍可能会减少购买决策的难度，Anthropic 今年首次开始与 AMD GPU 合作，目前已达成高达 2 吉瓦的协议。

CUDA 是 Nvidia 的编程平台，已有近二十年的历史，非常成熟。 AMD 有一个等效的 ROCm，以 HIP 作为其编程层。为 CUDA 编写的代码必须进行转换才能在那里工作，AMD 甚至为此过程构建了一个名为 HIPify 的工具。转换仍然存在转换成本，AMD 人工智能软件副总裁 Anush Elangovan 在 4 月份告诉《EE Times》，“Claude 比 HIPify 更好，因为它内置了网络搜索。”

自去年 8 月以来，AMD 一直在论证人工智能可以编写此类代码，并推出了当时达不到人类专家水平的研究代理。同年 9 月，AMD 首席执行官苏姿丰 (Lisa Su) 在Possible 播客上表示，大部分人工智能软件都是用 CUDA 编写的，需要“翻译成 AMD”，并且“现在很多工作都可以用软件来完成”。

今年 7 月初，AMD 人工智能高级副总裁 Vamsi Boppana 表示，其工程师正在使用人工智能模型生成 GPU 内核，Su 表示，当她询问她的团队是否正在帮助 Anthropic 工程师开发 MI355X 时，她被告知他们不需要任何帮助。 Boppana 表示，在某些情况下，生成的内核甚至“比大多数手动调整的版本更好”。根据 7 月份与 Anthropic 达成的协议，AMD 还使用 Claude 来优化其 Instinct GPU 的工作负载并加速 ROCm 开发。

在 7 月份的 AMD 高级人工智能活动中，OpenAI 的 Philippe Tillet 表示，一旦 OpenAI 拿到了 Helios 机架，一名工程师就在几天内确认一切正常，并且“从某种意义上说，代理正在接管我们的工作，就像内核工程师一样。”活动之前，AMD 公司副总裁兼公司数据中心 GPU 业务总经理 Andrew Dieckman 告诉记者，他与 AMD 客户关于 CUDA 的对话几乎为零。

• 日期：2026 年 7 月 23 日 |人物：Philippe Tillet，OpenAI |他们所说或表明的内容：“从某种意义上说，代理人正在接管我们的工作，就像核心工程师一样” |地点：AMD 推进人工智能主题演讲

• 日期：2026 年 7 月 23 日 |人物：Tom Brown，Anthropic 联合创始人兼首席计算官 |他们所说或展示的内容：一位工程师要求 Claude 拿出一个 MI355X 机架，并让它“整个周末”运行 |地点：AMD 推进人工智能主题演讲

• 日期：2026 年 11 月 10 日 |人物：Tom Brown，Anthropic 联合创始人兼首席计算官 |他们所说或展示的内容：Mythos“让 Claude 在短短三天内在 AMD 上运行，基本上没有人为干预”；幻灯片脚注限制了一个模型的三天提示处理时间|地点：Anthropic 的 IPO 路演视频

不过，直到本周，所有这些都来自 AMD 或其舞台，而不是来自 Anthropic 自己的投资者。 Anthropic 购买芯片而不是出售它们，而且该公司将于下周进行 IPO，因此其多芯片方法（现在至少有一些数据支持）比芯片制造商的声明更有分量。它的招股说明书也以书面形式表示，尽管没有具体数字：“我们可以用以前所用时间的一小部分来安装新的芯片平台。”

• Anthropic 所说的：AMD 的推进人工智能主题演讲，7 月 23 日 |谁完成了这项工作：一名工程师和克劳德 |多长时间：未说明； “周末”继续跑步 |涵盖内容：MI355X 机架上的“领先型号”，性能不断攀升 |它取代了什么：所谓的“巨大努力”

• Anthropic 所说的：IPO 路演视频，旁白，11 月 10 日 |谁做的工作：神话，“基本上没有人为干预” |多长时间：三天（“只需三天”）|内容：让“Claude 在 AMD 上运行”； Claude“移植或编写了几乎 100% 的内核”|它取代了什么：“花费了数十名工程师几个月”的工作

• Anthropic 所说的地方：IPO 路演视频，幻灯片脚注，11 月 10 日 |谁完成了这项工作：克劳德神话预览|时长：大约三天（“~3 天的时间表”）|内容：“在 AMD MI355X GPU 上以有用的性能水平快速处理一个 Anthropic 模型” |它所取代的内容：六到 12 个月（“~6-12 个月的估计”），来自“推出新加速器的历史经验”

• Anthropic 如此表述：招股说明书（S-1/A 第 2 号），11 月 10 日 |谁做了这项工作：它的工程团队，“利用克劳德” |多长时间：无数字； “更快”|内容：将“新芯片平台投入生产”；没有名为 | 的芯片它取代了什么：所谓的“数月的密集工程工作”

工作负载的提示处理（预填充）部分是模型在开始回复之前读取并处理所给内容的步骤，Anthropic 没有透露是否也包括回复步骤（解码）。 Anthropic 的图表的轴标记为“搭载新芯片的时间”，显示两条线都达到了相同的“~100%”标记，但没有说明 100% 是什么。该公司还没有透露该模型在 AMD 的 GPU 上与 Nvidia 的 GPU 上运行的速度有多快，这就是我们希望看到的比较，以显示运行人工智能编写的代码的 AMD 芯片是否可以与 Nvidia 的芯片相媲美。

另一方面，Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋在 4 月份接受 Dwarkesh Patel 采访时表示，Nvidia 已经在自己的内核上使用了人工智能，并且最了解自己的芯片——“没有人比我们更了解我们的架构”——并且可以充分利用它们。当被问及为什么像 Anthropic 这样的实验室使用其他加速器时，他称 Anthropic 是“一个独特的实例，而不是一种趋势”。 Nvidia 和 AMD 等七家公司正在以 IPO 价格购买 260 亿美元的 Anthropic 股票，因此 Nvidia 投资的正是黄黄所说的例外公司。

7 月下旬，SemiAnalysis 发表了一篇文章“AMD 能否打破 CUDA 护城河？”，该文章本质上是说，软件创建与一年前的护城河已经不一样了。也就是说，AMD 的问题在于，通过代理编码，“每个代理都需要 GPU 来测试其代码”，这意味着编写代码的人工智能仍然需要硬件。它发现AMD内部一直缺乏用于此类开发的GPU，这阻碍了AMD的发展，并可能成为新的瓶颈。

这使得 CUDA 的护城河介于两者之间。让模型在新芯片上运行，曾经是昂贵的部件，现在似乎变得越来越便宜，而更好的人工智能可能会削弱英伟达“最了解自己的硬件”的说法。至于 Anthropic 的可替代池，其中的芯片并不是完全可互换的——例如，谷歌的 TPU 越来越专业化——并且要充分利用其中任何一个仍然需要对硬件进行测试。护城河正在变窄，但并没有消失。

Anthropic 的首款 AMD MI450 芯片预计将于 2027 年上半年在 Helios 机架中上市。这是新一代芯片，也是一个看看是否可以重复为期三天的启动的机会。 Anthropic 的 IPO 会提前进行，之后它将作为一家上市公司进行报告。
