title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
title_en: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions

inline_images.caption: siri ai
inline_images.alt: siri ai

author: Andrew Liszewski
article_content:
Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.

Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models.

Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.

Instead of having to wait until midnight each day for your usage to reset, most of Apple’s existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) will include higher daily limits at their same price. The $2.99/month 200GB subscription includes 2x the usage, the $9.99/month 2TB plan includes 5x the usage, while the $29.99/month 6TB and $59.99 12TB/month options bump the usage limit to 10x and 20x, respectively. Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that’s used on a first come, first served basis.

Last week Apple updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for that app’s intelligent assistant through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that are expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.

Instead of having to wait until midnight each day for your usage to reset, most of Apple’s existing iCloud Plus plans (excluding the 50GB option) will include higher daily limits at their same price. The $2.99/month 200GB subscription includes 2x the usage, the $9.99/month 2TB plan includes 5x the usage, while the $29.99/month 6TB and $59.99 12TB/month options bump the usage limit to 10x and 20x, respectively. Family members sharing an iCloud Plus subscription will have a shared usage pool that’s used on a first come, first served basis.

Last week Apple updated Logic Pro with an option to “Buy More Usage” for that app’s intelligent assistant through $49.99 Intelligence Usage Packs that are expected to be added to other Apple Creator Studio apps this month, including Pixelmator Pro, Final Cut Pro, Motion, plus Pages, Keynote, and Numbers.

title: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines
title_en: OpenAI wants to stop deepfakes from overwhelming child abuse tiplines

inline_images.caption: STK155_OPEN_AI_CVirginia_C (1)
inline_images.alt: STK155_OPEN_AI_CVirginia_C (1)

author: Lauren Feiner
article_content:
OpenAI is announcing a tool that it says will help child sexual abuse investigators cut through the noise to find harmful material they can act on quickly.

At a Monday press briefing in Washington, DC, OpenAI announced a classifier it says can better detect abusive imagery of kids, including whether it’s AI-generated. It’s also offering free access to vetted organizations, giving developers more guidance on how to detect this type of content, and helping to train law enforcement on how AI can aid their investigations. The news comes as policymakers and others are pushing for more safety restrictions on AI tools, accusing OpenAI and other companies of facilitating harm to children.

In recent years, AI-generated sexual images of children have threatened to overwhelm systems like the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) CyberTipline, which collects and triages reports of child sexual abuse material (CSAM). The CyberTipline received 400,000 generative AI-related reports in 2025, an exponential increase from the 67,000 it received in 2024, and researchers have warned that the influx could make NCMEC’s workload “unmanageable.” The US government has stated that both AI-generated and non-AI-generated CSAM is illegal, and 48 states have laws to address sexually explicit AI deepfakes. But the tools to make them are widely available, and researchers say that a flood of fake images can make it harder to tell when a child is actively experiencing harm.

"The influx of AI-generated CSAM reports to NCMEC is “explosive”"

North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson, who cochairs the AG Alliance’s AI Task Force, said at OpenAI’s event that the influx of AI-generated CSAM reports to NCMEC is “explosive” — and if they keep going that way, “it is going to mean that we fail in our mission.” Tech companies are facing a range of policy proposals that could require them to take more action against CSAM and other potentially harmful content for kids. The Take It Down Act now requires social media platforms to remove real or AI-generated nonconsensual intimate images within 48 hours, and the newly elected Congress could seek to take stronger action against AI companies like SpaceXSI, whose Grok chatbot went on an undressing spree earlier this year. Last month eight states sued OpenAI for a separate set of alleged harms to children, citing lawsuits alleging ChatGPT encouraged illegal substance use and suicide.

OpenAI says its classifier dramatically cuts down on false positives, flagging 48 percent fewer images, while the images it did identify were twice as likely to contain abusive material. It’s designed to catch abusive AI-generated images produced by a variety of tools, including open-source models and nudifying apps. It’s also the first broadly available CSAM classifier with a specific flag for AI-generated material, said OpenAI’s head of child safety public policy, John Buckley, at the briefing. “It’s important for industry to be able to understand what images may contain a fictional child versus a real child,” Buckley added. “That triage is critical in law enforcement reporting flows.” He also emphasized, however, that laws should recognize the harm of AI-generated CSAM: “It potentially erodes social norms in offending against children, and it’s often found colocated with child sexual abuse imagery of real children,” Buckley said.

"OpenAI says its classifier dramatically cuts down on false positives, flagging 48 percent fewer images"

OpenAI’s own ChatGPT image generator is designed to deny user requests for CSAM. Now, users who attempt to produce it will be shown a new warning developed with expert guidance to try to encourage them to seek help. A first offense will trigger a 24-hour pause in accessing ChatGPT and warn the user their account could be permanently closed, while offering support resources to combat the behavior. OpenAI says it reports “all instances of CSAM” to NCMEC. In a statement, Buckley explained that the 24-hour pause is based on expert advice for best practices “and international evidence on what works to prevent and respond to CSAM seeking vs CSAM generation.” The point is “to interrupt harmful behavior and direct people toward specialist help to stop it.”

Jackson said that North Carolina and many other states now have laws that cover synthetic CSAM, but that partnering with a tech company like OpenAI to help deter its creation is a fairly novel approach to an emerging issue. “Most of what AGs do is accountability work,” he told reporters at the briefing. “Most of our jurisdiction kicks in after the fact to hold people accountable for harm. But with this, we wanted to see if it was possible to develop a model of working together to prevent that harm. And I would say it’s still basically an experiment.”

article_content_zh:
OpenAI 宣布推出一款工具，据称该工具将帮助儿童性虐待调查人员消除噪音，找到可以快速采取行动的有害材料。

在周一于华盛顿特区举行的新闻发布会上，OpenAI 宣布了一款分类器，据称可以更好地检测儿童的虐待图像，包括它是否是人工智能生成的。它还提供对经过审查的组织的免费访问，为开发人员提供有关如何检测此类内容的更多指导，并帮助培训执法人员了解人工智能如何协助他们的调查。这一消息发布之际，政策制定者和其他人士正在推动对人工智能工具实施更多安全限制，指责 OpenAI 和其他公司助长了对儿童的伤害。

近年来，人工智能生成的儿童性图像已经威胁到国家失踪和受虐儿童中心 (NCMEC) Cyber​​Tipline 等系统，该中心负责收集和分类儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM) 的报告。 Cyber​​Tipline 在 2025 年收到了 400,000 份与生成人工智能相关的报告，比 2024 年收到的 67,000 份呈指数增长，研究人员警告说，这些报告的涌入可能会使 NCMEC 的工作量“难以管理”。美国政府表示，人工智能生成和非人工智能生成的 CSAM 都是非法的，并且 48 个州制定了法律来解决露骨的人工智能深度伪造问题。但制作它们的工具很广泛，研究人员表示，大量的虚假图像会让我们更难判断孩子何时正在遭受伤害。

AG 联盟 AI 工作组联合主席、北卡罗来纳州总检察长杰夫·杰克逊 (Jeff Jackson) 在 OpenAI 的活动上表示，向 NCMEC 提交的 AI 生成的 CSAM 报告的涌入是“爆炸性的”——如果他们继续这样下去，“将意味着我们的使命失败。”科技公司正面临一系列政策建议，这些建议可能要求他们对 CSAM 和其他对儿童可能有害的内容采取更多行动。 《Take It Down Act》现在要求社交媒体平台在 48 小时内删除真实的或人工智能生成的非自愿亲密图像，新当选的国会可能会寻求对 SpaceXSI 等人工智能公司采取更强硬的行动，该公司的 Grok 聊天机器人在今年早些时候进行了脱衣狂欢。上个月，八个州起诉 OpenAI，指控其对儿童造成一系列伤害，并援引指控 ChatGPT 鼓励非法药物使用和自杀的诉讼。

OpenAI 表示，它的分类器大大减少了误报，标记的图像减少了 48%，而它识别出的图像包含滥用内容的可能性是原来的两倍。它旨在捕获由各种工具（包括开源模型和裸体应用程序）生成的滥用人工智能生成的图像。 OpenAI 儿童安全公共政策负责人 John Buckley 在简报会上表示，这也是第一个广泛使用的 CSAM 分类器，带有针对 AI 生成材料的特定标志。巴克利补充说：“对于行业来说，能够了解哪些图像可能包含虚构的孩子和真实的孩子非常重要。” “这种分类对于执法报告流程至关重要。”不过，他也强调，法律应该认识到人工智能生成的 CSAM 的危害：“它可能会侵蚀犯罪儿童的社会规范，而且它经常与真实儿童的儿童性虐待图像同时出现，”巴克利说。

OpenAI 自己的 ChatGPT 图像生成器旨在拒绝用户对 CSAM 的请求。现在，尝试生成它的用户将看到在专家指导下开发的新警告，以鼓励他们寻求帮助。首次违规将触发 ChatGPT 访问 24 小时暂停，并警告用户其帐户可能会被永久关闭，同时提供支持资源来打击该行为。 OpenAI 表示，它向 NCMEC 报告“所有 CSAM 实例”。巴克利在一份声明中解释说，24 小时的暂停是基于专家对最佳实践的建议，“以及关于如何有效预防和应对 CSAM 寻求与 CSAM 生成的国际证据”。重点是“阻止有害行为并引导人们寻求专家帮助来制止这种行为。”

Jackson 表示，北卡罗来纳州和许多其他州现在都制定了涵盖合成 CSAM 的法律，但与 OpenAI 这样的科技公司合作来帮助阻止其创建，是解决新兴问题的一种相当新颖的方法。 “总检察长所做的大部分工作是问责工作，”他在新闻发布会上告诉记者。 “我们的大部分司法管辖权都是在事后开始追究人们对伤害的责任。但通过这一点，我们想看看是否有可能开发出一种共同合作的模式来防止这种伤害。我想说，这基本上仍然是一个实验。”

Jackson said that North Carolina and many other states now have laws that cover synthetic CSAM, but that partnering with a tech company like OpenAI to help deter its creation is a fairly novel approach to an emerging issue. “Most of what AGs do is accountability work,” he told reporters at the briefing. “Most of our jurisdiction kicks in after the fact to hold people accountable for harm. But with this, we wanted to see if it was possible to develop a model of working together to prevent that harm. And I would say it’s still basically an experiment.”

article_content:
OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra helped produce a proof that could solve a 50-year-old problem in particle physics.

Physicist Nathaniel Craig of UC Santa Barbara, currently a visiting scientist at OpenAI, presented the approach on the OpenAI blog and as a preprint paper. Craig leads the particle theory group at UCSB and is a permanent member of its Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics.

Physicists can simulate parts of the Standard Model, the theory describing all known particles and fundamental forces, on a computer grid called a lattice. That has already led to breakthroughs like calculating the proton's mass from first principles. But putting the full theory on a lattice has been impossible. The weak force, which governs certain types of radioactive decay, treats left- and right-handed particles differently. On simple lattices, this asymmetry creates unwanted ghost particles. Special lattice particles called overlap fermions can filter them out, but for over 25 years, nobody could set their phase correctly.

Craig had a strategy to fix the phase by comparing progressively finer lattices, but couldn't prove it worked in all the cases it needed to cover. GPT-6 Astra turned the idea into a working construction and took the lead on the detailed proof. Lattice field theorists Maarten Golterman, Andreas Kronfeld, and Yigal Shamir reviewed the proof and raised questions that Craig says helped build confidence in the result. He calls the work "much more a beginning than an end"and says a lot remains before realistic simulations are possible.

The result follows a run of AI advances in mathematics that started in January 2026. In May, OpenAI's disproof of Erdős's unit distance conjecture became the first AI proof worthy of math's top journal. Days later, Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved nine of 353 open Erdős problems for a few hundred dollars, and by October its results had passed peer review.

The most far-reaching claim came in September, when OpenAI submitted a 166-page proof for the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem and the Clay Mathematics Institute said it had "apparently been settled". The solution remains under review, and mathematicians have questioned whether OpenAI fully understands its own proof. Across the field, mathematicians have mixed feelings as AI keeps cracking unsolved problems.

summary_zh: OpenAI的研究员利用GPT-6 Astra构建并验证了粒子物理标准模型中困扰学界25年的手征费米子相位难题
article_content_zh:
OpenAI的GPT-6 Astra帮助提供了一个证明，可以解决粒子物理学中一个50年的问题。

加州大学圣巴巴拉分校的物理学家 Nathaniel Craig 目前是 OpenAI 的访问科学家，他在 OpenAI 博客上和预印本论文中介绍了该方法。克雷格领导着加州大学圣巴巴拉分校的粒子理论小组，并且是卡维理理论物理研究所的永久成员。

物理学家可以在称为晶格的计算机网格上模拟标准模型的部分内容，该理论描述了所有已知的粒子和基本力。这已经带来了一些突破，比如根据第一原理计算质子的质量。但将完整的理论放在格子上是不可能的。弱力控制某些类型的放射性衰变，它以不同的方式对待左手粒子和右手粒子。在简单晶格上，这种不对称性会产生不需要的鬼粒子。称为重叠费米子的特殊晶格粒子可以将它们过滤掉，但 25 年来，没有人能够正确设置它们的相位。

克雷格有一个通过比较逐渐精细的晶格来修复相位的策略，但无法证明它在它需要涵盖的所有情况下都有效。 GPT-6 Astra 将这个想法变成了可行的结构，并率先进行了详细的证明。格场理论家 Maarten Golterman、Andreas Kronfeld 和 Yigal Shamir 审查了证明并提出了问题，克雷格表示这些问题有助于建立对结果的信心。他称这项工作“更多的是一个开始而不是结束”，并表示在现实模拟成为可能之前还有很多工作要做。

这一结果是自 2026 年 1 月开始的人工智能在数学领域取得的一系列进展之后得出的。5 月，OpenAI 对 Erdős 单位距离猜想的反驳成为第一个值得数学顶级期刊认可的人工智能证明。几天后，Google Deepmind 的 AlphaProof Nexus 以数百美元的价格解决了 353 个开放式 Erdős 问题中的 9 个，到 10 月，其结果已通过同行评审。

影响最深远的说法发生在 9 月份，当时 OpenAI 提交了一份 166 页的纳维-斯托克斯千年奖问题证明，克莱数学研究所表示该问题“显然已经解决”。该解决方案仍在审查中，数学家质疑 OpenAI 是否完全理解自己的证明。随着人工智能不断解决未解决的问题，整个领域的数学家们心情复杂。

title: Q&A with Satya Nadella on code verification becoming more important as code generation gets cheap, Microsoft's voluntary exit offers, decision models, and more (Gergely Orosz/The Pragmatic Engineer)
title_en: Q&A with Satya Nadella on code verification becoming more important as code generation gets cheap, Microsoft's voluntary exit offers, decision models, and more (Gergely Orosz/The Pragmatic Engineer)
author: The Pragmatic Engineer
article_content:
Gergely OroszNov 16, 2026 78 8Share TranscriptListen and watch now on YouTube, Apple, and Spotify. See the episode transcript at the top of this page, and timestamps for the episode at the bottom.

• turbopuffer – a ridiculously scalable, fast and cheap hybrid search engine, built on top of object storage, used by cutting-edge companies like Anthropic, Linear, Ramp and many others. Many companies that switch to turbopuffer are cutting their search bills by 50% or more and getting much faster results. Check it out. Also, check out the new and improved The Pragmatic Engineer search I built on top of turbopuffer!

• Linear – one of the big challenges for us devs is the sheer amount of code to review. Linear Diffs is a new feature for reviewing PRs inside of Linear, with all the context in one place. It also supports stacked PRs. Check it out

• WorkOS – WorkOS built Airlock, the authorization layer for AI agents. It evaluates every request against the agent’s intent + your rules, and either allows it, denies it, or routes it to a human. Works with Claude Code, Codex & MCP gateways. Learn more

What does software engineering look like when generating the code becomes cheap and verifying it is the hard part?

There can be few people in tech more qualified to tackle this hot topic than Satya Nadella. Microsoft’s CEO started his career as a software engineer – a rare thing among Big Tech CEOs. Satya joins me to discuss how building software is changing at Microsoft, and what it means for us, software engineers.

We start with Microsoft’s embrace of open source from the mid-2010s and the lessons learned from building VS Code in the open. I ask how Microsoft went from holding an early lead with GitHub Copilot to having to catch up with Cursor and Claude Code, and what it reveals about building products around rapidly improving models.

Satya also explains what a “software factory” means to him, why specifications and verification are becoming more important, and how teams that work on products like the Windows operating system are adapting. We also touch on Microsoft’s voluntary exit offers, AI-related anxiety around engineering careers, and hear Nadella caution against drawing long-term conclusions from the slowdown in junior hiring.

We also explore open and local models, why companies need to control their own AI infrastructure, and how to build safeguards around increasingly capable agents. Satya also has some advice for engineers who want to excel during this period of change – and why he would like to spend more time on building.

I appreciated how grounded and thoughtful Satya was – and how pragmatic he is in suggesting to verify anything and everything related with LLMs, and not blindly trust anything or anyone (including vendors or AI models!) 12 of the most interesting takeaways I noted:

1. A new form of software engineering: teams building software factories to improve their work. Satya cites the Azure networking team which manages 500+ fiber network operators and recently built an agentic system to better manage emails and processes. Now, they operate much more efficiently as a result. Satya sees this as the reality of “AI transformation”: brownfield work on building software factories to improve how teams operate, all while continuing the day-to-day work.

2. GitHub Copilot fell behind Claude Code because the IDE faded out in just six months. Dev tools are in Microsoft’s DNA, but it was completely unprepared for Claude Code retiring the concept of the IDE in favor of the command line. Satya admits this move by Anthropic caught them off guard, and it taught him that when a non-linear model jump occurs, the form factor of using that model can change fast. He also admits the IDE “faded away” over the course of just six months, and Microsoft’s stronghold in dev tools had been the IDE, with VS Code. It sounds like Microsoft learned a lesson here and is now more nimble with dev tools, and less attached to past form factors.

3. “Own the intelligence”: avoid lock-in & treat agents as an insider risk. Satya cautions companies to avoid lock-in with any single model provider by ensuring that the harness, memory, and model are not coupled, so that they can be changed with ease. He also thinks more companies should consider using open models as a way to protect their core intellectual property (IP) from leaking out, and build private evals to decide what models to use and upgrade to. He also says that models are intelligent but unreliable, so it’s best to treat them as “insider risks” and build a separate system to verify that agentic systems work as expected.

4. Microsoft is betting on “hybrid intelligence.” Satya questions why we rely on the cloud for AI infrastructure when last year’s frontier-equivalent model can already run on a laptop, while the frontier-equivalent model from as recently as the previous quarter can run on desktops. He predicts the concept of “hybrid intelligence” will gain traction, of having local AI models running on laptops and desktops, and a model router deciding when to use cheap, “unmetered” local models, and when to route to a more capable, expensive one in the cloud. Microsoft is building infra to support such routing with its Microsoft AI (MAI) models and Surface Laptop Ultra lineups.

5. Code generation has become cheap, but verification is still hard. Satya reveals he’s been thinking a lot lately about how challenging it is to verify the correctness of code generated today. Models doing a “critique” on generated code is one solution, but it involves model alignment issues, such as a model achieving its goal in undesirable ways; for example, making tests pass by deleting failing tests. Satya also thinks we’ll start to build more verification loops based on production traces, in a kind of “recursive self-improvement” (RSI). But for this, models need to be able to verify fixes, meaning we return to the verification problem! We didn’t arrive at any definite solutions for this during the conversation, which tells me this is a problem space that will keep many of us engineers busy!

6. What’s with those voluntary exit offers? I asked Satya directly why Microsoft recently made voluntary exit offers to most of its software engineers for the first time in the company’s history. I also wanted to know if it could mean layoffs in the future. Unsurprisingly, his reply was diplomatic, and my more direct interpretation is this:

Large transformations/reorgs are likely because teams will change in size (many getting smaller) and function, with many new AI-related teams being formed.

There’s high demand internally for new, AI-related roles like forward-deployed engineers.

A voluntary exit offer can motivate engineers who feel “stuck” on their current team (for example, if there’s less opportunity to do AI-related work) to take interviews elsewhere, and, with an offer in hand, depart with a smaller “bonus.” Satya admits that even inside Microsoft, not all teams got the memo about becoming more AI-native. Those affected can accept a voluntary exit offer until December, and it’s safe to assume many are indeed interviewing at other places!

There is a lot of change ahead. My take is that any “pre-AI” company will have to restructure itself, not just Microsoft. At least Satya is candid about it.

7. The cause of the junior hiring slowdown is that companies are figuring out the new way to work. I asked if Microsoft is hiring new grads and juniors, and Satya admits there’s a slowdown there (and at many places). He identifies a process that’s currently taking place as the reason why:

At Microsoft, most teams are busy coming up with new ways of working, so it’s not a good time to bring in new hires. Satya expects this “reorg” phase to be temporary, after which hiring will pick up.

8. Microsoft has started a “preceptorship” program for AI-accelerated development. In collaboration with Carnegie Mellon University, Microsoft launched the PRAISE program (Preceptorship for AI-accelerated Software Engineering). It’s actually a concept borrowed from nursing, where new nurses are paired with experienced ones to develop real-world experience and confidence. Preceptors are experienced software engineers who coach “preceptees” on using AI tools thoughtfully, while building strong systems thinking, taste, and judgement. This is the kind of program I wish more companies would consider partnering with educational institutions on; perhaps this one will inspire other engineering leaders.

9. The next big engineering challenge: building “software factories” within teams and companies. Satya believes every company needs to control their AI infra – the harness, context, memory, model – and that verification of the generated code is a hard, currently unsolved, problem. Inside Microsoft, he sees lots of teams building their own “software factories” to improve team and org operations. As we talked, it became evident that building software factories looks set to be a widespread engineering problem across the industry because it’s a novel challenge without many existing “blueprints”. It will be slightly different for every team and company. There’s going to be lots of work in this space!

10. “Migrating” to AI is quite different from migrating to a new technology. We talk about how “migrating” to become “AI-native” feels similar to a brownfield project introducing a new technology, such as moving over from HTML+JavaScript to React. Satya also perceives some differences:

When a new model launches with new capabilities, it can invalidate existing setups, just as models like Opus 4.5-and-above have invalidated IDEs.

11. Satya is very enthusiastic about decision models. Satya loves how decision models like ‘Jev’ and Microsoft’s ‘Decision-1’ are a kind of new primitive. He says: “These decision models are kind of like Excel macros. What happened to spreadsheets with macros can happen with code with intelligence embedded as a primitive. This primitive has a distribution, it doesn’t need to be generated again and again, it’s token-efficient. I think that this is one of those places where software engineering remains very much alive. Decision models are like the stored procedure of the intelligence era.”

12. Satya’s advice for winning with AI: stop reading & listening about it, and start using it more. He says:

“It’s ironic on a podcast to say, but it’s “do more, learn more, and be hands-on.” Experience it firsthand. If I could change the ratio of my “talk” to “do,” I would. This is the time. If there’s one piece of advice – whether you’re mid-career, a CEO, or a fresh college grad – it’s that the more you can take the time to learn, to be in teams that are doing it, then the better that is versus anything else I can think of.”

article_content_zh:
Gergely OroszNov 16, 2026 78 8Share 文字记录立即在 YouTube、Apple 和 Spotify 上收听和观看。请参阅本页顶部的剧集记录，以及底部的剧集时间戳。

•turbopuffer – 一种可扩展性极强、快速且廉价的混合搜索引擎，建立在对象存储之上，被 Anthropic、Linear、Ramp 等尖端公司使用。许多改用涡轮增压技术的公司将搜索费用削减了 50% 或更多，并且更快地获得结果。一探究竟。另外，请查看我在涡轮增压器之上构建的新的和改进的实用工程师搜索！

• 线性——我们开发人员面临的一大挑战是需要审查的代码量巨大。 Linear Diffs 是一项新功能，用于审查 Linear 内部的 PR，将所有上下文集中在一个地方。它还支持堆叠 PR。一探究竟

• WorkOS – WorkOS 内置Airlock，AI 代理的授权层。它会根据代理的意图+您的规则来评估每个请求，然后允许、拒绝或将其路由给人工。可与 Claude Code、Codex 和 MCP 网关配合使用。了解更多

当生成代码变得便宜而验证它是困难的部分时，软件工程会是什么样子？

在科技界，很少有人比萨提亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 更有资格解决这个热门话题。微软首席执行官的职业生涯始于软件工程师——这在大型科技公司的首席执行官中很少见。 Satya 与我一起讨论 Microsoft 的软件构建发生了怎样的变化，以及这对我们软件工程师意味着什么。

我们从 Microsoft 从 2010 年代中期开始拥抱开源以及从公开构建 VS Code 中汲取的经验教训开始。我问微软是如何从 GitHub Copilot 的早期领先地位发展到必须赶上 Cursor 和 Claude Code 的，以及它揭示了围绕快速改进的模型构建产品的哪些内容。

Satya 还解释了“软件工厂”对他意味着什么、为什么规范和验证变得越来越重要，以及开发 Windows 操作系统等产品的团队如何适应。我们还谈到了微软的自愿退出提议、围绕工程职业的人工智能相关焦虑，并听到纳德拉警告不要从初级招聘放缓中得出长期结论。

我们还探索开放和本地模型，为什么公司需要控制自己的人工智能基础设施，以及如何围绕能力日益增强的代理建立保障措施。 Satya 还为想要在这一变革时期脱颖而出的工程师提供了一些建议，以及他为什么愿意花更多时间进行构建。

我很欣赏萨蒂亚的脚踏实地和深思熟虑，以及他在建议验证与法学硕士相关的任何事情和所有事情方面的务实态度，而不是盲目地信任任何东西或任何人（包括供应商或人工智能模型！）我注意到的 12 个最有趣的要点：

1. 一种新的软件工程形式：团队构建软件工厂来改进他们的工作。 Satya 引用了 Azure 网络团队的例子，该团队管理着 500 多家光纤网络运营商，并且最近构建了一个代理系统来更好地管理电子邮件和流程。现在，他们的运营效率大大提高了。 Satya 认为这是“人工智能转型”的现实：棕地致力于建设软件工厂，以改善团队的运作方式，同时继续日常工作。

2. GitHub Copilot 落后于 Claude Code，因为 IDE 在短短六个月内就淡出了人们的视线。开发工具是微软的 DNA，但它完全没有准备好 Claude Code 放弃 IDE 的概念，转而支持命令行。 Satya 承认 Anthropic 的这一举动让他们措手不及，这让他明白，当发生非线性模型跳跃时，使用该模型的外形尺寸可能会快速变化。他还承认 IDE 在短短六个月的时间里就“消失了”，微软在开发工具领域的据点一直是 IDE 和 VS Code。听起来微软在这里吸取了教训，现在开发工具更加灵活，并且不再拘泥于过去的外形因素。

3.“拥有情报”：避免锁定并将代理视为内部风险。 Satya 警告公司要避免与任何单一模型提供商锁定，确保线束、内存和模型不耦合，以便可以轻松更改。他还认为更多的公司应该考虑使用开放模型来保护其核心知识产权（IP）免遭泄露，并建立私人评估来决定使用和升级到哪些模型。他还表示，模型是智能的，但不可靠，因此最好将它们视为“内部风险”，并构建一个单独的系统来验证代理系统是否按预期工作。

4. 微软押注于“混合智能”。 Satya 质疑为什么我们要依赖云来构建人工智能基础设施，去年的前沿等效模型已经可以在笔记本电脑上运行，而上个季度的前沿等效模型也可以在台式机上运行。他预测“混合智能”的概念将获得关注，即让本地人工智能模型在笔记本电脑和台式机上运行，​​并由模型路由器决定何时使用廉价的、“不计量”的本地模型，以及何时路由到云中功能更强大、更昂贵的模型。微软正在构建基础设施，以通过其 Microsoft AI (MAI) 模型和 Surface Laptop Ultra 系列支持此类路由。

title: California AG Rob Bonta sues OpenAI over the Hugging Face incident, alleging OpenAI endangered the public by testing its models without adequate safeguards (Politico)
title_en: California AG Rob Bonta sues OpenAI over the Hugging Face incident, alleging OpenAI endangered the public by testing its models without adequate safeguards (Politico)
author: Politico
content_snippet: California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI over the cyberattack its rogue AI agents launched this summer against the tech platform Hugging Face.
summary_en: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging that the company failed to implement adequate safety safeguards while testing AI agents on the Hugging Face platform, thereby endangering public safety. The suit targets the company’s deployment protocols and challenges the adequacy of their isolation mechanisms when exposing models to live environments.

title: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
title_en: Moonshot AI pivots Kimi models from coding to science as benchmark gains flatten
author: Manuel Uth
article_content:
Because Moonshot AI sees diminishing returns in coding, the Beijing startup is redirecting its Kimi language models toward biology, chemistry, and pharma research. International director Giacomo Ficari said at the Web Summit in Lisbon that science demands smarter AI models than law, finance, or code.

Beijing startup DP Technology is integrating Kimi K3.1 Pro into its research assistant BioMaster. In one test, the AI analyzed gene data from 3,696 mouse pancreatic cells and flagged 100 candidate genes in 90 minutes instead of an estimated four hours of human work.

Fully independent breakthroughs are still a long way off. On TCSExam, a 100-problem theoretical CS benchmark, leading models produced verifiable proofs but couldn't crack any open conjectures alone. US rivals hit similar limits. Anthropic's Claude found an enzyme system in September, but mathematicians criticized OpenAI's claimed math and physics breakthroughs. The pharma industry isn't sold yet either. A June Citi survey of 50 US research leaders found 72 percent already using AI broadly, but only 24 percent expect it to noticeably improve drug development success rates.

article_content_zh:
由于 Moonshot AI 看到编码的回报递减，这家北京初创公司正在将其 Kimi 语言模型转向生物学、化学和制药研究。国际总监 Giacomo Ficari 在里斯本网络峰会上表示，科学需要比法律、金融或代码更智能的人工智能模型。

北京初创公司 DP Technology 正在将 Kimi K3.1 Pro 集成到其研究助手 BioMaster 中。在一项测试中，人工智能分析了 3,696 个小鼠胰腺细胞的基因数据，并在 90 分钟内标记了 100 个候选基因，而不是人类估计需要 4 个小时的工作。

完全独立的突破还有很长的路要走。在 TCSExam（一个包含 100 个问题的理论计算机科学基准测试）上，领先的模型提供了可验证的证明，但无法单独破解任何开放的猜想。美国竞争对手也遇到了类似的限制。 Anthropic 的 Claude 在 9 月份发现了一种酶系统，但数学家批评 OpenAI 所声称的数学和物理突破。制药行业也还没有被出售。花旗 6 月对 50 名美国研究领导者进行的一项调查发现，72% 的人已经广泛使用人工智能，但只有 24% 的人预计人工智能将显着提高药物开发的成功率。

article_content_en:
Because Moonshot AI sees diminishing returns in coding, the Beijing startup is redirecting its Kimi language models toward biology, chemistry, and pharma research. International director Giacomo Ficari said at the Web Summit in Lisbon that science demands smarter AI models than law, finance, or code.

Beijing startup DP Technology is integrating Kimi K3.1 Pro into its research assistant BioMaster. In one test, the AI analyzed gene data from 3,696 mouse pancreatic cells and flagged 100 candidate genes in 90 minutes instead of an estimated four hours of human work.

Fully independent breakthroughs are still a long way off. On TCSExam, a 100-problem theoretical CS benchmark, leading models produced verifiable proofs but couldn't crack any open conjectures alone. US rivals hit similar limits. Anthropic's Claude found an enzyme system in September, but mathematicians criticized OpenAI's claimed math and physics breakthroughs. The pharma industry isn't sold yet either. A June Citi survey of 50 US research leaders found 72 percent already using AI broadly, but only 24 percent expect it to noticeably improve drug development success rates.

title: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back
title_en: Nvidia’s board is reportedly ‘not considering’ hiring Jensen Huang back

inline_images.caption: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
inline_images.alt: Digital photo collage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Nvidia’s board of directors “isn’t considering” having Jensen Huang return as CEO, according to a report from CNBC. A source tells the outlet the board “is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back.”

Since Huang’s resignation last week, tech executives, along with current and former Nvidia employees, have called for his reinstatement. An online petition to bring Huang back as CEO has amassed more than 180,000 signatures, including from major figures like Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, and Replit CEO Amjad Masad.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that it “certainly isn’t a bad idea” for Huang to return to Nvidia. A report from the Financial Times also suggests that Huang floated the idea of returning as CEO with some of his colleagues.

Nvidia appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO. The company has also hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate Huang’s conduct.

英伟达董事会“不考虑”让黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官。一位消息人士告诉媒体，董事会“专注于对黄进行调查，而不是讨论让他回来。”

自黄上周辞职以来，科技高管以及英伟达现任和前任员工一直呼吁让他复职。一份要求黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官的网上请愿书已收集了超过 18 万个签名，其中包括 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney)、SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 和 Replit 首席执行官阿姆贾德·马萨德 (Amjad Masad) 等重要人物。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，黄回到英伟达“当然不是一个坏主意”。英国《金融时报》的一篇报道还表明，黄与他的一些同事提出了重新担任首席执行官的想法。

Nvidia 任命其首席财务官 Colette Kress 为临时首席执行官。该公司还聘请了 Wachtell Lipton 来调查黄的行为。

title: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back
title_en: The open-source movement wants Jensen Huang back

inline_images.caption: Jensen Huang with microphone in one hand and waving the other
inline_images.alt: Jensen Huang with microphone in one hand and waving the other

author: James Donnell
article_content:
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here .

On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world.

These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech).

Huang had become a sort of ringleader for those who defend open source to policymakers against concerns that such models come with no guardrails and cede AI leadership to China, where the most powerful and popular open-source models are created. They now want their most influential voice returned to his post.

But it’s not just Huang’s extramarital affairs that threaten his (and Nvidia’s) credibility as an advocate for open-source AI. New research into China’s startups using Nvidia’s chips, and a new rule from the US Department of Commerce announced Monday, could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress.

On Thursday, the day Huang resigned, ex-OpenAI researcher Will DePue published findings online suggesting that China’s AI companies had far more access to Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell chips than previously estimated. China is banned from accessing Nvidia’s most cutting-edge chips to help protect America’s AI lead.

It’s unclear how they would have gained access to the chips. DePue claims the results were verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic, but an independent analysis has not confirmed the results. (DePue did not respond to a request for an interview. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.)

The findings do not establish that Nvidia helped Chinese companies obtain the chips, and the broader problem of chip smuggling was already known to extend well beyond Nvidia’s control.

But in suggesting that Nvidia may have profited from the rise of Chinese AI startups, whose models are increasingly being used by American companies instead of domestic alternatives, the findings do leave Huang in an awkward position. He has championed open-source AI as a way to strengthen American technological leadership. “Without open source, startups can’t thrive, university researchers can’t do research, you can’t teach AI, scientists can’t use AI,” he said last December during a talk about helping the US win the AI race against China.

It also makes the idea of reinstating Huang even more of a long shot. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent even said last week that Nvidia should not consider someone from inside the company to replace him. The new findings lower Huang’s chances further.

What happens next? Nvidia announced in September it would acquire Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion. Its support for open source also serves a straightforward financial interest: The more businesses that build their own models instead of forking over money to Anthropic and OpenAI, the more chips Nvidia can sell.

But a new rule from the US Department of Commerce could mean the models popular on Hugging Face will soon stop getting smarter. The rule aims to prevent Chinese companies from training models on Nvidia chips that they can’t own directly, but that they can access remotely in data centers in countries like Malaysia—a workaround that has helped China’s open-source models get so good.

The open-source world rallied around Huang because of his influence on policymakers. That was important, since the rise of China’s open-source models has splintered some in Trump’s orbit. If Huang is out, who is next?

article_content_zh:
这个故事最初出现在我们关于人工智能的每周通讯《算法》中。要首先在您的收件箱中收到此类故事，请在此处注册。

周五，一份恢复黄仁勋担任 Nvidia 首席执行官的请愿书开始在社交媒体上流传，到周一，该请愿书列出了一些著名的签名者，包括埃隆·马斯克和几位有影响力的 Nvidia 研究人员。但梳理一下这 115,000 多个名字，你会发现黄的支持者中有一个重要派别——人工智能模型共享中心 Hugging Face、风险投资公司 Andreessen Horowitz 和红杉资本的高层——来自科技界的特定领域。

这些名字对开源人工智能的开发有着既得利益，与 ChatGPT 或 Claude 不同，这些模型可以独立于大型科技公司下载和运行。此类模型的支持者表示，将人工智能集中在少数强大的公司手中将使其他所有人的处境变得更糟（对于人工智能行业的左翼批评者来说，这种担忧听起来并不奇怪，如果这么多开源倡导者不是风险资本家，当初创公司可以在不向大型科技公司支付费用的情况下建立更便宜的人工智能时，他们就能获利）。

黄仁勋已经成为那些为政策制定者捍卫开源的人的头目，他们担心这些模型没有护栏，并将人工智能领导地位让给中国，而中国创造了最强大和最受欢迎的开源模型。他们现在希望他们最有影响力的声音回到他的岗位上。

但威胁他（和英伟达）作为开源人工智能倡导者的信誉的不仅仅是黄的婚外情。针对使用英伟达芯片的中国初创公司的新研究，以及美国商务部周一宣布的新规定，可能会对该运动的声誉及其技术进步造成打击。

周四，也就是黄仁勋辞职的当天，前 OpenAI 研究员 Will DePue 在网上发布了调查结果，表明中国的人工智能公司获得英伟达先进 Blackwell 芯片的机会比之前估计的要多得多。中国被禁止使用英伟达最尖端的芯片，以帮助保护美国的人工智能领先地位。

目前尚不清楚他们如何获得这些芯片。 DePue 声称该结果已得到 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的高级研究人员的验证，但独立分析尚未证实该结果。 （DePue 没有回复采访请求。Nvidia 没有立即回复评论请求。）

调查结果并不能证明英伟达帮助中国公司获得了芯片，而且众所周知，更广泛的芯片走私问题远远超出了英伟达的控制范围。

但在暗示英伟达可能从中国人工智能初创公司的崛起中获利（中国人工智能初创公司的模型越来越多地被美国公司而不是国内替代品使用）时，这一发现确实让黄处于尴尬的境地。他倡导开源人工智能，以此作为加强美国技术领先地位的一种方式。去年 12 月，他在一次有关帮助美国赢得与中国的人工智能竞赛的演讲中表示：“如果没有开源，初创公司就无法蓬勃发展，大学研究人员就无法进行研究，就无法教授人工智能，科学家就无法使用人工智能。”

这也使得让黄复职的想法更加渺茫。美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特上周甚至表示，英伟达不应考虑公司内部的人来取代他。新的发现进一步降低了黄的机会。

接下来会发生什么？ Nvidia 在 9 月份宣布将以近 130 亿美元收购 Hugging Face。它对开源的支持也服务于直接的经济利益：越多的企业构建自己的模型而不是向 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 花钱，Nvidia 可以销售的芯片就越多。

但美国商务部的一项新规定可能意味着 Hugging Face 上流行的模型将很快停止变得更加智能。该规则旨在阻止中国公司在英伟达芯片上训练模型，这些模型无法直接拥有，但可以在马来西亚等国家的数据中心远程访问——这种解决方法帮助中国的开源模型变得如此出色。

由于黄仁勋对政策制定者的影响力，开源世界聚集在他周围。这很重要，因为中国开源模式的崛起已经在特朗普的轨道上分裂了一些人。如果黄某出局，下一个是谁？

article_content_en:
This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here .

On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world.

These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry’s critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech).

Huang had become a sort of ringleader for those who defend open source to policymakers against concerns that such models come with no guardrails and cede AI leadership to China, where the most powerful and popular open-source models are created. They now want their most influential voice returned to his post.

But it’s not just Huang’s extramarital affairs that threaten his (and Nvidia’s) credibility as an advocate for open-source AI. New research into China’s startups using Nvidia’s chips, and a new rule from the US Department of Commerce announced Monday, could deal a blow to both the movement’s reputation and its technical progress.

On Thursday, the day Huang resigned, ex-OpenAI researcher Will DePue published findings online suggesting that China’s AI companies had far more access to Nvidia’s advanced Blackwell chips than previously estimated. China is banned from accessing Nvidia’s most cutting-edge chips to help protect America’s AI lead.

It’s unclear how they would have gained access to the chips. DePue claims the results were verified by senior researchers at OpenAI and Anthropic, but an independent analysis has not confirmed the results. (DePue did not respond to a request for an interview. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.)

The findings do not establish that Nvidia helped Chinese companies obtain the chips, and the broader problem of chip smuggling was already known to extend well beyond Nvidia’s control.

But in suggesting that Nvidia may have profited from the rise of Chinese AI startups, whose models are increasingly being used by American companies instead of domestic alternatives, the findings do leave Huang in an awkward position. He has championed open-source AI as a way to strengthen American technological leadership. “Without open source, startups can’t thrive, university researchers can’t do research, you can’t teach AI, scientists can’t use AI,” he said last December during a talk about helping the US win the AI race against China.

It also makes the idea of reinstating Huang even more of a long shot. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent even said last week that Nvidia should not consider someone from inside the company to replace him. The new findings lower Huang’s chances further.

What happens next? Nvidia announced in September it would acquire Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion. Its support for open source also serves a straightforward financial interest: The more businesses that build their own models instead of forking over money to Anthropic and OpenAI, the more chips Nvidia can sell.

But a new rule from the US Department of Commerce could mean the models popular on Hugging Face will soon stop getting smarter. The rule aims to prevent Chinese companies from training models on Nvidia chips that they can’t own directly, but that they can access remotely in data centers in countries like Malaysia—a workaround that has helped China’s open-source models get so good.

The open-source world rallied around Huang because of his influence on policymakers. That was important, since the rise of China’s open-source models has splintered some in Trump’s orbit. If Huang is out, who is next?

title: OpenAI releases a new image classifier and ChatGPT warnings to combat CSAM
title_en: OpenAI releases a new image classifier and ChatGPT warnings to combat CSAM
author: Ivan Mehta
article_content:
OpenAI today announced new tools to combat child sexual abuse material (CSAM) amid growing safety concerns around the use of AI tools. These features include a new image classifier to detect CSAM, warnings and temporary blocks to prevent users from creating or accessing content that sexualizes children, a new guideline for developers, and a set of tools for law enforcement.

The company unveiled a new image classifier that can detect CSAM images, including the ones generated by AI. OpenAI is giving select companies access to its classifier through its API at no cost. The tool looks for visual signs of abuse in images not seen before and assigns a score that can give an indicative direction to reviewers about dealing with CSAM.

OpenAI said that it developed this classifier with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), and it is working with Tech Coalition and ROOST to share access to the tool. In its early testing with partners, the AI company found that the classifier flags 48% fewer images while finding the same number of abusive images, reducing the work of reviewers. Plus, images flagged by the classifier are twice as likely to be abusive images.

What’s more, the company is adding new warning screens in ChatGPT to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children. ChatGPT will show an alert to users attempting such prompts, direct users toward specialized support to stop harmful behavior, and also suspend the account for 24 hours as a warning. The app already blocks CSAM content and requests related to it. It said that repeated offences could lead to the account being removed permanently.

OpenAI noted that it formed the message and guidelines around this behavior with organizations and researchers, including Protect Children, the Lucy Faithfull Foundation, and Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, who independently evaluated a trial of deterrent messages.

The company is also publishing guidelines for developers using OpenAI tools to prevent, detect, and help users report CSAM content. It said that in early testing, the guidelines have helped a number of developers adopt child safety tooling and register to report CSAM to NCMEC. OpenAI is also equipping law enforcement dealing with child safety with AI-powered features like dedicated plug-ins, investigative tools, and complex data analysis, with access managed by program administrators. It is also providing training to investigators along with a field guide on how to use AI.

OpenAI has had several lawsuits against the company blaming its technology for harming users, especially children. Safety-focused nonprofit Common Sense Media labeled OpenAI’s tech as “unacceptable risk” for teens. Other AI chatbots — specifically Grok — have been used to create nonconsensual sexualized imagery, including of children.

The AI startup had made changes in the last 12 months to its technology, including releasing a safety blueprint, updating content guidelines to bar inappropriate content, retuning its model to prevent them from generating harmful content, and releasing a special version of ChatGPT for teens.

article_content_zh:
由于人工智能工具的使用安全问题日益引起人们的关注，OpenAI 今天宣布推出新工具来打击儿童性虐待材料 (CSAM)。这些功能包括用于检测 CSAM 的新图像分类器、用于防止用户创建或访问儿童色情内容的警告和临时阻止、针对开发人员的新指南以及一套执法工具。

该公司推出了一种新的图像分类器，可以检测 CSAM 图像，包括人工智能生成的图像。 OpenAI 允许特定公司通过其 API 免费访问其分类器。该工具会在图像中查找以前未见过的滥用行为的视觉迹象，并给出一个分数，为审稿人处理 CSAM 提供指示性指导。

OpenAI 表示，该分类器是与国家失踪和受虐儿童中心 (NCMEC) 合作开发的，并且正在与 Tech Coalition 和 ROOST 合作，共享该工具的访问权限。在与合作伙伴的早期测试中，这家人工智能公司发现，分类器在发现相同数量的滥用图像的同时，标记的图像减少了 48%，从而减少了审核人员的工作。另外，被分类器标记的图像是滥用图像的可能性是其两倍。

更重要的是，该公司正在 ChatGPT 中添加新的警告屏幕，以防止用户访问使儿童色情的材料。 ChatGPT 将向尝试此类提示的用户显示警报，引导用户寻求专门支持以阻止有害行为，并暂停帐户 24 小时作为警告。该应用程序已阻止 CSAM 内容和与其相关的请求。它表示，屡次违规可能会导致该帐户被永久删除。

OpenAI 指出，它与保护儿童组织、Lucy Faithfull 基金会和塔斯马尼亚大学的 Joel Scanlan 等组织和研究人员一起制定了围绕这种行为的信息和指南，后者独立评估了一项威慑信息试验。

该公司还为使用 OpenAI 工具的开发人员发布了指南，以防止、检测和帮助用户报告 CSAM 内容。它表示，在早期测试中，该指南已帮助许多开发者采用儿童安全工具，并注册向 NCMEC 报告 CSAM。 OpenAI 还为处理儿童安全问题的执法部门配备了人工智能驱动的功能，如专用插件、调查工具和复杂的数据分析，并由程序管理员管理访问权限。它还为调查人员提供培训以及如何使用人工智能的现场指南。

OpenAI 已对该公司提起多起诉讼，指责其技术伤害用户，尤其是儿童。专注于安全的非营利组织 Common Sense Media 将 OpenAI 的技术标记为青少年“不可接受的风险”。其他人工智能聊天机器人——特别是 Grok——已被用来创建未经同意的性图像，包括儿童图像。

这家人工智能初创公司在过去 12 个月中对其技术进行了更改，包括发布安全蓝图、更新内容指南以禁止不当内容、重新调整其模型以防止生成有害内容，以及为青少年发布特殊版本的 ChatGPT。

article_content_en:
OpenAI today announced new tools to combat child sexual abuse material (CSAM) amid growing safety concerns around the use of AI tools. These features include a new image classifier to detect CSAM, warnings and temporary blocks to prevent users from creating or accessing content that sexualizes children, a new guideline for developers, and a set of tools for law enforcement.

The company unveiled a new image classifier that can detect CSAM images, including the ones generated by AI. OpenAI is giving select companies access to its classifier through its API at no cost. The tool looks for visual signs of abuse in images not seen before and assigns a score that can give an indicative direction to reviewers about dealing with CSAM.

OpenAI said that it developed this classifier with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), and it is working with Tech Coalition and ROOST to share access to the tool. In its early testing with partners, the AI company found that the classifier flags 48% fewer images while finding the same number of abusive images, reducing the work of reviewers. Plus, images flagged by the classifier are twice as likely to be abusive images.

What’s more, the company is adding new warning screens in ChatGPT to prevent users from accessing material that sexualizes children. ChatGPT will show an alert to users attempting such prompts, direct users toward specialized support to stop harmful behavior, and also suspend the account for 24 hours as a warning. The app already blocks CSAM content and requests related to it. It said that repeated offences could lead to the account being removed permanently.

OpenAI noted that it formed the message and guidelines around this behavior with organizations and researchers, including Protect Children, the Lucy Faithfull Foundation, and Joel Scanlan at the University of Tasmania, who independently evaluated a trial of deterrent messages.

The company is also publishing guidelines for developers using OpenAI tools to prevent, detect, and help users report CSAM content. It said that in early testing, the guidelines have helped a number of developers adopt child safety tooling and register to report CSAM to NCMEC. OpenAI is also equipping law enforcement dealing with child safety with AI-powered features like dedicated plug-ins, investigative tools, and complex data analysis, with access managed by program administrators. It is also providing training to investigators along with a field guide on how to use AI.

OpenAI has had several lawsuits against the company blaming its technology for harming users, especially children. Safety-focused nonprofit Common Sense Media labeled OpenAI’s tech as “unacceptable risk” for teens. Other AI chatbots — specifically Grok — have been used to create nonconsensual sexualized imagery, including of children.

The AI startup had made changes in the last 12 months to its technology, including releasing a safety blueprint, updating content guidelines to bar inappropriate content, retuning its model to prevent them from generating harmful content, and releasing a special version of ChatGPT for teens.

title: Altman Says AI Industry ‘Will Be Fine’ After Huang’s Ouster
title_en: Altman Says AI Industry ‘Will Be Fine’ After Huang’s Ouster
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Jensen Huang helped power the AI boom. But can the industry keep moving without him at Nvidia?

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman believes it can. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in San Francisco, Altman said the artificial intelligence industry would be “fine” without Huang leading Nvidia.

He also acknowledged the former CEO’s extraordinary contribution to the sector, calling him a hero while adding that “heroes have flaws”. The comments mark Altman’s first public comments on Huang’s sudden resignation from Nvidia last week.

They come at a time when the chipmaker’s leadership transition has raised questions about the future of a company central to the global AI ecosystem.

OpenAI's CEO said it was difficult to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen Huang and the company he built. Nvidia’s graphics processing units, or GPUs, have become essential for training and running large AI models, making the company a critical supplier to OpenAI and other AI firms.

However, Sam Altman stopped short of saying whether Huang should return to the company. Asked about the possibility, he said he did not know enough to answer.

His response acknowledged Huang’s influence without taking a position on Nvidia’s internal leadership decisions. Altman also expressed empathy for Huang, drawing a parallel with his own removal from OpenAI by its board in 2023.

Jensen Huang resigned after reports of extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman who is not related to him and is reportedly suspected by US officials of passing information to Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia appointed its Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor. The transition matters because Nvidia has become more than a chip supplier to the AI industry.

OpenAI and Nvidia have developed a close relationship over the past decade, spanning chips, data centres and financing.

Nvidia has also agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion to support OpenAI’s new data centre project in Ohio, according to the report. Asked whether he was concerned about Nvidia honouring its commitments after Huang’s departure, Altman said he was not.

He described Nvidia as a “behemoth of a company” and said people continued to trust its financial guarantees.

Who will succeed Jensen Huang? The race to find Nvidia's next chief begins

Huang’s exit has unsettled parts of Silicon Valley. Some technology executives and investors fear Nvidia could become more cautious about the large financial commitments that have helped fund the AI boom.

A campaign urging the company’s board to reinstate Huang has also attracted support from prominent industry figures. Sam Altman, however, pointed to the strength of demand and revenue across AI products.

He said the industry was growing strongly enough to withstand the uncertainty around Nvidia’s leadership.

His words do not diminish Jensen Huang’s role in building the AI ecosystem. Instead, they point to a distinction between the influence of one leader and the momentum of an entire industry.

Nvidia’s next chapter will show whether the company can maintain its pace without the person who led it for decades.

article_content_zh:
黄仁勋帮助推动了人工智能的繁荣。但如果没有他在英伟达，这个行业还能继续发展吗？

OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 相信它可以。 Altman 在旧金山举行的 Semafor 硅谷与世界活动上发表讲话时表示，如果没有黄仁勋领导 Nvidia，人工智能行业也会“很好”。

他还承认这位前首席执行官对该行业的非凡贡献，称他为英雄，同时补充说“英雄也有缺点”。这是奥特曼首次就黄仁勋上周突然从英伟达辞职一事发表公开评论。

它们出现之际，这家芯片制造商的领导层换届引发了人们对这家全球人工智能生态系统核心公司的未来的质疑。

OpenAI 首席执行官表示，很难想象如果没有黄仁勋和他创建的公司，人工智能革命将会发生。 Nvidia 的图形处理单元（GPU）对于训练和运行大型人工智能模型至关重要，这使得该公司成为 OpenAI 和其他人工智能公司的重要供应商。

不过，山姆·奥尔特曼没有透露黄是否应该回到公司。当被问及这种可能性时，他说他不知道如何回答。

他的回应承认了黄仁勋的影响力，但没有对英伟达的内部领导决策表明立场。 Altman 也表达了对黄的同情，并与 2023 年他自己被 OpenAI 董事会除名的情况进行了类比。

黄仁勋因婚外情报道而辞职，其中包括一名与黄仁勋没有亲属关系的女性黄仁勋，据报道美国官员怀疑她向中国情报机构传递信息。

英伟达任命其首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)为临时首席执行官，同时董事会也在寻找永久继任者。这一转变很重要，因为英伟达已经不仅仅是人工智能行业的芯片供应商。

OpenAI 和 Nvidia 在过去十年中在芯片、数据中心和融资领域建立了密切的合作关系。

Nvidia 还同意提供高达 1050 亿美元的担保，以支持 OpenAI 在俄亥俄州的新数据中心项目。当被问及他是否担心黄仁勋离开后英伟达兑现承诺时，奥特曼表示不担心。

他将英伟达描述为“一家庞然大物”，并表示人们仍然信任其财务担保。

谁将接替黄仁勋？寻找英伟达下一任首席执行官的竞赛开始

黄仁勋的退出让硅谷的部分地区感到不安。一些技术高管和投资者担心，英伟达可能会对为人工智能热潮提供资金的巨额财务承诺变得更加谨慎。

一项敦促公司董事会恢复黄先生职位的运动也吸引了业内知名人士的支持。然而，山姆·奥尔特曼指出了人工智能产品的需求和收入的强劲。

他表示，该行业的增长势头足以承受英伟达领导地位的不确定性。

他的话并没有削弱黄仁勋在构建人工智能生态系统中的作用。相反，他们指出了一位领导者的影响力与整个行业的势头之间的区别。

英伟达的下一章将展示该公司是否能够在没有几十年来领导该公司的人的情况下保持其步伐。

paragraphs: Jensen Huang helped power the AI boom. But can the industry keep moving without him at Nvidia?

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman believes it can. Speaking at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event in San Francisco, Altman said the artificial intelligence industry would be “fine” without Huang leading Nvidia.

He also acknowledged the former CEO’s extraordinary contribution to the sector, calling him a hero while adding that “heroes have flaws”. The comments mark Altman’s first public comments on Huang’s sudden resignation from Nvidia last week.
They come at a time when the chipmaker’s leadership transition has raised questions about the future of a company central to the global AI ecosystem.

OpenAI's CEO said it was difficult to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen Huang and the company he built. Nvidia’s graphics processing units, or GPUs, have become essential for training and running large AI models, making the company a critical supplier to OpenAI and other AI firms.
However, Sam Altman stopped short of saying whether Huang should return to the company. Asked about the possibility, he said he did not know enough to answer.

His response acknowledged Huang’s influence without taking a position on Nvidia’s internal leadership decisions. Altman also expressed empathy for Huang, drawing a parallel with his own removal from OpenAI by its board in 2023.

Jensen Huang resigned after reports of extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a woman who is not related to him and is reportedly suspected by US officials of passing information to Chinese intelligence.

Nvidia appointed its Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while its board searches for a permanent successor. The transition matters because Nvidia has become more than a chip supplier to the AI industry.
OpenAI and Nvidia have developed a close relationship over the past decade, spanning chips, data centres and financing.

Nvidia has also agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion to support OpenAI’s new data centre project in Ohio, according to the report. Asked whether he was concerned about Nvidia honouring its commitments after Huang’s departure, Altman said he was not.
He described Nvidia as a “behemoth of a company” and said people continued to trust its financial guarantees.
Who will succeed Jensen Huang? The race to find Nvidia's next chief begins

Huang’s exit has unsettled parts of Silicon Valley. Some technology executives and investors fear Nvidia could become more cautious about the large financial commitments that have helped fund the AI boom.

A campaign urging the company’s board to reinstate Huang has also attracted support from prominent industry figures. Sam Altman, however, pointed to the strength of demand and revenue across AI products.
He said the industry was growing strongly enough to withstand the uncertainty around Nvidia’s leadership.
His words do not diminish Jensen Huang’s role in building the AI ecosystem. Instead, they point to a distinction between the influence of one leader and the momentum of an entire industry.
Nvidia’s next chapter will show whether the company can maintain its pace without the person who led it for decades.

title: Nvidia board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC
title_en: Nvidia board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO, source tells CNBC
author: Seema Mody and Kif Leswing
article_content:
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.

The board is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity in order to discuss internal matters. Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.

Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company he founded, after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came days after Huang admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had an affair with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence, as well as affairs with employees at Nvidia.

Over the weekend, the Financial Times reported that Huang had discussed coming back with allies. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on speculation on Sunday.

Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO.

An online petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn 180,000 signatures as well as support from major figures including Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is open to Jensen Huang returning as CEO of Nvidia.

"It was not put at risk, and our country is now stronger than ever before,"Trump told reporters when asked about U.S. national security concerns.

On Friday, a representative for Nvidia's board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role.

article_content_zh:
一位知情人士告诉 CNBC，英伟达董事会并未考虑让黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官。

这位因讨论内部事务而要求匿名的人士表示，董事会的重点是对黄进行调查，而不是讨论让他回来。英伟达已聘请 Wachtell Lipton 律师事务所牵头调查黄的行为以及其是否危害国家安全或公司机密。

上周，黄在担任首席执行官 33 年后，从他创办​​的英伟达公司辞职。几天前，黄承认了婚外情，有新闻报道称他与为客户工作的爱丽丝·黄(Alice Huang)有染，并据称与中国情报部门有联系，并与英伟达(Nvidia)的员工有染。

周末，英国《金融时报》报道称，黄已经与盟友讨论了回归事宜。 Altimeter Capital 的布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 周一向 CNBC 表示，黄仁勋并未与他讨论复出事宜。

周日，黄的代表拒绝就猜测发表评论。

科技界的许多人都呼吁黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官。

一份要求他复职的在线请愿书已吸引了 18 万人签名，并得到了埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk)、Y Combinator 首席执行官加里·谭 (Garry Tan) 和 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 等重要人物的支持。

美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周一表示，他对黄仁勋重新担任英伟达首席执行官持开放态度。

当被问及美国国家安全问题时，特朗普对记者说：“它没有面临风险，我们的国家现在比以往任何时候都更强大。”

周五，英伟达董事会的一名代表表示，正在为英伟达首席执行官职位选择一家猎头公司。

author: Anthropic
article_content:
Over the last several months, frontier models have become much better at discovering vulnerabilities. We remain optimistic that this will help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities faster than ever before. However, the speed at which AI is improving has changed how we think about our own disclosure practices.

We’re shortening the disclosure window in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported to vendors and maintainers on or after January 1, 2027. In-progress reports as of that date will keep their existing deadlines.

In addition to shortening the disclosure window, we are making two related changes. First, we will aim to escalate to an external vulnerability coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 if a maintainer does not respond to our initial vulnerability report. Second, we will wait 30 days instead of 45 after a patch is available before sharing full technical details. The rest of our policy remains the same.

Finally, there are high- and critical-severity vulnerabilities that we reported over 90 days ago and that now exceed the deadline in our current CVD policy that have not yet been disclosed publicly. We are now notifying the maintainers of these projects that we are providing them an additional 30 days, after which time we will publish these reports on our dashboard in line with our updated policy starting January 1, 2027.

Many coordinated disclosure norms, including those found in our own policy, were developed well before AI could discover vulnerabilities. These policies assumed that fixes moved at human speed and that independent rediscovery of the same bug was unlikely. Neither assumption holds today. Models can now help develop fixes, and a bug that one model can find is increasingly likely to be found by another. We are seeing a higher rate of vulnerability rediscovery as these capabilities increase. A 90-day window made sense when a vulnerability could be expected to stay private for months. We no longer believe it can, and these changes are intended to keep pace with progress in AI capabilities and strike the right balance for defenders.

Some vulnerabilities still can’t be fixed quickly. Flaws in hard-to-deploy software, such as critical infrastructure, and flaws that require changes to a specification or RFC can’t always be resolved in 30 or 45 days. In these cases, we will work with the vendor on a remediation timeline. Our seven-day disclosure window for any vulnerability under active exploitation remains unchanged. This new policy update will not apply to AI-discovered findings that have not received human review, such as those found by OSS Scanner.

We recognize that shorter timelines may put more pressure on software maintainers. To reduce that burden, we will continue to include actionable guidance with each report, along with a patch or mitigation where possible, to best enable the maintainer to confirm a finding and fix the vulnerability. We will also continue to agree on a sustainable pace with maintainers before sending a large volume of findings to a single project.

We offer programs to help maintainers and defenders work at this new pace. Maintainers of critical open-source projects can apply to OSS Scanner, a no-cost service that periodically scans their code with our strongest models and sends them findings directly. Eligible maintainers and contributors can apply to the Claude for Open Source Program for six months of Claude Ultra at no cost. And security professionals, including open-source maintainers, can apply to our Cyber Verification Program, which tailors Claude’s safeguards to enable legitimate defensive work.

article_content_zh:
在过去的几个月里，前沿模型在发现漏洞方面变得更加出色。我们仍然乐观地认为，这将帮助防御者比以往更快地发现和修复漏洞。然而，人工智能改进的速度改变了我们对自己的披露实践的看法。

我们将协调漏洞披露 (CVD) 政策中的披露窗口从 90 天缩短到 30 天（对于高严重性和关键严重性问题），对于所有其他问题则从 45 天缩短。新的时间表适用于 2027 年 1 月 1 日或之后向供应商和维护人员报告的漏洞。截至该日期正在进行的报告将保留现有的截止日期。

除了缩短披露窗口外，我们还进行了两项相关的更改。首先，如果维护人员未对我们的初始漏洞报告做出回应，我们的目标是在 15 天（而不是 30 天）后将问题升级给外部漏洞协调员。其次，我们将在补丁发布后等待 30 天而不是 45 天，然后再分享完整的技术细节。我们政策的其余部分保持不变。

最后，我们在 90 多天前报告了一些高危和危急严重的漏洞，这些漏洞现在已经超过了我们当前 CVD 政策的截止日期，但尚未公开披露。我们现在通知这些项目的维护者，我们将为他们提供额外的 30 天时间，之后我们将根据自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起更新的政策在我们的仪表板上发布这些报告。

许多协调一致的披露规范，包括我们自己政策中的规范，都是在人工智能发现漏洞之前就制定的。这些政策假设修复工作以人类的速度进行，并且独立地重新发现相同的错误是不可能的。这两种假设在今天都不成立。模型现在可以帮助开发修复程序，并且一个模型可以找到的错误越来越有可能被另一个模型发现。随着这些功能的增强，我们发现漏洞重新发现率更高。当漏洞预计会在数月内保持私密状态时，90 天的窗口是有意义的。我们不再相信它可以，这些变化旨在跟上人工智能能力的进步，并为防御者取得适当的平衡。

一些漏洞仍然无法快速修复。难以部署的软件（例如关键基础设施）中的缺陷以及需要更改规范或 RFC 的缺陷并不总能在 30 或 45 天内得到解决。在这些情况下，我们将与供应商合作制定补救时间表。我们对任何被主动利用的漏洞的 7 天披露窗口保持不变。此新政策更新不适用于人工智能发现的未经人工审核的结果，例如 OSS Scanner 发现的结果。

我们认识到，较短的时间可能会给软件维护人员带来更大的压力。为了减轻这种负担，我们将继续在每份报告中提供可操作的指导，并在可能的情况下提供补丁或缓解措施，以最好地使维护人员能够确认发现并修复漏洞。在向单个项目发送大量调查结果之前，我们还将继续与维护人员就可持续的步伐达成一致。

我们提供计划来帮助维护者和防御者以这种新的节奏工作。关键开源项目的维护者可以申请 OSS Scanner，这是一项免费服务，可以使用我们最强大的模型定期扫描他们的代码，并直接向他们发送结果。符合条件的维护者和贡献者可以向 Claude 开源计划免费申请六个月的 Claude Ultra。安全专业人员，包括开源维护人员，可以申请我们的网络验证计划，该计划定制克劳德的保护措施以实现合法的防御工作。

article_content:
November 16, 2026 · Research · Science

We’re expanding the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to give up to 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to ChatGPT.

The program began as a pilot in July. Applications for the next round open Monday, November 23. We’ll award 50,000 new grants to eligible researchers on a first-come, first-served basis. Each grant gives the recipient and up to two collaborators free access to ChatGPT Plus. If you’re already on the waitlist and qualify, we’ll email you before applications open with instructions for activating your account.

Participants can use OpenAI’s frontier models and get training on how to use ChatGPT in their research. By default, we don’t use data shared through the program to train our models.

### What we learned from the pilot

20,000 researchers in 33 countries have joined the program since the pilot began in July. Shuqi Li, a researcher at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Harvard Medical School, looks for new drug targets that could ultimately shorten tuberculosis treatment. He is exploring whether ChatGPT can help link lab and patient data to speed up antibiotic development. Arthur Porto, assistant curator of AI biodiversity at the Florida Museum of Natural History, and his team uses AI tools to turn photographs of museum specimens into searchable databases. They also created a 3D model of a butterfly whose wings change color as you turn it, just like the real specimen.

We’re also publishing Science at the Frontier: How Scientists Use ChatGPT, new research from our Economic Research team examining how more than 1,800 researchers used ChatGPT during the program’s summer pilot. Surveyed participants estimated that, without AI, the same research work at the same quality would have taken nearly twice as long.

We want more researchers to have the tools and support to pursue ambitious questions and make discoveries that improve people’s lives. That is central to our mission of ensuring that AGI benefits all of humanity.

### Building on what we learned

The program’s summer pilot helped us understand how researchers use ChatGPT and how we can improve their experience. Based on feedback from researchers, we’re moving away from lottery-based selection. For the next round, we’ll provide access to the first 50,000 applications who meet the eligibility requirements.

The pilot gave researchers access to ChatGPT Pro. When we reviewed pilot usage, we found that most participants would have stayed within ChatGPT Plus usage limits. Based on that finding, we’re offering Plus for new grants so we can extend access to more research teams.

Each grant for this round covers the recipient and up to two collaborators, supporting up to 150,000 researchers. Our goal for the program as a whole is to reach 200,000 researchers, double the goal we announced when the pilot launched in July.

We’ll continue learning from participants about the application process, the capabilities they need, and the support that helps them use these tools in their research. This feedback will help us refine the program and shape future rounds.

### Supporting researchers across fields

Different scientific fields will use AI in different ways, and researchers will need different kinds and levels of support. We’re working with scientific communities to understand those needs and shape our tools, training, and programs around them.

Our support also includes helping scientific communities turn AI-generated results into deeper understanding and new discoveries. In mathematics, we contributed $5 million to a new Simons Foundation initiative to help mathematicians examine, understand, and build on results produced by AI.

We’re also providing different ways for researchers and institutions to access our tools. ChatGPT for Academic Researchers is just one way we’re helping researchers access advanced AI tools.

Through ChatGPT Edu, universities can give their campus communities access to ChatGPT for research, teaching, and learning, with tools for analyzing data and administrative controls for managing access.

For researchers working in biology, GPT‑Rosalind brings together specialized biological reasoning and access to scientific tools and databases. The Rosalind Academic Plan helps bring these capabilities to eligible labs at U.S. universities, offering up to 30 seats at no cost for up to 12 months. Access to GPT‑Rosalind requires approval through our trusted-access process.

Visit our researcher access guide to learn more about ChatGPT Edu, GPT‑Rosalind, and ChatGPT for Academic Researchers.

As these efforts grow, researchers’ experiences will help us understand where our tools are useful, where they fall short, and what support is needed. We’ll use that feedback to improve our programs, develop training and learning resources, and create opportunities for researchers to exchange approaches with one another.

Our goal is to give more researchers the tools and support to pursue ambitious questions—and to keep improving that support as their research and our capabilities evolve.

Learn more about the program.

article_content_zh:
十一月 16, 2026 · 研究 · 科学

我们正在扩大针对学术研究人员的 ChatGPT 计划，让全球多达 200,000 名研究人员免费访问 ChatGPT。

该计划于七月开始试点。下一轮申请将于 11 月 23 日星期一开放。我们将按照先到先得的原则向符合条件的研究人员提供 50,000 笔新资助。每笔资助都可以让接受者和最多两名合作者免费访问 ChatGPT Plus。如果您已经在候补名单上并且符合资格，我们会在申请开放之前向您发送电子邮件，其中包含激活您帐户的说明。

参与者可以使用 OpenAI 的前沿模型，并接受如何在研究中使用 ChatGPT 的培训。默认情况下，我们不使用通过程序共享的数据来训练我们的模型。

### 我们从试点中学到了什么

自 7 月份试点开始以来，已有 33 个国家的 20,000 名研究人员加入了该计划。布莱根妇女医院和哈佛医学院的研究员 Shuqi Li 正在寻找最终可以缩短结核病治疗时间的新药物靶点。他正在探索 ChatGPT 是否可以帮助连接实验室和患者数据，以加快抗生素的开发。佛罗里达自然历史博物馆人工智能生物多样性助理馆长 Arthur Porto 和他的团队使用人工智能工具将博物馆标本的照片转化为可搜索的数据库。他们还创建了蝴蝶的 3D 模型，其翅膀会随着转动而改变颜色，就像真实的标本一样。

我们还发布了《科学前沿：科学家如何使用 ChatGPT》，这是我们经济研究团队的新研究，研究了 1,800 多名研究人员在该项目夏季试点期间如何使用 ChatGPT。接受调查的参与者估计，如果没有人工智能，相同质量的相同研究工作将花费近两倍的时间。

我们希望更多的研究人员拥有工具和支持来追求雄心勃勃的问题并做出改善人们生活的发现。这是我们确保通用人工智能造福全人类的使命的核心。

### 以我们学到的知识为基础

该计划的夏季试点帮助我们了解研究人员如何使用 ChatGPT 以及我们如何改善他们的体验。根据研究人员的反馈，我们正在放弃基于抽签的选择。在下一轮中，我们将向前 50,000 名符合资格要求的申请提供访问权限。

该试点项目让研究人员能够访问 ChatGPT Pro。当我们审查试点使用情况时，我们发现大多数参与者都会遵守 ChatGPT Plus 使用限制。基于这一发现，我们将向 Plus 提供新的资助，以便我们可以将访问范围扩大到更多的研究团队。

此轮的每笔资助涵盖接受者和最多两名合作者，支持多达 150,000 名研究人员。我们整个计划的目标是覆盖 200,000 名研究人员，是我们 7 月份试点启动时宣布的目标的两倍。

我们将继续向参与者了解申请流程、他们所需的功能以及帮助他们在研究中使用这些工具的支持。这些反馈将帮助我们完善计划并塑造未来的轮次。

### 支持跨领域的研究人员

不同的科学领域会以不同的方式使用人工智能，研究人员需要不同种类和水平的支持。我们正在与科学界合作，了解这些需求，并围绕它们制定我们的工具、培训和计划。

我们的支持还包括帮助科学界将人工智能生成的结果转化为更深入的理解和新发现。在数学方面，我们向西蒙斯基金会的一项新计划捐赠了 500 万美元，以帮助数学家检查、理解人工智能产生的结果并以此为基础。

我们还为研究人员和机构提供不同的方式来访问我们的工具。面向学术研究人员的 ChatGPT 只是我们帮助研究人员访问先进人工智能工具的一种方式。

通过 ChatGPT Edu，大学可以让其校园社区访问 ChatGPT 进行研究、教学和学习，并提供用于分析数据的工具和用于管理访问的管理控制。

对于从事生物学工作的研究人员来说，GPT‑Rosalind 汇集了专业的生物推理以及对科学工具和数据库的访问。 Rosalind 学术计划帮助将这些功能引入美国大学符合条件的实验室，免费提供最多 30 个席位，为期长达 12 个月。访问 GPT‑Rosalind 需要通过我们的可信访问流程获得批准。

请访问我们的研究人员访问指南，了解有关 ChatGPT Edu、GPT‑Rosalind 和面向学术研究人员的 ChatGPT 的更多信息。

随着这些努力的不断发展，研究人员的经验将帮助我们了解我们的工具在哪里有用、在哪里不足以及需要哪些支持。我们将利用这些反馈来改进我们的项目、开发培训和学习资源，并为研究人员相互交流方法创造机会。

我们的目标是为更多研究人员提供工具和支持来追求雄心勃勃的问题，并随着他们的研究和我们能力的发展不断改进这种支持。

了解有关该计划的更多信息。

Our goal is to give more researchers the tools and support to pursue ambitious questions—and to keep improving that support as their research and our capabilities evolve.
