title_zh: 数十亿安全保险资金如何押注于人工智能债务
summary_zh: 美国寿险业AI债持仓半年暴增24%至852亿美元，且呈现出通过SPV绕道借贷的复杂化趋势，引发金融稳定性监管担忧
article_content_zh:
虽然这仅占人寿保险公司总债务的 2.1%，但其风险预计将迅速增长。人寿保险公司可以持有高达 1850 亿美元的人工智能资产。据穆迪称，预计将在明年年底前完成投资。

人寿保险公司持有 A.I. 约 15% 的股份。根据巴克莱最近的估计，截至 6 月 30 日的数据中心债务。

这些债务投资带有多重风险。其一，只有 Nvidia、Meta、Alphabet、SpaceX、Anthropic 和 OpenAI 等少数科技公司为这些交易提供担保，风险集中。科技公司也有很多方法可以摆脱这些人工智能。如果项目的开发被延迟。

德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校法学院助理教授安德鲁·格拉纳托（Andrew Granato）表示：“人寿保险行业现在实际上支持了人工智能行业的大部分。”他研究了私募股权与保险公司之间的重叠。

“我们都应该关注这一点，尤其是在债务交易变得更加不透明的情况下，”他补充道。

让大量的保险资金投入有风险的人工智能成为可能。交易者是穆迪和标准普尔全球评级等信用评级机构。他们为这个迅速扩大的债务池提供了相对安全的信用评级，这些评级符合保险公司投资特定资产所需的标准。

这些活动大部分是由隶属于保险公司的华尔街巨头公司推动的，有时还帮助管理他们的投资。购买了部分 xAI 债务的 Athene 是华尔街阿波罗公司的子公司。

“雅典娜为我们认为人工智能生态系统中最安全、最有防御能力的部分提供资金，”阿波罗发言人在一份声明中表示。

xAI 的所有者 SpaceX 没有回应置评请求。

保险公司被人工智能所吸引。债务，因为它被认为是安全的，但仍然提供跑赢市场的回报。人工智能。反过来，公司也开始将人寿保险行业视为支持其数据中心扩展的关键。

上个月，数据中心公司 CoreWeave 的联合创始人兼首席开发官 Brannin McBee 告诉英国《金融时报》，他将保险公司视为未来借款的“无限”资金来源。

“就像，这就是世界上保险部分的所有资金，”他说。

他的言论吓坏了 CoreWeave 的投资者和贷方。第二天，其股票大幅下跌，债券价格也迅速下跌。由于投资者对债务风险更加警惕，其他人工智能相关公司和数据中心项目的债券最近几周也有所下跌。

CoreWeave 的发言人拒绝发表评论。

Ares Management 是大声表达担忧的贷方之一，该公司是最大的私人信贷公司之一，拥有 6,910 亿美元的资产。

在最近的一份时事通讯中，阿瑞斯认为，科技巨头已经找到了通过“双面交易”让保险公司参与高风险债务交易的方法。科技公司正在创建复杂的金融实体，这些实体被赋予与科技公司本身几乎相同的安全信用评级。但是，阿瑞斯表示，与科技巨头直接借钱相比，这些实体偿还债务的保证更少。

该公司在时事通讯中写道：“有时，结构复杂性和金融工程并不是用来改善风险，而是用来隐藏风险。”

Ares 引用了位于路易斯安那州里奇兰教区的 Meta 数据中心作为一个典型的例子。

Meta 并未完全拥有该项目，而是仅持有 20% 的股份，而投资公司 Blue Owl 则拥有其余股份。

然而，由于 Meta 提供的担保，S&P Global 对该项目 270 亿美元的债务的评级仅比 Meta 强劲的企业评级低一级。其中包括 20 年 280 亿美元的租赁担保，或者如果 Meta 离开则寻找租户。

这一评级为人寿保险公司打开了大门，据穆迪称，寿险公司为本次交易提供了 34 亿美元的资金。

但 Meta 并不承诺偿还该项目投资者的债务。 Meta 发言人在一份声明中写道，“Meta 不保证偿还债券。”

蓝猫头鹰发言人在一份声明中表示：“当机构投资者和保险公司购买这些债务时，他们并不是在承担隐性风险。他们购买的是世界上一些最强企业信用的合同义务。”

另一个例子是，Meta 在 3 月份签署了一项采购 A.I. 的协议。四个数据中心的 CoreWeave 计算能力。

当 CoreWeave 寻求与这些项目相关的 85 亿美元贷款的评级时，评级机构关注的是 Meta 的强劲信用评级，而不是 CoreWeave 的垃圾级信用评级，并给予该交易最高评级之一。根据标准普尔市场情报 (S&P Market Intelligence) 的数据，保险公司也是 CoreWeave 项目债务的买家。

但投资者越来越质疑像 Meta 这样的大公司是否值得如此高的评级。

哥伦比亚商学院教授 Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh 表示：“这些公司不再像以前那样安全了。” “他们在玩这个游戏，可以假装自己没有这些责任。”

例如，Meta 已签署了 3560 亿美元的租赁合同，其中包括尚未启动的数据中心。这一数额是该公司在最新季度报告中报告的 840 亿美元债务的四倍。 Meta 已承诺追加 4550 亿美元的交易，用于购买芯片、其他基础设施和硬件，该协议无法取消。

上个月，标准普尔全球宣布将 Meta 的 2027 年信用评级展望从稳定调整为负面，理由是未来租赁量激增以及 Meta 将人工智能转化为能力的不确定性。支出转化为收入。不过目前，Meta 的评级保持不变。

标准普尔全球评级公司专注于 Meta 的分析师 Naveen Sarma 在接受采访时表示，他的公司并不将未来的租赁承诺视为现有债务，因为 Meta 在开始使用数据中心之前不必开始支付租赁费用。

Meta 发言人表示，该公司“谨此表示不同意”标准普尔的前景。 “我们看到了重要的产品和商业机会，这支持了我们非常强大的信用状况，”他说。

穆迪在最近的一篇论文中承认了科技公司账簿上所有债务累积的风险。但穆迪发言人表示，在对公司信用进行评级时，该公司并不将这些承诺视为现有债务。

至于 SpaceX，该公司的审计师确定，该公司今年早些时候打算从账簿中借钱购买芯片的资金最终应记录为公司债务。

但马斯克和华尔街继续寻找创新方法来继续借贷。本月早些时候，马斯克筹集了 400 亿美元来资助更多人工智能项目。通过一家金融实体筹措资金，该实体将暂时将这笔债务从 SpaceX 的账簿中剔除。

马斯克在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示，SpaceX 可以完成这笔交易，因为“我们是投资级的”。

article_content_en:
When Elon Musk needed help financing a large purchase of artificial intelligence chips earlier this year, Wall Street offered an elegant solution.

Mr. Musk and his team of advisers created a financial entity that would borrow billions to buy the chips and then lease them back to xAI, his artificial intelligence effort. This way, xAI wasn’t technically the borrower, which helped make its official debt load look smaller to investors.

To help fund this complicated arrangement, $2.4 billion of the debt was sold to an insurance company called Athene, which manages life insurance policies and annuities for retirees, according to a Moody’s Ratings report.

The deal was part of an increasingly popular playbook: tapping insurance companies, which are historically among the most cautious investors, to make loans to tech titans like Mr. Musk and further fuel the A.I. boom.

The amount of A.I. debt being held by insurance companies has soared this year. U.S. life insurers, including some of the largest like Athene and Corebridge Financial, held $85.2 billion in A.I. debt as of June 30, up 24 percent from six months prior, according to Moody’s.

While this accounts for just 2.1 percent of life insurers’ total debt, their exposure is expected to grow quickly. Life insurers could hold up to $185 billion of A.I. investments by the end of next year, according to Moody’s.

Life insurers owned about 15 percent of A.I. data center debt as of June 30, according to a recent estimate by Barclay’s.

These debt investments carry multiple risks. For one, only a few technology companies, including Nvidia, Meta, Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI, are providing the guarantees for these deals, which concentrates the risk. There are also often ways for tech companies to walk away from these A.I. projects if their development is delayed.

“The life insurance industry is now in effect backing large swaths of the A.I. industry,” said Andrew Granato, an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin School of Law, who has studied the overlap between private equity and insurers.

“We should all be concerned about this, especially as the debt deals get more opaque,” he added.

Making possible this flood of insurance money into risky A.I. deals are credit rating agencies like Moody’s and S&P Global Ratings. They have blessed this rapidly expanding pool of debt with relatively safe credit ratings, which meet the criteria that insurance firms need to invest in a particular asset.

Much of this activity is being driven by giant Wall Street firms that are affiliated with insurance companies and sometimes help manage their investments. Athene, which bought some of the xAI debt, is a subsidiary of the Wall Street firm Apollo.

“Athene finances what we view as the safest and most defensible parts of the A.I. ecosystem,” an Apollo spokeswoman said in a statement.

SpaceX, which owns xAI, did not respond to a request for comment.

Insurers are attracted to A.I. debt because it is regarded as secure, but still offers market-beating returns. A.I. companies, in turn, have come to view the life insurance industry as crucial to supporting their data center expansions.

Last month, Brannin McBee, a co-founder and chief development officer of the data center company CoreWeave, told The Financial Times that he viewed insurers as an “unlimited” source of capital for future borrowing.

“Like, that’s all the money in the world that sits in the insurance tranche,” he said.

His comments spooked CoreWeave’s investors and lenders. Its stock dropped sharply the next day and the price of its bonds fell quickly, too. The bonds of other A.I.-related companies and data center projects have also dropped in recent weeks as investors have become more wary of debt risks.

A spokesman for CoreWeave declined to comment.

One of the lenders loudly voicing concerns is Ares Management, one of the largest private credit firms with $691 billion in assets.

In a recent newsletter, Ares argues that tech giants have found ways to bring insurers into risky debt deals with “two-faced transactions.” The tech companies are creating complex financial entities that are being assigned nearly the same secure credit ratings as the tech companies themselves. But, Ares said, there are fewer guarantees that these entities will repay the debt than if the tech giants had borrowed the money directly.

“Sometimes structural complexity and financial engineering are not used to improve risk, but to hide it,” the firm wrote in the newsletter.

Ares cites Meta’s data center in Richland Parish, La., as a prime example.

Rather than owning the project outright, Meta took only a 20 percent stake while the investment firm Blue Owl owns the rest.

Yet, S&P Global was comfortable enough to rate the project’s $27 billion in debt just one notch below Meta’s strong corporate rating because of guarantees the tech company provided. Those included a $28 billion lease guarantee over 20 years or to find a tenant if Meta walked away.

That rating helped open the door for life insurers, which, according to Moodys, funded $3.4 billion of the deal.

But Meta is not promising to repay the project’s debt investors. In a statement, a Meta spokesperson wrote that “Meta has not guaranteed repayment of the bonds.”

In a statement, a Blue Owl spokesman said: “When institutional investors and insurers buy this debt, they are not taking a hidden risk. They are buying exposure to the contractual obligations of some of the strongest corporate credits in the world.”

In another example, Meta signed a deal in March to procure A.I. computing capacity from CoreWeave in four data centers.

When CoreWeave sought a rating for an $8.5 billion loan tied to these projects, the rating agencies looked at Meta’s strong credit rating rather than CoreWeave’s, which is in junk territory, and gave the deal one of its highest ratings. Insurers were buyers of the CoreWeave projects’ debt also, according to S&P Market Intelligence.

But investors are increasingly questioning whether giant companies like Meta deserve such high ratings.

“These companies are not as safe as they once were,” Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, a professor at Columbia Business School, said. “They’re sort of playing this game where they can pretend like they don’t have these liabilities.”

Meta, for example, has signed $356 billion in leases, including for data centers that it has not yet started. That amount is four times larger than the $84 billion of debt that it reported in its latest quarterly filing. Meta has committed an additional $455 billion in deals to buy chips, other infrastructure and hardware, agreements that it cannot cancel.

Last month, S&P Global announced it had revised its 2027 outlook for Meta’s credit rating to negative from stable, citing the surge in future leases and uncertainty about Meta’s ability to turn A.I. spending into revenue. For now, though, Meta’s rating remains the same.

In an interview, Naveen Sarma, an S&P Global Ratings analyst focused on Meta, said his firm did not consider a future lease commitment as existing debt because Meta does not have to start making the lease payments until it starts using the data center.

The Meta spokesperson said the company “respectfully disagrees” with S&P’s outlook. “We see significant product and business opportunities ahead of us, supporting our very strong credit profile,” he said.

Moody’s acknowledged the risk of all the debt accumulating off the tech companies’ books in a recent paper. But the firm does not consider those commitments to be existing debt when rating a company’s credit, a Moody’s spokeswoman said.

As for SpaceX, the company’s auditors determined the money that it intended to borrow off its books earlier this year to buy chips should ultimately be recorded as company debt.

But Mr. Musk and Wall Street continue to find innovative ways to keep borrowing. Earlier this month, Mr. Musk raised $40 billion to finance more A.I. chips through a financial entity that will keep that debt off SpaceX’s books for now.

SpaceX could pull off the deal, Mr. Musk said in a post on X, because “we’re investment grade.”

author: New York Post
article_content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump said Monday he “would not mind” if Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO, claiming that the tech boss had “learned a big lesson” from his romantic entanglement with a suspected Chinese spy.

“I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that,” Trump told reporters as he left the White House for a trip to the Philippines and China in response to a Financial Times report that Huang had put together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his return.

Huang stepped down Friday following revelations of a series of extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at a Singapore-based Nvidia client suspected by US intelligence of being in the pay of Beijing.

“I don’t know that she’s a Chinese spy,” Trump said of Alice Huang, reflecting reported internal dissension over the intelligence community’s assessment.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

title: Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop
title_en: Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop
author: Duncan Riley
article_content:
A new report out today from Google LLC’s Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that for the first time, attackers have used an artificial intelligence framework running with no human in the loop to turn security patches into exploits.

Called exploit_agent, the framework turned up on an exposed staging server, where it was wired into several frontier and locally hosted large language models. Its job, according to GTIG, is continuous comparison of popular web application code before and after each patch announcement. Once a likely flaw is identified, the exploit it drafts is executed automatically.

Data taken from victims was sitting on the same server, alongside scripts for brute-forcing, installing webshells and even removing webshells left by rival attackers. Victim telemetry suggests the operator was most interested in French websites tied to media, entertainment and education. Written in Russian, one comment in the framework’s configuration file tells whoever set it up to enter the keys “right here, not in the chat.”

In the previous edition of the quarterly tracker two months ago, GTIG said it had not observed fully autonomous attack pipelines deployed against targets in the wild. That changed over the past quarter, according to the new report, titled “Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold.” Because the source material for a patched flaw is finite, GTIG believes attackers may find it more efficient to point LLMs at n-day vulnerabilities than to hunt for zero-days.

How quickly the gap between disclosure and a working exploit can close shows in the case of two flaws in print management servers from PaperCut Software Pty Ltd., chained together and exploited as zero-days in late August. Security researchers and Huntress Labs Inc. used large language models to generate working exploits within a day of disclosure.

A campaign tracked by GreyNoise Intelligence Inc. four days after disclosure is believed to have relied on LLMs to build its exploits before it hit hundreds of organizations. One foothold in that campaign reached domain administrator within minutes, GreyNoise found.

Elsewhere, open-source agentic penetration testing frameworks are being used to automate discrete steps of live intrusions. During one intrusion against the U.S. aerospace sector, a threat actor was observed using the multi-agent framework CAIRN.

Another actor ran a customized platform built on PentAGI between late August and early October to scan a wide range of organizations in Asia for vulnerabilities. For now, the noisy forensic trail left by unrestricted autonomous execution is said to make the frameworks easier to detect.

According to GTIG, influence operations now use models for far more than writing posts. Using cloud phone farms, a turnkey platform that one commercial contractor was building with help from the Gemini API is designed to run more than 100,000 social media accounts. To make generated photos pass as smartphone shots, prompts behind a separate platform, which targeted political sentiment across Europe and the Middle East, are said to have called for deliberate camera flaws.

Among government-backed actors, photos on the fake recruiter profiles that a suspected North Korean group tracked as UNC6836 used to approach cryptocurrency organizations in North America and Europe were found to carry Google’s SynthID watermarks. By way of altered.claude/settings.json files in internal code repositories, the group later rigged each launch of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code to download its SOMBERMEME backdoor.

Google said it disabled the accounts and assets tied to the Gemini misuse it found. Google DeepMind has also used the findings to strengthen its classifiers.

article_content_zh:
谷歌有限责任公司的谷歌威胁情报小组今天发布的一份新报告发现，攻击者首次使用无人参与的人工智能框架将安全补丁转化为漏洞。

该框架名为exploit_agent，出现在一个暴露的临时服务器上，它被连接到几个前沿和本地托管的大型语言模型中。据 GTIG 称，其工作是在每个补丁发布前后持续比较流行的 Web 应用程序代码。一旦发现可能的缺陷，它所起草的漏洞就会自动执行。

从受害者那里获取的数据与暴力破解、安装 Webshel​​l 甚至删除竞争对手留下的 Webshel​​l 的脚本一起位于同一服务器上。受害者遥测表明，该运营商对与媒体、娱乐和教育相关的法国网站最感兴趣。该框架的配置文件中的一条注释是用俄语写的，告诉设置它的人“就在这里，而不是在聊天中”输入按键。

在两个月前的上一期季度跟踪报告中，GTIG 表示，它没有观察到针对野外目标部署的完全自主的攻击管道。根据题为“代理威胁活动跨越重大阈值”的新报告，这种情况在过去一个季度发生了变化。由于修补缺陷的源材料是有限的，GTIG 认为攻击者可能会发现让法学硕士针对 n 天漏洞比寻找 0 天漏洞更有效。

PaperCut Software Pty Ltd. 的打印管理服务器中存在两个缺陷，这两个缺陷相互关联并在 8 月下旬被作为零日漏洞利用，这说明了披露与有效利用之间的差距能够以多快的速度缩小。安全研究人员和 Huntress Labs Inc. 使用大型语言模型在披露后的一天内生成了有效的漏洞。

GreyNoise Intelligence Inc. 在披露四天后跟踪的一项活动据信是依靠法学硕士来构建其漏洞，然后才袭击数百个组织。 GreyNoise 发现，该活动的一个立足点在几分钟内就到达了域管理员。

在其他地方，开源代理渗透测试框架被用来自动化实时入侵的离散步骤。在一次针对美国航空航天领域的入侵中，观察到威胁行为者使用多代理框架 CAIRN。

另一位参与者在 8 月底到 10 月初期间运行了一个基于 PentAGI 构建的定制平台，以扫描亚洲的各种组织是否存在漏洞。目前，不受限制的自主执行留下的嘈杂的取证痕迹据说使框架更容易被检测到。

GTIG 表示，影响力运营现在使用模型的用途远远超出了撰写帖子的范围。一家商业承包商在 Gemini API 的帮助下构建了一个统包平台，该平台使用云电话农场，旨在运行超过 100,000 个社交媒体帐户。为了让生成的照片像智能手机拍摄的照片一样，一个单独的平台背后的提示据称要求故意制造相机缺陷，该平台针对整个欧洲和中东的政治情绪。

在政府支持的参与者中，一个被怀疑为 UNC6836 的朝鲜组织用来接触北美和欧洲的加密货币组织的虚假招聘人员资料中的照片被发现带有谷歌的 SynthID 水印。通过内部代码存储库中的 alter.claude/settings.json 文件，该组织后来操纵了 Anthropic PBC 的 Claude Code 的每次启动，以下载其 SOMBERMEME 后门。

谷歌表示，它已禁用与发现的 Gemini 滥用行为相关的账户和资产。谷歌 DeepMind 还利用这些发现来增强其分类器。

paragraphs: A new report out today from Google LLC’s Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that for the first time, attackers have used an artificial intelligence framework running with no human in the loop to turn security patches into exploits.

Called exploit_agent, the framework turned up on an exposed staging server, where it was wired into several frontier and locally hosted large language models. Its job, according to GTIG, is continuous comparison of popular web application code before and after each patch announcement. Once a likely flaw is identified, the exploit it drafts is executed automatically.

Data taken from victims was sitting on the same server, alongside scripts for brute-forcing, installing webshells and even removing webshells left by rival attackers. Victim telemetry suggests the operator was most interested in French websites tied to media, entertainment and education. Written in Russian, one comment in the framework’s configuration file tells whoever set it up to enter the keys “right here, not in the chat.”

In the previous edition of the quarterly tracker two months ago, GTIG said it had not observed fully autonomous attack pipelines deployed against targets in the wild. That changed over the past quarter, according to the new report, titled “Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold.” Because the source material for a patched flaw is finite, GTIG believes attackers may find it more efficient to point LLMs at n-day vulnerabilities than to hunt for zero-days.

How quickly the gap between disclosure and a working exploit can close shows in the case of two flaws in print management servers from PaperCut Software Pty Ltd., chained together and exploited as zero-days in late August. Security researchers and Huntress Labs Inc. used large language models to generate working exploits within a day of disclosure.

A campaign tracked by GreyNoise Intelligence Inc. four days after disclosure is believed to have relied on LLMs to build its exploits before it hit hundreds of organizations. One foothold in that campaign reached domain administrator within minutes, GreyNoise found.

Elsewhere, open-source agentic penetration testing frameworks are being used to automate discrete steps of live intrusions. During one intrusion against the U.S. aerospace sector, a threat actor was observed using the multi-agent framework CAIRN.

Another actor ran a customized platform built on PentAGI between late August and early October to scan a wide range of organizations in Asia for vulnerabilities. For now, the noisy forensic trail left by unrestricted autonomous execution is said to make the frameworks easier to detect.

According to GTIG, influence operations now use models for far more than writing posts. Using cloud phone farms, a turnkey platform that one commercial contractor was building with help from the Gemini API is designed to run more than 100,000 social media accounts. To make generated photos pass as smartphone shots, prompts behind a separate platform, which targeted political sentiment across Europe and the Middle East, are said to have called for deliberate camera flaws.

Among government-backed actors, photos on the fake recruiter profiles that a suspected North Korean group tracked as UNC6836 used to approach cryptocurrency organizations in North America and Europe were found to carry Google’s SynthID watermarks. By way of altered.claude/settings.json files in internal code repositories, the group later rigged each launch of Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code to download its SOMBERMEME backdoor.
Google said it disabled the accounts and assets tied to the Gemini misuse it found. Google DeepMind has also used the findings to strengthen its classifiers.

title: Cyber Startup Corma Raises $125 Million for Defensive AI Agents
title_en: Cyber Startup Corma Raises $125 Million for Defensive AI Agents

inline_images.caption: Cyber Startup Corma Raises $125 Million for Defensive AI Agents (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: Cyber Startup Corma Raises $125 Million for Defensive AI Agents (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: Cyber Startup Corma Raises $125 Million for Defensive AI Agents (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: Cyber Startup Corma Raises $125 Million for Defensive AI Agents

author: Angus Loten
article_content:
Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million to build automated agents that run on cyber-trained artificial-intelligence models.

Led by venture investor New Enterprise Associates, the Series A funding round comes three months after Corma emerged from stealth with $60 million in seed capital. NEA joins existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue. The latest round boosts Corma’s market valuation to $1 billion, the company said.

The same AI that is getting better at writing code is getting better at breaking it. Vulnerabilities are just another kind of bug, and agents can now exploit what they find end to end. Defense is a different problem: it means digging through audit logs, security events and network flows, correlating weak signals across systems and over long time horizons, and staying consistent across thousands of decisions in a row. Corma, a startup that trains its own foundation models for that work, has reached unicorn status three months after emerging from stealth.

Corma trains foundation models for defensive cybersecurity and deploys them as an AI workforce that works alongside enterprise security teams. A foundation model here means a base AI model trained at scale for a specific domain rather than adapted from a general-purpose one. According to Sequoia Capital, Corma trains its model with reinforcement learning on simulated enterprise networks that include their tools, telemetry and noise. The model is not a technology supplied to other security vendors. It powers Corma’s own workforce, which runs inside the security tools a customer already uses and carries out tasks from start to finish. In effect, Corma trains the model and places it with customers as AI staff. CEO Alon Pluda told Israeli outlet Calcalist, “We don’t replace anyone and we are not a product,” and said the company sells virtual human resources.

The company says coding models were never optimized for defensive work, so the progress that makes AI a better attacker barely moves defense. It is headquartered in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, and its team includes researchers from Google DeepMind and security experts from Israel’s Unit 8200.

Alon Pluda is co-founder and CEO. Sequoia Capital, which led Corma’s seed round, has described him as one of the most elite hackers in the world.

Corma announced a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation. NEA led the round, with existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue participating. It comes three months after Corma disclosed a $60 million seed led by Sequoia in August, bringing total funding to $185 million.

According to the company, demand has surged across the Fortune 100, Fortune 500 and Fortune Global 500 since it left stealth, and it has expanded server capacity 24x to keep up. It says some large enterprises already had the Corma workforce in place when “Black October,” a wave of critical vulnerabilities and breaches in widely used software, hit in October. Pluda said securing enough compute has been one of the company’s hardest problems. NEA partner Aaron Jacobson said Corma is building the intelligence layer defensive security needs, and called it the only company taking on the problem in a way that scales across organizations. Corma plans to use the new funds to scale its foundation models and compute, and said it will share its next-generation models soon.

Corma’s closest rivals are startups automating security operations with AI. 7AI raised a $130 million Series A, which it billed as the largest in cybersecurity history, led by Index Ventures. Torq raised a $140 million Series D and became a unicorn. Exaforce raised a $125 million Series B for its agentic SOC, bringing total funding to $200 million. While they ship agents and platforms that automate security operations, Corma pitches an AI workforce driven by its own model instead of software. The comparison Corma itself draws is with general-purpose frontier models, which it argues are a poor fit for defensive work.

article_content_zh:
网络安全初创公司 Corma 筹集了 1.25 亿美元，用于构建在经过网络训练的人工智能模型上运行的自动化代理。

由风险投资者 New Enterprise Associates 领投的 A 轮融资是在 Corma 凭借 6000 万美元的种子资本脱颖而出的三个月后进行的。 NEA 加入了现有投资者红杉资本、Khosla Ventures 和 Coatue 的行列。该公司表示，最新一轮融资将 Corma 的市场估值提升至 10 亿美元。

越来越擅长编写代码的人工智能也越来越擅长破坏代码。漏洞只是另一种错误，代理现在可以端到端地利用他们发现的内容。防御是一个不同的问题：它意味着挖掘审计日志、安全事件和网络流，跨系统和长时间跨度关联微弱信号，并在连续数千个决策中保持一致。 Corma 是一家为这项工作训练自己的基础模型的初创公司，在走出隐秘状态三个月后已达到独角兽地位。

Corma 训练防御性网络安全的基础模型，并将其部署为与企业安全团队一起工作的人工智能劳动力。这里的基础模型是指针对特定领域进行大规模训练的基础人工智能模型，而不是改编自通用模型。据红杉资本称，Corma 在模拟企业网络上通过强化学习来训练其模型，其中包括其工具、遥测和噪声。该模型不是向其他安全供应商提供的技术。它为 Corma 自己的员工提供动力，这些员工在客户已经使用的安全工具内运行，并从头到尾执行任务。实际上，Corma 训练了模型并将其作为人工智能员工交给客户。首席执行官 Alon Pluda 告诉以色列媒体 Calcalist，“我们不会取代任何人，我们也不是产品”，并表示该公司出售虚拟人力资源。

该公司表示，编码模型从未针对防御工作进行过优化，因此使人工智能成为更好的攻击者的进步几乎无法推动防御。它的总部位于特拉维夫和旧金山，其团队包括来自谷歌 DeepMind 的研究人员和来自以色列 8200 部队的安全专家。

阿隆·普拉达 (Alon Pluda) 是联合创始人兼首席执行官。领投 Corma 种子轮融资的红杉资本将他描述为世界上最精英的黑客之一。

Corma 宣布完成 1.25 亿美元的 A 轮融资，估值为 10 亿美元。 NEA 领投此轮融资，现有投资者红杉资本、Khosla Ventures 和 Coatue 参与其中。三个月前，Corma 在 8 月份披露了由红杉资本领投的 6000 万美元种子资金，使总资金达到 1.85 亿美元。

据该公司称，自其退出以来，财富 100 强、财富 500 强和财富全球 500 强的需求激增，并且它已将服务器容量扩大了 24 倍以跟上。报告称，当“黑色十月”（广泛使用的软件中出现一系列严重漏洞和违规事件）10 月份袭来时，一些大型企业已经配备了 Corma 员工。 Pluda 表示，确保足够的计算能力一直是该公司最困难的问题之一。 NEA 合作伙伴 Aaron Jacobson 表示，Corma 正在构建情报层防御安全需求，并称其是唯一一家以跨组织规模的方式解决该问题的公司。 Corma 计划利用新资金扩展其基础模型和计算，并表示将很快分享其下一代模型。

Corma 最接近的竞争对手是利用人工智能实现安全运营自动化的初创公司。 7AI 筹集了 1.3 亿美元的 A 轮融资，据称这是网络安全历史上规模最大的一轮融资，由 Index Ventures 领投。 Torq 筹集了 1.4 亿美元的 D 轮融资，成为独角兽。 Exaforce 为其代理 SOC 筹集了 1.25 亿美元的 B 轮融资，使总资金达到 2 亿美元。虽然 Corma 提供自动化安全操作的代理和平台，但 Corma 却推出了由自己的模型而不是软件驱动的人工智能劳动力。 Corma 本身进行的比较是与通用前沿模型进行的比较，它认为该模型不太适合防御工作。

[Context & Motivation] The year-old startup's agents are custom-trained for defensive cybersecurity — Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million ….
[Key Metrics] Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million to build automated agents that run on cyber-trained artificial-intelligence models.
paragraphs: Cybersecurity startup Corma raised $125 million to build automated agents that run on cyber-trained artificial-intelligence models.

Led by venture investor New Enterprise Associates, the Series A funding round comes three months after Corma emerged from stealth with $60 million in seed capital. NEA joins existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue. The latest round boosts Corma’s market valuation to $1 billion, the company said.

The same AI that is getting better at writing code is getting better at breaking it. Vulnerabilities are just another kind of bug, and agents can now exploit what they find end to end. Defense is a different problem: it means digging through audit logs, security events and network flows, correlating weak signals across systems and over long time horizons, and staying consistent across thousands of decisions in a row. Corma, a startup that trains its own foundation models for that work, has reached unicorn status three months after emerging from stealth.

Corma trains foundation models for defensive cybersecurity and deploys them as an AI workforce that works alongside enterprise security teams. A foundation model here means a base AI model trained at scale for a specific domain rather than adapted from a general-purpose one. According to Sequoia Capital, Corma trains its model with reinforcement learning on simulated enterprise networks that include their tools, telemetry and noise. The model is not a technology supplied to other security vendors. It powers Corma’s own workforce, which runs inside the security tools a customer already uses and carries out tasks from start to finish. In effect, Corma trains the model and places it with customers as AI staff. CEO Alon Pluda told Israeli outlet Calcalist, “We don’t replace anyone and we are not a product,” and said the company sells virtual human resources.

The company says coding models were never optimized for defensive work, so the progress that makes AI a better attacker barely moves defense. It is headquartered in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, and its team includes researchers from Google DeepMind and security experts from Israel’s Unit 8200.
Alon Pluda is co-founder and CEO. Sequoia Capital, which led Corma’s seed round, has described him as one of the most elite hackers in the world.

Corma announced a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation. NEA led the round, with existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures and Coatue participating. It comes three months after Corma disclosed a $60 million seed led by Sequoia in August, bringing total funding to $185 million.

According to the company, demand has surged across the Fortune 100, Fortune 500 and Fortune Global 500 since it left stealth, and it has expanded server capacity 24x to keep up. It says some large enterprises already had the Corma workforce in place when “Black October,” a wave of critical vulnerabilities and breaches in widely used software, hit in October. Pluda said securing enough compute has been one of the company’s hardest problems. NEA partner Aaron Jacobson said Corma is building the intelligence layer defensive security needs, and called it the only company taking on the problem in a way that scales across organizations. Corma plans to use the new funds to scale its foundation models and compute, and said it will share its next-generation models soon.

Corma’s closest rivals are startups automating security operations with AI. 7AI raised a $130 million Series A, which it billed as the largest in cybersecurity history, led by Index Ventures. Torq raised a $140 million Series D and became a unicorn. Exaforce raised a $125 million Series B for its agentic SOC, bringing total funding to $200 million. While they ship agents and platforms that automate security operations, Corma pitches an AI workforce driven by its own model instead of software. The comparison Corma itself draws is with general-purpose frontier models, which it argues are a poor fit for defensive work.

title: Audible is trying to make it easier to find audiobooks you’ll actually like
title_en: Audible is trying to make it easier to find audiobooks you’ll actually like

inline_images.caption: Audible audio discovery hero
inline_images.alt: Audible audio discovery hero

author: Jess Weatherbed
article_content:
Audible is introducing an AI-assisted synopsis feature that’s designed to help users determine whether they’ll enjoy an audiobook before they jump in and start listening to it. The new audio discovery feature combines audiobook samples, AI overviews, and author commentary to give users more information before choosing their next story, in addition to recommended audiobook collections that are personalized to individual listening tastes.

Audio discovery provides a soundbite synopsis, with the aim of preventing Audible users from having to research titles on other platforms. The feature plays users a snippet of the audiobook and a brief AI-generated overview including its themes and listener reactions, drawing from reviews and other publicly available data. It can also include commentary from an author or Audible editor, which is pulled directly from past Audible interviews.

“Picking your next listen should feel like getting a tip from a friend. With audio discovery, you’ll get a quick audio take on why the title might be right for you, from our editors, fellow listeners, or even the author,” Audible chief product and analytics officer Andy Tsao said in the announcement. “Some of the best listening experiences are those rare finds or hidden gems, and we want to make those great discoveries happen more often and more easily.”

Audio discovery is rolling out on select English-language titles in the US, with plans to eventually expand to other regions.

Audible is also using AI to personalize audiobook collections around users’ listening tastes, in an effort to make titles that don’t appear on best-selling lists easier to discover. Like audio discovery, these personalized collections are rolling out to customers in the US, and also include commentary from Audible’s editors.

These are the latest AI-powered features that Audible is introducing in an effort to attract new users and fend off growing competition from rival platforms like Spotify. As part of this update, Audible is also expanding two beta features: Ask a Question, which allows users to ask AI about characters, plot points, references, and more; and Recaps, which provides spoiler-free audio summaries of what the user has already listened to. These are now available for a “select set” of additional English-language titles in the US, according to Audible, with a broader rollout planned to start in December.

article_content_zh:
Audible 推出了一项人工智能辅助概要功能，旨在帮助用户在开始收听有声读物之前确定他们是否会喜欢有声读物。新的音频发现功能结合了有声读物样本、人工智能概述和作者评论，除了根据个人聆听品味个性化推荐的有声读物合集之外，还可以在选择下一个故事之前为用户提供更多信息。

音频发现提供了原声摘要，旨在防止 Audible 用户在其他平台上研究标题。该功能向用户播放有声读物的片段以及人工智能生成的简短概述，包括其主题和听众的反应，这些概述来自评论和其他公开数据。它还可以包括作者或 Audible 编辑的评论，这些评论直接摘自过去的 Audible 采访。

Audible 首席产品官 Andy Tsao 在声明中表示：“选择你的下一首歌曲应该感觉就像从朋友那里得到提示。通过音频发现，你可以从我们的编辑、其他听众甚至作者那里快速了解为什么这个标题可能适合你。” “一些最好的聆听体验是那些罕见的发现或隐藏的宝石，我们希望让这些伟大的发现更频繁、更容易地发生。”

音频发现功能正在美国的部分英语游戏中推出，并计划最终扩展到其他地区。

Audible 还利用人工智能根据用户的聆听品味个性化有声读物收藏，努力让未出现在畅销书排行榜上的图书更容易被发现。与音频发现一样，这些个性化合集正在向美国客户推出，其中还包括 Audible 编辑的评论。

这些是 Audible 推出的最新人工智能功能，旨在吸引新用户并抵御 Spotify 等竞争对手平台日益激烈的竞争。作为本次更新的一部分，Audible 还扩展了两个测试版功能：提问，允许用户向 AI 询问角色、情节点、参考资料等； Recaps，它提供用户已经听过的内容的无剧透音频摘要。据 Audible 称，这些内容现已在美国推出“精选集”的其他英语游戏，并计划于 12 月开始更广泛的推广。

title: Google Maps can now create trip itineraries for you
title_en: Google Maps can now create trip itineraries for you

inline_images.caption: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber
inline_images.alt: Amazon’s Zoox robotaxis are now available via Uber

author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries for you and provide real-time details about each stop. The update, which is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app, lets you plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days.

As an example, Google says you can use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping, or have it create a schedule for a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. From there, Ask Maps will generate a day-by-day schedule with a list of stops, while also showing your route and numbered pins for each location on the map. You can share the itinerary with friends or family members, as well as export it to Google Docs on desktop.

You can ask Maps to show your trip schedule before you leave, or select the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. Along with directions, Google Maps will display real-time information about traffic, a location’s hours, and more. You can also view “know before you go” details about parking, car charging, weather conditions, potential delays, and tolls during your trip.

In addition to trip planning, you can now use Ask Maps to find specific beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments, and have it call the locations for you. You can also use Ask Maps to find saved places on your list by asking something like, “Which spots on saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”

Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Trip-planning and saved list search is rolling out to the more than 200 countries where Ask Maps is available, while “know before you go” tips and appointment-finding are launching in the US to start.

谷歌正在为地图推出一项新的人工智能旅行规划功能，该功能允许该应用程序为您创建自定义行程并提供有关每个站点的实时详细信息。该更新将在应用程序内的 Gemini 支持的 Ask Maps 聊天机器人中推出，让您可以计划一日郊游或为期数天的旅行。

举例来说，谷歌表示，你可以使用 Ask Maps 来计划假日购物的一日游，或者让它为三天的公路旅行制定时间表，其中包括沿海徒步旅行和海滨用餐。从那里，Ask Maps 将生成包含停靠点列表的每日时间表，同时还会在地图上显示您的路线和每个位置的编号图钉。您可以与朋友或家人分享行程，也可以将其导出到桌面上的 Google 文档。

您可以在出发前要求地图显示您的行程安排，或者在聊天记录中选择“行程”徽章。除了路线之外，谷歌地图还将显示有关交通、地点时间等的实时信息。您还可以查看“出发前了解”有关旅途中停车、汽车充电、天气状况、潜在延误和通行费的详细信息。

除了旅行计划之外，您现在还可以使用“询问地图”来查找特定的美容、宠物护理、汽车和家庭维修预约，并让它为您呼叫地点。您还可以使用“询问地图”来查找列表中保存的地点，方法是询问“我的列表中保存的哪些地点在接下来的 30 分钟内可供 5 个人使用？”

Google 正在将 Ask Maps 扩展到欧洲 30 多个国家，包括西班牙、德国和英国。旅行计划和已保存列表搜索功能正在向 200 多个提供“地图查询”功能的国家/地区推出，而“行前了解”提示和预约查找功能则首先在美国推出。

paragraphs: Google is launching a new AI trip-planning feature for Maps that allows the app to create custom itineraries for you and provide real-time details about each stop. The update, which is rolling out to the Gemini-powered Ask Maps chatbot inside the app, lets you plan a one-day outing or a trip spanning several days.

As an example, Google says you can use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping, or have it create a schedule for a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. From there, Ask Maps will generate a day-by-day schedule with a list of stops, while also showing your route and numbered pins for each location on the map. You can share the itinerary with friends or family members, as well as export it to Google Docs on desktop.

You can ask Maps to show your trip schedule before you leave, or select the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. Along with directions, Google Maps will display real-time information about traffic, a location’s hours, and more. You can also view “know before you go” details about parking, car charging, weather conditions, potential delays, and tolls during your trip.

In addition to trip planning, you can now use Ask Maps to find specific beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments, and have it call the locations for you. You can also use Ask Maps to find saved places on your list by asking something like, “Which spots on saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”

Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Trip-planning and saved list search is rolling out to the more than 200 countries where Ask Maps is available, while “know before you go” tips and appointment-finding are launching in the US to start.

You can also view “know before you go” details about parking, car charging, weather conditions, potential delays, and tolls during your trip.

title: AI startup Numa raises $45 million to help car dealerships leave the paperwork behind
title_en: AI startup Numa raises $45 million to help car dealerships leave the paperwork behind
title_zh: 汽车经销商客户服务 AI 平台 Numa 完成 4500 万美元 C 轮融资，投后估值达 5 亿美元
author: Camila Grigera Naón
article_content:
Artificial intelligence promises to untangle the messy workflows that have long plagued legacy industries. One startup is bringing that pitch to car dealerships. On Monday, Oakland-based company Numa announced a $45 million Series C round to build out an AI operating system designed to handle the daily grind of dealership customer service, from answering calls and booking appointments to keeping customers updated on their cars.

It works like this: Numa’s AI agents connect to a dealership’s software to check inventory down to a car’s trim and features, pull repair updates and log sales leads alongside conversation transcripts. The platform also handles routine warranty paperwork and flags exchanges that may signal an unhappy customer for managers to review.

“Think about things like filling out warranty paperwork. That is a drudgery of a job that nobody wants to do, and people do it poorly. You can apply an AI and do it instantly,” Numa CEO Tasso Roumeliotis told Fortune.

Blue Cloud Ventures led the round, bringing Numa’s total funding to $96 million. Threshold Ventures, Costanoa Ventures, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures, Mitsui and Tokio Marine also participated. Founded in 2017, Numa previously raised seed and Series A funding from investors including Draper Fisher Jurvetson. The latest round valued Numa at $500 million after the investment, according to a source familiar with the company.

Numa’s pitch comes as more companies put AI agents to work. In a survey of roughly 2,100 senior leaders across 20 countries and industries ranging from automotive to healthcare, accounting and consulting firm KPMG found that 34% reported widespread employee adoption of AI agents in the third quarter of 2026, up from 25% in the first quarter.

For Roumeliotis, Numa began with a familiar team and a new problem to solve.

He had previously built Location Labs, a mobile technology company that tapped into the early spread of GPS-enabled cellphones to help people track one another’s locations. After selling the business in 2015, he joined venture firm Draper Fisher Jurvetson as an entrepreneur-in-residence.

While he was there, former colleagues from Location Labs approached him with a proposition: They wanted to build another company together. The group included engineers, product specialists and executives who had taken on bigger roles under Roumeliotis.

In 2017, they launched Number AI to help small businesses receive and respond to texts through their existing landline numbers, using natural language processing to bring newer technology to businesses still relying on older tools.

But as they worked with car dealerships, they found problems that went beyond missed messages. Employees juggled calls, paperwork and manual follow-ups, leaving customers waiting. The team narrowed its focus to the automotive industry and renamed the company Numa.

Blue Cloud Ventures also saw an opportunity in dealerships still relying on older software.

“I look at the auto dealership… as a little bit like jumbo shrimp. It’s a massive niche,” Mir Arif, the venture capital firm’s managing partner, told Fortune. “All of them [are still] working off legacy software or literally pen and paper.”

Today, the company has about 160 employees across its Bay Area headquarters, a sales and marketing office in Kansas City and an AI development office in Montreal. More than 1,500 dealerships in the U.S. and Canada use its software, including Longo Toyota, Norm Reeves Honda and Gold Coast Cadillac.
article_content_zh:
人工智能有望理顺长期困扰传统行业的繁琐业务流程，一家初创公司正将这一方案落地于汽车经销行业。周一，总部位于加州奥克兰的 Numa 公司宣布完成 4500 万美元 C 轮融资，用于构建专为汽车经销商日常客户服务打造的 AI 操作系统，覆盖接听电话、预约保养以及向车主实时同步维修进展等全流程业务。

其运作模式如下：Numa 的 AI 智能体可直接与经销商现有的业务系统无缝集成，精准核验具体到车辆配置与功能特性的库存数据，调取维保进度记录，并将对话实录与销售线索自动同步沉淀。该平台还支持自动处理常规保修单据与文书流转，并在监测到车主可能存在不满情绪时及时标记，供管理人员复核干预。

“以填写质保文书这类工作为例，那是一项枯燥繁琐、没人愿意做且极易出错的苦差事。现在通过引入 AI，这一切可以瞬间自动化完成。” Numa 首席执行官塔索·鲁梅里奥蒂斯（Tasso Roumeliotis）在接受《财富》（Fortune）专访时表示。

本轮融资由 Blue Cloud Ventures 领投，使 Numa 的累计融资额达到 9600 万美元。Threshold Ventures、Costanoa Ventures、Touring Capital、Gradient Ventures 以及三井物产（Mitsui）和东京海上日动（Tokio Marine）等机构参投。Numa 成立于 2017 年，早期曾获得包括 Draper Fisher Jurvetson 在内的风投机构天使轮与 A 轮投资。据知情人士透露，本轮投资完成后，Numa 的投后估值已达 5 亿美元。

Numa 融资方案的落地正值全球企业加速推进 AI 智能体部署之际。四大会计师事务所毕马威（KPMG）对遍布 20 个国家、涵盖汽车至医疗保健等多个行业的约 2100 名高管展开的调研显示，2026 年第三季度已有 34% 的企业广泛采用 AI 智能体，显著高于第一季度的 25%。

对于创始人鲁梅里奥蒂斯而言，Numa 的诞生是一支经验丰富的熟人团队与一个全新行业痛点的碰撞结合。

他此前曾创立移动技术企业 Location Labs，在配备 GPS 功能的早期智能手机普及阶段，利用定位技术帮助用户相互追踪地理位置。2015 年出售该公司后，他以驻场企业家身份加入了知名风投机构 Draper Fisher Jurvetson。

在驻场期间，原 Location Labs 的前同事主动找到他并提议：希望能够再次携手打造一家全新企业。这支核心团队包括曾在鲁梅里奥蒂斯麾下担任要职的顶尖工程师、产品专家与高管。

2017 年，他们创立了 Number AI，旨在通过现有的固定电话号码帮助小微企业收发短信，利用自然语言处理技术为仍在使用传统工具的商户提供现代化通讯赋能。

但在深入对接汽车经销商的过程中，团队发现行业面临的问题远不止错过沟通信息那么简单。一线员工常常在电话轰炸、海量文书与人工跟进之间疲于奔命，导致客户被迫长时间等待。团队随后将战略重心收窄至汽车行业，并将公司正式更名为 Numa。

领投方 Blue Cloud Ventures 同样在依然重度依赖老旧过时软件的汽车经销网络中嗅到了巨大商业机遇。

“在我看来，汽车经销网络有点像‘巨型虾’——它是一个体量庞大却极度专一的垂直利基市场，” 该风险投资机构执行管理合伙人米尔·阿里夫（Mir Arif）向《财富》表示，“几乎所有车商要么在使用二十年前的老旧软件，要么干脆还在依赖纸笔做账记录。”

如今，Numa 在旧金山湾区总部、堪萨斯城销售市场办公室以及蒙特利尔 AI 研发中心共拥有约 160 名员工。美国和加拿大超过 1500 家汽车经销门店已部署其 AI 软件，其中包括全美最大丰田车行 Longo Toyota、Norm Reeves Honda 以及 Gold Coast Cadillac 等标杆企业。

2017 年，他们创立了 Number AI，旨在通过现有的固定电话号码帮助小微企业收发短信，利用自然语言处理技术为仍在使用传统工具的商户提供现代化通讯赋能。
但在深入对接汽车经销商的过程中，团队发现行业面临的问题远不止错过沟通信息那么简单。一线员工常常在电话轰炸、海量文书与人工跟进之间疲于奔命，导致客户被迫长时间等待。团队随后将战略重心收窄至汽车行业，并将公司正式更名为 Numa。
领投方 Blue Cloud Ventures 同样在依然重度依赖老旧过时软件的汽车经销网络中嗅到了巨大商业机遇。
“在我看来，汽车经销网络有点像‘巨型虾’——它是一个体量庞大却极度专一的垂直利基市场，” 该风险投资机构执行管理合伙人米尔·阿里夫（Mir Arif）向《财富》表示，“几乎所有车商要么在使用二十年前的老旧软件，要么干脆还在依赖纸笔做账记录。”
如今，Numa 在旧金山湾区总部、堪萨斯城销售市场办公室以及蒙特利尔 AI 研发中心共拥有约 160 名员工。美国和加拿大超过 1500 家汽车经销门店已部署其 AI 软件，其中包括全美最大丰田车行 Longo Toyota、Norm Reeves Honda 以及 Gold Coast Cadillac 等标杆企业。
subheadings: Finding a ‘massive niche’
article_content_en:
Artificial intelligence promises to untangle the messy workflows that have long plagued legacy industries. One startup is bringing that pitch to car dealerships. On Monday, Oakland-based company Numa announced a $45 million Series C round to build out an AI operating system designed to handle the daily grind of dealership customer service, from answering calls and booking appointments to keeping customers updated on their cars.

It works like this: Numa’s AI agents connect to a dealership’s software to check inventory down to a car’s trim and features, pull repair updates and log sales leads alongside conversation transcripts. The platform also handles routine warranty paperwork and flags exchanges that may signal an unhappy customer for managers to review.

“Think about things like filling out warranty paperwork. That is a drudgery of a job that nobody wants to do, and people do it poorly. You can apply an AI and do it instantly,” Numa CEO Tasso Roumeliotis told Fortune.

Blue Cloud Ventures led the round, bringing Numa’s total funding to $96 million. Threshold Ventures, Costanoa Ventures, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures, Mitsui and Tokio Marine also participated. Founded in 2017, Numa previously raised seed and Series A funding from investors including Draper Fisher Jurvetson. The latest round valued Numa at $500 million after the investment, according to a source familiar with the company.

Numa’s pitch comes as more companies put AI agents to work. In a survey of roughly 2,100 senior leaders across 20 countries and industries ranging from automotive to healthcare, accounting and consulting firm KPMG found that 34% reported widespread employee adoption of AI agents in the third quarter of 2026, up from 25% in the first quarter.

For Roumeliotis, Numa began with a familiar team and a new problem to solve.

He had previously built Location Labs, a mobile technology company that tapped into the early spread of GPS-enabled cellphones to help people track one another’s locations. After selling the business in 2015, he joined venture firm Draper Fisher Jurvetson as an entrepreneur-in-residence.

While he was there, former colleagues from Location Labs approached him with a proposition: They wanted to build another company together. The group included engineers, product specialists and executives who had taken on bigger roles under Roumeliotis.

In 2017, they launched Number AI to help small businesses receive and respond to texts through their existing landline numbers, using natural language processing to bring newer technology to businesses still relying on older tools.

But as they worked with car dealerships, they found problems that went beyond missed messages. Employees juggled calls, paperwork and manual follow-ups, leaving customers waiting. The team narrowed its focus to the automotive industry and renamed the company Numa.

Blue Cloud Ventures also saw an opportunity in dealerships still relying on older software.

“I look at the auto dealership… as a little bit like jumbo shrimp. It’s a massive niche,” Mir Arif, the venture capital firm’s managing partner, told Fortune. “All of them [are still] working off legacy software or literally pen and paper.”

Today, the company has about 160 employees across its Bay Area headquarters, a sales and marketing office in Kansas City and an AI development office in Montreal. More than 1,500 dealerships in the U.S. and Canada use its software, including Longo Toyota, Norm Reeves Honda and Gold Coast Cadillac.

title: US Moves to Curb Remote Access to Nvidia's Advanced AI Chips
title_en: US Moves to Curb Remote Access to Nvidia's Advanced AI Chips
author: Maggie Eastland and Magan Crane
article_content:
WASHINGTON — The US Commerce Department moved on Monday to limit several countries from providing Chinese companies remote access to advanced artificial intelligence chips through overseas data centers, significantly expanding export controls to close a critical cloud computing loophole.

Under the interim final rule issued by the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the US government is establishing mandatory export license requirements for transferring advanced semiconductors and cloud compute capacity to five intermediary nations: Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil.

The new regulation directly targets data centers and neocloud operators globally that provide high aggregate Total Processing Performance (TPP) computing power to entities headquartered in China or Macau. Existing facilities catering to these clients have been granted a 90-day grace period to apply for licenses and transition operations into compliance.

The aggressive policy shift comes as Washington intensifies scrutiny over how restricted American technology reaches Chinese tech giants despite sweeping hardware export restrictions. In recent months, reports revealed that companies in China had increasingly bypassed physical chip embargos by renting computing clusters running Nvidia Corp. H100 and H200 accelerators stationed across Southeast Asia.

Enforcement concerns escalated following the sudden departure of former Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, amid congressional inquiries into transactions with Singapore-based provider Megaspeed International. Megaspeed had imported billions of dollars worth of Nvidia hardware between 2023 and 2025, leasing high-performance clusters to overseas clients including Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and ByteDance Ltd.

While renting cloud compute does not violate legacy rules restricted to physical hardware delivery, the Commerce Department determined that remote access effectively nullifies national security protections by enabling Chinese frontier labs to train advanced large language models using American supercomputing infrastructure.

Under the new framework, cloud providers must implement verified customer identity protocols and adhere to strict compute quotas. Global data center operators serving clients in designated restricted regions will be prohibited from dedicating more than 50% of aggregate cluster capacity to Chinese firms without explicit Commerce Department authorization.

The interim rule takes effect immediately with an open public comment period. Lawmakers on Capitol Hill welcomed the measure as an essential step toward hardening the semiconductor perimeter, with members of the House Foreign Affairs Committee indicating plans for oversight hearings on export control enforcement mechanisms.

article_content_zh:
华盛顿——美国商务部周一采取行动，限制多个国家通过海外数据中心向中国企业提供先进人工智能芯片的远程访问权限，大幅扩展了出口管制范围，以堵塞关键的云计算监管漏洞。

根据美国工业与安全局（BIS）发布的临时最终规则，美国政府对向五个中间国家转移先进半导体及云算力设立了强制性出口许可证要求：这五个国家分别是新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西。

该新规直接针对全球范围内向总部位于中国大陆或澳门的实体提供高聚合总处理性能（TPP）算力的数据中心与“新云”（neocloud）运营商。目前正为这些客户提供服务的基础设施获得了 90 天的宽限期，以便申请许可证并调整运营以符合监管要求。

这一强硬的政策转向出台之际，华盛顿正进一步强化对受限美国技术如何绕过全面硬件出口禁令流入中国科技巨头的审查。近几个月以来的多份报道显示，中国企业越来越多地通过租用部署在东南亚各地、配备英伟达 H100 和 H200 加速卡的计算集群，来规避实物芯片禁运。

随着英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋突然离任，执法层面的担忧急剧升温，国会正对英伟达与新加坡云算力提供商 Megaspeed International 之间的交易展开调查。Megaspeed 在 2023 年至 2025 年期间进口了价值数十亿美元的英伟达硬件，并将高性能计算集群转租给包括阿里巴巴集团和字节跳动在内的海外客户。

尽管租用云算力并不违反仅限于实物硬件交付的传统出口管制规则，但商务部认定，远程访问实质上削弱了国家安全保护屏障，使中国前沿实验室得以利用美国超算基础设施训练先进的大语言模型。

在新的监管框架下，云服务提供商必须执行经核验的客户身份识别协议（KYC），并恪守严格的算力配额。为指定受限地区客户提供服务的全球数据中心运营商，在未经商务部明确批准的情况下，严禁将超过 50% 的集群总算力分配给中国企业。

该临时规则立即生效，并开启公开征求意见期。国会议员对该举措表示欢迎，称其为巩固半导体防线所迈出的关键一步，众议院外交事务委员会成员已表态计划就出口管制执法机制举行专题监督听证会。

author: Joe Tidy
article_content:
A hacker has pleaded guilty to a string of online crimes, including trying to extort the makers of Grand Theft Auto 6 after stealing dozens of unfinished clips of the game.

21-year-old Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, carried out the hack in 2022, and was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.

But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.

On Monday, Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

Kurtaj breached Rockstar Games in 2022 whilst he was on bail for multiple other hacking offences and under police protection.

He was being housed in a Travelodge in Bicester to protect him from rival hackers who threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished and hugely anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6.

He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."

The company refused to cooperate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.79m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

At the time, doctors deemed Kurtaj unfit to stand in a traditional trial due to the severity of his autism, so instead he was given what is known as a trial of the facts.

The jury was asked to determine whether or not he committed the alleged acts - not if he did so with criminal intent.

In December 2023 the court ruled that he would remain at a secure hospital for life unless doctors deem him no longer a danger.

A routine assessment late last year deemed that he was now fit to stand a criminal trial which was scheduled to take place at Woolwich Crown Court.

But Kurtaj pleaded guilty to all offences.

He sat in the dock with short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt but no tie.

The now 21-year-old blinked frequently during the hearing and stood to confirm his name, and pled guilty to all counts with no visible emotion.

Those included hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber where he used social engineering techniques to gain access to internal systems.

The court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.

Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 from individual victims.

Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers whilst in custody including multiple biting incidents.

Whilst in prison he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

Kurtaj will be sentenced at a later date.

In the 2023 original trial, another Lapsus$member, who was 17, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court.

The 17-year-old, who could not be named at the time due to his age, was sentenced to an 18-month Youth Rehabilitation Order, including intense supervision and a ban on using VPNs online.

Earlier this year that same hacker, now named as Thalha Jubair, was jailed for five years and six months after continuing his cyber crime offences with another group known as Scattered Spider.

Amongst victims was Transport for London which was subjected to a disruptive cyber attack that caused around £39m of damage and caused chaos inside the firm.

article_content_zh:
一名黑客承认了一系列网络犯罪行为，包括在窃取了《侠盗猎车手 6》游戏的数十个未完成的剪辑后试图勒索该游戏的制作者。

来自牛津的 21 岁的 Arion Kurtaj 于 2022 年实施了黑客攻击，最初由于他患有严重的自闭症，他被判处在安全医院无限期住院。

但不同寻常的是，他随后被认为适合接受审判，并于一月份被释放到普通监狱。

周一，Kurtaj 在伍尔维奇刑事法庭承认了他在 16 岁和 17 岁时与黑客团伙 Lapsus$ 一起实施的 Rockstar Games 黑客事件以及其他几起黑客事件。

Kurtaj 于 2022 年入侵了 Rockstar Games，当时他因多次其他黑客犯罪而被保释并受到警方保护。

他被安置在比斯特的一家 Travelodge 旅馆中，以保护他免受竞争对手黑客的威胁，这些黑客威胁要攻击他，因为他被盗的比特币藏匿处。

电脑被没收后，Kurtaj 使用插入酒店房间电视的 Amazon Fire Stick 以及蓝牙键盘和鼠标对 Rockstar 进行了攻击。

他窃取了公司内部数据，包括 90 个剪辑，显示了未完成且备受期待的《侠盗猎车手 6》的近 60 分钟的游戏过程。

然后他闯入公司内部的 Slack 消息系统宣称：“如果 Rockstar 在 24 小时内没有通过 Telegram 联系我，我将开始发布源代码。”

该公司拒绝合作，因此他以 TeaPotUberHacker 用户名将剪辑和源代码发布到论坛上。

Rockstar Games 表示，该公司花费了 500 万美元（379 万英镑）从黑客攻击中恢复过来，再加上数千个小时的员工时间。

该公司还表示，这次泄露首次揭露了游戏中的一个可玩角色是女性——出于营销目的，该公司正在严密保守这一秘密。

当时，由于库尔塔吉患有严重的自闭症，医生认为他不适合参加传统的审判，因此他接受了所谓的事实审判。

陪审团被要求确定他是否实施了所指控的行为，而不是确定他是否具有犯罪意图。

2023 年 12 月，法院裁定他将终生留在安全的医院，除非医生认为他不再构成危险。

去年年底的例行评估认为，他现在适合接受定于伍尔维奇刑事法庭进行的刑事审判。

但库尔塔杰承认所有罪行。

他坐在被告席上，留着短发和蓬乱的胡须，穿着西装和扣上扣子的白衬衫，但没有打领带。

现年 21 岁的他在听证会上频繁眨眼，并站起来确认自己的名字，并对所有罪名表示认罪，没有任何明显的情绪波动。

其中包括对 BT/EE、Revolut 和 Uber 的黑客攻击，他使用社会工程技术来访问内部系统。

法庭获悉，他在攻击 Uber 期间发布了一张阴茎照片，试图迫使该公司支付赎金。

据估计，他对这些公司的黑客攻击造成了约 1000 万英镑的损失。

他和该团伙的其他成员利用从公司窃取的数据，瞄准了加密货币投资者。

检方辩称，该团伙从受害人个人身上窃取了至少 30 万美元。

库尔塔杰还承认在拘留期间对工人进行人身攻击，包括多次咬人事件。

在狱中，他因向警方发送嘲讽短信并在 Snapchat 上发布更新后因携带手机被捕。

库尔塔杰将在晚些时候被判刑。

在 2023 年的初审中，另一名 17 岁的 Lapsus$ 成员在南华克刑事法院被判有罪。

这名 17 岁的男子因年龄原因当时无法透露姓名，他被判处 18 个月的青少年改造令，包括严格监管和禁止在线使用 VPN。

今年早些时候，这名现名为 Thalha Jubair 的黑客在继续与另一个名为“分散蜘蛛”的组织进行网络犯罪后被判入狱五年零六个月。

伦敦交通局也是受害者之一，该公司遭受了破坏性网络攻击，造成约 3900 万英镑的损失，并在公司内部造成混乱。

article_content_en:
A hacker has pleaded guilty to a string of online crimes, including trying to extort the makers of Grand Theft Auto 6 after stealing dozens of unfinished clips of the game.

21-year-old Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, carried out the hack in 2022, and was originally sentenced to an indefinite stay in a secure hospital due to the severity of his autism.

But, in an unusual move, he was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial and released to a normal prison in January.

On Monday, Kurtaj pleaded guilty at Woolwich Crown Court to the Rockstar Games hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

Kurtaj breached Rockstar Games in 2022 whilst he was on bail for multiple other hacking offences and under police protection.

He was being housed in a Travelodge in Bicester to protect him from rival hackers who threatened to attack him for his stolen stashes of Bitcoin.

With his computer confiscated, Kurtaj hacked Rockstar using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into his hotel room television along with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished and hugely anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6.

He then broke into the company's internal Slack messaging system to declare: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code."

The company refused to cooperate so he posted the clips and source code on a forum under the username TeaPotUberHacker.

Rockstar Games said it cost the firm $5m (£3.79m) to recover from the hack, plus thousands of hours of staff time.

The company also said the breach revealed for the first time that one of the playable characters in the game was a woman - a secret it was guarding closely for marketing purposes.

At the time, doctors deemed Kurtaj unfit to stand in a traditional trial due to the severity of his autism, so instead he was given what is known as a trial of the facts.

The jury was asked to determine whether or not he committed the alleged acts - not if he did so with criminal intent.

In December 2023 the court ruled that he would remain at a secure hospital for life unless doctors deem him no longer a danger.

A routine assessment late last year deemed that he was now fit to stand a criminal trial which was scheduled to take place at Woolwich Crown Court.

But Kurtaj pleaded guilty to all offences.

He sat in the dock with short hair and an unkempt beard and wore a suit and buttoned-up white shirt but no tie.

The now 21-year-old blinked frequently during the hearing and stood to confirm his name, and pled guilty to all counts with no visible emotion.

Those included hacks on BT/EE, Revolut and Uber where he used social engineering techniques to gain access to internal systems.

The court heard that during his hack on Uber he posted a picture of a penis as part of his attempts to force the company to pay a ransom.

His hacks on the companies are estimated to have caused around £10m of damage.

Using the data stolen from the firms, he and other members of the gang targeted cryptocurrency investors.

The prosecution argued that the gang stole at least $300,000 from individual victims.

Kurtaj also pleaded guilty to physical assaults on workers whilst in custody including multiple biting incidents.

Whilst in prison he was caught with a mobile phone after sending a taunting text message to police and posting updates on Snapchat.

Kurtaj will be sentenced at a later date.

In the 2023 original trial, another Lapsus$member, who was 17, was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court.

The 17-year-old, who could not be named at the time due to his age, was sentenced to an 18-month Youth Rehabilitation Order, including intense supervision and a ban on using VPNs online.

Earlier this year that same hacker, now named as Thalha Jubair, was jailed for five years and six months after continuing his cyber crime offences with another group known as Scattered Spider.

Amongst victims was Transport for London which was subjected to a disruptive cyber attack that caused around £39m of damage and caused chaos inside the firm.

title: The Download: testing tech promises and searching for cognitive immortality
title_en: The Download: testing tech promises and searching for cognitive immortality
author: Thomas Macaulay
article_content:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

How do you measure progress towards the future? In the Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review , our series “ Are we there yet? ” examines how far six potentially transformative technologies have come after years of promises.

We spoke to experts, researchers and engineers to find out what’s holding them back, then scored each on a progress meter from zero to ten. Find out how we rated each of these technologies—and how close they are to delivering on their promise. Nuclear-powered spaceships Exercise in a pill Interspecies communication Solid-state batteries Cleaning up PFAS Eliminating traffic deaths

Subscribe now to get every issue of our print magazine as soon as it lands.

Could technology keep your brain going beyond death? Far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to make it happen, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores these ideas and how close they might be to reality.

Join science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado for this subscriber-only discussion tomorrow.

Tune in live on Tuesday, November 17 at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST .

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia CEO He’s discussed with confidants the possibility of returning. ( FT $) + Elon Musk has joined 165,000 signatories calling for his recall. ( Guardian ) + The Treasury Secretary wants them to hire an outsider. ( Axios ) + Megaspeed says the alleged China spy left the company last year. ( BBC ) + Trump plans to name Nvidia an AI “national champion.” ( WSJ $) + Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 SpaceX has caught a rocket returning from orbit for the first time The feat brings fully reusable rockets closer to reality. ( Guardian ) + The feat shows what audacious engineering can achieve. ( Atlantic $) + Meanwhile, Ukraine says SpaceX is lying about Starshield speed restrictions. ( Reuters $)

3 The US and allies have agreed to guard AI supply chains from China Ten countries will collaborate to secure critical technologies. ( FT $) + Chinese AI stocks have plunged on export control fears. ( Information $) + Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The US flight shutdown exposed weaknesses in air traffic technology Officials blamed the disruption on a faulty router installation. ( Reuters $) + It was a terrible week of outages. ( WP $)

5 The first in-body CRISPR treatment is set to reach patients next year The treatment could gain FDA approval as early as March. ( Nature ) + CRISPR has created female clones of male mice. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Congress plans to make data centers pay billions more for power A proposed bill would shift grid costs onto tech companies. ( NYT $) + Utilities also want tech giants to pay more for power. ( Bloomberg $) + Is data center hatred all about electricity? ( MIT Technology Review )

7 Apple plans to launch its first smart glasses next year It’s betting on Siri to give the specs an edge. ( Verge )

8 Bill Gates has made billions from climate-polluting landfills His investment in a landfill operator is worth $29 billion. ( ProPublica )

9 A new AI device turns everyday objects into needy virtual pets The tiny gadgets aim to encourage healthier everyday habits. ( Wired $)

10 Scientists made monkeys watch Minions to study their brains Their findings challenge traditional vision models. ( 404 Media )

—Helen Toner, former OpenAI board member, tells The Verge that AI needs stronger governance than trusting tech executives to do the right thing.

When Kenneth Wehr started managing the Greenlandic-language version of Wikipedia, he discovered that almost every article had been written by people who didn’t speak the language.

A growing number of them had been copy-pasted into Wikipedia from machine translators—and were riddled with elementary mistakes. This is beginning to cause a wicked problem.

AI systems, from Google Translate to ChatGPT, learn new languages by scraping text from Wikipedia. This could push the most vulnerable languages on Earth toward the precipice.

We can still have nice things

+ Adelaide Zoo is celebrating its first cassowary eggs in 34 years. + Photos fill the frame at the Epson Pano awards , which celebrate panoramic photography. + Indonesia has called an early halt to the world’s largest deforestation project , saving up to 4 million acres. + After over a month on the loose in Yellowstone, a little dog called Luna has been reunited with her owners.

article_content_en:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

How do you measure progress towards the future? In the Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review , our series “ Are we there yet? ” examines how far six potentially transformative technologies have come after years of promises.

We spoke to experts, researchers and engineers to find out what’s holding them back, then scored each on a progress meter from zero to ten. Find out how we rated each of these technologies—and how close they are to delivering on their promise. Nuclear-powered spaceships Exercise in a pill Interspecies communication Solid-state batteries Cleaning up PFAS Eliminating traffic deaths

Subscribe now to get every issue of our print magazine as soon as it lands.

Could technology keep your brain going beyond death? Far-thinking technologists are exploring ways to make it happen, from gradual brain replacement to uploading memories to the cloud. MIT Technology Review’s latest Roundtables event explores these ideas and how close they might be to reality.

Join science editor Mary Beth Griggs and senior editor for biomedicine Antonio Regalado for this subscriber-only discussion tomorrow.

Tune in live on Tuesday, November 17 at 5:00 p.m. GMT / 12:00 p.m. EST / 9:00 a.m. PST .

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

1 Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia CEO He’s discussed with confidants the possibility of returning. ( FT $) + Elon Musk has joined 165,000 signatories calling for his recall. ( Guardian ) + The Treasury Secretary wants them to hire an outsider. ( Axios ) + Megaspeed says the alleged China spy left the company last year. ( BBC ) + Trump plans to name Nvidia an AI “national champion.” ( WSJ $) + Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

2 SpaceX has caught a rocket returning from orbit for the first time The feat brings fully reusable rockets closer to reality. ( Guardian ) + The feat shows what audacious engineering can achieve. ( Atlantic $) + Meanwhile, Ukraine says SpaceX is lying about Starshield speed restrictions. ( Reuters $)

3 The US and allies have agreed to guard AI supply chains from China Ten countries will collaborate to secure critical technologies. ( FT $) + Chinese AI stocks have plunged on export control fears. ( Information $) + Nvidia privately said it can track chips to China. ( MIT Technology Review )

4 The US flight shutdown exposed weaknesses in air traffic technology Officials blamed the disruption on a faulty router installation. ( Reuters $) + It was a terrible week of outages. ( WP $)

5 The first in-body CRISPR treatment is set to reach patients next year The treatment could gain FDA approval as early as March. ( Nature ) + CRISPR has created female clones of male mice. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Congress plans to make data centers pay billions more for power A proposed bill would shift grid costs onto tech companies. ( NYT $) + Utilities also want tech giants to pay more for power. ( Bloomberg $) + Is data center hatred all about electricity? ( MIT Technology Review )

7 Apple plans to launch its first smart glasses next year It’s betting on Siri to give the specs an edge. ( Verge )

8 Bill Gates has made billions from climate-polluting landfills His investment in a landfill operator is worth $29 billion. ( ProPublica )

9 A new AI device turns everyday objects into needy virtual pets The tiny gadgets aim to encourage healthier everyday habits. ( Wired $)

10 Scientists made monkeys watch Minions to study their brains Their findings challenge traditional vision models. ( 404 Media )

—Helen Toner, former OpenAI board member, tells The Verge that AI needs stronger governance than trusting tech executives to do the right thing.

When Kenneth Wehr started managing the Greenlandic-language version of Wikipedia, he discovered that almost every article had been written by people who didn’t speak the language.

A growing number of them had been copy-pasted into Wikipedia from machine translators—and were riddled with elementary mistakes. This is beginning to cause a wicked problem.

AI systems, from Google Translate to ChatGPT, learn new languages by scraping text from Wikipedia. This could push the most vulnerable languages on Earth toward the precipice.

We can still have nice things

+ Adelaide Zoo is celebrating its first cassowary eggs in 34 years. + Photos fill the frame at the Epson Pano awards , which celebrate panoramic photography. + Indonesia has called an early halt to the world’s largest deforestation project , saving up to 4 million acres. + After over a month on the loose in Yellowstone, a little dog called Luna has been reunited with her owners.

title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
title_en: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
author: Jagmeet Singh
article_content:
Dreamteam, a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.

The funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation.

Traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring.

Dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks. Salespeople spent considerable time updating records, yet managers still struggled to get a reliable picture of their business. “In all these years, I have never come across an instance where I could click a button and get a forecast from the CRM,” he said.

That experience led Venkatraman to co-found Dreamteam in 2025 with Senthil Kanthaswamy (pictured above, center), who spent more than nine years at Freshworks, most recently as a product leader at Freshservice, and Ramesh Parthasarathy (pictured above, left), who previously worked on AI and platform engineering at Freshworks.

At the heart of Dreamteam’s CRM is what it calls the Company Brain. This acts as virtual memory, pulling together information from emails, meetings, and other customer interactions to build a shared record of customer relationships. Four built-in AI agents use that information to research prospects, draft follow-up emails, flag potential risks to deals, and configure CRM workflows, with sales teams retaining control over what gets sent to customers.

Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries in the three months since it began actively selling its product, with most paying for the service, Venkatraman said. The startup has also replaced established CRM platforms at several businesses, including Salesforce at healthcare company DMS Health and HubSpot at other customers.

The advertising sales team at media streaming company Plex also chose Dreamteam over HubSpot and other AI-native CRM alternatives, Venkatraman told TechCrunch. Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer Scott Olechowski said Dreamteam’s ability to integrate with AI tools already used across the company was a “game changer.”

Replacing established CRM platforms at scale may prove more difficult. In a blog post earlier this year, venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) argued that while AI could transform how businesses manage customer relationships, existing CRMs are likely to remain the systems where customer records are stored, with a new generation of AI-powered tools capturing much of the value by working on top of them.

Venkatraman acknowledged that Salesforce and HubSpot are unlikely to disappear anytime soon, but noted that their entrenched positions do not guarantee they will dominate the next generation of CRM software.

“We see this as an electric-car moment for systems of record,” he said, adding that AI requires a fundamental rethink of how CRMs are built — not simply adding new features to existing platforms.

Kanthaswamy believes startups have a window of two to five years to gain ground before established CRM providers can fully adapt to AI. Rebuilding software around a fundamentally different architecture takes time, he stated, giving newer companies an opportunity to attract customers while incumbents work to overhaul their existing products.

Dreamteam also plans to expand beyond sales into other parts of the customer lifecycle, including onboarding, customer support, and upselling. The startup already has a feature called Magic Apps that allows users to create custom applications and dashboards within the CRM using natural-language instructions, without writing code.

Currently, Dreamteam employs more than 35 people, with its engineering team based in Chennai and its go-to-market operations in the United States. Kanthaswamy said the startup aims to reach eight figures in annual revenue by the end of 2027, though he declined to disclose the startup’s current revenue.
