title: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
title_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered

inline_images.caption: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered

author: Robbie Whelan and Anissa Gardizy and Kate Clark
article_content:
In his final months as chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang was laying the groundwork to pull back the company’s approach to backstopping the AI economy.

Now, with a finance chief at the helm who was already wary of some deals the ousted chief forged, the startups who had been counting on Nvidia’s support expect an even greater pullback.

Just last month, the CEOs of emerging cloud companies that buy Nvidia chips and rent out computing power gathered in Berlin

Huang told his partners that if their companies wanted allocations of Nvidia’s prized GPUs, they would need to secure upfront payments from customers, people in attendance said. That would make their projects easier to finance and ensure that Nvidia wasn’t alone in being a source of financial support.

“You’re not charging what you should be charging,” he said, telling them that Elon Musk was renting Nvidia chips to customers at better rates than they were. “I don’t even need you guys. I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it!” he said, according to two executives who heard the remarks and one who was briefed on them shortly after.

Weeks later, Huang resigned after revelations that he had engaged in at least two affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset and another with one of his direct reports. His interim successor, finance chief Colette Kress, has at times pushed back against some of the company’s big deals and sought to rein in Nvidia.

Many companies that had relied on Nvidia are now worried.

UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated in a recent note that an Nvidia financing pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market, starving companies of support as interest rates rise.

The chip giant spent much of the past year on a dealmaking spree to provide financial backstops to emerging companies, lend its balance sheet to support debt financings of data-center projects, and even act as a customer of last resort for its own chips. The firm agreed to rent its chips from some customers to signal to lenders that those companies had solid contracts in-hand.

Earlier this year, Nvidia signaled it was preparing to roll out new financial incentives and do more deals than ever.

Rivals, such as Alphabet’s Google and Advanced Micro Devices, were offering these companies similar incentives, and Huang didn’t want to lose market share. Among the executives leading the charge was Nico Caprez, an Nvidia vice president who is also Huang’s son-in-law.

Nvidia announced its financing program in July, but by August, Huang and Kress questioned the return on investment from some deals.

When Nvidia used its creditworthy balance sheet to help OpenAI sign a massive data center lease in Piketon, Ohio, with SoftBank’s SB Energy, it cut the scale of its commitment in August during negotiations. Kress had become skeptical of the scale of the deal.

Huang told his finance team in August that the company was under pressure, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. Major cloud providers were making plans to use alternative chips and lessen their reliance on the firm, and Nvidia was staring at a glut of chip wafers and memory it had committed to buying, he told them.

The then-CEO pressed staff to develop a way to decide whether guarantees were worthwhile. Later that month, it paused some deals in that initiative, the Journal reported.

U.K.-based neocloud Nscale is still negotiating with Nvidia and other investors to provide financial backing for a $45-billion data center for Anthropic in West Virginia, the Journal reported.

In addition to its extensive backstopping, the chip maker also made a string of equity investments in AI startups. In total, Nvidia has participated in a record 129 venture-capital deals this year, as of Nov. 10, accounting for 27% of global VC deal value, according to PitchBook, up from a total of 49 such deals in 2023.

CEOs of startups that had closed deals with Nvidia breathed a sigh of relief that their deals made it through before Huang’s ouster.

Perplexity Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas shared that Nvidia closed a $3 billion investment in the company with his employees during a weekly all-hands at the startup’s San Francisco headquarters on Oct. 30, a person familiar with the meeting said. It was one day after news broke that the Nvidia CEO was seen as a target of a Chinese spy plot.

The AI search company is now raising additional capital at a higher valuation of $38 billion before the new investment, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia recently made an offer to Reflection AI, an open-source model developer valued at $25 billion, to license its technology and hire away some of its talent, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang had publicly praised the company. An agreement hadn’t been reached before he left, the people said.

Nvidia has also been finalizing a massive investment in Thinking Machines Lab, another provider of open-source models, valuing the company at $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Thinking Machines is confident the deal will be completed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Some details of Nvidia’s recent investments were earlier reported by the Financial Times and The Information.

Reflection and Thinking Machines are burning huge amounts of capital each month to pay for the computing power to develop their AI models, but haven’t yet developed a way to generate substantial revenue.

Some founders and venture-capital backers of companies with little to no sales said that if Nvidia did pull back from future equity investments, they could struggle to find capital to keep their cash-hungry businesses going, let alone secure a lucrative exit.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 英伟达创始人黄仁勋周四宣布辞去CEO职务，公司由原首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）接任临时CEO。此前有报道指控黄仁勋涉及个人不当关系，并牵扯进英伟达芯片在东南亚违规转运至中国的供应链调查风险中。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Thursday, with CFO Colette Kress appointed as interim CEO. The departure follows reports of personal misconduct involving investigations into potential diversion of restricted Nvidia chips to China via Southeast Asian partners.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 英伟达不仅面临顶级创始人的治理真空，更严峻的是其长期依赖的东南亚高性能计算（HPC）云厂商渠道或将面临美方出口管制审查的收紧。新任管理层需立即调整高度激进的融资与销售策略，以应对市场对供应链合规透明度的极度不安。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Nvidia faces not only a leadership vacuum but also acute scrutiny of its secondary sales channels in Southeast Asia, which may trigger tighter U.S. export compliance enforcement. The new leadership must urgently recalibrate aggressive sales strategies to restore market confidence in supply chain integrity.

article_content_zh:
在担任 Nvidia 首席执行官的最后几个月里，黄仁勋正在为撤回该公司支持人工智能经济的做法奠定基础。

现在，由于财务主管已经对被罢黜的主管伪造的一些交易持谨慎态度，一直指望英伟达支持的初创公司预计会出现更大的回调。

就在上个月，购买英伟达芯片并出租算力的新兴云公司的首席执行官齐聚柏林

与会人士表示，黄告诉他的合作伙伴，如果他们的公司想要分配 Nvidia 珍贵的 GPU，他们需要从客户那里获得预付款。这将使他们的项目更容易融资，并确保英伟达不是唯一一个提供财务支持的来源。

他说：“你没有收取应有的费用。”他告诉他们，埃隆·马斯克以比他们更好的价格向客户出租 Nvidia 芯片。 “我什至不需要你们。我可以把所有这些能力都给埃隆！埃隆想要它！”据两位听到这番言论的高管以及一位不久后听取简报的高管透露，他是这样说道的。

几周后，黄在被曝至少有过两起婚外情后辞职，其中一桩是与美国官员认为是中国情报人员的一名女性发生的，另一桩是与他的一名直接下属发生的。他的临时继任者、首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)有时会反对该公司的一些重大交易，并试图控制英伟达。

许多曾经依赖英伟达的公司现在都感到担忧了。

瑞银 (UBS) 分析师蒂姆·阿库里 (Tim Arcuri) 在最近的一份报告中估计，英伟达 (Nvidia) 融资撤回可能会导致市场损失 500 亿美元或更多美元，随着利率上升，企业将缺乏支持。

这家芯片巨头去年大部分时间都在大肆进行交易，为新兴公司提供财务支持，借出资产负债表来支持数据中心项目的债务融资，甚至充当自己芯片的最后客户。该公司同意从一些客户那里租用芯片，以向贷方表明这些公司手头有可靠的合同。

今年早些时候，英伟达表示正准备推出新的财务激励措施，并进行比以往更多的交易。

Alphabet 旗下的谷歌和 Advanced Micro Devices 等竞争对手正在向这些公司提供类似的激励措施，而黄仁勋不想失去市场份额。牵头的高管包括英伟达副总裁尼科·卡普雷斯 (Nico Caprez)，他也是黄仁勋的女婿。

英伟达在 7 月份宣布了融资计划，但到了 8 月份，黄仁勋和克雷斯对一些交易的投资回报提出了质疑。

当英伟达利用其信誉良好的资产负债表帮助 OpenAI 与软银旗下的 SB Energy 签署俄亥俄州皮克顿的大规模数据中心租赁协议时，英伟达在 8 月份的谈判中削减了承诺规模。克雷斯对这笔交易的规模产生了怀疑。

据《华尔街日报》此前报道，黄在 8 月份告诉他的财务团队，公司面临压力。他告诉他们，主要的云提供商正在计划使用替代芯片并减少对公司的依赖，而英伟达正面临着其承诺购买的芯片晶圆和内存过剩的问题。

时任首席执行官敦促员工制定一种方法来决定担保是否值得。据《华尔街日报》报道，当月晚些时候，该公司暂停了该计划中的一些交易。

据《华尔街日报》报道，英国 Neocloud Nscale 仍在与 Nvidia 和其他投资者进行谈判，为 Anthropic 位于西弗吉尼亚州的价值 450 亿美元的数据中心提供财务支持。

除了广泛的支持外，这家芯片制造商还对人工智能初创公司进行了一系列股权投资。根据 PitchBook 的数据，截至 11 月 10 日，英伟达今年总共参与了创纪录的 129 笔风险投资交易，占全球风险投资交易价值的 27%，高于 2023 年的 49 笔此类交易。

那些已经与英伟达达成交易的初创公司的首席执行官们松了一口气，因为他们的交易在黄仁勋下台之前就已经完成了。

据一位知情人士透露，Perplexity 首席执行官 Aravind Srinivas 表示，10 月 30 日，英伟达在该初创公司旧金山总部举行的每周全体会议上，与员工一起完成了对该公司 30 亿美元的投资。一天前，有消息传出，英伟达首席执行官被视为中国间谍阴谋的目标。

据知情人士透露，这家人工智能搜索公司目前正在筹集额外资金，在新投资之前，估值将达到 380 亿美元。

据知情人士透露，英伟达最近向估值 250 亿美元的开源模型开发商 Reflection AI 提出要约，以许可其技术并挖走其部分人才。黄曾公开赞扬该公司。知情人士称，在他离开之前尚未达成协议。

据知情人士透露，英伟达还敲定了对另一家开源模型提供商 Thinking Machines Lab 的巨额投资，该公司估值为 400 亿美元。据一位知情人士透露，Thinking Machines 有信心完成这笔交易。

英国《金融时报》和《信息报》早些时候报道了英伟达近期投资的一些细节。

Reflection and Thinking Machines 每个月都会燃烧大量资金来支付开发人工智能模型的计算能力，但尚未开发出一种产生大量收入的方法。

一些销售额很少甚至没有销售额的公司的创始人和风险资本支持者表示，如果英伟达确实从未来的股权投资中撤出，他们可能很难找到资金来维持急需现金的业务，更不用说确保利润丰厚的退出了。

Huang told his partners that if their companies wanted allocations of Nvidia’s prized GPUs, they would need to secure upfront payments from customers, people in attendance said. That would make their projects easier to finance and ensure that Nvidia wasn’t alone in being a source of financial support.

“You’re not charging what you should be charging,” he said, telling them that Elon Musk was renting Nvidia chips to customers at better rates than they were. “I don’t even need you guys. I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it!” he said, according to two executives who heard the remarks and one who was briefed on them shortly after.

Weeks later, Huang resigned after revelations that he had engaged in at least two affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset and another with one of his direct reports. His interim successor, finance chief Colette Kress, has at times pushed back against some of the company’s big deals and sought to rein in Nvidia.
Many companies that had relied on Nvidia are now worried.
UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated in a recent note that an Nvidia financing pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market, starving companies of support as interest rates rise.

The chip giant spent much of the past year on a dealmaking spree to provide financial backstops to emerging companies, lend its balance sheet to support debt financings of data-center projects, and even act as a customer of last resort for its own chips. The firm agreed to rent its chips from some customers to signal to lenders that those companies had solid contracts in-hand.
Earlier this year, Nvidia signaled it was preparing to roll out new financial incentives and do more deals than ever.

Rivals, such as Alphabet’s Google and Advanced Micro Devices, were offering these companies similar incentives, and Huang didn’t want to lose market share. Among the executives leading the charge was Nico Caprez, an Nvidia vice president who is also Huang’s son-in-law.
Nvidia announced its financing program in July, but by August, Huang and Kress questioned the return on investment from some deals.

When Nvidia used its creditworthy balance sheet to help OpenAI sign a massive data center lease in Piketon, Ohio, with SoftBank’s SB Energy, it cut the scale of its commitment in August during negotiations. Kress had become skeptical of the scale of the deal.

Huang told his finance team in August that the company was under pressure, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. Major cloud providers were making plans to use alternative chips and lessen their reliance on the firm, and Nvidia was staring at a glut of chip wafers and memory it had committed to buying, he told them.
The then-CEO pressed staff to develop a way to decide whether guarantees were worthwhile. Later that month, it paused some deals in that initiative, the Journal reported.
U.K.-based neocloud Nscale is still negotiating with Nvidia and other investors to provide financial backing for a $45-billion data center for Anthropic in West Virginia, the Journal reported.

In addition to its extensive backstopping, the chip maker also made a string of equity investments in AI startups. In total, Nvidia has participated in a record 129 venture-capital deals this year, as of Nov. 10, accounting for 27% of global VC deal value, according to PitchBook, up from a total of 49 such deals in 2023.
CEOs of startups that had closed deals with Nvidia breathed a sigh of relief that their deals made it through before Huang’s ouster.

Perplexity Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas shared that Nvidia closed a $3 billion investment in the company with his employees during a weekly all-hands at the startup’s San Francisco headquarters on Oct. 30, a person familiar with the meeting said. It was one day after news broke that the Nvidia CEO was seen as a target of a Chinese spy plot.
The AI search company is now raising additional capital at a higher valuation of $38 billion before the new investment, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia recently made an offer to Reflection AI, an open-source model developer valued at $25 billion, to license its technology and hire away some of its talent, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang had publicly praised the company. An agreement hadn’t been reached before he left, the people said.

Nvidia has also been finalizing a massive investment in Thinking Machines Lab, another provider of open-source models, valuing the company at $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Thinking Machines is confident the deal will be completed, according to a person familiar with the matter.
Some details of Nvidia’s recent investments were earlier reported by the Financial Times and The Information.

Reflection and Thinking Machines are burning huge amounts of capital each month to pay for the computing power to develop their AI models, but haven’t yet developed a way to generate substantial revenue.

Some founders and venture-capital backers of companies with little to no sales said that if Nvidia did pull back from future equity investments, they could struggle to find capital to keep their cash-hungry businesses going, let alone secure a lucrative exit.

title: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
title_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered

inline_images.caption: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered

author: Robbie Whelan and Anissa Gardizy and Kate Clark
article_content:
In his final months as chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang was laying the groundwork to pull back the company’s approach to backstopping the AI economy.

Now, with a finance chief at the helm who was already wary of some deals the ousted chief forged, the startups who had been counting on Nvidia’s support expect an even greater pullback.

Just last month, the CEOs of emerging cloud companies that buy Nvidia chips and rent out computing power gathered in Berlin

Huang told his partners that if their companies wanted allocations of Nvidia’s prized GPUs, they would need to secure upfront payments from customers, people in attendance said. That would make their projects easier to finance and ensure that Nvidia wasn’t alone in being a source of financial support.

“You’re not charging what you should be charging,” he said, telling them that Elon Musk was renting Nvidia chips to customers at better rates than they were. “I don’t even need you guys. I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it!” he said, according to two executives who heard the remarks and one who was briefed on them shortly after.

Weeks later, Huang resigned after revelations that he had engaged in at least two affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset and another with one of his direct reports. His interim successor, finance chief Colette Kress, has at times pushed back against some of the company’s big deals and sought to rein in Nvidia.

Many companies that had relied on Nvidia are now worried.

UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated in a recent note that an Nvidia financing pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market, starving companies of support as interest rates rise.

The chip giant spent much of the past year on a dealmaking spree to provide financial backstops to emerging companies, lend its balance sheet to support debt financings of data-center projects, and even act as a customer of last resort for its own chips. The firm agreed to rent its chips from some customers to signal to lenders that those companies had solid contracts in-hand.

Earlier this year, Nvidia signaled it was preparing to roll out new financial incentives and do more deals than ever.

Rivals, such as Alphabet’s Google and Advanced Micro Devices, were offering these companies similar incentives, and Huang didn’t want to lose market share. Among the executives leading the charge was Nico Caprez, an Nvidia vice president who is also Huang’s son-in-law.

Nvidia announced its financing program in July, but by August, Huang and Kress questioned the return on investment from some deals.

When Nvidia used its creditworthy balance sheet to help OpenAI sign a massive data center lease in Piketon, Ohio, with SoftBank’s SB Energy, it cut the scale of its commitment in August during negotiations. Kress had become skeptical of the scale of the deal.

Huang told his finance team in August that the company was under pressure, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. Major cloud providers were making plans to use alternative chips and lessen their reliance on the firm, and Nvidia was staring at a glut of chip wafers and memory it had committed to buying, he told them.

The then-CEO pressed staff to develop a way to decide whether guarantees were worthwhile. Later that month, it paused some deals in that initiative, the Journal reported.

U.K.-based neocloud Nscale is still negotiating with Nvidia and other investors to provide financial backing for a $45-billion data center for Anthropic in West Virginia, the Journal reported.

In addition to its extensive backstopping, the chip maker also made a string of equity investments in AI startups. In total, Nvidia has participated in a record 129 venture-capital deals this year, as of Nov. 10, accounting for 27% of global VC deal value, according to PitchBook, up from a total of 49 such deals in 2023.

CEOs of startups that had closed deals with Nvidia breathed a sigh of relief that their deals made it through before Huang’s ouster.

Perplexity Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas shared that Nvidia closed a $3 billion investment in the company with his employees during a weekly all-hands at the startup’s San Francisco headquarters on Oct. 30, a person familiar with the meeting said. It was one day after news broke that the Nvidia CEO was seen as a target of a Chinese spy plot.

The AI search company is now raising additional capital at a higher valuation of $38 billion before the new investment, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia recently made an offer to Reflection AI, an open-source model developer valued at $25 billion, to license its technology and hire away some of its talent, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang had publicly praised the company. An agreement hadn’t been reached before he left, the people said.

Nvidia has also been finalizing a massive investment in Thinking Machines Lab, another provider of open-source models, valuing the company at $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Thinking Machines is confident the deal will be completed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Some details of Nvidia’s recent investments were earlier reported by the Financial Times and The Information.

Reflection and Thinking Machines are burning huge amounts of capital each month to pay for the computing power to develop their AI models, but haven’t yet developed a way to generate substantial revenue.

Some founders and venture-capital backers of companies with little to no sales said that if Nvidia did pull back from future equity investments, they could struggle to find capital to keep their cash-hungry businesses going, let alone secure a lucrative exit.

content_snippet: Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in deals after a stretch in which Nvidia aggressively financed computing deals and startup investments
summary_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid espionage and misconduct scandals, with CFO Colette Kress appointed as interim CEO, triggering a reassessment of Nvidia's aggressive AI infrastructure financing. Nvidia has provided approximately $36 billion in off-balance-sheet credit support to 'neocloud' providers like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the new management is expected to pivot toward requiring upfront customer payments to mitigate credit risks.

In total, Nvidia has participated in a record 129 venture-capital deals this year, as of Nov. 10, accounting for 27% of global VC deal value, according to PitchBook, up from a total of 49 such deals in 2023.

CEOs of startups that had closed deals with Nvidia breathed a sigh of relief that their deals made it through before Huang’s ouster.

Perplexity Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas shared that Nvidia closed a $3 billion investment in the company with his employees during a weekly all-hands at the startup’s San Francisco headquarters on Oct. 30, a person familiar with the meeting said. It was one day after news broke that the Nvidia CEO was seen as a target of a Chinese spy plot.

The AI search company is now raising additional capital at a higher valuation of $38 billion before the new investment, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia recently made an offer to Reflection AI, an open-source model developer valued at $25 billion, to license its technology and hire away some of its talent, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang had publicly praised the company. An agreement hadn’t been reached before he left, the people said.

Nvidia has also been finalizing a massive investment in Thinking Machines Lab, another provider of open-source models, valuing the company at $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Thinking Machines is confident the deal will be completed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Some details of Nvidia’s recent investments were earlier reported by the Financial Times and The Information.

Reflection and Thinking Machines are burning huge amounts of capital each month to pay for the computing power to develop their AI models, but haven’t yet developed a way to generate substantial revenue.

Some founders and venture-capital backers of companies with little to no sales said that if Nvidia did pull back from future equity investments, they could struggle to find capital to keep their cash-hungry businesses going, let alone secure a lucrative exit.

title_zh: 英伟达向 AI 经济体“敞开支票簿”疯狂砸钱的时代已屈指可数
summary_zh: 英伟达CEO黄仁勋因丑闻辞职，现任CFO柯蕾特·克雷斯代理CEO，市场担忧英伟达对AI初创企业的激进融资支持将面临政策收紧
article_content_zh:
在担任 Nvidia 首席执行官的最后几个月里，黄仁勋正在为撤回该公司支持人工智能经济的做法奠定基础。

现在，由于财务主管已经对被罢黜的主管伪造的一些交易持谨慎态度，一直指望英伟达支持的初创公司预计会出现更大的回调。

就在上个月，购买英伟达芯片并出租算力的新兴云公司的首席执行官齐聚柏林

与会人士表示，黄告诉他的合作伙伴，如果他们的公司想要分配 Nvidia 珍贵的 GPU，他们需要从客户那里获得预付款。这将使他们的项目更容易融资，并确保英伟达不是唯一一个提供财务支持的来源。

他说：“你没有收取应有的费用。”他告诉他们，埃隆·马斯克以比他们更好的价格向客户出租 Nvidia 芯片。 “我什至不需要你们。我可以把所有这些能力都给埃隆！埃隆想要它！”据两位听到这番言论的高管以及一位不久后听取简报的高管透露，他是这样说道的。

几周后，黄在被曝至少有过两起婚外情后辞职，其中一桩是与美国官员认为是中国情报人员的一名女性发生的，另一桩是与他的一名直接下属发生的。他的临时继任者、首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)有时会反对该公司的一些重大交易，并试图控制英伟达。

许多曾经依赖英伟达的公司现在都感到担忧了。

瑞银 (UBS) 分析师蒂姆·阿库里 (Tim Arcuri) 在最近的一份报告中估计，英伟达 (Nvidia) 融资撤回可能会导致市场损失 500 亿美元或更多美元，随着利率上升，企业将缺乏支持。

这家芯片巨头去年大部分时间都在大肆进行交易，为新兴公司提供财务支持，借出资产负债表来支持数据中心项目的债务融资，甚至充当自己芯片的最后客户。该公司同意从一些客户那里租用芯片，以向贷方表明这些公司手头有可靠的合同。

今年早些时候，英伟达表示正准备推出新的财务激励措施，并进行比以往更多的交易。

Alphabet 旗下的谷歌和 Advanced Micro Devices 等竞争对手正在向这些公司提供类似的激励措施，而黄仁勋不想失去市场份额。牵头的高管包括英伟达副总裁尼科·卡普雷斯 (Nico Caprez)，他也是黄仁勋的女婿。

英伟达在 7 月份宣布了融资计划，但到了 8 月份，黄仁勋和克雷斯对一些交易的投资回报提出了质疑。

当英伟达利用其信誉良好的资产负债表帮助 OpenAI 与软银旗下的 SB Energy 签署俄亥俄州皮克顿的大规模数据中心租赁协议时，英伟达在 8 月份的谈判中削减了承诺规模。克雷斯对这笔交易的规模产生了怀疑。

据《华尔街日报》此前报道，黄在 8 月份告诉他的财务团队，公司面临压力。他告诉他们，主要的云提供商正在计划使用替代芯片并减少对公司的依赖，而英伟达正面临着其承诺购买的芯片晶圆和内存过剩的问题。

时任首席执行官敦促员工制定一种方法来决定担保是否值得。据《华尔街日报》报道，当月晚些时候，该公司暂停了该计划中的一些交易。

据《华尔街日报》报道，英国 Neocloud Nscale 仍在与 Nvidia 和其他投资者进行谈判，为 Anthropic 位于西弗吉尼亚州的价值 450 亿美元的数据中心提供财务支持。

除了广泛的支持外，这家芯片制造商还对人工智能初创公司进行了一系列股权投资。根据 PitchBook 的数据，截至 11 月 10 日，英伟达今年总共参与了创纪录的 129 笔风险投资交易，占全球风险投资交易价值的 27%，高于 2023 年的 49 笔此类交易。

那些已经与英伟达达成交易的初创公司的首席执行官们松了一口气，因为他们的交易在黄仁勋下台之前就已经完成了。

据一位知情人士透露，Perplexity 首席执行官 Aravind Srinivas 表示，10 月 30 日，英伟达在该初创公司旧金山总部举行的每周全体会议上，与员工一起完成了对该公司 30 亿美元的投资。一天前，有消息传出，英伟达首席执行官被视为中国间谍阴谋的目标。

据知情人士透露，这家人工智能搜索公司目前正在筹集额外资金，在新投资之前，估值将达到 380 亿美元。

据知情人士透露，英伟达最近向估值 250 亿美元的开源模型开发商 Reflection AI 提出要约，以许可其技术并挖走其部分人才。黄曾公开赞扬该公司。知情人士称，在他离开之前尚未达成协议。

据知情人士透露，英伟达还敲定了对另一家开源模型提供商 Thinking Machines Lab 的巨额投资，该公司估值为 400 亿美元。据一位知情人士透露，Thinking Machines 有信心完成这笔交易。

英国《金融时报》和《信息报》早些时候报道了英伟达近期投资的一些细节。

Reflection and Thinking Machines 每个月都会燃烧大量资金来支付开发人工智能模型的计算能力，但尚未开发出一种产生大量收入的方法。

一些销售额很少甚至没有销售额的公司的创始人和风险资本支持者表示，如果英伟达确实从未来的股权投资中撤出，他们可能很难找到资金来维持急需现金的业务，更不用说确保利润丰厚的退出了。

paragraphs: In his final months as chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang was laying the groundwork to pull back the company’s approach to backstopping the AI economy.
Now, with a finance chief at the helm who was already wary of some deals the ousted chief forged, the startups who had been counting on Nvidia’s support expect an even greater pullback.
Just last month, the CEOs of emerging cloud companies that buy Nvidia chips and rent out computing power gathered in Berlin

Huang told his partners that if their companies wanted allocations of Nvidia’s prized GPUs, they would need to secure upfront payments from customers, people in attendance said. That would make their projects easier to finance and ensure that Nvidia wasn’t alone in being a source of financial support.

“You’re not charging what you should be charging,” he said, telling them that Elon Musk was renting Nvidia chips to customers at better rates than they were. “I don’t even need you guys. I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it!” he said, according to two executives who heard the remarks and one who was briefed on them shortly after.

Weeks later, Huang resigned after revelations that he had engaged in at least two affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset and another with one of his direct reports. His interim successor, finance chief Colette Kress, has at times pushed back against some of the company’s big deals and sought to rein in Nvidia.
Many companies that had relied on Nvidia are now worried.
UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated in a recent note that an Nvidia financing pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market, starving companies of support as interest rates rise.

The chip giant spent much of the past year on a dealmaking spree to provide financial backstops to emerging companies, lend its balance sheet to support debt financings of data-center projects, and even act as a customer of last resort for its own chips. The firm agreed to rent its chips from some customers to signal to lenders that those companies had solid contracts in-hand.
Earlier this year, Nvidia signaled it was preparing to roll out new financial incentives and do more deals than ever.

Rivals, such as Alphabet’s Google and Advanced Micro Devices, were offering these companies similar incentives, and Huang didn’t want to lose market share. Among the executives leading the charge was Nico Caprez, an Nvidia vice president who is also Huang’s son-in-law.
Nvidia announced its financing program in July, but by August, Huang and Kress questioned the return on investment from some deals.

When Nvidia used its creditworthy balance sheet to help OpenAI sign a massive data center lease in Piketon, Ohio, with SoftBank’s SB Energy, it cut the scale of its commitment in August during negotiations. Kress had become skeptical of the scale of the deal.

Huang told his finance team in August that the company was under pressure, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. Major cloud providers were making plans to use alternative chips and lessen their reliance on the firm, and Nvidia was staring at a glut of chip wafers and memory it had committed to buying, he told them.
The then-CEO pressed staff to develop a way to decide whether guarantees were worthwhile. Later that month, it paused some deals in that initiative, the Journal reported.
U.K.-based neocloud Nscale is still negotiating with Nvidia and other investors to provide financial backing for a $45-billion data center for Anthropic in West Virginia, the Journal reported.

In addition to its extensive backstopping, the chip maker also made a string of equity investments in AI startups. In total, Nvidia has participated in a record 129 venture-capital deals this year, as of Nov. 10, accounting for 27% of global VC deal value, according to PitchBook, up from a total of 49 such deals in 2023.
CEOs of startups that had closed deals with Nvidia breathed a sigh of relief that their deals made it through before Huang’s ouster.

Perplexity Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas shared that Nvidia closed a $3 billion investment in the company with his employees during a weekly all-hands at the startup’s San Francisco headquarters on Oct. 30, a person familiar with the meeting said. It was one day after news broke that the Nvidia CEO was seen as a target of a Chinese spy plot.
The AI search company is now raising additional capital at a higher valuation of $38 billion before the new investment, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia recently made an offer to Reflection AI, an open-source model developer valued at $25 billion, to license its technology and hire away some of its talent, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang had publicly praised the company. An agreement hadn’t been reached before he left, the people said.

Nvidia has also been finalizing a massive investment in Thinking Machines Lab, another provider of open-source models, valuing the company at $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Thinking Machines is confident the deal will be completed, according to a person familiar with the matter.
Some details of Nvidia’s recent investments were earlier reported by the Financial Times and The Information.

Reflection and Thinking Machines are burning huge amounts of capital each month to pay for the computing power to develop their AI models, but haven’t yet developed a way to generate substantial revenue.

title: Mount Thor raises $45 million to build Mac data centers for AI agents
title_en: Mount Thor raises $45 million to build Mac data centers for AI agents
author: Bradley C
article_content:
Mount Thor, a Bay Area startup building cloud infrastructure on Apple silicon, announced today that it has raised $45 million across Seed and Series A rounds. The pitch to its investors was simple: AI agents are incredible on Apple silicon, and nobody is renting them at data-center scale.

CRV and Conviction co-led the Series A. Chad Byers and Offline Ventures co-led the Seed. CSC Leasing, Enea Capital, Long Journey Ventures, and Upper90 participated, along with angel investors from OpenAI, Meta, Cognition, Together AI, and Vercel. The company also raised separate non-dilutive financing for new hardware as well.

Mount Thor runs macOS on Apple silicon as elastic compute instances, just as a cloud provider rents Linux VMs. Customers get on-demand fleets of Macs for work that only happens on macOS: training computer-use models in reinforcement learning environments, running secure macOS sandboxes for agents, long-running instances that let an agent work across a user’s devices under one Apple ID, and build and test farms for Apple software.

There are two ways to use its solution. With managed compute, customers pick a machine class and image, and get either a full bare-metal Mac or an isolated macOS VM with administrator access, provisioned through a web portal, a command-line tool, Kubernetes, or the API, and billed per Mac on a 24-hour basis. With customer-managed compute, an organization runs its own Macs at a Mount Thor site using its own MDM, while Mount Thor operates the facility and provides inventory by serial number, problem reporting, and event notifications.

The argument is that agents are becoming macOS users, and the demand for Apple’s platform now scales with the number of agents rather than the number of people.

“Making Apple’s operating system and silicon available at datacenter-scale is a massive untapped opportunity in AI infrastructure,” said Peter Voell, Founder and CEO of Mount Thor. “Decades of investment in accessibility and human-computer interaction make macOS the best place for agents to work and for humans to hold them accountable. And with chips like the M5 Ultra, Apple silicon is becoming a high performance, more power- and cost- efficient platform for production inference.”

The other half of its pitch is inference. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio shipped in August with up to 512GB of unified memory, which puts large open-weight models within reach of a single machine at a fraction of the power draw of a traditional GPU-based server. Mount Thor says a focus of the new funding is building what it calls the best inference lab for open-source models on Apple silicon.

“Mount Thor sits at the intersection of two important shifts: the rapidly expanding capabilities of autonomous agents and the increasing demand for compute that can support both local and cloud workloads,” said Brittany Walker, General Partner at CRV. “We’re thrilled to back Peter and the team as they make it easier to use Apple’s platforms at scale for agentic AI.”

The team comes from Cerebras, CoreWeave, Fluidstack, Nebius, OpenAI, and xAI. The company was founded this year and deployed its first data center in under six months.

### Wrap up

Macs in the cloud are not new as AWS has rented Mac instances for a few years, and MacStadium has been doing so longer than AWS. Mount Thor’s pitch is that the larger customer is an AI agent that needs a Mac to do its job, and that demand grows with the number of agents rather than the number of developers.

The company says the funding will go toward expanding its compute footprint and building out the team, and that it plans to add capacity quickly to keep up with customer demand.

article_content_zh:
Mount Thor 是一家在 Apple 芯片上构建云基础设施的湾区初创公司，今天宣布已通过种子轮和 A 轮融资筹集 4500 万美元。向投资者推销的内容很简单：苹果芯片上的人工智能代理令人难以置信，而且没有人在数据中心规模上租用它们。

CRV 和 Conviction 共同领投了 A 轮融资。Chad Byers 和 Offline Ventures 共同领投了种子轮融资。 CSC Leasing、Enea Capital、Long Journey Ventures 和 Upper90 参与其中，还有来自 OpenAI、Meta、Cognition、Together AI 和 Vercel 的天使投资者。该公司还为新硬件筹集了单独的非稀释性融资。

Mount Thor 在 Apple 芯片上运行 macOS 作为弹性计算实例，就像云提供商租用 Linux 虚拟机一样。客户可以按需获得一组 Mac 来完成仅在 macOS 上进行的工作：在强化学习环境中训练计算机使用模型、为代理运行安全的 macOS 沙箱、让代理在一个 Apple ID 下跨用户设备工作的长期运行实例，以及为 Apple 软件构建和测试场。

有两种方法可以使用其解决方案。通过托管计算，客户可以选择机器类别和映像，并获得完整的裸机 Mac 或具有管理员访问权限的独立 macOS 虚拟机，通过 Web 门户、命令行工具、Kubernetes 或 API 进行配置，并按 24 小时按 Mac 计费。通过客户管理的计算，组织可以使用自己的 MDM 在 Mount Thor 站点运行自己的 Mac，而 Mount Thor 则运营该设施并按序列号提供库存、问题报告和事件通知。

争论的焦点是，客服人员正在成为 macOS 用户，而对苹果平台的需求现在随着客服人员的数量而不是人数的增加而增加。

Mount Thor 创始人兼首席执行官 Peter Voell 表示：“在数据中心规模上提供苹果操作系统和芯片是人工智能基础设施领域一个尚未开发的巨大机遇。” “数十年在可访问性和人机交互方面的投资使 macOS 成为智能体工作和人类追究其责任的最佳场所。借助 M5 Ultra 等芯片，Apple 芯片正在成为一个高性能、更省电且更具成本效益的生产推理平台。”

它的另一半内容是推理。 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 于 8 月份发货，配备高达 512GB 的统一内存，这使得大型开放式重量模型可以在单台机器上运行，而功耗只是传统的基于 GPU 的服务器的一小部分。 Mount Thor 表示，新资金的重点是在苹果芯片上建立所谓的最佳开源模型推理实验室。

CRV 普通合伙人 Brittany Walker 表示：“Mount Thor 处于两个重要转变的交汇点：自主代理功能的快速扩展以及对支持本地和云工作负载的计算需求的不断增长。” “我们很高兴能够支持 Peter 和他的团队，因为他们让大规模使用 Apple 平台实现代理 AI 变得更加容易。”

该团队来自 Cerebras、CoreWeave、Fluidstack、Nebius、OpenAI 和 xAI。该公司成立于今年，并在不到六个月的时间内部署了第一个数据中心。

### 包起来

云中的 Mac 并不新鲜，因为 AWS 租用 Mac 实例已经有几年了，而且 MacStadium 这样做的时间比 AWS 还要长。 Mount Thor 的主张是，更大的客户是需要 Mac 来完成工作的 AI 代理，并且这种需求随着代理数量而不是开发人员数量的增长而增长。

该公司表示，这笔资金将用于扩大其计算范围和建设团队，并计划快速增加容量以满足客户需求。

article_content_en:
Mount Thor, a Bay Area startup building cloud infrastructure on Apple silicon, announced today that it has raised $45 million across Seed and Series A rounds. The pitch to its investors was simple: AI agents are incredible on Apple silicon, and nobody is renting them at data-center scale.

CRV and Conviction co-led the Series A. Chad Byers and Offline Ventures co-led the Seed. CSC Leasing, Enea Capital, Long Journey Ventures, and Upper90 participated, along with angel investors from OpenAI, Meta, Cognition, Together AI, and Vercel. The company also raised separate non-dilutive financing for new hardware as well.

Mount Thor runs macOS on Apple silicon as elastic compute instances, just as a cloud provider rents Linux VMs. Customers get on-demand fleets of Macs for work that only happens on macOS: training computer-use models in reinforcement learning environments, running secure macOS sandboxes for agents, long-running instances that let an agent work across a user’s devices under one Apple ID, and build and test farms for Apple software.

There are two ways to use its solution. With managed compute, customers pick a machine class and image, and get either a full bare-metal Mac or an isolated macOS VM with administrator access, provisioned through a web portal, a command-line tool, Kubernetes, or the API, and billed per Mac on a 24-hour basis. With customer-managed compute, an organization runs its own Macs at a Mount Thor site using its own MDM, while Mount Thor operates the facility and provides inventory by serial number, problem reporting, and event notifications.

The argument is that agents are becoming macOS users, and the demand for Apple’s platform now scales with the number of agents rather than the number of people.

“Making Apple’s operating system and silicon available at datacenter-scale is a massive untapped opportunity in AI infrastructure,” said Peter Voell, Founder and CEO of Mount Thor. “Decades of investment in accessibility and human-computer interaction make macOS the best place for agents to work and for humans to hold them accountable. And with chips like the M5 Ultra, Apple silicon is becoming a high performance, more power- and cost- efficient platform for production inference.”

The other half of its pitch is inference. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio shipped in August with up to 512GB of unified memory, which puts large open-weight models within reach of a single machine at a fraction of the power draw of a traditional GPU-based server. Mount Thor says a focus of the new funding is building what it calls the best inference lab for open-source models on Apple silicon.

“Mount Thor sits at the intersection of two important shifts: the rapidly expanding capabilities of autonomous agents and the increasing demand for compute that can support both local and cloud workloads,” said Brittany Walker, General Partner at CRV. “We’re thrilled to back Peter and the team as they make it easier to use Apple’s platforms at scale for agentic AI.”

The team comes from Cerebras, CoreWeave, Fluidstack, Nebius, OpenAI, and xAI. The company was founded this year and deployed its first data center in under six months.

### Wrap up

Macs in the cloud are not new as AWS has rented Mac instances for a few years, and MacStadium has been doing so longer than AWS. Mount Thor’s pitch is that the larger customer is an AI agent that needs a Mac to do its job, and that demand grows with the number of agents rather than the number of developers.

The company says the funding will go toward expanding its compute footprint and building out the team, and that it plans to add capacity quickly to keep up with customer demand.

title: Toronto-based Blue J, which provides AI-powered tax research software, raised a $176M Series E round led by JMI Equity at a $700M+ valuation (Alex Riehl/BetaKit)
title_en: Toronto-based Blue J, which provides AI-powered tax research software, raised a $176M Series E round led by JMI Equity at a $700M+ valuation (Alex Riehl/BetaKit)

inline_images.caption: A person working on a laptop holding a debit card.
inline_images.alt: A person working on a laptop holding a debit card.

author: BetaKit
article_content:
Toronto-based Blue J has raised a $176-million USD ($249-million CAD) Series E round after more than doubling its annual recurring revenue in just over a year.

The round, which Blue J announced on Tuesday morning, values the AI-powered tax research software provider at more than $700 million USD. US-based growth equity firm JMI Equity led the round, with existing investors Oak HC/FT, Sapphire Ventures, and Intrepid Growth Partners also participating.

Blue J CEO Ben Alarie told BetaKit in a Monday interview that the round featured a secondary capital component, buying out “long holders” and a small amount for long-term employees, but did not disclose how much of the round this included.

“I’m excited about building Canada’s next great tech company right here from Toronto.”

Founded in 2015 by Alarie, CTO Brett Janssen, Anthony Niblett, and Albert Yoon, Blue J aims to make the law more transparent and accessible for tax practitioners. Blue J claims its AI-powered platform can answer questions about federal, state, and local taxes in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company said the proceeds will help it scale its agentic AI for tax work feature, Workflows, as well as expand in the UK and internationally. While Blue J’s platform is versed in UK tax law, Alarie said the company still doesn’t have “boots on the ground” in the country.

“This will be about establishing a UK office and making a more concerted effort to take Blue J to market in the UK,” Alarie said, adding with a smirk that the office will be “probably big, in time.”

Alarie foresees the forthcoming upgrade to Blue J’s Workflows fundamentally changing his business. He wants Blue J to be able to produce hundreds of deliverables, from helping its accountant users draft a memo to responding to a notice of assessment from the Canada Revenue Agency. With these features, Blue J will move from an AI-powered tax research platform to a tax research and advisory platform.

“Our ambition is, by the end of next year, to have built out all of these workflow capabilities to effectively assist with just about any kind of work product that a tax professional routinely does in their practice,” Alarie said. “So it’s a big build.”

RELATED: Blue J raises $167.4-million CAD Series D after AI tax research platform more than doubles revenue

The Series E round comes just 15 months after Blue J raised a $122-million USD ($167.4-million CAD) Series D round, which was also on the heels of rapid growth, to expand its team, product, and market reach. While specific revenue figures weren’t disclosed (Alarie only said it’s in the “mid eight-figures”), Blue J claims its annual recurring revenue grew 165 percent since the Series D round, and that its revenue has grown 529 percent in the last three years. Blue J has added roughly 2,500 customers since the end of 2025, bringing it up to a total of 6,500 customers; growth that Alarie credits to Blue J’s effectiveness as a product.

“Tax technical stuff is really, really hard to research, and I can tell you this as somebody who’s been a tax professor for 22 years,” Alarie said. “It’s a painful problem to solve, and Blue J makes it, I like to think, rather delightful.”

As Alarie prepares Blue J to take flight, he said he’s excited to work with lead investor JMI, which has backed multiple scaling Canadian tech firms, including Clio, Safe Software, PointClickCare, Vena, and Jane.

“They’ve done a phenomenal job at helping companies like Blue J scale from where we are today to being much, much larger businesses,” Alarie said. “They really excel [at] helping people like me, a first-time founder, navigate as we scale this business to the next level.”

To support its growth, Blue J has doubled its head count over the past year, and expects to exceed 200 employees by year-end. While some of these may be in the UK or the US, Alarie expects the majority to be based in Blue J’s “center of gravity.”

“Our hearts are in Toronto,” Alarie said. “I’m excited about building Canada’s next great tech company right here from Toronto.”

title_zh: 多伦多AI税务研究平台Blue J获1.76亿美元E轮融资
summary_zh: 总部位于多伦多的Blue J完成1.76亿美元E轮融资，估值超7亿美元，资金将用于扩展代理人AI税务工作流及英国市场布局
article_content_zh:
总部位于多伦多的 Blue J 已在 E 轮融资中筹集了 1.76 亿美元（2.49 亿加元），其年度经常性收入在短短一年多的时间里就增加了一倍多。

Blue J 于周二上午宣布了这一轮融资，对这家人工智能税务研究软件提供商的估值超过 7 亿美元。美国成长型股权公司 JMI Equity 领投此轮融资，现有投资者 Oak HC/FT、Sapphire Ventures 和 Intrepid Growth Partners 也参与其中。

Blue J 首席执行官 Ben Alarie 在周一接受 BetaKit 采访时表示，本轮融资包含二级资本成分，即买断“长期持有者”股份和少量长期员工股份，但没有透露这轮融资的金额。

“我很高兴能够在多伦多建立加拿大下一家伟大的科技公司。”

Blue J 由 Alarie、首席技术官 Brett Janssen、Anthony Niblett 和 Albert Yoon 于 2015 年创立，旨在使法律对税务从业者来说更加透明和易于理解。 Blue J 声称其人工智能平台可以回答有关美国、加拿大和英国联邦、州和地方税收的问题。

该公司表示，所得收益将帮助其扩大其税务工作代理人工智能功能 Workflows 的规模，并在英国和国际范围内扩张。虽然 Blue J 的平台精通英国税法，但阿拉里表示，该公司在英国仍然没有“实地部署”。

阿拉里说：“这将是为了建立一个英国办事处，并更加一致地努力将 Blue J 推向英国市场。”他笑着补充说，这个办事处“迟早可能会变得很大”。

Alarie 预计 Blue J 工作流程即将升级，将从根本上改变他的业务。他希望 Blue J 能够生成数百份可交付成果，从帮助其会计师用户起草备忘录到回复加拿大税务局的评估通知。凭借这些功能，Blue J 将从人工智能驱动的税务研究平台转变为税务研究和咨询平台。

阿拉里说：“我们的目标是，到明年年底，建立所有这些工作流程功能，以有效协助税务专业人员在实践中日常执行的几乎任何类型的工作产品。” “所以这是一个很大的建筑。”

相关：人工智能税务研究平台收入增加一倍以上后，Blue J 筹集了 1.674 亿加元的 D 轮融资

距离 E 轮融资仅 15 个月前，Blue J 筹集了 1.22 亿美元（1.674 亿加元）的 D 轮融资，该轮融资也是在快速增长之后进行的，旨在扩大其团队、产品和市场覆盖范围。虽然具体收入数字没有披露（Alarie 仅表示在“八位数左右”），但 Blue J 声称自 D 轮融资以来其年度经常性收入增长了 165%，并且在过去三年中其收入增长了 529%。自 2025 年底以来，Blue J 已增加约 2,500 名客户，使其客户总数达到 6,500 名； Alarie 将这种增长归功于 Blue J 作为产品的有效性。

“税务技术问题真的非常难以研究，作为一个已经担任了 22 年税务教授的人，我可以告诉你这一点，”阿拉里说。 “这是一个很难解决的问题，但我认为 Blue J 让它变得相当令人愉快。”

当 Alarie 准备 Blue J 起飞时，他表示很高兴能与主要投资者 JMI 合作，JMI 已支持多家规模不断扩大的加拿大科技公司，包括 Clio、Safe Software、PointClickCare、Vena 和 Jane。

阿拉里说：“他们在帮助 Blue J 这样的公司从今天的规模发展成为规模更大的企业方面做得非常出色。” “他们非常擅长帮助像我这样的首次创始人，帮助我们将业务扩展至新的水平。”

title: SK Hynix Plans Chip Testing Hub to Boost Smaller Korean Players
title_en: SK Hynix Plans Chip Testing Hub to Boost Smaller Korean Players
author: Yoolim Lee
article_content:
By Kwanwoo Jun South Korean memory-chip giant SK Hynix plans to spend 1.4 trillion won, equivalent to $1.05 billion, over the next five years to support small local suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, in order to strengthen the competitiveness of its supply chain.

As part of the plan, SK Hynix will open a semiconductor testing facility, jointly funded with about 875 billion won in investment, in May 2027 at its chip-making complex in Yongin, south of Seoul, the company said Monday. The facility now under construction, named Trinity Fab, is the result of a three-way partnership between SK Hynix, the central government and the Yongin municipal government, which have committed 443.2 billion won, 373.6 billion won and 57.7 billion won, respectively, the company said.

By sharing the facility, which will feature a large clean room and state-of-the-art testing equipment based on 12-inch wafers, domestic suppliers will be able to reduce the costs and time needed to bring their products to commercial production and market, it said. SK Hynix also plans to provide suppliers with technical and financial support, if needed, at the facility.

The initiative provides local material, component, and equipment suppliers with a 12-inch wafer testing environment, supported by a 2 trillion KRW (approx. $1.5 billion) guarantee program to lower entry barriers into the semiconductor supply chain.

article_content_zh:
韩国存储芯片巨头 SK 海力士计划在未来五年内斥资 1.4 万亿韩元（约合 10.5 亿美元）支持本土小型半导体材料、零部件和设备供应商，以增强其供应链的竞争力。

SK 海力士周一表示，作为该计划的一部分，SK 海力士将于 2027 年 5 月在首尔南部龙仁市的芯片制造厂开设一家半导体测试设施，该设施由共同投资约 8750 亿韩元共同出资。该公司表示，目前正在建设的工厂名为 Trinity Fab，是 SK 海力士、中央政府和龙仁市政府三方合作的成果，三方分别投入了 4432 亿韩元、3736 亿韩元和 577 亿韩元。

据称，通过共享该设施，该设施将配备大型洁净室和基于12英寸晶圆的最先进的测试设备，国内供应商将能够减少将其产品推向商业生产和市场所需的成本和时间。 SK 海力士还计划根据需要在该工厂向供应商提供技术和财务支持。

title: SK hynix sets $1 billion chip-supplier support plan
title_en: SK hynix sets $1 billion chip-supplier support plan
author: Reuters
article_content:
SEOUL, Nov 16 (Reuters) - South Korea's SK Hynix said on Monday it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market.

The chipmaker also outlined plans for a jointly funded 874.6 billion won testing facility at its semiconductor complex in Yongin, south of Seoul, where smaller suppliers will be able to test products under conditions similar to those on commercial chip production lines.

Here are some details:

• SK Hynix said its supplier support programme covers four stages - research and development, testing, mass production and sales. It aims to help smaller companies overcome financing and technology hurdles.

• The testing facility, named Trinity Fab, is a partnership between SK Hynix, the central government and local governments. It is scheduled to open in May 2027. SK Hynix will contribute 443.2 billion won, the central government 373.6 billion won and local governments 57.7 billion won, according to the company.

• Trinity Fab will house around 50 semiconductor tools, including lithography and etching equipment, allowing suppliers to test materials and components on 12-inch wafers.

• To reduce financial risks for suppliers, SK Hynix said it will share development costs in advance and provide compensation if a joint project fails.

• An independent foundation will operate the test facility to protect the intellectual property of participating suppliers, the company said.

• The initiative also includes establishing an overseas marketing support centre to help domestic suppliers expand internationally and reduce reliance on imported chip components.

• SK Hynix and financial institutions will also provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation, while other programmes offer low-interest loans and technical consulting to suppliers, including smaller subcontractors.

article_content_zh:
首尔，11月16日（路透社）- 韩国 SK海力士周一宣布，计划在未来五年内投入 1.4 万亿韩元（约合 10.5 亿美元），支持韩国本土半导体材料、零部件和设备供应商，旨在随着人工智能（AI）芯片市场竞争白热化，全面强化自身供应链韧性。

这家芯片制造商还公布了一项耗资 8746 亿韩元的测试中心联合投资规划，该设施位于首尔以南的龙仁半导体产业集群，将允许中小型供应商在与商业芯片生产线相似的实际工况下验证其产品性能。

以下为该扶持计划的核心细节：

• SK海力士表示，其供应商扶持方案涵盖研发、测试、量产和销售四个阶段，旨在帮助中小企业克服资金和技术门槛。

• 该测试中心被命名为“Trinity Fab”，由 SK海力士与韩国中央政府及地方政府共同联合出资建设，预计将于 2027 年 5 月正式投入运营。根据公司公布的数据，SK海力士出资 4432 亿韩元，中央政府出资 3736 亿韩元，地方政府出资 577 亿韩元。

• Trinity Fab 测试中心将部署约 50 台先进制程设备（包括光刻机和刻蚀机等关键机台），使供应商能够在 12 英寸（300毫米）标准硅片上完成材料和组件的工艺验证。

• 为了降低供应商的研发财务风险，SK海力士表示将提前垫付部分开发成本，并在联合研发项目未能成功时提供专项补偿。

• 公司表示，该测试设施将由一家独立非营利基金会负责日常运营，以严格保护参与供应商的核心知识产权与商业机密。

• 该倡议还包括设立海外营销支持中心，协助韩国本土供应商拓展国际市场，并逐步降低对海外进口半导体关键零部件的依赖度。

• SK海力士还将与金融机构合作，在韩国贸易保险公社的担保下提供 2 万亿韩元的融资支持，同时开展其他项目向供应链企业（包括小型分包商）提供低息贷款和技术咨询服务。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] The program is intended to strengthen the company’s supply chain amid intensifying competition in the market for artificial intelligence chips, Channel NewsAsia reports.

paragraphs: SEOUL, Nov 16 (Reuters) - South Korea's SK Hynix said on Monday it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment, aiming to strengthen its supply chain as competition intensifies in the AI chip market.

The chipmaker also outlined plans for a jointly funded 874.6 billion won testing facility at its semiconductor complex in Yongin, south of Seoul, where smaller suppliers will be able to test products under conditions similar to those on commercial chip production lines.
Here are some details:

• SK Hynix said its supplier support programme covers four stages - research and development, testing, mass production and sales. It aims to help smaller companies overcome financing and technology hurdles.

• The testing facility, named Trinity Fab, is a partnership between SK Hynix, the central government and local governments. It is scheduled to open in May 2027. SK Hynix will contribute 443.2 billion won, the central government 373.6 billion won and local governments 57.7 billion won, according to the company.
• Trinity Fab will house around 50 semiconductor tools, including lithography and etching equipment, allowing suppliers to test materials and components on 12-inch wafers.
• To reduce financial risks for suppliers, SK Hynix said it will share development costs in advance and provide compensation if a joint project fails.
• An independent foundation will operate the test facility to protect the intellectual property of participating suppliers, the company said.
• The initiative also includes establishing an overseas marketing support centre to help domestic suppliers expand internationally and reduce reliance on imported chip components.

• SK Hynix and financial institutions will also provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation, while other programmes offer low-interest loans and technical consulting to suppliers, including smaller subcontractors.
paragraphs_zh: 首尔，11月16日（路透社）- 韩国 SK海力士周一宣布，计划在未来五年内投入 1.4 万亿韩元（约合 10.5 亿美元），支持韩国本土半导体材料、零部件和设备供应商，旨在随着人工智能（AI）芯片市场竞争白热化，全面强化自身供应链韧性。
这家芯片制造商还公布了一项耗资 8746 亿韩元的测试中心联合投资规划，该设施位于首尔以南的龙仁半导体产业集群，将允许中小型供应商在与商业芯片生产线相似的实际工况下验证其产品性能。
以下为该扶持计划的核心细节：
• SK海力士表示，其供应商扶持方案涵盖研发、测试、量产和销售四个阶段，旨在帮助中小企业克服资金和技术门槛。
• 该测试中心被命名为“Trinity Fab”，由 SK海力士与韩国中央政府及地方政府共同联合出资建设，预计将于 2027 年 5 月正式投入运营。根据公司公布的数据，SK海力士出资 4432 亿韩元，中央政府出资 3736 亿韩元，地方政府出资 577 亿韩元。
• Trinity Fab 测试中心将部署约 50 台先进制程设备（包括光刻机和刻蚀机等关键机台），使供应商能够在 12 英寸（300毫米）标准硅片上完成材料和组件的工艺验证。
• 为了降低供应商的研发财务风险，SK海力士表示将提前垫付部分开发成本，并在联合研发项目未能成功时提供专项补偿。
• 公司表示，该测试设施将由一家独立非营利基金会负责日常运营，以严格保护参与供应商的核心知识产权与商业机密。
• 该倡议还包括设立海外营销支持中心，协助韩国本土供应商拓展国际市场，并逐步降低对海外进口半导体关键零部件的依赖度。
• SK海力士还将与金融机构合作，在韩国贸易保险公社的担保下提供 2 万亿韩元的融资支持，同时开展其他项目向供应链企业（包括小型分包商）提供低息贷款和技术咨询服务。

title: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools
title_en: Apple’s new study looks to improve the effectiveness of AI health tools

inline_images.caption: applestudy1b
inline_images.alt: applestudy1b

author: The Verge AI
article_content:
Apple announced a new study today with the goal of better understanding how people interact with conversational AI health tools and how useful their responses actually are. The company is conducting the Apple Health AI Usage Study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform used by healthcare professionals that generates answers based on medical information from sources like The New England Journal of Medicine. Participants will use a new iOS app to ask medical questions and then rate the responses based on criteria including accuracy, detail, and relevance.

The app is now available for download, and enrollment starts today, with Apple looking for up to 200,000 people to contribute. Participants 21 and older must be based in the US, and although the app doesn’t use Apple Intelligence, it does require an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 26 or later.

Study participants can use the app to ask health-related questions and receive easily understandable responses with links to peer-reviewed clinical sources. The app relies on text-based prompts, and while dictation is an option using the iOS keyboard, the app isn’t integrated with Siri or Apple Intelligence.

[Image: Participants in the study will be given the opportunity to rate responses to health questions from the app. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/applestudy2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all]

During enrolment, participants are given the option to share Apple HealthKit data, like their activity, sleep, or clinical lab results, so responses will include more context about their own personal health. But privacy is a priority, and Apple says it has taken measures to ensure users’ information remains confidential and the data collected won’t be used to train AI models. The aim is to improve the design and functionality of AI-powered health tools so they can deliver relevant health information that’s easier for users to understand and act on.

“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life. Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” said Sumbul Desai, MD, Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness.

title_zh: 苹果启动健康AI应用效能研究计划
summary_zh: 苹果联手临床AI平台OpenEvidence启动大规模健康AI交互研究，招募20万名美国用户评估医疗问答工具准确性
article_content_zh:
苹果今天宣布了一项新研究，旨在更好地了解人们如何与对话式人工智能健康工具互动以及他们的反应实际上有多有用。该公司正在与 OpenEvidence 合作开展 Apple Health AI 使用研究，OpenEvidence 是医疗保健专业人员使用的临床 AI 平台，可根据《新英格兰医学杂志》等来源的医疗信息生成答案。参与者将使用新的 iOS 应用程序提出医疗问题，然后根据准确性、细节和相关性等标准对回答进行评分。

该应用程序现已可供下载，并于今日开始注册，Apple 正在寻找最多 20 万人参与贡献。 21 岁及以上的参与者必须居住在美国，尽管该应用程序不使用 Apple Intelligence，但它确实需要运行 iOS 26 或更高版本的 iPhone 15 Pro。

研究参与者可以使用该应用程序提出与健康相关的问题，并收到易于理解的答复，其中包含同行评审的临床资源的链接。该应用程序依赖于基于文本的提示，虽然可以使用 iOS 键盘进行听写，但该应用程序未与 Siri 或 Apple Intelligence 集成。

在注册过程中，参与者可以选择共享 Apple HealthKit 数据，例如他们的活动、睡眠或临床实验室结果，因此回复将包括更多有关他们个人健康状况的背景信息。但隐私是重中之重，苹果表示已采取措施确保用户信息保密，并且收集的数据不会用于训练人工智能模型。目的是改进人工智能健康工具的设计和功能，以便它们能够提供更容易让用户理解和采取行动的相关健康信息。

“在 Apple，我们相信负责任的创新始于科学严谨性和临床基础。健康是非常个性化的，进行专门的研究是了解人们如何在日常生活中参与、理解和评估健康 AI 的最深思熟虑的方式。这项研究的见解将有助于推进更广泛的科学对话，并确保随着技术的发展，我们继续构建值得信赖的工具，真正为人们的健康之旅提供支持，无论他们身在何处。”Apple 健康与健身副总裁 Sumbul Desai 医学博士说道。

title: Samsung conquered AI chips. Now it wants to build data centres
title_en: Samsung conquered AI chips. Now it wants to build data centres
author: Song Jung-a
article_content:
After conquering memory chips, Samsung wants to turn other parts of its sprawling business into AI supply chain champions, but analysts question whether it can replicate its success with semiconductors across the group.

In the past year, the South Korean conglomerate has taken steps to try to become a one-stop provider of AI infrastructure. It has invested $1bn in a KKR- and Nvidia-backed data centre operator, acquired a European cooling systems maker and signed a partnership with OpenAI to develop AI infrastructure.

The group’s hope is to be able to offer a service in which it can build data centres through its construction arm, operate them through its IT services unit and provide energy storage systems through its battery maker, in addition to supplying memory chips.

“Moving forward, Samsung is poised to expand its role from a traditional hardware component supplier to an active architect of the global AI infrastructure ecosystem,” it said following its $1bn investment in Helix Digital Infrastructure in September.

Samsung is betting that its future in the AI boom lies beyond semiconductors, a highly lucrative but also highly cyclical industry.

While best known for Samsung Electronics — the manufacturing juggernaut that makes chips, Galaxy smartphones and household appliances — Samsung Group is a vast conglomerate with businesses as wide-ranging as insurance and security services.

Many of them started as internal units to serve the conglomerate and still count Samsung as their primary customer, but the group hopes some of the subsidiaries can expand to external clients as AI demand takes hold.

Samsung SDS, which began as an in-house IT services provider and operates data centres mostly to support the group, is in early-stage talks with Anthropic and OpenAI to potentially sign them on as tenants. Analysts expect the company to generate annual data centre revenue of Won6.6tn ($4.9bn) by 2031, roughly six times current levels.

Last year, Samsung signed a partnership with OpenAI to supply advanced memory chips to the company’s Stargate data centre initiative.

The agreement included Samsung SDS collaborating with OpenAI on designing, developing and operating data centres. Construction arm Samsung C&T and shipbuilder Samsung Heavy Industries also said they would work with the US tech company on developing floating data centres.

Morgan Stanley said in a recent report that Samsung SDS was well positioned to benefit from a surge in data centre construction, a trend reinforced by governments around the world passing laws requiring information to be stored domestically.

McKinsey estimates global data centre capacity demand could almost triple by 2030, with AI workloads accounting for about 70 per cent of the total. Meeting AI computing needs alone could require $5.2tn in capital expenditure.

“Samsung has an opportunity to provide a total solution,” said Joungho Kim, a professor of electrical engineering at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology. “US Big Tech companies are strong in AI and software, but they rely heavily on external suppliers for hardware.”

However, recent tech earnings have sparked investor concerns about the astronomical sums being spent on AI infrastructure and whether future demand will justify the cost.

Electoral victories of Democratic candidates in the US who pledged to halt data centre construction in their states have added to worries of regulatory pushback.

But Sanjeev Rana, head of Korea research at CLSA, said that while there would be “ups and downs” in the market, the spending was “structural”.

“In several years [and] decades, we are going to see huge investments in AI data centre-related products,” he said.

For Samsung, the challenge is bringing together disparate parts of its business empire.

Until 2017, the conglomerate had a Future Strategy Office responsible for group-wide decisions, but it was dismantled following a political corruption scandal involving its leadership.

Since then, Samsung has relied on so-called co-ordination bodies that are more lightly staffed, have fewer resources and are split based on business lines.

Analysts said the lack of a central decision-making body could complicate efforts to pursue more ambitious AI infrastructure projects that require close co-operation.

“Samsung has a broad range of capabilities, but it has been relatively weak at bringing them together [into an integrated offering],” said Peter Lee, an analyst at Citi.

There are also questions about experience serving external customers at scale as several subsidiaries remain heavily dependent on Samsung for work.

Rana said the group’s more immediate opportunity was in designing the systems inside data centres rather than operating the facilities themselves.

Samsung already supplies a range of components used in AI infrastructure including high-bandwidth memory chips, advanced packaging substrates for semiconductors and backup battery units for servers.

“Improving and extending the advantages in components will serve it better. And these are high-margin businesses,” said Rana. “Owning or operating data centres, I am not sure actually that will play to their strengths.”

Many of them started as internal units to serve the conglomerate and still count Samsung as their primary customer, but the group hopes some of the subsidiaries can expand to external clients as AI demand takes hold.

Samsung SDS, which began as an in-house IT services provider and operates data centres mostly to support the group, is in early-stage talks with Anthropic and OpenAI to potentially sign them on as tenants. Analysts expect the company to generate annual data centre revenue of Won6.6tn ($4.9bn) by 2031, roughly six times current levels.

Last year, Samsung signed a partnership with OpenAI to supply advanced memory chips to the company’s Stargate data centre initiative.

The agreement included Samsung SDS collaborating with OpenAI on designing, developing and operating data centres. Construction arm Samsung C&T and shipbuilder Samsung Heavy Industries also said they would work with the US tech company on developing floating data centres.

Morgan Stanley said in a recent report that Samsung SDS was well positioned to benefit from a surge in data centre construction, a trend reinforced by governments around the world passing laws requiring information to be stored domestically.

McKinsey estimates global data centre capacity demand could almost triple by 2030, with AI workloads accounting for about 70 per cent of the total. Meeting AI computing needs alone could require $5.2tn in capital expenditure.

“Samsung has an opportunity to provide a total solution,” said Joungho Kim, a professor of electrical engineering at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology. “US Big Tech companies are strong in AI and software, but they rely heavily on external suppliers for hardware.”

However, recent tech earnings have sparked investor concerns about the astronomical sums being spent on AI infrastructure and whether future demand will justify the cost.

Electoral victories of Democratic candidates in the US who pledged to halt data centre construction in their states have added to worries of regulatory pushback.

But Sanjeev Rana, head of Korea research at CLSA, said that while there would be “ups and downs” in the market, the spending was “structural”.

“In several years [and] decades, we are going to see huge investments in AI data centre-related products,” he said.

For Samsung, the challenge is bringing together disparate parts of its business empire.

Until 2017, the conglomerate had a Future Strategy Office responsible for group-wide decisions, but it was dismantled following a political corruption scandal involving its leadership.

Since then, Samsung has relied on so-called co-ordination bodies that are more lightly staffed, have fewer resources and are split based on business lines.

Analysts said the lack of a central decision-making body could complicate efforts to pursue more ambitious AI infrastructure projects that require close co-operation.

“Samsung has a broad range of capabilities, but it has been relatively weak at bringing them together [into an integrated offering],” said Peter Lee, an analyst at Citi.

There are also questions about experience serving external customers at scale as several subsidiaries remain heavily dependent on Samsung for work.

Rana said the group’s more immediate opportunity was in designing the systems inside data centres rather than operating the facilities themselves.

Samsung already supplies a range of components used in AI infrastructure including high-bandwidth memory chips, advanced packaging substrates for semiconductors and backup battery units for servers.

“Improving and extending the advantages in components will serve it better. And these are high-margin businesses,” said Rana. “Owning or operating data centres, I am not sure actually that will play to their strengths.”

title: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch £1m partnership
title_en: The King’s Trust and OpenAI launch £1m partnership
author: OpenAI
article_content:
The new partnership will help young people build AI skills for the future workforce, prioritizing those not in education or employment.

The King’s Trust has announced a major partnership with OpenAI designed to help up to 25,000 young people build AI skills for work, prioritizing those not in education, employment or training.

OpenAI is making a £1m donation to the youth charity to support this work.

This is part of a wider program of nationally recognized AI qualifications that The Trust will launch in the coming months, designed to help young people stay ahead of a changing labor market.

The announcement comes as The King’s Trust marks its 50th year and looks to the future, helping ensure young people are supported to succeed in an increasingly AI-enabled world.

The King’s Trust and OpenAI have launched a £1 million partnership to help young people across the UK build AI skills for work, prioritizing those who are not in education, employment or training (NEET). The program aims to support up to 25,000 young people over the next 18 months, helping them develop practical skills and confidence to move toward education and employment in an AI-enabled economy.

The program will help address a gap in young people’s experience of AI while responding to their appetite to learn. The Open University’s Business Barometer 2026 found that 68% of 16–24-year-olds surveyed who were not in education, employment or training would be willing to train or upskill to improve their job prospects.

The partnership will help prepare young people for the opportunities and challenges of a rapidly changing world of work by combining opportunities to learn AI skills with recognized qualifications and practical experience. It forms part of a wider program of nationally recognized AI qualifications being developed by The King’s Trust, designed to equip young people with the skills employers need as AI transforms the world of work.

Working with employers, AI specialists and young people, The King’s Trust is exploring the skills young people will need in a world of work where AI is becoming part of everyday life, and how these can complement the employability skills already embedded across its programs.

Building on a 50-year legacy of supporting more than 1.3 million young people, The King’s Trust wants to ensure the next generation gains the skills and confidence needed to thrive in an AI-enabled economy.

Ahead of the final report of the independent Young People and Work review, the Rt Hon Alan Milburn welcomed the partnership, reflecting on the shared ambition to improve young people’s opportunities to learn and earn.

For OpenAI, the partnership forms part of a broader commitment to helping young people develop the skills and confidence to benefit from AI. It builds on wider efforts to make practical AI learning more accessible, including through OpenAI Academy, which provides free learning resources for students, job-seekers and other learners.

新的合作伙伴关系将帮助年轻人为未来的劳动力培养人工智能技能，优先考虑那些没有接受过教育或就业的人。

国王信托基金会（在新窗口中打开）宣布与 OpenAI 建立重要合作伙伴关系，旨在帮助多达 25,000 名年轻人培养工作所需的人工智能技能，优先考虑那些没有接受教育、就业或培训的年轻人。

OpenAI 正在向青年慈善机构捐赠 100 万英镑来支持这项工作。

这是该信托基金将在未来几个月推出的更广泛的国家认可人工智能资格计划的一部分，旨在帮助年轻人在不断变化的劳动力市场中保持领先地位。

这一消息发布之际，国王信托基金会正值成立 50 周年，并着眼于未来，帮助确保年轻人在人工智能日益普及的世界中获得成功。

国王信托基金会和 OpenAI 启动了一项 100 万英镑的合作伙伴关系，帮助英国各地的年轻人培养工作所需的人工智能技能，优先考虑那些没有接受教育、就业或培训的人 (NEET)。该计划旨在在未来 18 个月内为多达 25,000 名年轻人提供支持，帮助他们培养实用技能和信心，以在人工智能经济中接受教育和就业。

该计划将有助于弥补年轻人在人工智能体验方面的差距，同时满足他们的学习欲望。开放大学的 2026 年商业晴雨表（在新窗口中打开）发现，在接受调查的 16 至 24 岁未接受教育、就业或培训的人中，68% 愿意接受培训或提升技能以改善其就业前景。

该合作伙伴关系将通过将学习人工智能技能的机会与公认的资格和实践经验相结合，帮助年轻人为快速变化的工作世界的机遇和挑战做好准备。它是国王信托基金正在开发的更广泛的国家认可人工智能资格计划的一部分，旨在为年轻人提供雇主在人工智能改变工作世界时所需的技能。

国王信托基金与雇主、人工智能专家和年轻人合作​​，正在探索年轻人在人工智能正在成为日常生活一部分的工作世界中所需的技能，以及这些技能如何补充其项目中已经嵌入的就业技能。

国王信托基金会以 50 年来支持超过 130 万年轻人的传统为基础，希望确保下一代获得在人工智能经济中蓬勃发展所需的技能和信心。

在独立的年轻人与工作审查最终报告发布之前，艾伦·米尔本 (Alan Milburn) 阁下对此次合作表示欢迎，并反思了改善年轻人学习和赚钱机会的共同目标。

对于 OpenAI 来说，此次合作是其更广泛承诺的一部分，旨在帮助年轻人培养从人工智能中受益的技能和信心。它建立在更广泛的努力基础上，使实用的人工智能学习变得更加容易，包括通过 OpenAI Academy 为学生、求职者和其他学习者提供免费的学习资源。

title: Anthropic Is About to Become the World’s Most Important AI Stock
title_en: Anthropic Is About to Become the World’s Most Important AI Stock
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
At the $74 midpoint, each founder's stake is worth roughly $17.8 billion to $18.1 billion before accounting for the shares they plan to sell in the offering. One cofounder, little known outside the company, owns more stock than CEO Dario Amodei. Large founder allocations are not unusual in Silicon Valley.

Snap's Evan Spiegel and Bobby Murphy, for example, retained enough super-voting stock to control about 89% of the voting power after the company's 2017 IPO. What makes Anthropic unique is the number of founders with huge stakes and how evenly those stakes are divided. Anthropic cofounder and Chief Compute Officer Tom Brown owns about 244 million shares of the AI startup, according to its S-1.

That narrowly tops the stakes of Anthropic's six other cofounders, who each own roughly 232 million to 243 million shares. At the $74 midpoint of Anthropic's expected IPO range, Brown's stake would be worth about $18.1 billion. The filing shows that Brown plans to sell 3.38 million shares in the offering, worth roughly $250 million at that price, leaving him with stock worth about $17.8 billion.

Brown co-founded Anthropic with the Amodei siblings and four others in January 2021. He now serves as chief compute officer, where he leads the technical organization responsible for "securing, scaling, and effectively using" Anthropic's computing resources, according to the filing.

Brown also played an important role in the technology that led to today's generative-AI boom. Before Anthropic, he worked at OpenAI, where the S-1 says he led the engineering of GPT-3. Brown and Dario Amodei also co-invented what Anthropic calls "deep RLHF," which the company said was central to transforming base large language models into conversational assistants such as Claude.

After Brown, Sam McCandlish has the next-largest disclosed stake, with about 243.4 million shares, worth roughly $18 billion at the midpoint. Christopher Olah holds about 242.9 million shares, followed by chief science officer Jared Kaplan with 242.4 million shares and Jack Clark with 242.3 million shares.

At the midpoint, their stakes are each worth about $17.9 billion before their planned IPO sales. Anthropic president Daniela Amodei owns 241.4 million shares, worth about $17.9 billion at the midpoint. CEO Dario Amodei owns 240.6 million shares, worth about $17.8 billion, and also controls voting proxies over another 4.6 million shares.

The founders' influence will extend far beyond their economic stakes. Immediately before the IPO, Anthropic plans to issue a special Class F share to an LLC controlled by the seven cofounders. That single share will carry 50.1% of Anthropic's total voting power on matters submitted to stockholders generally, including the election of directors other than those selected by Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust.

In another unusual twist, Anthropic says each of its cofounders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the company to philanthropic causes. Some of Silicon Valley's biggest companies and venture firms also stand to make huge windfalls from Anthropic's public-market debut.

Amazon and Google will each own more than 5% of Anthropic after the IPO conversions, making them two of the company’s largest strategic shareholders. At the midpoint of Anthropic's expected IPO range, Amazon's 1.92 billion shares would be worth about $142 billion, while Google's stake would be worth about $132 billion.

Among traditional venture firms, the filing provides unusually detailed numbers for Spark Capital because Spark partner Yasmin Razavi sits on Anthropic's board and was the first firm to invest when Anthropic was valued at $4.5 billion in 2023. Spark-affiliated funds have invested across at least six Anthropic financings since 2023.

Menlo Ventures led a round in 2024 when Anthropic was valued at about $18 billion. They have now invested over $1.3 billion in the company, also earning them a stake between 1.5% and 2%, according to a person familiar with the matter. Lightspeed Venture Partners is the largest venture shareholder, owning almost 2% of Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter.

They led a round at a $61.5 billion valuation in late 2024 and continued to double down. Iconiq also amassed a large stake by investing $6 billion in the company, according to a person familiar with the matter, giving the firm an ownership stake between 1.5% and 2%. Bessemer Venture Partners first invested in the Series D in 2024 and continued to write checks in every round since.

It has spent around $800 million on Anthropic, making it the firm's largest investment to date. Bessemer has an almost 1% stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter. Other major winners include Coatue, which has invested $4.75 billion, and Sound Ventures, which invested more than $400 million, according to people familiar with the matter.

Other major shareholders include Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia Capital, Salesforce Ventures, Mubadala and Founders Fund. Please send along your tips. Email Ben or Katie anytime or contact them on Signal at benbergman.11 and kroof.26.

article_content_zh:
Anthropic 的 IPO 超额认购，公司目标是 904 亿美元的联合发行 Fiona Craig 太平洋标准时间 2026 年 11 月 11 日星期三上午 6:33 阅读 5 分钟 ANTH.PVT 据彭博新闻社周三发布的报道，Anthropic （纳斯达克股票代码：ANT）收到的投资者订单数倍于其计划的首次公开募股 (IPO) 中可用的股票数量，该人工智能公司正在为潜在股票做准备市场上市。

彭博社援引知情人士的话报道称，潜在机构投资者的大量兴趣表明了所报告的需求，其中包括通常与锚定投资者相关的大额订单。

报告中引用的监管文件显示，Anthropic 正寻求通过 IPO 和同时进行的私募筹集高达 904 亿美元的资金。

该公司的目标是完全摊薄后估值约为 1.4 万亿美元，但最终发行价、估值和分配的股票数量仍可能发生变化。

彭博社报道称，Anthropic 计划 IPO 的需求已超过可用股票分配数倍。

大型机构订单（有时被称为锚定规模订单）对需求水平做出了贡献。

此类订单可以在确定最终发行价和股票分配之前向承销商提供机构参与的指示。

然而，初步的兴趣并不一定代表已完成的购买，最终的分配可能与最初的请求不同。

随着公司及其承销银行继续进行营销流程，Anthropic 发行的细节仍有待修改。

Anthropic 正准备通过首次公开募股和同步私募相结合的方式筹集高达 904 亿美元的资金。

根据报道的备案细节，此次融资总额将超过 SpaceX 计划的 IPO 规模。

这两笔交易将为投资者提供参与 Anthropic 股票发行的不同途径。

公开发行将通过股票市场上市提供股票，而私募将涉及向合格投资者单独分配。

该公司尚未最终确定发行条款，最终收益将取决于出售的股票数量及其最终定价。

所报告的融资目标将使 Anthropic 拟议的交易成为迄今为止宣布的最大的股票发行交易之一。

Anthropic 正在寻求约 1.4 万亿美元的完全摊薄估值。

完全稀释估值考虑了公司的股权，假设相关可转换证券、期权和其他潜在股票发行已反映在股票数量中。

彭博社此前曾报道过这一估值目标，但仍取决于此次发行的最终条款。

报告称，初始定价方式可以为IPO营销过程中的调整提供灵活性。

如果投资者需求继续超过可用分配，Anthropic 及其承销商可以考虑修改拟议发行价。

然而，所提供的报告中尚未披露最终定价决定。

最终估值将取决于股票价格以及公司上市时完全稀释后的股数。

在拟议的上市之前，Anthropic 还在扩大其机构投资者的范围。

该公司计划于周五举办一场直播活动，首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和摩根大通首席执行官杰米·戴蒙 (Jamie Dimon) 出席。

该活动是 Anthropic 在发行过程中与潜在投资者沟通的努力的一部分。

投资者演示和管理层讨论可以提供有关公司运营、财务状况、业务战略和发行收益计划的信息。

所提供的报告没有提供该活动的详细议程，也没有具体说明预计将讨论的财务信息。

计划中的演示文稿发布之际，该公司正在继续评估机构对其拟议股票出售的兴趣。

彭博社的报告还描述了涉及现有 Anthropic 投资者寻求将风险转移给其他潜在买家的活动。

一些投资者正在推销其预期 IPO 分配的部分资金，而 IPO 前股权的持有者则通过特殊目的工具提供投资敞口。

这些安排可以在公司公开市场首次亮相之前或前后提供间接购买公司股票的机会。

特殊目的工具是可以代表参与投资者持有资产的投资结构。

根据其条款，此类结构可能允许现有投资者减少风险敞口，同时收取与交易相关的费用。

这一活动还引发了有关现有投资者在上市期间可能寻求出售的股票数量的问题。

然而，该报告没有量化这些安排所涉及的股票数量，也没有确定公开交易开始后可能发生的抛售量。

根据报告中引用的文件，高盛和摩根士丹利担任 Anthropic 计划 IPO 的牵头银行。

另外 20 家银行参与了此次交易。

承销小组负责与发行过程相关的活动，包括投资者营销、订单收集和股票分配。

Anthropic 计划在纳斯达克全球精选市场上市，股票代码为 ANT。

最终发行价、股份分配和交易开始日期尚未在所提供的信息中得到确认。

随着交易的进展，该公司及其银行集团将继续评估投资者的需求。

Anthropic 计划在股票市场首次亮相，吸引了比现有股票数量多几倍的初步投资者订单。

该公司正在通过首次公开募股（IPO）和同时进行的私募融资寻求高达 904 亿美元的融资，据报道，完全摊薄后的估值目标约为 1.4 万亿美元。

此次发行由高盛和摩根士丹利牵头，另有 20 家银行参与。

Anthropic 还正在准备一场由首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和摩根大通首席执行官杰米·戴蒙 (Jamie Dimon) 参加的投资者活动，作为其机构营销活动的一部分。

与此同时，有关现有股东营销分配和通过特殊目的载体发行敞口的报告表明，二次投资安排正在与计划上市同时发展。

IPO 的最终规模、定价和分配仍可能发生变化，报告的需求水平并不能保证交易的最终结果。
