fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Anthropic researchers Jake Eaton and Michael Graczyk: Launched Claude Fable 5.2, utilizing code-driven brushstroke simulation for image generation
[Root Cause & Mechanism] To explore agentic, non-diffusion paths for AI art with better stylistic consistency and process interpretability
[Key Technical Spec] Abandoned diffusion model path in favor of code-driven brushstroke simulation.
[Key Position & Outlook] Established persona-driven artistic workflows to ensure stylistic consistency and control.
article_content_en:
Anthropic's new language model Claude Fable 5.2 can create complex and even photorealistic paintings by using code to place hundreds of thousands of individual brushstrokes on a virtual canvas.

Current image models like Midjourney typically use diffusion, which gradually refines a noisy image into a clear result. Fable 5.2 takes a different approach by simulating the physical painting process, including bristle texture, how the paint goes on, and mistakes it then has to paint over.

Developer Jake Eaton showed on X what the approach can do. Eaton works at Anthropic, where he regularly contributes to research on language model values, safety mechanisms, and AI agent behavior.

When he asked Fable 5.2 to create a painting as hard to distinguish from a photograph as possible, the model generated an image of a shopping cart in a parking garage using roughly 700,000 simulated brushstrokes.

According to Eaton, Claude works without an external image model and without pre-rendered or traced source images. Each piece is a Python program of 1,000 to 2,000 lines that drives a simulated paint engine. The approach resembles agentic image editing, where language models pick tools and evaluate results.

Earlier attempts with the sibling model Opus 5.5 drew criticism for merely imitating existing art. Eaton responded by having Fable 5.2 develop its own artist personas with fictional backstories and consistent styles. The model needs several thousand brushstrokes per painting, and Eaton redirects them with comments.

### Without an undo button, the model has to commit to every stroke

Anthropic engineer Michael Graczyk shared a chat log and video of an experiment in which he asked Fable 5.2 to paint a bird at sunrise. The model could only use code to simulate the physics of bristles, wet paint, and canvas texture. It had to output every brushstroke manually as its own coordinate line, with no way to undo strokes once placed. That's what sets this method apart from AI-generated videos, where models like Flux 3 generate image sequences and their temporal consistency directly.

The resulting 21-second video uses a counter to track how the painting takes shape from exactly 111 strokes on a blank canvas. For the first stroke, the model output the color code #30346a, a width of 90 pixels, and five slightly wobbling waypoints. Fable 5.2 said it added the roughly seven-pixel wobble on purpose because a human arm doesn't draw a perfectly straight line either.

Between passes, the model looked at the canvas and reacted to its own mistakes like a real painter would. When the bird's back came out too thin and scraggly, the AI laid a bolder stroke over it, so the stray bristle marks along the edges now look like ruffled feathers.

In a second, 280-stroke piece showing two people painting at dusk, a late lighting effect accidentally smeared paint tubes and a cup on the table. Claude repainted those objects after the fact. The model also had both figures paint with their outer hands so their inner shoulders could touch, just as the prompt requested.

### The same spatial reasoning transfers to physical robots

Fable 5.2's ability to plan step by step and self-correct under physical constraints isn't limited to virtual canvases. According to Anthropic, the model is built for extremely demanding long-horizon technical tasks, as is Mythos 5.2, a version designed for verified security and biology researchers.

In internal tests, Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in black hole physics, designed three working electronic devices with circuit board manufacturer Diode, and used more than 1,000 sub-agents to program its own laptop operating system in eight days.

AI researcher Aris Zhu tested how the model performs with real robotic arms. He pitted Fable 5.2 against OpenAI's competing model GPT-6 Astra, with each using a physical robot arm to paint Van Gogh's "The Starry Night."Anthropic reports a score of 64.9 percent for Fable 5.2 on its internal RoboDojo Sim benchmark, compared with 29.8 percent for GPT-6 Astra.

Zhu's real-world comparison still shows limits in fine motor control. Astra painted faster, and so far only OpenAI's model has managed to stand a domino on end. It did so by slowly loosening its gripper to use gravity as a pivot point.

title: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days
title_en: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days

inline_images.caption: Nvidia GTC Berlin
inline_images.alt: Nvidia GTC Berlin

author: The Verge AI
article_content:
On October 29th, The New York Times reported that Nvidia co-founder and showman CEO Jensen Huang appeared to be the target of a Chinese spy plot. Any major tech CEO potentially being compromised by the Chinese government is concerning — especially Jensen Huang. “If you could draw the network diagram of the entire US AI ecosystem, Nvidia would be at the center of that,” Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, previously told The Verge. “If you could draw the diagram of the entire Nvidia ecosystem, a single man is standing at the heart of all of that.”

The Times reported that Jensen Huang had developed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. Alice Huang had been on the American government’s radar for some time, perhaps as early as 2024. Her company was investigated by the US Commerce Department over suspicions it was illegally smuggling Nvidia’s AI chips into China in violation of US government trade restrictions. Singapore authorities confiscated her passport back in June of 2025, eventually barring her from the country, after she reportedly gave “inaccurate information” to police. And perhaps more concerningly, some US officials believed she was passing information, possibly about Nvidia’s designs or the White House’s deliberations over trade restrictions, directly back to Beijing.

This made her relationship with Jensen Huang concerning for multiple reasons. Nvidia’s chips are considered crucial to America’s AI superiority and a matter of national security by the White House. The government has restricted the sale of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China since the Biden administration. But Jensen Huang has routinely pushed to loosen those trade restrictions. Meanwhile, he had gotten quite cozy with President Trump, once even putting him on speakerphone on-stage at the All-In Summit.

Then last week, things escalated quickly.

On Friday, November 6th, the Times reported that Alice Huang was specifically recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO. Though, there is some disagreement among US intelligence officials over the strength of evidence tying Alice Huang to Beijing. While the paper did not confirm it at the time, rumors suggested the “close relationship” between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang was romantic in nature.

On Sunday, November 8th, Jensen Huang admitted to having an extramarital affair, but did not name the Megaspeed exec and alleged Chinese spy specifically. Nvidia’s board announced that it was launching an investigation into its CEO shortly after.

Many believed that Jensen Huang would survive the scandal. His company’s importance to America’s booming AI industry and his crucial role at the company seemed to make him nearly untouchable. He was, after all, the only CEO the company had ever known with no clear and obvious succession plan in place, and he sat atop an unusual corporate structure with around 60 direct reports. (These numbers are slightly outdated, but according to the Harvard Business Review, 10 to 20 is far more common among Fortune 500 companies, and Tim Cook reportedly had 17 in 2015, which was deemed “a lot” by Business Insider.)

Then on Wednesday, November 11th, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had a second affair — this one with one of his direct reports, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care. Whether that was the last straw or if they were afraid it would be merely the tip of the iceberg, the board was ready to push Jensen Huang out, according to reports circulating that evening. According to Bloomberg, he had accepted his fate Wednesday evening reportedly looking “broken and shattered” and telling people, “I’m a piece of shit.”

On Thursday, November 12th, Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as CEO of Nvidia.

CFO Colette Kress was immediately named interim CEO, and acknowledged to employees that this has been an “extraordinarily difficult period.” Harvey Jones was also named the first board chair in the company’s history, already signaling there would be some changes to the corporate structure. In a memo to employees, Jones said the company would “search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates.”

But the destabilizing impact was immediate. Nvidia’s stock closed at an all-time high of $239.24 on October 6th. It closed at $162.85 on November 13th. It’s hard to overstate the importance of Nvidia to the US’s AI arms race with China, and the industry in general. The company has invested $99 billion in various AI labs, startups, and neo clouds. Plus has announced plans to mobilize over $500 billion in financing for building out AI data centers and other infrastructure.

Even before Jensen Huang had resigned, Nvidia was already facing a shareholder lawsuit claiming the company had deceived investors. Jensen Huang and the company’s spokespeople insisted that the relationship with Alice Huang and Megaspeed was “completely normal and not unusual.” Only days later, Jensen Huang admitted to an extramarital affair that raised “national security concerns” without naming anyone specifically. According to Reuters, Jensen Huang misled several Nvidia leaders, “including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld” about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang.

Many in the AI industry and Silicon Valley jumped to Jensen Huang’s defense. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney called it a “sad day for NVIDIA, developers, America, and all humanity,” in a particularly hyperbolic post. Elon Musk said on X that it would “be an honor” to hire Jensen Huang. Many of Nvidia’s employees even voiced their support to “bring back THE boss,” on an internal post.

Some even speculated that Jensen Huang was the victim of a vast conspiracy, whether that was a coup by some faction within Nvidia, or perhaps the goal of China all along had simply been to chase him from the CEO chair.

By Thursday night, Reuters reported a third affair, this one also with an Nvidia employee, though no further information has emerged.

First and foremost for Nvidia, it must find a new CEO. It’s possible that Kress eventually ceases to be “interim” CEO, but other names, including Apple’s hardware chief Johny Srouji, have also been rumored. (Donald Trump believes they should hire Tim Cook, but to call that unlikely would be an understatement.)

It’s also possible that Nvidia will undergo a dramatic reorganization. Whoever takes over as CEO is unlikely to keep the 60 direct reports of Jensen Huang. With a first-ever board chair in Jones, it’s also possible that the board of directors will play a larger role in the company going forward.

The board’s investigation into Jensen Huang that began on November 8th is ongoing. The scandal is likely to drag on for some time. With the possibility that Jensen Huang will have to testify before Congress, the company may choose to be proactive about disclosing any additional information publicly.

The incoming Democratic majority is expected to come down harder on Silicon Valley than the current Republican Congress. While it’s unclear just how far the new House and Senate will go in trying to rein in the tech industry and its billionaire leaders, it’s possible it will try to make an example of Nvidia as an early act of strength. If Nvidia is found to have been turning a blind eye to companies like Megaspeed, which are suspected of funneling advanced chips to China, it could face civil or criminal penalties. And it seems increasingly likely that stricter trade restrictions will be implemented on Nvidia’s chips, which could increase tensions with China in an already costly trade war.

There is a possibility that Jensen Huang could face criminal charges. In May, he claimed that Nvidia had “zero percent” market share in China due to stringent export restrictions. But shortly after, Culper Research published a report claiming that in reality over 20 percent of the company’s 2026 compute revenue was from China, though that number has not been independently verified. The report cited “illegal GPU diversion and Southeast Asian intermediaries” as the primary source of those revenues. Among the largest of those intermediaries, according to Culper Research, was Megaspeed, which Nvidia repeatedly vouched for to the US government.

If proof is established that the CEO was knowingly helping Megaspeed or any other companies to illegally divert restricted chips to China, he could face criminal charges. And, as The Verge’s Elizabeth Lopatto put it, “under a functioning legal system, [he] could actually go to jail.”

There is the chance that members of the current administration are also tied up in this scandal, as it’s unclear how much the White House knew and when.

Considering Nvidia’s sizable investments, borrowing to build data centers, and the importance of its hardware, there are tons of open questions about how this impacts not just the AI industry, but the American economy as a whole. Nvidia is essentially propping up a large part of the tech industry and, if money stops flowing out of its coffers, it could drag a lot of other companies down with it.

There are also open questions about how this impacts the American public’s perception of the AI industry. The new Democratic majority was elected in part by campaigning against AI companies and the explosion of data center buildout across the country. That one of its more prominent CEOs is now embroiled in a spying scandal and multiple extramarital affairs probably isn’t going to endear the industry to the public.

* Megaspeed is just one of multiple companies that Nvidia has been approved to sell chips with suspicious offices. The New York Times described New Matrix’s headquarters as “a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be.”

* Jensen Huang’s connections to Super Micro are also under scrutiny. Earlier this year, one of its founders, an employee, and a contractor for the company were indicted by the Justice Department for conspiring to violate American export controls and divert Nvidia chips to China.

* While a lot has changed, it’s still worth reading the Times’ first big report from October 29th that lays the groundwork for the eventual deluge of international intrigue and infidelity that ultimately led to Jensen Huang’s downfall.

* The New York Times paints a fascinating portrait of Alice Huang who now finds herself at the center of an international espionage scandal.

* The Decoder interview with Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, digs into what China hoped to get out of Jensen Huang.

article_content_zh:
10 月 29 日，《纽约时报》报道称，英伟达联合创始人兼 CEO 黄仁勋似乎成为中国间谍阴谋的目标。任何可能受到中国政府损害的主要科技公司首席执行官都值得担忧——尤其是黄仁勋。 “如果你能画出整个美国人工智能生态系统的网络图，那么英伟达将处于其中的中心，”布鲁金斯学会约翰·L·桑顿中国中心的外交政策研究员凯尔·陈 (Kyle Chan) 此前告诉 The Verge。 “如果你能画出整个 Nvidia 生态系统的图表，就会发现有一个人站在这一切的核心。”

据《泰晤士报》报道，黄仁勋与新加坡数据中心公司 Megaspeed 的高管 Alice Huang（无亲属关系）建立了“密切关系”。 Alice Huang 早在 2024 年就已经受到美国政府的关注。她的公司因涉嫌违反美国政府贸易限制，将 Nvidia 的人工智能芯片非法走私到中国而受到美国商务部的调查。据报道，在她向警方提供“不准确信息”后，新加坡当局于 2025 年 6 月没收了她的护照，最终禁止她入境。也许更令人担忧的是，一些美国官员认为她正在将信息直接传回北京，这些信息可能涉及英伟达的设计或白宫对贸易限制的审议。

这让她与黄仁勋的关系因多种原因而令人担忧。白宫认为英伟达的芯片对美国的人工智能优势至关重要，而且事关国家安全。自拜登政府以来，政府一直限制英伟达最先进的芯片向中国销售。但黄仁勋经常推动放松这些贸易限制。与此同时，他与特朗普总统关系非常融洽，甚至有一次在全押峰会的舞台上让他打开免提电话。

然后上周，事情迅速升级。

11 月 6 日星期五，《泰晤士报》报道称，爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 被中国国家安全部专门招募来监视英伟达首席执行官。不过，美国情报官员对于将爱丽丝·黄与北京联系起来的证据的强度存在一些分歧。虽然该报当时没有证实这一点，但有传言称黄仁勋和黄爱丽之间的“亲密关系”本质上是浪漫的。

11 月 8 日星期日，黄仁勋承认自己有婚外情，但没有具体点名 Megaspeed 高管和被指控的中国间谍。不久后，英伟达董事会宣布对其首席执行官展开调查。

许多人相信黄仁勋会在丑闻中幸存下来。他的公司对美国蓬勃发展的人工智能行业的重要性以及他在公司中的关键作用似乎使他几乎不可撼动。毕竟，他是公司有史以来唯一一位没有制定清晰明确的继任计划的首席执行官，而且他领导着一个不寻常的公司结构，有大约 60 名直接下属。 （这些数字有点过时，但根据《哈佛商业评论》，财富 500 强公司中 10 到 20 个的情况更为常见，据报道，蒂姆·库克在 2015 年有 17 个，《商业内幕》认为这个数字“很多”。）

然后在 11 月 11 日星期三，《纽约时报》报道称黄仁勋有第二段恋情——这一次是与他的直接下属之一、英伟达医疗保健副总裁金伯利·鲍威尔 (Kimberly Powell) 发生的。据当晚流传的报道称，无论这是最后一根稻草，还是担心这只是冰山一角，董事会已经准备好将黄仁勋赶下台。据彭博社报道，周三晚上，他接受了自己的命运，据报道，他看上去“心碎且破碎”，并告诉人们，“我是一坨屎”。

11 月 12 日星期四，英伟达宣布黄仁勋辞去英伟达首席执行官职务。

首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯立即被任命为临时首席执行官，并向员工承认这是一个“异常困难的时期”。哈维·琼斯还被任命为公司历史上第一位董事会主席，这已经表明公司结构将会发生一些变化。琼斯在给员工的一份备忘录中表示，公司将“同时考虑内部和外部候选人，寻找永久继任者”。

但破坏稳定的影响是立竿见影的。 10 月 6 日，英伟达股价收于 239.24 美元的历史新高。 11 月 13 日收盘价为 162.85 美元。英伟达对于美国与中国的人工智能军备竞赛以及整个行业的重要性怎么强调都不为过。该公司已向各种人工智能实验室、初创公司和 Neo 云投资了 990 亿美元。 Plus宣布计划筹集超过5000亿美元的资金用于建设人工智能数据中心和其他基础设施。

甚至在黄仁勋辞职之前，英伟达就已经面临股东诉讼，指控该公司欺骗投资者。黄仁勋和该公司发言人坚称，与 Alice Huang 和 Megaspeed 的关系“完全正常，并不罕见”。几天后，黄仁勋承认了引发“国家安全担忧”的婚外情，但没有具体点名任何人。据路透社报道，黄仁勋在他与黄仁勋关系的性质上误导了几位英伟达领导人，“包括总法律顾问蒂姆·泰特和首席营销官艾莉森·瓦贡菲尔德”。

人工智能行业和硅谷的许多人都站出来为黄仁勋辩护。 Epic Games 首席执行官 Tim Sweeney 在一篇特别夸张的帖子中称这是“对 NVIDIA、开发者、美国和全人类来说悲伤的一天”。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 在 X 上表示，聘用黄仁勋将是“一种荣幸”。英伟达的许多员工甚至在内部帖子中表示支持“让老板回来”。

甚至有人猜测，黄仁勋是一个巨大阴谋的受害者，无论是英伟达内部某个派系的政变，还是中国一直以来的目标只是将他赶下CEO宝座。

title: Inside the first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, featuring AI announcers, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins, as the ceremony was mired in technical issues (Corbin Bolies/Variety)
title_en: Inside the first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, featuring AI announcers, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins, as the ceremony was mired in technical issues (Corbin Bolies/Variety)

inline_images.caption: The Sonic Intelligence Academy
inline_images.alt: The Sonic Intelligence Academy

author: Variety
article_content:
I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was “the winner…” followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson.

To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA’s “Verified Registry,” which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a “human + AI hybrid”).

Registered artists then nominate their peers in the 25 categories up for consideration — everything from “AI Song of the Year” to “Best AI Pop Song” to “Best AI Comedic Song” — and then vote on the winners. One of those nominees was Xania Monet, the AI persona of Telisha “Nikki” Jones, who a day earlier won the AI Album of the Year category at SIQA’s inaugural summit and who would eventually go on to win both artist and song of the year, three out of four of the awards’ top categories. (The fourth, producer of the year, went to “DJ Shawn Q.”)

The Sonic Intelligence Academy is the brainchild of software engineer Timirah “TJ” James and her sister Mia James. Since its January launch, it has worked to establish an awards program to counter the mainstream music industry’s aversion to AI. The group believes there needs to be infrastructure that supports those using AI to create music, rather than dismissing its existence, and it hopes to be an AI counterpart to the longstanding Recording Academy that governs the Grammy Awards. It advocates for artists to publicly associate themselves with their AI-powered work, eager to highlight the humans who helped create the product.

It’s a noble, if surprising, decision to embrace its role as counterculture when AI artists continue to pursue a Billboard charting position. Some of its methods are a little overt, perhaps intentionally: After some in the industry spurned the idea of AI-generated music charting on Billboard’s industry-standard charts, the group used a week in January ahead of the Grammys to launch its own charts exclusively for AI music. The Mayan is a 12-minute walk from the Crypto.com Arena, the Grammys’ longtime home.

The moves are not subtle, but subtlety is not the organization’s goal. The group and awards’ existence alone reflects those in the AI music space trying to move past the thorny legal questions surrounding AI music, which have led to lawsuits by artists and record labels against generators like Suno and Udio over copyright infringement, and into a realm of relevance within the genres they’re trying to embody.

It is, in a word, new, and new things mean kinks to work out.

The first kink I noticed was when, as I arrived 30 minutes before the red carpet was set to begin, the doors to the venue were locked. I had to pull on each door before someone opened one, which led me to the check-in stand (bypassing any form of security, which didn’t seem to exist). I entered the foyer and arrived at the makeshift red carpet, where about 12, mostly independent media ventures set up cameras to interview the various nominees, presenters, and VIPs who’d grace the roughly 7-foot-long red carpet in front of one of the two step-and-repeat backdrops. A spokesperson told me 29 media outlets had signed up to cover the event, but that some couldn’t make it because of the sudden flight ground-stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration around 12:30 p.m. PT. Whether human or AI, aviation afflictions come for us all.

The guests gracing the red carpet were not screens rolled out displaying AI avatars, contrary to a reasonable assumption. Instead, the human creators behind the digital faces strutted the carpet in their Sunday best, treating the night less as music’s biggest night and more as the biggest night for their music. Sequined dresses and colorful blazers strolled through, stopping to speak with outlets like Reuters to the fiery red mohawk-sporting, sequin-wearing host of “The Iconic Punk Oz” Oz Powers to, tucked against a wall and steps from the red carpet, an effective AI red carpet correspondent housed inside a tall, white faux-stone vessel. The contraption was developed by the event’s top sponsor, Deepgram, an AI startup specializing in text-to-speech agents.

The device, which knew the artists and pressed them about the event, struck in me a slight fear about whether people might opt for robot reporters instead of humans, though that fear subsided when I realized this device could not appear on the red carpet because it could not move. The creators seemed more eager to speak to the physical reporters anyway, with some of them emphasizing the human elements of their AI work. Fredro Starr, one half of the rap group Onyx, spent much of the carpet touting the human vocals that made up his AI-beat-laden record “It All Started in Brooklyn,” which he claimed was the first AI album on vinyl.

“You can’t replace [humans],” Starr told me, using the carpet to debut his new moniker, “Mad AI.” “The feeling that you get was what we bring with the spirit of hip-hop. So vocally, you can hear that, but the AI just took it to another level.”

Inside the theater, SIQA tried to bring a party-like feel to the function. A bar at the back of the venue —at a charge — kept well drinks flowing, and the bar top was littered with copies of a sponsored version of the newspaper “Rolling Out” featuring interviews with many of the nominees and James, the SIQA founder. One of those featured, Xania Monet founder Jones, sparked a wave of controversy last year when some of her Monet songs hit some of Billboard’s genre charts, leading to an interview with CBS’s Gayle King and to Kehlani slamming a $3 million record deal Jones received. As she waited for a drink by the bar ahead of the event’s start, Jones told me she wasn’t worried about the AI of it all overshadowing the pursuit of legitimacy within the greater music industry.

“AI is just a tool,” she said. “It just emphasizes what we do. I just feel like we should all be one.”

But despite that lofty goal, the kinks kept rearing their heads.

The event started about 30 minutes past its 6:15 p.m. start time, skipping a planned opening video montage for a dance break performed and choreographed by actor Giovanni Wilson with eight dancers to a seemingly AI-produced song that described — in literal terms — how we were at the inaugural AI music awards. The delay forced the show to skip introducing the nominees for the first half of the awards and instead have presenters just state the winner, robbing some attendees of hearing their names called for what felt like one of their biggest achievements.

The event was hosted by Wilson and podcast host Lana Hout, one half of the podcasting duo the “AI Chicks,” with a three-member house band of real people playing guitar, bass, keys and drums, soundtracking much of the night. The two hosts shared the only two microphones apparently available throughout the night, with a teleprompter loaded with the Claude-generated run-of-show, but they often seemed lost about what category, presenter, performance or commercial break was next.

At one point, Hout and Wilson were confused over whether they would cut to commercial or bring out the two presenters for best AI country artist. They then brought out the two country award presenters, only for Hout to walk back out mid-introduction to interrupt and say that, actually, they would go to commercial break. The award was eventually presented 13 minutes later with a different presenter.

Oftentimes, the use of AI seemed to hover over some of the technical hiccups. Deepgram was meant to power an AI voice that introduced the night’s presenters and nominees, but it often didn’t work and, when it did, talked over many of the presenters. Deepgram also had a commercial that played throughout the evening, but it would sometimes play at random moments even when a commercial break wasn’t called. The Deepgram team sat on the couch to my left, and when I looked over to see their reaction to the madness, one member had her head in her hands.

Early in the night, Wilson tried to introduce a trailer for his latest acting gig, the Terrance Howard-led film “A Good Hand Wasted” that he said used AI to help finish the project, but none of Wilson’s cues seemed to get it to play. Once it finally did, the screen only played a portion of the trailer before Howard’s face even appeared.

“So, ugh,” he said, before raising his hand to summon the audience’s applause.

The teleprompter was not much help, often shifting rapidly as presenters were speaking. The chaos led Wilson, who spent much of the night trying to maintain some decorum throughout the frustration, to joke they were “dealing with a prompter that has Tourette’s.”

Some of the greatest energy came from the evening’s nearly 10 performances, all of which made the cut despite the event running nearly 40 minutes behind schedule the entire night.

There had been some speculation over how, exactly, songs produced with AI and presented by AI avatars would play on stage. It turns out, through the power of lip-syncing and acting. Some acts, like country artist Ava Bentley and R&B artist EJ Rogers, lip-synced their entire performance, while others relied on hired performers who did even that for them. For “Chaisen Hale,” a project that features a video of an AI-generated boy with AI-generated vocals, a human lookalike singer named John Victor, 14, was brought out to lip-sync to the track. Attendees — including one duo, for some reason, dressed as Frankenstein and his bride — were generally riveted.

Nearly all of the performances were backed by the live band and dancers, who were provided to the artists for free by SIQA. Many who produce music with AI say they did so because they could not afford the studio musicians and resources required to bring their tracks to life, which made the reliance on the house band feel more like an opportunity to live out their dreams without the cost often paid by traditional artists who hire such musicians to produce their work.

Some of the only actual live vocals came from a rapper named GodFellow and Grammy-winning singers Eric Bellinger and Candace Wakefield, the latter of whom made a point to note the “hiccups” throughout the night and that she was singing live as she performed a song by AI artist “Aria Blue.” The performances captured much of what remained in the crowd, which grew smaller and smaller as the night progressed.

James, the SIQA founder, acknowledged the “technical difficulties” ahead of presenting Jones with her awards, but she promised those would be resolved ahead of next year’s ceremony.

“Because there will be a next year because this is the new music industry,” she told the crowd around 9:45 p.m., just as it was hitting its hard end time. ”SIQA has created the infrastructure for that industry and for all the artists coming up in that industry.”

And for many of the people in the room, that’s all they wanted. One artist, Sheena Taylor, accepted her award for best AI gospel song for a track called “I Denounce You, Satan,” by acknowledging the intense traumas she endured that led to a religious discovery. Another artist named Ramona Höffel, a 56-year-old woman who spends her days helping disabled people, flew in from Switzerland to represent her AI persona “Vireya” on her first-ever red carpet. (When I addressed her by her given name, she snapped at me.)

“I have a lot of ideas and wishes, and for a long time I paint, then I write, and that’s not enough,” she said, visibly nervous to be the first person to walk the red carpet. “The music gives me room to all this bring outside of my brain.”

I thought about Höffel’s words as I left the venue just after 10 p.m., well past the event’s scheduled 9:30 end, and into the downtown rain. To my right was a line forming to get into the venue for “Club 2010s” night, now delayed due to the prolonged awards show. It’s unclear whether AI music will generate an enduring monoculture in the way the music from the 2010s has, particularly as the larger music industry has mostly ostracized it. But it’s left people like Höffel feeling stronger, which is all someone like 2011 chart-topper Kelly Clarkson could ask for.

article_content_zh:
当我在走向人工智能音乐奖的路上听到的第一句话是“获胜者……”，然后是凯莉·克拉克森甜美的声音时，我知道事情有点不对劲。

为了获得奖项资格，艺术家需要将他们的曲目注册到 SIQA 的“验证注册表”，这表明歌曲是否完全由人工智能生成、在人工智能的帮助下制作，或者以克隆人的声音来主导曲调（该组织称之为“人类 + 人工智能混合体”）。

然后，注册艺术家在 25 个类别中提名他们的同行以供考虑——从“年度人工智能歌曲”到“最佳人工智能流行歌曲”再到“最佳人工智能喜剧歌曲”——然后投票选出获胜者。其中一位提名者是 Xania Monet，她是 Telisha “Nikki” Jones 的人工智能角色，一天前，她在 SIQA 首届峰会上赢得了年度人工智能专辑类别，并最终赢得了年度艺术家和年度歌曲，这是该奖项四个顶级类别中的三项。 （第四位，年度制作人，颁给了“DJ Shawn Q”。）

声波智能学院是软件工程师蒂米拉·“TJ”·詹姆斯和她的妹妹米娅·詹姆斯的创意。自一月份推出以来，它一直致力于建立一个奖项计划，以应对主流音乐行业对人工智能的厌恶。该组织认为，需要有基础设施来支持那些使用人工智能创作音乐的人，而不是忽视它的存在，并且它希望成为管理格莱美奖的长期录音学院的人工智能对手。它提倡艺术家公开将自己与人工智能驱动的作品联系起来，渴望突出帮助创造该产品的人类。

当人工智能艺术家继续追求广告牌排行榜的位置时，接受其反主流文化的角色是一个崇高但令人惊讶的决定。它的一些方法有点公开，也许是故意的：在一些业内人士拒绝在公告牌行业标准排行榜上人工智能生成音乐排行榜的想法之后，该组织利用一月份格莱美颁奖典礼前一周的时间推出了自己的专门针对人工智能音乐的排行榜。 Mayan酒店距离格莱美奖的长期所在地Crypto.com Arena体育场有12分钟步行路程。

这些举动并不微妙，但微妙并不是该组织的目标。该团体和奖项的存在本身就反映了人工智能音乐领域的人们试图摆脱围绕人工智能音乐的棘手法律问题，这些问题导致艺术家和唱片公司因侵犯版权而对 Suno 和 Udio 等生成器提起诉讼，并进入他们试图体现的流派的相关领域。

简而言之，新事物意味着需要解决的问题。

我注意到的第一个问题是，当我在红地毯开始前 30 分钟到达时，会场的门被锁上了。在有人打开一扇门之前，我必须拉上每一扇门，这将我带到办理登机手续的柜台（绕过任何形式的安检，而安检似乎并不存在）。我走进门厅，来到临时红地毯上，大约 12 家主要是独立的媒体企业架起了摄像机，采访各个提名者、主持人和贵宾，他们在两个步进重复背景之一前为大约 7 英尺长的红地毯增光添彩。一位发言人告诉我，已有 29 家媒体报名报道此次活动，但由于美国联邦航空管理局在中午 12 点 30 分左右突然发布航班地面停止令，一些媒体未能参加。 PT。无论是人类还是人工智能，航空苦难都会降临到我们所有人身上。

与合理的假设相反，走上红地毯的客人并不是显示人工智能头像的屏幕。相反，数字面孔背后的人类创造者以他们周日最好的姿态在地毯上昂首阔步，将这个夜晚视为音乐最盛大的夜晚，而更多地将其视为他们音乐最盛大的夜晚。亮片连衣裙和色彩缤纷的西装外套漫步其中，停下来与路透社等媒体交谈，与《标志性朋克绿野仙踪》中火红的莫霍克发型、穿着亮片的主持人奥兹·鲍尔斯 (Oz Powers) 交谈，他靠在墙边，距离红地毯几步之遥，是一位高效的人工智能红毯记者，住在一个高大的白色人造石容器内。该装置是由该活动的顶级赞助商 Deepgram 开发的，Deepgram 是一家专门从事文本转语音代理的人工智能初创公司。

这个设备认识艺术家，并向他们询问有关这一事件的信息，这让我有点担心人们是否会选择机器人记者而不是人类，尽管当我意识到这个设备因为无法移动而不能出现在红地毯上时，这种恐惧就消退了。无论如何，创作者似乎更渴望与现场记者交谈，其中一些人强调了人工智能工作中的人为因素。说唱乐队 Onyx 的成员弗雷德罗·斯塔尔 (Fredro Starr) 在地毯上花了很多时间来宣传人类的声音，这些声音构成了他的人工智能节拍唱片《一切都始于布鲁克林》，他声称这是第一张人工智能黑胶唱片专辑。

“你无法取代（人类），”斯塔尔告诉我，他在地毯上首次展示了他的新绰号“疯狂人工智能”。 “你得到的感觉就是我们用嘻哈精神带来的。所以从声音上来说，你可以听到，但人工智能只是将它提升到了另一个水平。”

在剧院内，SIQA 试图为活动带来一种派对般的感觉。会场后面的一个收费酒吧让饮料畅通无阻，酒吧顶部散落着赞助版的《Rolling Out》报纸，其中采访了许多提名者和 SIQA 创始人詹姆斯。其中一位特色人物是 Xania Monet 创始人琼斯，去年她的一些莫奈歌曲登上了 Billboard 的一些流派排行榜，引发了一场争议，导致哥伦比亚广播公司盖尔·金 (Gayle King) 接受采访，凯拉尼 (Kehlani) 猛烈抨击了琼斯收到的 300 万美元唱片合约。活动开始前，当她在酒吧等待喝一杯时，琼斯告诉我，她并不担心人工智能会掩盖整个音乐行业对合法性的追求。

“人工智能只是一个工具，”她说。 “它只是强调我们所做的事情。我只是觉得我们都应该成为一体。”

尽管目标如此崇高，但那些怪癖却不断抬头。

title: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove
title_en: AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove

inline_images.caption: Photo Illustration of AI DJ
inline_images.alt: Photo Illustration of AI DJ

author: Reece Rogers
article_content:
I usually can’t pinpoint the moment I stop using a software feature, with most tools drifting out of fashion without an expiration date. That’s not the case with YouTube Music’s “Beyond the Beat,” an AI-generated DJ that explains songs to you.

YouTube Music is my music-streaming service of choice. And since I’m a software reporter, I always enable the beta features available through YouTube Labs, which include Beyond the Beat. YouTube’s AI DJ randomly interjects for about 30 seconds between songs, teeing up the vibe shift and providing context about the next track.

More listeners are encountering synthetic commentary built into their music streaming apps. While YouTube launched this experimental AI DJ in 2025, Spotify first introduced a similar tool back in 2023. It doubled down on its AI DJ efforts in November, expanding the different personalities available to users and adding more controls over the commentary.

These AI DJs aren’t just annoying. Their attempts to provide helpful context and mimic human candor ultimately fall flat. Lucky for me, both features are optional and avoidable.

After months of leaving it enabled, a bad experience with Beyond the Beat this week pushed me to swear off AI DJs altogether. I was listening to a pop divas playlist as part of my morning workout and got slapped with 30 seconds of exposition after a Slayyyter track:

“Hey Boy delivers that high-energy surge perfectly, but we're shifting our focus to a sharper, more visceral reality. In Rock Music, Charli XXC [sic] weaves in a biting, dark sense of humor regarding the physical toll of her relentless 2024 and 2025 touring. She turns the genuine nerve damage she sustained on the road into a strange sort of battle scar, reclaiming the exhaustion of a weary party girl as a badge of honor. It's an unflinching look at the cost behind the spectacle, where the grind of the industry becomes the actual subject matter. Here is Rock Music by Charli XXC [sic].”

What a lengthy paragraph of platitudes with little substance. That’s not even mentioning how the AI DJ butchered the pronunciation of a little-known, indie act called Charli XCX. This flub reflected my overall experience with YouTube Music’s AI DJ. It took me out of the groove and didn’t feel additive.

In another example, it went in-depth on the meaning of Olivia Rodrigo’s Expectations remix featuring Chappell Roan, calling it a "structural interpretation” that unpacks the “nuances of queer dating.” Then YouTube Music played the original track, sans Roan; so much for the queer yearning.

Curious how Spotify’s AI DJ experience would compare, I upgraded my account to the premium tier for access to that beta software. One of the biggest recent changes to Spotify’s AI DJ was adding new voices to the lineup, so I went into my settings and played the introduction clips for each of the eight English-language voices.

Maybe I was already a bit miffed from my YouTube Music experience because these voices immediately started to frustrate me. Multiple voices leaned into filler words such as “you know” and “like,” as the AI described the next songs it would play. Knowing an AI voice is being trained to use filler words to sound more human gave me the uncanny-valley ick.

Spotify’s AI DJ was fairly different from YouTube Music’s version. On Spotify, the AI DJ is also an algorithmically guided experience that picks songs for you based on past listening habits and song requests. Overall, Spotify’s synthetic commentary felt tighter and more tolerable than YouTube’s blabbering DJ. That said, neither software experience was enjoyable enough for me to return.

Although Spotify claims it has “80 percent of listeners coming back to DJ week after week,” according to the company’s launch blog, I won’t be one of them. My rejection of AI DJs isn’t based on how they audibly sound. The voices, from both companies, are decent and sound convincingly human. The content of their commentary is what truly turns me off. Whether it’s empty platitudes or mimicking human mistakes, I’ve heard enough.

article_content_zh:
YouTube Music 是我选择的音乐流媒体服务。由于我是一名软件记者，因此我总是启用 YouTube 实验室提供的测试版功能，其中包括 Beyond the Beat。 YouTube 的 AI DJ 在歌曲之间随机插入约 30 秒，营造氛围转变并提供有关下一首曲目的背景信息。

越来越多的听众正在遇到内置于音乐流媒体应用程序中的综合评论。 YouTube 在 2025 年推出了这款实验性 AI DJ，而 Spotify 早在 2023 年就首次推出了类似的工具。该公司在 11 月加倍加大了 AI DJ 的力度，扩大了用户可用的不同个性，并增加了对评论的更多控制。

这些人工智能 DJ 不仅令人讨厌。他们试图提供有用的背景并模仿人类的坦诚，最终以失败告终。对我来说幸运的是，这两个功能都是可选且可以避免的。

在启用它几个月后，本周 Beyond the Beat 的一次糟糕体验迫使我完全放弃人工智能 DJ。作为早上锻炼的一部分，我正在听流行歌星的播放列表，在 Slayyyter 曲目之后，我被长达 30 秒的解释所困扰：

“Hey Boy 完美地传达了那种高能量的冲击力，但我们正在将注意力转向更尖锐、更发自内心的现实。在《摇滚音乐》中，Charli XXC [原文如此]以一种尖锐的黑色幽默感讲述了她在 2024 年和 2025 年无情的巡演中所遭受的身体伤害。她将在路上遭受的真正的神经损伤变成了一种奇怪的战斗伤疤，将疲惫的派对女孩的疲惫重新视为荣誉徽章。这是对这一奇观背后的成本的坚定审视，其中行业的苦差事成为了真正的主题，这是 Charli XXC 的摇滚音乐[原文如此]。”

多么冗长的陈词滥调，内容却很少。更不用说 AI DJ 是如何毁掉一个鲜为人知的独立艺人 Charli XCX 的发音的了。这个失误反映了我对 YouTube Music 的 AI DJ 的整体体验。它让我脱离了困境，并且没有感觉有任何附加。

在另一个例子中，它深入探讨了奥利维亚·罗德里戈（Olivia Rodrigo）与查普尔·罗恩（Chappell Roan）合作的《期望》混音版的含义，称其为“结构性解释”，揭示了“酷儿约会的细微差别”。然后 YouTube Music 播放了原曲（没有 Roan）；奇怪的渴望就到此为止。

我很好奇 Spotify 的 AI DJ 体验会如何比较，因此我将我的帐户升级到高级级别以访问该测试版软件。 Spotify 的 AI DJ 最近最大的变化之一是在阵容中添加了新的声音，因此我进入我的设置并播放了八种英语声音中每一种的介绍剪辑。

也许我已经对 YouTube Music 体验感到有点恼火了，因为这些声音立即开始让我感到沮丧。当人工智能描述它将要播放的下一首歌曲时，多个声音倾向于使用“你知道”和“喜欢”等填充词。知道人工智能的声音正在被训练使用填充词来听起来更人性化，这让我产生了一种恐怖谷般的恶心。

Spotify 的 AI DJ 与 YouTube Music 的版本有很大不同。在 Spotify 上，AI DJ 也是一种算法引导的体验，可以根据过去的收听习惯和歌曲请求为您挑选歌曲。总体而言，Spotify 的综合评论比 YouTube 喋喋不休的 DJ 感觉更紧凑、更容易忍受。也就是说，这两种软件的体验都不足以让我再次回来。

尽管 Spotify 声称，根据该公司的发布博客，它有“80% 的听众每周都会回归 DJ”，但我不会成为其中之一。我对人工智能 DJ 的拒绝并不是因为他们听起来如何。两家公司的声音都很体面，听起来也很人性化。他们评论的内容真正让我感到厌烦。无论是空洞的陈词滥调还是模仿人类的错误，我已经听够了。

Overall, Spotify’s synthetic commentary felt tighter and more tolerable than YouTube’s blabbering DJ. That said, neither software experience was enjoyable enough for me to return.

Although Spotify claims it has “80 percent of listeners coming back to DJ week after week,” according to the company’s launch blog, I won’t be one of them. My rejection of AI DJs isn’t based on how they audibly sound. The voices, from both companies, are decent and sound convincingly human. The content of their commentary is what truly turns me off. Whether it’s empty platitudes or mimicking human mistakes, I’ve heard enough.
paragraphs: I usually can’t pinpoint the moment I stop using a software feature, with most tools drifting out of fashion without an expiration date. That’s not the case with YouTube Music’s “Beyond the Beat,” an AI-generated DJ that explains songs to you.

YouTube Music is my music-streaming service of choice. And since I’m a software reporter, I always enable the beta features available through YouTube Labs, which include Beyond the Beat. YouTube’s AI DJ randomly interjects for about 30 seconds between songs, teeing up the vibe shift and providing context about the next track.

More listeners are encountering synthetic commentary built into their music streaming apps. While YouTube launched this experimental AI DJ in 2025, Spotify first introduced a similar tool back in 2023. It doubled down on its AI DJ efforts in November, expanding the different personalities available to users and adding more controls over the commentary.
These AI DJs aren’t just annoying. Their attempts to provide helpful context and mimic human candor ultimately fall flat. Lucky for me, both features are optional and avoidable.

After months of leaving it enabled, a bad experience with Beyond the Beat this week pushed me to swear off AI DJs altogether. I was listening to a pop divas playlist as part of my morning workout and got slapped with 30 seconds of exposition after a Slayyyter track:

“Hey Boy delivers that high-energy surge perfectly, but we're shifting our focus to a sharper, more visceral reality. In Rock Music, Charli XXC [sic] weaves in a biting, dark sense of humor regarding the physical toll of her relentless 2024 and 2025 touring. She turns the genuine nerve damage she sustained on the road into a strange sort of battle scar, reclaiming the exhaustion of a weary party girl as a badge of honor. It's an unflinching look at the cost behind the spectacle, where the grind of the industry becomes the actual subject matter. Here is Rock Music by Charli XXC [sic].”

What a lengthy paragraph of platitudes with little substance. That’s not even mentioning how the AI DJ butchered the pronunciation of a little-known, indie act called Charli XCX. This flub reflected my overall experience with YouTube Music’s AI DJ. It took me out of the groove and didn’t feel additive.

In another example, it went in-depth on the meaning of Olivia Rodrigo’s Expectations remix featuring Chappell Roan, calling it a "structural interpretation” that unpacks the “nuances of queer dating.” Then YouTube Music played the original track, sans Roan; so much for the queer yearning.

Curious how Spotify’s AI DJ experience would compare, I upgraded my account to the premium tier for access to that beta software. One of the biggest recent changes to Spotify’s AI DJ was adding new voices to the lineup, so I went into my settings and played the introduction clips for each of the eight English-language voices.

Maybe I was already a bit miffed from my YouTube Music experience because these voices immediately started to frustrate me. Multiple voices leaned into filler words such as “you know” and “like,” as the AI described the next songs it would play. Knowing an AI voice is being trained to use filler words to sound more human gave me the uncanny-valley ick.

Spotify’s AI DJ was fairly different from YouTube Music’s version. On Spotify, the AI DJ is also an algorithmically guided experience that picks songs for you based on past listening habits and song requests. Overall, Spotify’s synthetic commentary felt tighter and more tolerable than YouTube’s blabbering DJ. That said, neither software experience was enjoyable enough for me to return.

Although Spotify claims it has “80 percent of listeners coming back to DJ week after week,” according to the company’s launch blog, I won’t be one of them. My rejection of AI DJs isn’t based on how they audibly sound. The voices, from both companies, are decent and sound convincingly human. The content of their commentary is what truly turns me off. Whether it’s empty platitudes or mimicking human mistakes, I’ve heard enough.

title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
title_en: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
author: Matthias Bastian
article_content:
In a statement to Reuters, Megaspeed said Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang officially left the company on August 30, 2025, and has no current role there. Huang became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed in March 2023, according to Washington-based research group C4ADS. The company said it conducted "legitimate and lawful business"and had retained external legal counsel to conduct an internal investigation.

The New York Times reported in October 2025 that Megaspeed was under investigation over whether it helped Chinese customers obtain export-controlled Nvidia chips. There has also been speculation that Alice Huang may be a Chinese spy, which has not been confirmed.

Original article, November 15, 2026:

Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion worth of Nvidia high-performance chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, according to documents reviewed by the Wall Street Journal. The company is owned by Alice Huang, the former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Megaspeed shipped the chips to buyers in China who maintained long-standing business ties with local tech giants, the WSJ reports. The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that the US had sought to keep out of China through export controls. Megaspeed reportedly gained preferential access to scarce AI chips as an Nvidia cloud partner, apparently because it counted Chinese cloud and tech company Alibaba as a major client.

Nvidia officially reported $12.4 billion in China revenue over six months, accounting for 7 percent of total revenue. Short-selling firm Culper Research estimates, however, that more than 20 percent of Nvidia's revenue in the last fiscal year came from Chinese customers. A significant share of that China business may have flowed through indirect channels.

Megaspeed 在给路透社的一份声明中表示，中国女商人 Alice Huang 于 2025 年 8 月 30 日正式离开该公司，目前在该公司没有任何职位。据华盛顿研究组织 C4ADS 称，黄仁勋于 2023 年 3 月成为 Megaspeed 的控股股东。该公司表示，其开展了“合法合法的业务”，并聘请了外部法律顾问进行内部调查。

《纽约时报》2025 年 10 月报道称，Megaspeed 因是否帮助中国客户获得受出口管制的 Nvidia 芯片而受到调查。还有人猜测黄爱丽可能是中国间谍，但尚未得到证实。

原文，2026 年 11 月 15 日：

据《华尔街日报》查阅的文件显示，2024 年 3 月至 2025 年 6 月期间，Megaspeed 为中国企业安排了价值近 120 亿美元的 Nvidia 高性能芯片订单。该公司的所有者是爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang)，她是已被罢黜的英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的前情人。据《华尔街日报》报道，Megaspeed 将这些芯片运送给了与当地科技巨头保持着长期业务关系的中国买家。这些订单涵盖了美国试图通过出口管制阻止其进入中国的数十万个芯片。据报道，Megaspeed 作为 Nvidia 云合作伙伴获得了稀缺人工智能芯片的优先使用权，显然是因为它将中国云和科技公司阿里巴巴视为主要客户。

英伟达官方公布的六个月内中国营收为124亿美元，占总营收的7%。然而，卖空公司 Culper Research 估计，英伟达上一财年超过 20% 的收入来自中国客户。中国业务的很大一部分可能是通过间接渠道进行的。

title: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets
title_en: This AI Tamagotchi Turns Everyday Objects Into Needy Virtual Pets

inline_images.caption: Image may contain Plant Potted Plant Art Collage Pottery Jar Bathroom Indoors Room and Toilet
inline_images.alt: Image may contain Plant Potted Plant Art Collage Pottery Jar Bathroom Indoors Room and Toilet

author: Julian Chokkattu
article_content:
You forgot to water the plant. Instead of seeing yellowing leaves, you see a cute plant-shaped pet on a tiny screen, looking sad and dejected. Maybe that'll give you the push you needed to grab the watering can. As you pour water into the soil, the plant pet on the screen gets excited and happy.

That's the idea behind OATs, or Object Agent Twins—micro-agent AI avatars on tiny E Ink displays designed to pair with everyday household objects. The tech was created by Daehwa Kim, a fifth-year PhD student in Carnegie Mellon's Future Interfaces Group. Kim presented the project at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology in Detroit in early November, a forum where academics and industry experts explore human-computer interfaces, and she earned two Honorable Mention awards.

You might remember Tamagotchi, the popular egg-shaped toys from the ’90s that housed digital pets requiring real-time care and attention. Kim’s goal was to bring a similar experience to physical objects in our lives. “We bring this joy of caring from virtual to physical objects,” she tells WIRED. While folks have encouraged Kim to sell OAT kits online, she hasn't decided whether to pursue it as a business opportunity.

Kim says everyone spends all day staring at mobile devices, and AI agents—even if they're designed to handle tasks on your behalf—still demand attention from your smartphone screen. OATs were a way to bring those interactions out into the real world.

Giving AI a physical body isn't new, as companies rush to create “the next smartphone,” whether that's failed attempts like the Humane Ai Pin, OpenAI's upcoming hardware created in collaboration with famed ex-Apple designer Jony Ive, or Meta's Muse Charm. The pocket-sized gadget houses Meta's popular Muse AI agent and is expected to launch in December. Increasingly, though, companies have leaned on “cuteness” in their strategy for widespread adoption.

OATs have an E Ink display connected to internal and external sensors that can track things like moisture, temperature, humidity, light, occupancy, and motion. (The hardware is relatively cheap, around $20 for the main module.) The sprites are created with Google Gemini's Nano Banana image-generation service, creating a suite of emotions for various states based on the sensor data. You can set all of this up through a web portal, where you can name your OAT and choose which sensors to use for the object you're attaching it to.

The web app will generate “Positive” and “Negative” behaviors based on your object's name and description. So if the OAT is attached to a plant, positive triggers could be “consistent air temperature readings” and “low humidity levels” if the plant of choice prefers dry environments. However, you can customize these behaviors to suit your specific plant type.

It can be used for very simple things. Want to use your skateboard more often? Attach the OAT to your board, and if it hasn't detected motion for a few days, the avatar will look sad and lonely. You don't want that, do you? As Kim says, “These kinds of inanimate objects can be more expressive.” When you hop on the board, the OAT avatar will be happy, with fun faces.

The catch is that the system's battery life is really short, showing why this is more of a proof of concept than anything else. OATs last around three to four days, but paired with the sound-level sensor, they'll only last a day. It has a USB-C port for charging the lithium-ion polymer battery.

Kim says she distributed OATs to many people and found that they used them in three different ways. One is, “Am I being used?” Like when you attach an OAT to a coffee machine and have the avatar get excited when the machine starts grinding beans. The second is for warning people near an object. For example, 3D printers release toxic fumes during use, and attaching an OAT to one can warn people that the device is operational. And the third is to track their own behaviors. Someone attached an OAT to a dumbbell to track how often they lifted weights, encouraging themselves to exercise regularly so they wouldn't disappoint the AI pet.

The demo at the symposium was popular, and Kim turned it into a competition to see who could come up with the most interesting ideas about what objects to pair with the OATs. Kim's website features a gallery with sprites people made, from an animated conference badge to a panda avatar for an Owala water bottle.

But the demo also ignited a huge discussion about anthropomorphizing artificial intelligence, and whether it’s proper to give these sprites humanlike traits and emotions to make people feel connected with them.

It's already a topic in play within the AI industry. Companies often refer to their chatbot behaviors in human terms, like when they “hallucinate.” Anthropic announced a “dreaming” feature this summer where its AI agent cleaned up its local memory as a background process. These anthropomorphized terms can distort moral judgments about AI and cause people to overly trust the tools.

Kim says that's why OATs have very limited interactions, restricted to expressive emotions and the E Ink display.

“Anthropomorphism can be very useful in certain ways, like helping people to change their behaviors,” Kim says. “People name their car, and they name their bike. I rarely see people who name their iPhone. I feel like in the future of computing we will have more of a relationship with AI, but we should definitely be careful not to abuse this."

title_zh: 这个人工智能电子宠物将日常物品变成了需要帮助的虚拟宠物
summary_zh: 卡内基梅隆大学研究团队发布OATs项目，通过E Ink显示屏与多传感器将物理对象转化为交互式AI数字宠物
article_content_zh:
你忘了给植物浇水。你看到的不是泛黄的叶子，而是小屏幕上一只可爱的植物形状的宠物，看起来悲伤而沮丧。也许这会给你提供抓住喷壶所需的推动力。当你将水倒入土壤中时，屏幕上的植物宠物会变得兴奋和快乐。

这就是 OAT（即对象代理双胞胎）背后的理念——微型电子墨水显示屏上的微代理人工智能化身，旨在与日常家居用品配对。该技术是由卡内基梅隆大学未来接口小组五年级博士生 Daehwa Kim 创建的。 Kim 于 11 月初在底特律举行的 ACM 用户界面软件和技术研讨会上展示了该项目，该论坛是学术界和行业专家探讨人机界面的论坛，她获得了两项荣誉奖。

您可能还记得电子宠物，这是 90 年代流行的蛋形玩具，里面装有需要实时护理和关注的数字宠物。 Kim 的目标是为我们生活中的物体带来类似的体验。她告诉《连线》杂志：“我们将这种护理的乐趣从虚拟物体转移到了实体物体上。”虽然人们鼓励 Kim 在网上销售燕麦套件，但她尚未决定是否将其作为一个商业机会。

Kim 表示，每个人都整天盯着移动设备，而人工智能代理——即使它们是为了代表你处理任务而设计的——仍然需要你的智能手机屏幕关注。 OAT 是将这些互动带入现实世界的一种方式。

为人工智能赋予实体并不新鲜，因为各家公司都在争先恐后地打造“下一代智能手机”，无论是像Humane Ai Pin（OpenAI 即将推出的与著名前苹果设计师 Jony Ive 合作开发的硬件）这样的失败尝试，还是 Meta 的 Muse Charm。这款口袋大小的小工具内置了 Meta 广受欢迎的 Muse AI 代理，预计将于 12 月推出。然而，越来越多的公司在其广泛采用的策略中依靠“可爱”。

OAT 有一个电子墨水显示屏，连接到内部和外部传感器，可以跟踪湿度、温度、湿度、光线、占用和运动等信息。 （硬件相对便宜，主模块大约 20 美元。）精灵是使用 Google Gemini 的 Nano Banana 图像生成服务创建的，根据传感器数据为各种状态创建一套情绪。您可以通过门户网站来设置所有这些，您可以在其中命名您的 OAT 并选择要用于将其附加到的对象的传感器。

网络应用程序将根据对象的名称和描述生成“积极”和“消极”行为。因此，如果将燕麦附着在植物上，如果选择的植物喜欢干燥的环境，那么积极的触发因素可能是“一致的气温读数”和“低湿度水平”。但是，您可以自定义这些行为以适合您的特定植物类型。

它可以用于非常简单的事情。想更频繁地使用你的滑板吗？将 OAT 连接到你的主板上，如果它几天没有检测到运动，头像会看起来悲伤和孤独。你不想要那样，是吗？正如金所说，“这些无生命的物体可以更具表现力。”当你跳上棋盘时，OAT 头像会很高兴，表情有趣。

问题是该系统的电池寿命非常短，这说明了为什么这更像是一个概念验证而不是其他任何东西。 OAT 的使用寿命约为三到四天，但与声级传感器配合使用时，它们只能持续一天。它有一个 USB-C 端口，用于为锂离子聚合物电池充电。

Kim 说，她向很多人分发了燕麦，发现人们以三种不同的方式使用它们。一是“我被利用了吗？”就像当你将燕麦连接到咖啡机上并让虚拟人物在机器开始磨豆时感到兴奋一样。第二个用于警告物体附近的人。例如，3D 打印机在使用过程中会释放有毒烟雾，将 OAT 连接到 3D 打印机上可以警告人们该设备正在运行。第三是跟踪自己的行为。有人在哑铃上贴了一个 OAT，用来追踪他们举重的频率，鼓励自己定期锻炼，这样就不会让人工智能宠物失望。

研讨会上的演示很受欢迎，Kim 将其变成了一场竞赛，看看谁能就哪些物体与 OAT 配对提出最有趣的想法。 Kim 的网站设有一个画廊，里面有人们制作的精灵，从动画会议徽章到奥瓦拉水瓶的熊猫头像。

但该演示也引发了一场关于人工智能拟人化的激烈讨论，以及是否应该赋予这些精灵类似人类的特征和情感，以使人们感到与它们有联系。

这已经成为人工智能行业的一个热门话题。公司经常用人类的术语来描述他们的聊天机器人行为，比如他们“产生幻觉”的时候。 Anthropic 今年夏天宣布了一项“梦想”功能，其人工智能代理将清理其本地内存作为后台进程。这些拟人化的术语可能会扭曲对人工智能的道德判断，并导致人们过度信任这些工具。

Kim 说，这就是为什么 OAT 的交互非常有限，仅限于表达情感和电子墨水显示。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: OATs项目通过低门槛硬件结合边缘计算，避开了大模型硬件追求高性能计算的红海，切中了物联网设备交互极其匮乏的痛点。这种以‘情绪化交互’为核心的轻量级硬件范式，为家电物联网设备的人机协作界面提供了一种低功耗、易落地的技术替代方案。
ai_analysis.insight_en: By leveraging low-cost hardware and edge-computing, the OATs project bypasses the hardware performance arms race in AI and addresses the interaction void in IoT. This emotionally-driven, lightweight interface paradigm presents a low-power, commercially viable alternative for human-machine collaboration in household appliances.

article_content_en:
You forgot to water the plant. Instead of seeing yellowing leaves, you see a cute plant-shaped pet on a tiny screen, looking sad and dejected. Maybe that'll give you the push you needed to grab the watering can. As you pour water into the soil, the plant pet on the screen gets excited and happy.

That's the idea behind OATs, or Object Agent Twins—micro-agent AI avatars on tiny E Ink displays designed to pair with everyday household objects. The tech was created by Daehwa Kim, a fifth-year PhD student in Carnegie Mellon's Future Interfaces Group. Kim presented the project at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology in Detroit in early November, a forum where academics and industry experts explore human-computer interfaces, and she earned two Honorable Mention awards.

You might remember Tamagotchi, the popular egg-shaped toys from the ’90s that housed digital pets requiring real-time care and attention. Kim’s goal was to bring a similar experience to physical objects in our lives. “We bring this joy of caring from virtual to physical objects,” she tells WIRED. While folks have encouraged Kim to sell OAT kits online, she hasn't decided whether to pursue it as a business opportunity.

Kim says everyone spends all day staring at mobile devices, and AI agents—even if they're designed to handle tasks on your behalf—still demand attention from your smartphone screen. OATs were a way to bring those interactions out into the real world.

Giving AI a physical body isn't new, as companies rush to create “the next smartphone,” whether that's failed attempts like the Humane Ai Pin, OpenAI's upcoming hardware created in collaboration with famed ex-Apple designer Jony Ive, or Meta's Muse Charm. The pocket-sized gadget houses Meta's popular Muse AI agent and is expected to launch in December. Increasingly, though, companies have leaned on “cuteness” in their strategy for widespread adoption.

OATs have an E Ink display connected to internal and external sensors that can track things like moisture, temperature, humidity, light, occupancy, and motion. (The hardware is relatively cheap, around $20 for the main module.) The sprites are created with Google Gemini's Nano Banana image-generation service, creating a suite of emotions for various states based on the sensor data. You can set all of this up through a web portal, where you can name your OAT and choose which sensors to use for the object you're attaching it to.

The web app will generate “Positive” and “Negative” behaviors based on your object's name and description. So if the OAT is attached to a plant, positive triggers could be “consistent air temperature readings” and “low humidity levels” if the plant of choice prefers dry environments. However, you can customize these behaviors to suit your specific plant type.

It can be used for very simple things. Want to use your skateboard more often? Attach the OAT to your board, and if it hasn't detected motion for a few days, the avatar will look sad and lonely. You don't want that, do you? As Kim says, “These kinds of inanimate objects can be more expressive.” When you hop on the board, the OAT avatar will be happy, with fun faces.

The catch is that the system's battery life is really short, showing why this is more of a proof of concept than anything else. OATs last around three to four days, but paired with the sound-level sensor, they'll only last a day. It has a USB-C port for charging the lithium-ion polymer battery.

Kim says she distributed OATs to many people and found that they used them in three different ways. One is, “Am I being used?” Like when you attach an OAT to a coffee machine and have the avatar get excited when the machine starts grinding beans. The second is for warning people near an object. For example, 3D printers release toxic fumes during use, and attaching an OAT to one can warn people that the device is operational. And the third is to track their own behaviors. Someone attached an OAT to a dumbbell to track how often they lifted weights, encouraging themselves to exercise regularly so they wouldn't disappoint the AI pet.

The demo at the symposium was popular, and Kim turned it into a competition to see who could come up with the most interesting ideas about what objects to pair with the OATs. Kim's website features a gallery with sprites people made, from an animated conference badge to a panda avatar for an Owala water bottle.

But the demo also ignited a huge discussion about anthropomorphizing artificial intelligence, and whether it’s proper to give these sprites humanlike traits and emotions to make people feel connected with them.

It's already a topic in play within the AI industry. Companies often refer to their chatbot behaviors in human terms, like when they “hallucinate.” Anthropic announced a “dreaming” feature this summer where its AI agent cleaned up its local memory as a background process. These anthropomorphized terms can distort moral judgments about AI and cause people to overly trust the tools.

Kim says that's why OATs have very limited interactions, restricted to expressive emotions and the E Ink display.

“Anthropomorphism can be very useful in certain ways, like helping people to change their behaviors,” Kim says. “People name their car, and they name their bike. I rarely see people who name their iPhone. I feel like in the future of computing we will have more of a relationship with AI, but we should definitely be careful not to abuse this."

title: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service
title_en: Australia's central bank finds AI hitting young workers first, especially in software and customer service

inline_images.caption: In jobs with high potential AI exposure (quintile 5), employment among young people has declined since late 2022, while employment among older workers has risen. | Source: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA)
inline_images.caption_en: In jobs with high potential AI exposure (quintile 5), employment among young people has declined since late 2022, while employment among older workers has risen. | Source: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA)

author: Manuel Uth
article_content:
AI has barely displaced any jobs in Australia so far, but young workers entering highly exposed fields like software development are faring worse.

An analysis by Mike Major for Australia's central bank (RBA) built a monitoring system that focuses on the areas where effects are likely to appear first, namely entry-level workers and highly AI-exposed occupations such as programming, clerical work, and customer service.

According to the analysis, job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, with the steepest drop in the highest-exposure group. In that group, workers aged 15 to 24 and young college graduates have weaker employment rates and higher unemployment than older workers.

Major cautions against drawing early conclusions, since the study does not establish direct causation and measures only theoretical exposure, not actual use by companies. Post-pandemic shifts in the business cycle or in remote work could also be driving the numbers. According to SEEK data, AI is complementing existing work while also creating new demand for AI skills.

### Other studies paint a similar picture, with caveats

An August 2025 Stanford study based on millions of US payroll records found a similar pattern, with employment among 22- to 25-year-olds in AI-exposed occupations down 13 percent in relative terms since late 2022 and nearly 20 percent among young software developers. More experienced workers in the same occupations held steady or gained ground.

A March 2026 Anthropic study also found signs of declining hiring among 22- to 25-year-olds in exposed occupations, with job-finding rates down about 14 percent. It found no systematic rise in overall unemployment, however. Theoretical automation potential and actual AI use are far apart, according to the study.

Anthropic offers a company-level example. According to an internal review, the share of junior hires in technical roles has fallen from 27 percent to 9 percent since early 2025. In August 2026, AI agents across the company were already logging six times as many hours as human employees. Anthropic concedes that, as an extremely AI-intensive software company, it is a special case. Even so, researchers warn of a "tragedy of the cognitive commons", in which disappearing junior roles lead to a future shortage of experienced professionals, assuming those professionals are still needed.

A large study of 25,000 workers in Denmark confirms the lack of economy-wide impact. Despite a 64 percent AI adoption rate, researchers found no measurable changes in wages or hours worked. Workers saved an average of just 2.8 percent of their working time.

A January 2026 analysis of 10.6 million LinkedIn profiles and US unemployment data, however, cautions against blaming the downturn on AI alone. The research team led by Morgan Frank at the University of Pittsburgh found that the problems in exposed occupations started in early 2022, months before ChatGPT launched. Macroeconomic factors like the Fed's shift in interest rate policy or a correction after pandemic-era hiring surges may play a bigger role than previously assumed.

At the same time, AI is creating new demand. According to the World Economic Forum's "Future of Jobs Report 2025", 77 percent of surveyed companies are prioritizing upskilling over job cuts. WEF researchers project a net gain of 78 million jobs by 2030. According to LinkedIn, AI-related job postings grew sixfold in one year.

summary_en: Mike Major, a researcher at the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), found that demand for entry-level roles in high-exposure sectors like software, customer service, and clerical work has structurally declined since late 2022. The data corroborates a global trend where AI-driven automation of repetitive tasks disproportionately hampers early-career employment, while senior-level positions remain relatively insulated.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AI不仅在执行层面提升效率，其更大的隐性成本在于摧毁了产业界“师徒制”人才培育链路，即所谓的认知公共资源危机。长期来看，初级岗位的缺位将导致资深专家储备断档，使得企业未来在高端技术岗位上陷入严重的结构性人才短缺。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Beyond operational efficiency, AI poses a risk to the 'cognitive commons' by dismantling the apprenticeship pipeline essential for long-term skill acquisition. This structural attrition of junior roles will inevitably lead to a future talent drought for senior-level expertise, creating an unsustainable dependence on automated systems.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 澳大利亚储备银行（RBA）研究员Mike Major通过监测分析指出，自2022年底生成式AI普及以来，编程、客户服务及办公职能等高暴露领域初级岗位需求呈结构性下滑。数据验证了全球范围内的同类趋势，即AI在替代初级重复性劳动的过程中，导致应届生及年轻劳动者就业门槛显著抬升，而资深人员岗位则保持相对稳定。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Mike Major, a researcher at the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), found that demand for entry-level roles in high-exposure sectors like software, customer service, and clerical work has structurally declined since late 2022. The data corroborates a global trend where AI-driven automation of repetitive tasks disproportionately hampers early-career employment, while senior-level positions remain relatively insulated.

article_content_zh:
到目前为止，人工智能在澳大利亚几乎没有取代任何工作，但进入软件开发等高度暴露领域的年轻工人的情况更糟。

澳大利亚央行 (RBA) 的迈克·梅杰 (Mike Major) 进行的一项分析建立了一个监控系统，重点关注可能首先出现影响的领域，即初级工人和高度人工智能暴露的职业，如编程、文书工作和客户服务。

分析显示，自 2022 年底 ChatGPT 推出以来，所有群体的招聘信息均有所下降，其中曝光率最高的群体降幅最大。在这一群体中，15岁至24岁的工人和年轻的大学毕业生的就业率比年长工人低，失业率也高。

主要警告不要得出早期结论，因为该研究没有建立直接因果关系，并且仅衡量理论暴露，而不是公司的实际使用情况。大流行后商业周期或远程工作的变化也可能推动这一数字。 SEEK数据显示，人工智能正在补充现有工作，同时也创造了对人工智能技能的新需求。

### 其他研究也描绘了类似的景象，但也有一些警告

斯坦福大学 2025 年 8 月基于数百万美国薪资记录进行的一项研究发现了类似的模式，自 2022 年底以来，22 至 25 岁的人工智能相关职业的就业率相对下降了 13%，年轻软件开发人员的就业率下降了近 20%。相同职业中更有经验的工人保持稳定或取得进展。

2026 年 3 月的一项 Anthropic 研究还发现，22 至 25 岁人群中暴露职业的招聘量出现下降迹象，求职率下降了约 14%。然而，它发现总体失业率没有系统性上升。研究表明，理论上的自动化潜力和实际的人工智能应用相距甚远。

Anthropic 提供了一个公司层面的例子。根据内部审查，自 2025 年初以来，技术岗位初级员工的比例已从 27% 下降至 9%。到 2026 年 8 月，全公司的人工智能代理的工作时间已经是人类员工的六倍。 Anthropic 承认，作为一家人工智能极其密集的软件公司，这是一个特例。即便如此，研究人员警告称，将会出现“认知共享的悲剧”，即初级角色的消失会导致未来经验丰富的专业人员的短缺，假设这些专业人员仍然需要。

一项针对丹麦 25,000 名工人的大型研究证实，这对整个经济没有影响。尽管人工智能采用率为 64%，但研究人员发现工资或工作时间没有发生可衡量的变化。工人们平均只节省了 2.8% 的工作时间。

然而，2026 年 1 月对 1060 万个 LinkedIn 个人资料和美国失业数据的分析警告，不要将经济衰退仅仅归咎于人工智能。匹兹堡大学摩根·弗兰克 (Morgan Frank) 领导的研究团队发现，暴露职业的问题早在 2022 年初就开始出现，即 ChatGPT 推出前几个月。美联储利率政策的转变或大流行时期招聘激增后的调整等宏观经济因素可能比之前假设的发挥更大的作用。

与此同时，人工智能正在创造新的需求。根据世界经济论坛的《2025 年就业未来报告》，77% 的受访企业将技能提升置于裁员之上。世界经济论坛研究人员预计，到 2030 年，就业岗位将净增加 7800 万个。根据 LinkedIn 的数据，与人工智能相关的职位发布在一年内增长了六倍。
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】澳大利亚储备银行（RBA）研究员 Mike Major在澳大利亚劳动力就业市场：分析AI技术对初级岗位（15-24岁群体）的替代影响，并对比全球相关行业数据
【起因与机理】衡量AI普及对宏观就业结构及长期人才培育机制的潜在负面冲击
【核心事实细节】AI导致编程及办公类初级岗位招聘需求出现结构性萎缩。
【各方立场与态度】初级岗位减少可能引发未来行业资深专业人才储备断档。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] To evaluate structural shifts in employment and the long-term sustainability of the talent pipeline

[Industry Impact & Outlook] Long-term risk of 'tragedy of the cognitive commons' and talent pipeline stagnation.
article_content_en:
AI has barely displaced any jobs in Australia so far, but young workers entering highly exposed fields like software development are faring worse.

An analysis by Mike Major for Australia's central bank (RBA) built a monitoring system that focuses on the areas where effects are likely to appear first, namely entry-level workers and highly AI-exposed occupations such as programming, clerical work, and customer service.

According to the analysis, job postings have fallen across all groups since ChatGPT launched in late 2022, with the steepest drop in the highest-exposure group. In that group, workers aged 15 to 24 and young college graduates have weaker employment rates and higher unemployment than older workers.

Major cautions against drawing early conclusions, since the study does not establish direct causation and measures only theoretical exposure, not actual use by companies. Post-pandemic shifts in the business cycle or in remote work could also be driving the numbers. According to SEEK data, AI is complementing existing work while also creating new demand for AI skills.

### Other studies paint a similar picture, with caveats

An August 2025 Stanford study based on millions of US payroll records found a similar pattern, with employment among 22- to 25-year-olds in AI-exposed occupations down 13 percent in relative terms since late 2022 and nearly 20 percent among young software developers. More experienced workers in the same occupations held steady or gained ground.

A March 2026 Anthropic study also found signs of declining hiring among 22- to 25-year-olds in exposed occupations, with job-finding rates down about 14 percent. It found no systematic rise in overall unemployment, however. Theoretical automation potential and actual AI use are far apart, according to the study.

Anthropic offers a company-level example. According to an internal review, the share of junior hires in technical roles has fallen from 27 percent to 9 percent since early 2025. In August 2026, AI agents across the company were already logging six times as many hours as human employees. Anthropic concedes that, as an extremely AI-intensive software company, it is a special case. Even so, researchers warn of a "tragedy of the cognitive commons", in which disappearing junior roles lead to a future shortage of experienced professionals, assuming those professionals are still needed.

A large study of 25,000 workers in Denmark confirms the lack of economy-wide impact. Despite a 64 percent AI adoption rate, researchers found no measurable changes in wages or hours worked. Workers saved an average of just 2.8 percent of their working time.

A January 2026 analysis of 10.6 million LinkedIn profiles and US unemployment data, however, cautions against blaming the downturn on AI alone. The research team led by Morgan Frank at the University of Pittsburgh found that the problems in exposed occupations started in early 2022, months before ChatGPT launched. Macroeconomic factors like the Fed's shift in interest rate policy or a correction after pandemic-era hiring surges may play a bigger role than previously assumed.

At the same time, AI is creating new demand. According to the World Economic Forum's "Future of Jobs Report 2025", 77 percent of surveyed companies are prioritizing upskilling over job cuts. WEF researchers project a net gain of 78 million jobs by 2030. According to LinkedIn, AI-related job postings grew sixfold in one year.

author: Jonathan Kemper
article_content:
Meituan releases the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model built for AI agents. It was trained entirely on Chinese hardware and performs at the level US models like Claude Opus 5 reached a few months ago on coding benchmarks.

The LongCat team at Chinese food delivery company Meituan has released the weights for LongCat-2.5, one week after the model's official unveiling. LongCat-2.5 is built for agents that work through long, multi-step tasks autonomously, particularly coding. According to Meituan, it comes close to top Western models on several benchmarks.

LongCat-2.5 is a mixture-of-experts model that activates only a subset of its specialized subnetworks for each token it processes. Out of 1.6 trillion total parameters, roughly 48 billion are active per token. Through the API, the model handles up to one million tokens at once and generates responses up to 128,000 tokens long. It understands text, images, and video, responds in text, and lets users toggle reasoning on and off.

### LongCat-2.5 converts images into tokens

LongCat-2.5 builds on its predecessor LongCat-2.0 and adds image understanding. Many multimodal models bolt on a separate image encoder after the fact. LongCat-2.5 instead converts images into tokens that the model processes alongside text, as is standard practice for today's LLMs. The approach draws on the research model LongCat-Next and aims to improve visual coding, design, and 3D tasks.

For reinforcement learning, the team used real software tasks from GitHub pull requests along with recreated agent failures. To make sure the model actually solved the tasks during training, the developers blocked internet access in the training environments, removed Git history and cached files, and had a language model check its solutions for tricks. The team also distilled the capabilities of several specialized teacher models for agent work, reasoning, and dialog into LongCat-2.5.

### A sample deployment runs on 194 Huawei chips

Meituan quantizes the experts' weights and activations to 4-bit precision, which Chinese chips can process natively. In Meituan's load tests, throughput rises 43.3 percent for prompt processing and 42.77 percent for response generation compared with an 8-bit version. Meituan says accuracy stays on par with the uncompressed model.

This version is available in a separate repository. The self-hosting guide describes a cluster of 194 Huawei Ascend accelerators from the Atlas A2 series. Two handle image processing, 64 handle prompt ingestion, and 128 handle response generation. There's no guidance for Nvidia GPUs.

### LongCat-2.5 trails Opus 5 slightly on terminal tasks

The LongCat team reports 88.4 points on Terminal Bench v2.1, a benchmark that measures how well agents solve command-line tasks. Meituan lists Claude Opus 5 at 89.1, GPT-5.6 Sol at 88.8, and Deepseek-V4.1-Flash at the top of the table with 90.6.

DeepSWE tests how well models fix bugs in real code repositories. Here LongCat-2.5 jumps from 9.7 to 64.6 points, placing it behind every other model in the table except Claude Opus 4.8, with Deepseek-V4.1-Flash leading at 74.2 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 72.7. The more recent Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol are not included in the table.

Terminal Bench v4.0, the harder variant, puts LongCat-2.5 at 38.5 points, slightly above GPT-5.6 Sol's 37.3 but well below Opus 5's 53.9. The model posts 91.9 on the web search benchmark BrowseComp, the highest score in the table, though Meituan ran this test in its own environment.

The weights are available under the MIT license, which allows commercial use, modification, and redistribution. Users can also try LongCat-2.5 in a chat interface at https://longcat.ai/. Its API supports both the OpenAI and Anthropic formats and plugs into agent harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes. At launch, Meituan is charging a limited-time promotional price equivalent to roughly €0.27 per million input tokens and €1.07 per million output tokens.

Meituan says it trained the predecessor LongCat-2.0 in late June entirely on a cluster of more than 50,000 Chinese AI chips. Before that, the model ran anonymously as "Owl Alpha"on OpenRouter. Chinese open-weight models like Kimi K3.1 and GLM-5.3 have largely caught up with top US models on common benchmarks.

Open-weight models optimized for Chinese chips from the start make that hardware more attractive outside China too. Beyond multimodal agent models, Meituan is also working on image generators. The company previously released LongCat-Image, an open-source text-to-image model that gets by with just 6 billion parameters and prioritizes efficiency over sheer model size.

title_zh: 美团发布LongCat-2.5：全国产算力底座下的万亿参数模型
summary_zh: 美团发布1.6万亿参数多模态Agent模型LongCat-2.5，完全基于国产硬件训练，性能对标Claude Opus 5
article_content_zh:
美团发布LongCat-2.5权重，这是一个为AI智能体构建的1.6万亿参数模型。它完全在中国硬件上进行训练，其性能达到了 Claude Opus 5 等美国模型几个月前在编码基准上达到的水平。

在该模型正式发布一周后，中国食品配送公司美团的 LongCat 团队发布了 LongCat-2.5 的权重。 LongCat-2.5 是为能够自主完成长期、多步骤任务（尤其是编码）的代理而构建的。据美团称，它在多项基准测试中接近西方顶级机型。

LongCat-2.5 是一个专家混合模型，它只为其处理的每个令牌激活其专用子网络的子集。在 1.6 万亿个参数中，每个代币大约有 480 亿个参数处于活跃状态。通过 API，该模型可以一次处理多达 100 万个令牌，并生成长达 128,000 个令牌的响应。它可以理解文本、图像和视频，以文本形式做出响应，并允许用户打开和关闭推理。

### LongCat-2.5 将图像转换为token

LongCat-2.5 建立在其前身 LongCat-2.0 的基础上，并增加了图像理解功能。许多多模态模型事后都安装了单独的图像编码器。 LongCat-2.5 相反，将图像转换为模型与文本一起处理的标记，这是当今法学硕士的标准做法。该方法借鉴了 LongCat-Next 研究模型，旨在改进视觉编码、设计和 3D 任务。

对于强化学习，该团队使用了来自 GitHub 拉取请求的真实软件任务以及重新创建的代理故障。为了确保模型在训练期间确实解决了任务，开发人员在训练环境中阻止了互联网访问，删除了 Git 历史记录和缓存文件，并让语言模型检查其解决方案是否存在技巧。该团队还将几个专门的教师模型用于代理工作、推理和对话的功能提炼到 LongCat-2.5 中。

### 在 194 个华为芯片上运行的示例部署

美团将专家的权重和激活量化到 4 位精度，中国芯片可以本地处理。在美团的负载测试中，与 8 位版本相比，即时处理吞吐量提高了 43.3%，响应生成吞吐量提高了 42.77%。美团表示，准确性与未压缩模型保持一致。

该版本可在单独的存储库中找到。自托管指南描述了由 Atlas A2 系列的 194 个华为 Ascend 加速器组成的集群。两个处理图像处理，64 个处理提示摄取，以及 128 个处理响应生成。没有针对 Nvidia GPU 的指南。

### LongCat-2.5 在终端任务上稍微落后于 Opus 5

LongCat 团队在 Terminal Bench v2.1 上获得了 88.4 分，这是衡量代理解决命令行任务效果的基准。美团将 Claude Opus 5 列为 89.1，GPT-5.6 Sol 为 88.8，Deepseek-V4.1-Flash 以 90.6 名列榜首。

DeepSWE 测试模型在真实代码存储库中修复错误的效果。这里，LongCat-2.5 从 9.7 分跃升至 64.6 分，落后于表中除 Claude Opus 4.8 之外的所有其他模型，其中 Deepseek-V4.1-Flash 领先，得分为 74.2，GPT-5.6 Sol 得分为 72.7。较新的 Claude Opus 5.5 和 GPT-6.1 Sol 未包含在表中。

Terminal Bench v4.0（较难的变体）将 LongCat-2.5 评为 38.5 分，略高于 GPT-5.6 Sol 的 37.3，但远低于 Opus 5 的 53.9。该模型在网络搜索基准 BrowseComp 上得分为 91.9，是表中的最高分，尽管美团在自己的环境中运行了此测试。

这些权重可在 MIT 许可下使用，允许商业使用、修改和重新分发。用户还可以在 https://longcat.ai/ 的聊天界面中试用 LongCat-2.5。其 API 支持 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 格式，并可插入 Claude Code、Codex 和 Hermes 等代理工具中。在推出时，美团点评的限时促销价格约为每百万个输入代币 0.27 欧元，每百万个输出代币 1.07 欧元。

美团表示，它于 6 月底完全在超过 50,000 个中国人工智能芯片的集群上训练了前身 LongCat-2.0。在此之前，该模型以“Owl Alpha”的身份在 OpenRouter 上匿名运行。 Kimi K3.1和GLM-5.3等中国开放重量型号在共同基准上已基本赶上美国顶级型号。

从一开始就针对中国芯片进行优化的开放权重模型也使硬件在中国以外也更具吸引力。除了多模式代理模型之外，美团还致力于图像生成器的研究。该公司之前发布了 LongCat-Image，这是一种开源文本到图像模型，仅需要 60 亿个参数，并且优先考虑效率而不是模型大小。
